author: jorgensandhaug
body:
> **Do not land this until a release containing #6280 is the previous production release** (that is, until `scripts/runtime-posture-baseline.json` pins a source commit that includes #6280). Before then, the previous release's readiness rejects the runtime grant this migration makes on a SECURITY DEFINER routine it does not know, and old API and worker pods would fail readiness during the rolling deploy. The "Previous-binary database readiness" check fails on this PR until the baseline advances; that is the gate working, not a flake.

## Problem

#6280 (keep a browser while its agent works or waits) creates `opengeni_private.list_agent_held_browser_sessions` in migration 1002 with its runtime `EXECUTE` withheld for one release, following the two-release rule in `docs/migrations-expand-contract.md`. Until the grant, `listAgentHeldBrowserSessions` checks the privilege first and lists nothing, so the API renews no browser holds on any placement.

## Change

- Migration `1004_browser_hold_runtime_grant.sql` (rolling) grants `EXECUTE` on the routine to every configured application role, as 0950 did for the recording retention inventory.
- `runtime-posture.ts`: the routine leaves `DEFERRED_RUNTIME_PRIVATE_ROUTINES`, so readiness and provisioning now require the grant.
- `listAgentHeldBrowserSessions` drops its grant check and calls the routine directly.
- `grantDeferredRuntimeAccess` (test helper) no longer grants it; the worker listing test no longer needs the grant step and covers the full listing behaviour.
- `runtime-posture-compatibility-postgres.test.ts`: this binary reports `runtime role lacks EXECUTE` when the grant is revoked.
- `slack-bot-migration-compatibility.test.ts`: the 0864 reprovisioning pins no longer expect the routine withheld.
- `docs/migrations-expand-contract.md`, changeset, release schema contract list.

Migration number 1004 leaves 1003 for the index in #6294, which should land first; renumber with `scripts/renumber-migration.ts --next` if the order changes.

## Model-visible text and prompt cache

None. 0 bytes.

## Tests

- Root of this branch is #6280's head; the diff is only the grant.
- Pass locally: `runtime-posture.test.ts` (134), worker `idle-interaction-release` and `embedded-lifecycle` (45), `release-schema-contract` (27), the five migration checks, db typecheck, oxfmt, oxlint.
- `runtime-posture-compatibility-postgres.test.ts`: the new "this binary requires the definer and table grants 0947, 0950 and 1004 make" passes. The three pinned-previous-binary tests fail with `unknown routine opengeni_private.list_agent_held_browser_sessions(integer, bigint) exposes SECURITY DEFINER execution`, which is the landing condition above; they pass once the baseline pins a release that knows the routine.
- The real-database posture suites (0864, 0733, 0726 and `runtime-posture.test.ts`) pass, 152 tests, apart from the three pinned-previous-binary tests above.

## Risks

- Landing before the baseline advances would break the rolling deploy's old pods (see the top).
- Once granted, every API replica renews holds every 2 minutes, as #6280 describes.

author: pdbethke
body:
These come from kirby-app's 0.22.0 demo recording (pdbethke/kirby-app#64: Drago vs GORGON, 135 events, recorded through the api harness with a mock medialib that always takes the first offer). I reproduced the fight in-engine with `FirstLegalChooser` on the same seeds before changing anything.

## Defects (fixed)

**1. BODY that gets through costs STUN** (6E2 p.105: "1 STUN for every 1 point of BODY damage that gets through his defenses"; Ogre takes "5 BODY, 0 STUN" and so "takes 5 STUN regardless of his defenses").
- Root cause: no damage door applied the floor. `actions/base.py` took STUN as `stun*mult - total_defense` and stopped there.
- Effect in the demo: Drago's Armor Piercing RKA against GORGON (ED 35, which AP halves to 17; rED 0) did 8/6/6/6 BODY with `stun_dealt` 0/0/0/1. The payload and `VitalsChanged` agreed with each other; both were below the rule.
- Fix: `resolution.damage.stun_for_body_taken`, a floor (never an addition) applied last, to damage taken. It is wired into the attack pipeline, lingering doses, impact/fall and collapse.
- `test_dr_50_normal_does_not_apply_to_killing` asserted the defect (STUN 0 with 4 BODY through). It is corrected.

**2. A repeated Presence Attack rolls a die less** (6E2 p.140: "-1d6 on the second attack, -2d6 on the third attack, and so forth").
- Root cause: never modelled, so every shout rolled PRE/5 - 1. That is in neither the engine nor the old driver.
- Fix: `pre_attacks/landing.py`, where `repeats_against` counts each attacker's earlier PAs per target from the log. A group roll is made at the most dice any target faces, and each target is judged on his own dice.
- A 0d6 shout can affect nobody, so `without_spent_shouts` removes it from the menu in `_situation_for`.
- Demo: GORGON rolled 4d6 in all 8 Phases. Now 4, 3, 2, 1, and then the offer is gone.

## Correct behaviour (now pinned)

- **"No effect" ×8 was legitimate.** Every total (9–19) was under Drago's PRE 20 (6E2 p.139).
- **No chooser can spend every Phase on PAs.** The one-free-PA-a-Phase ruling (`in_the_phase.py`) takes PA off the menu once he has made one, so the returned Phase has to be spent on something else. Pinned by `test_shouting_never_takes_the_whole_phase`.
- **"Abort to Dodge right after his own action".** This was a Dodge taken in his own Phase, after a No-Time PA (6E2 p.20, p.25, p.56). The engine records every Dodge through `mark_aborting`, which is why the row is `AbortDeclared`. `abort_windows` gives up THIS Phase (T1 S12) because his slot was unspent.
- **"He still acts at T2 S3".** That is right: T2 S3 is his next Phase, and the +3 DCV ran until it (6E2 p.56). The out-of-turn Abort question is still asked only of a man with an attack coming at him (`loop/reactions.py`).
- **The Holds come from the recorder.** The mock takes the first offer, and once enraged GORGON's first offer after the PA was `hold`. GORGON has no ranged attack at 25 m.

## Notes for consumers

- kirby-app could label an `AbortDeclared` that is followed by the same man's `PhaseSpent(reason="acted")` in the same Segment as a Dodge, not an Abort.
- PA payloads now carry `dice` after the repeat penalty, with a repeat line in `audit`.
- The event schema is unchanged and the version is not bumped (CHANGELOG `0.22.1 — unreleased`).

Not investigated, flagged: an Enraged man is offered `hold` (6E1 p.424-425 not checked).

## Tests

- New seam tests (through `run_phase`): `tests/loop/test_body_through_is_stun_taken.py`, `test_a_repeated_presence_attack_weakens.py` and `test_a_dodge_on_his_own_phase.py`.
- Four of the new tests fail on origin/main. The pins pass there.
- Full suite, fresh build docs: 3248 passed, 3 xfailed (origin/main: 3239 passed).

author: wixette
body:
M6, the second milestone of 0.1.0: the main app's frame and the Weave workspace, at `index.html`. Notes and acceptance spec: [design/m6-notes.md](design/m6-notes.md).

**What it builds**
- **The frame.** The top bar holds the app's own: Learn and Weave, Share, the language, About. Below it sit the cards, the stage and the cloth. On a phone, the stage is on top, with a sheet below it (peek, half, full).
- **The stage.** It shows one, two or four views: the section, side, front, the loom in 3D, or any of the five units alone. Each view names itself in its own corner, and each 3D view has an ⓘ with its unit's idea. Wide screens open with two views.
- **Time, under the stage:** the status caption, then the six moments as a stepper (a state, not buttons), then the controls. Play is the largest, and reset is as large as the steps.
- **Settings beside what they change:**
  - the head and tie-up are a chip over the cards, showing their values;
  - the colours are a palette over the cloth;
  - the chain's end is a switch that laces or opens the chain.
- **Panels** resize by their edges and close to a rail, by pointer or keyboard, and their sizes are remembered.
- **Keyboard:** Space, ← →, 1–4, F, Esc.
- **Sound:** one sound per moment of a pick, with placeholders in `audio/` (`pnpm sounds`) until the recorded files take their names.
- **Languages:** the frame, the 3D parts' names and the units' ideas, in all ten.

**Fixes found on the way**
- A shared link now keeps the moment within the pick.
- The chain draws a wide card whole.
- The frame's names for screen readers follow the language.

**Checks**
- `pnpm test`: 310 pass, including a test that every named 3D part has a message matching the model's own English name.
- `pnpm selftest`: all 8 pages pass, including the app's 9 new checks (S-1 to S-9). The frame is checked at five sizes, from a phone to a 1920 desktop.
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm check:refs` and `reuse lint`: clean.

The layout was reviewed at the planned stop, and the reviewer's later points on the controls and settings are in.

author: madenvel
body:
Closes #180.

## Each folder is a visit

Opening a folder used to change the page in place, so Back left My Library whatever depth you were at. Each folder you open is now a visit of its own, and Back goes back up the way you came.

- **Up one folder and crumbs:** where they lead to the folder this one was opened from, they act exactly as Back, so going in and out doesn't pile up history. Otherwise they open that folder as a new visit, which Back undoes. Examples: Up from a folder the page reopened on, or a crumb several levels up.
- **Saved path:** going back to a folder makes it the one My Library reopens on.

## Folders reopen where they were left

A folder you go back to is one of the six visits kept in memory, so it comes back exactly as it was. A folder opened again as a new visit, or after its visit was dropped, reopens at the same scroll position with the rows it had loaded and no new request to the server.

- The 32 folders left most recently are kept until the server changes.
- A folder's place is recorded when it goes out of sight, so a visit dropped from history much later can't write an older place over a newer one.
- A folder the library has updated since it was left reopens at the same place and refreshes in place.
- Rows above a folder reopened far down are laid out on the way there and dropped, and they don't load their artwork.

## Fast scroller on Android

Every browsing list at least four screens long gets a thumb at its trailing edge while it scrolls. That covers folders, catalog listings, albums, playlists, collections, an artist's releases and tracks, and search results. The thumb fades 1.5s after the list stops; on folder pages it sits below the folder actions held under the bar. A collection being edited and a catalog's overview of shelves have none.

- Where the listing says how long it is, the thumb spans all of it, not just the loaded rows. Dragged past them, it loads up to its position in one request (at most 500 rows) and the list follows. Taken back up, it stops loading.
- Held over subfolders, which the server lists by name, a bubble beside it shows the initial of the folder at the top. Folders are the only listing known to be ordered by name, so tracks and other listings get no bubble.
- Rows passed while dragging don't load their artwork.
- The thumb is neutral grey per PALETTE.md: `textMuted`, and `textSecondary` while held. The bubble is `surfaceOverlay` with a `borderDefault` edge.
- Linux and the other desktops keep their existing scrollbar.

## Implementation

- `SearchSessionNotifier.openFolder` pushes a visit. `showFolderAt` (crumbs) and `showEnclosingFolder` (Up) call `goBack()` when the previous visit is that folder, and push one otherwise. `goBack` saves the folder path it returns to.
- `lib/widgets/fast_scroller.dart`: `FastScroller` (its paging inputs are optional, for search results, which hold everything already), plus `DeferringScrollController`, which tells rows to put off loading images while the list jumps.
- `InfiniteListView` gains `place` / `onLeave` to restore and report where a list was. It reports when its `TickerMode` turns off (hidden under a newer visit), or on dispose if it was still shown. It also gains `fastScroll` to add the thumb, and loads up to the row the thumb was dragged to.
- `docs/browsing-design-guide.md`: the Folder section and the History status line describe the new behaviour.

## Testing

- `flutter analyze` is clean.
- The full `flutter test` suite passes.
- `test/folder_history_test.dart` drives the full browse view:
  - Back from a folder returns to its parent at the same scroll position
  - Up from a folder just opened returns to the parent's own visit
  - a crumb to an older folder opens it as a new visit at its saved position (this one fails if the hide-time save is turned off)
- `test/folder_navigation_test.dart` covers the history rules at the provider level.
- `test/folder_page_test.dart` covers the saved places and the fast scroller. `test/catalog_header_test.dart` checks that a long catalog's thumb drags to its last row.
- The app was not run on a device.

author: detherington
body:
The iPad view decided whether a stroke has pressure from its landing sample alone (`touch.type == .pencil && touch.force > 0`). Apple's documentation says a Pencil's force "is estimated at first, and may not always be updated", so a Pencil Pro landing at an estimated zero had its whole stroke drawn from speed, as if it were the USB-C Pencil.

Now, in `PaintingView.strokeHasPressure(beginning:)`, a Pencil stroke starts with pressure if the landing sample reads a force, if an update to that force is expected (`estimatedPropertiesExpectingUpdates` contains `.force`), or if this Pencil has reported force before in the session. The USB-C Pencil reads zero and expects no update, so it still draws from speed; a finger never has pressure, as before.

Safety net: a stroke that began without pressure switches to the Pencil's own the moment a nonzero force arrives, in a later sample or through `touchesEstimatedPropertiesUpdated`. `CanvasViewModel.strokeReportsPressure()` does the switch in the engine: samples already drawn keep their pressure, later ones use the Pencil's, and the recording's `hasPressure` follows so a replay matches.

Tests: one new engine test for the mid-stroke switch and the recording. Mac suite 289 run, 3 skipped, 0 failures (a first run had three failures in `ShellTests`' wide-window test, a window clamped to the screen; green on rerun, unrelated). iOS build clean; a finger stroke on the iPad simulator still logs as from speed at the same pressure as before. The Pencil path cannot be exercised on a simulator: reasoned and compiled, not yet tried with a Pencil in hand, which `docs/ios-plan.md` notes. Refined force values are still not applied back to samples already drawn.

author: benchmarkcd
body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## What changed

Session refresh, follow-up reminders, a required next step, logged email, and admin owner assignment. Existing RLS policies, `esc()` escaping, and dirty-row saves are unchanged. Reset All Data is not back.

- **Stay signed in.** The access token is refreshed with `refresh_token` about 90 seconds before expiry, when the tab becomes visible, and after a 401. The same request is retried after a successful refresh. Sign-out happens only when the refresh fails and the access token is already expired, or the server still returns 401. Pending edits are stored in `localStorage` (`refuge_pending_edits`, not the old full-cache key) and written back after the next sign-in. The login screen says **Not saved, sign in again**.
- **Follow-ups.** A Follow-ups view and a dashboard card list overdue tasks, tasks due today, and active contacts with no logged activity in N days. N is `quietDays` on the `settings` row of `app_settings` (default 30), edited by admins in Settings. Admins can filter by person. Fundraisers see only their own.
- **Daily digest.** `supabase/functions/daily-digest` plus `pg_cron` in the new migration. Not deployed. No secrets are in the repo.
- **Required next step.** Active pipeline stages (Prospect, Discovery Meeting, Committed, Onboarding, Active Investor) need an open task due today or later. Cold, Declined, On Hold, and Exited do not. A **No next step** badge and filter stay until a future task exists. Changing stage, completing or deleting the last open task, or logging an activity opens a dismissible Set next step dialog (action, date, +2d / +1w / +2w, optional template).
- **Email.** See the audit below. Send logs an email activity and can create the next-step task.
- **Owners.** Admins get an Owner control on one contact and in the bulk bar, and the owner name on contact cards. Fundraisers never see the control. Owner changes go through `set_contact_owner`, not the dirty upsert, so a later save does not overwrite `owner_id`.

### Email audit

Before this change, the Google Identity Services script was loaded and unused. Sign in with Google is Supabase Auth only and does not grant `gmail.send`. `copyTemplate` copied merged text and did not log anything. `openInGmail` opened a Gmail compose URL and did not log an activity or create a task. "Log Email" was a separate manual activity.

Sending now uses Google Identity Services in the browser with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send` and a public OAuth client ID saved in Settings. There is no client secret and no backend. If the client ID is empty, or Gmail rejects the send, the page opens the Gmail compose link and logs the activity as **opened in Gmail** (`gmailStatus: opened`). A successful API send is logged as `sent`, with type `email`, subject, a 240-character snippet, date, and sender. Merge fields: `[INVESTOR_NAME]`, `[AMOUNT]`, `[OFFERING]`, `[FUNDRAISER_NAME]`, `[FUNDRAISER_EMAIL]`.

## Migration to run

Run only `supabase/migrations/rls_roles_followups.sql` in the Supabase SQL editor for project `uivltttwigqejmqqfxuj`, after `rls_roles.sql`. The filename sorts after that file. It is idempotent, adds `owner_id` before the functions that use it, and does not drop existing policies.

It creates:

- `digest_sends` (service role only)
- `list_auth_users()` — security definer, `is_admin()` required, reads `auth.users`
- `set_contact_owner(contact_id text, new_owner uuid)` — security definer, `is_admin()` required, sets `owner_id` on the contact and cascades to investments, activities, and tasks by `data->>'contactId'`
- `pg_cron` job `daily-followup-digest` at `30 11,12 * * *` (11:30 and 12:30 UTC)

If `CREATE EXTENSION` for `pg_cron` or `pg_net` fails, enable both under Database → Extensions and run the file again.

Then store the cron secret in Vault (same string as `DIGEST_CRON_SECRET`, not committed):

```sql
select vault.create_secret(
  '<long random string>',
  'digest_cron_secret',
  'Follow-up digest cron'
);
```

The function sends only when America/New_York is in the 7:00 hour, so one of those two UTC runs is about 7:30 AM New York in both EDT and EST. `digest_sends` stops a second send the same New York day.

## Edge Function deploy

Not deployed from this PR. Mail uses the Gmail API with a refresh token (no paid email vendor). `DIGEST_PROVIDER=webhook` posts the same `{to, subject, text, html}` JSON to another URL if you would rather not use Gmail.

`SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` are injected. Do not set them. `verify_jwt` is false because pg_cron has no user JWT. The function still requires `x-digest-secret` or a service-role bearer token.

```bash
supabase login
supabase link --project-ref uivltttwigqejmqqfxuj

supabase secrets set --project-ref uivltttwigqejmqqfxuj \
  DIGEST_CRON_SECRET='<same string stored in vault.digest_cron_secret>' \
  DIGEST_PROVIDER='gmail' \
  DIGEST_GMAIL_CLIENT_ID='<oauth client id>' \
  DIGEST_GMAIL_CLIENT_SECRET='<oauth client secret>' \
  DIGEST_GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN='<refresh token for the mailbox that sends the digest>'

supabase functions deploy daily-digest --project-ref uivltttwigqejmqqfxuj --no-verify-jwt --use-api
```

Mint the refresh token in [OAuth 2.0 Playground](https://developers.google.com/oauthplayground/) with your own client id and secret and scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`, signed in as the mailbox that should send the digest.

Webhook instead of Gmail:

```bash
supabase secrets set --project-ref uivltttwigqejmqqfxuj \
  DIGEST_PROVIDER='webhook' \
  DIGEST_WEBHOOK_URL='https://<your-endpoint>'
```

Dry run, no mail:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://uivltttwigqejmqqfxuj.supabase.co/functions/v1/daily-digest?dry=1&force=1' \
  -H 'x-digest-secret: <DIGEST_CRON_SECRET>'
```

`force=1` ignores the 7:00 New York hour. `resend=1` sends again even if today was already claimed. Leave both off for cron.

## Google OAuth setup (Dana)

In-app send is separate from the digest mailbox.

1. In Google Cloud Console, enable the Gmail API. Do not put a client secret in the CRM.
2. OAuth consent screen: add scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send`. This is a restricted scope. An Internal screen works only for Google accounts in that Workspace, so `info@benchmarkcd.com` can use it only if that account is in the same Workspace. An External screen shows a consent warning until Google verifies the app. Until consent works, Send opens Gmail and still logs the activity as opened in Gmail.
3. Create a **Web application** OAuth client. Authorized JavaScript origin: `https://benchmarkcd.github.io`.
4. As an admin, paste the client ID into Settings → Google OAuth client ID and save. It is stored in `app_settings`, not in git.

Each person consents once in the browser for their own Google account.

## Test checklist

Automated here: `node tests/digest.test.mjs`, `node tests/static.test.mjs`, and `node tests/browser-check.mjs` (Chrome, no Supabase login). The new SQL was checked statically and was not executed against Postgres.

### Admin (Dana, Blake, or Julie / info@benchmarkcd.com)

- Sign in, edit a contact, wait until the access token is near expiry or force a 401, and confirm the edit still saves. If refresh cannot continue, the banner says **Not saved, sign in again**, the edit is still there after sign-in, and it syncs.
- Follow-ups shows your overdue and due-today tasks and gone-quiet contacts. The person filter can show one fundraiser or everyone. The dashboard card matches your own list.
- Settings: change gone-quiet days, reload, and confirm the list uses the new N.
- An active contact with no future open task shows **No next step**. Filter contacts and the pipeline on it. Advance a stage, complete the last open task, or log an activity and confirm the Set next step dialog. Dismiss it and confirm the badge remains. Save +2d / +1w / +2w and confirm the badge clears.
- Send a template with merge fields. With a client ID, it

body:

_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9TSbb9RiQLSUNmAoRYsMSCQ)_

Fixes #26346

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:记录动态里点自己的回应撤回时，改走服务端新开的「撤回自己回应」专用接口 `DELETE /api/v1/comments/reactions/:id`,不再走通用数据删除接口;撤回按钮的权限判断不再要求 `delete` 授权。
- **为什么改**:普通成员(只有全员默认授权、没有职位)能加回应却永远撤不回：通用删除要对象级 `delete` 授权，而全员授权集按 ADR-0090 D5 不能带它。服务端那一半已在 PR #26345 落地。
- **风险与回滚**:风险低，只动回应芯片的撤回一条写路径和地图里一行;别人的回应仍然不会出现撤回(点了是加自己的)。回滚即 revert 本 PR,旧路径回来，普通成员重新撤不回。
- **先看**:① `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` 的 `handleToggleReaction` 里 `write` 的撤回分支;② `ui/packages/core/src/utils/affordanceGrants.ts` 的 `feedReactionRemove` 行;③ `RecordDetailView.feedGrant-12082.test.tsx` 新增的 describe 块。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.feedGrant-12082.test.tsx`,预期全绿，其中 "a member with no grant beyond create on sys_comment_reaction adds a reaction and takes it back" 断言请求打到 `/api/v1/comments/reactions/new-row`、方法 DELETE。
- **需要你做的**:无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **The take-back's door.** On the records store, a click on the caller's own reaction chip now removes the row through the unreact door, `DELETE /api/v1/comments/reactions/:id` (mounted by `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, server half in #26345), called through the page's existing authenticated fetch and `VITE_SERVER_URL` base, the way the record page already reaches non-data routes. No body and no query parameter are sent. A non-2xx answer is a refused write: the existing settle step puts the reaction back and raises the one "Your reaction was not saved" toast. The generic `DELETE /api/v1/data/sys_comment_reaction/:id` is no longer called from the feed. No `@objectstack/client` method is added.
- **The affordance row.** `feedReactionRemove` in `AFFORDANCE_GRANTS` changes value from `{ crud: 'delete', grant: 'delete' }` to `{ crud: null, grant: 'create' }`. `crud: null` because the write no longer goes through the object's data door (the same meaning the attachment rows carry); `grant: 'create'` because the take-back is offered to whoever may react. The row's TYPE keeps its shape (`AffordanceGrantRow`, same two keys) and `ConsoleAffordance` keeps the same member set; no export is added or removed.
- **Mine.** Which chip offers a take-back is unchanged: the click handler already takes back only when the caller's id is among the emoji's reactors, and removes only the row id the read or the create recorded for the caller (`groupReactionRows` keys on the row's server-stamped `user_id`). A click on another member's chip adds the caller's own reaction.
- **Docs.** `ui/content/docs/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx` no longer says a take-back needs the delete grant.
- **sdui record.** None. The per-package records were retired by #26367 while this PR was open. The main merge took the modify/delete with `git rm`, and CI's Build & E2E UI regenerates the manifest (`sdui.manifest.json` unchanged: 106 components).

## Tests

New regression cases (in `RecordDetailView.feedGrant-12082.test.tsx`, describe "a take-back goes through the unreact door, and only on the caller's own reaction"):

- a member with only the create grant on `sys_comment_reaction` adds 🎉 and clicks it again: one call to `/api/v1/comments/reactions/new-row` with `{ method: 'DELETE', credentials: 'include' }`, no data-door delete, and the chip goes away;
- another member's 👍 chip: the click creates the caller's own row, and the unreact door is never called;
- the door answers 403: the reaction is put back (count 1) and `toast.error` is raised once.

Forced test edits:

1. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.feedGrant-12082.test.tsx` — the authenticated-fetch mock now returns a hoisted mock (it returned a bare `vi.fn()`); "a take-back asks the delete grant … writes nothing" becomes "a take-back reads no delete grant … removes it through the unreact door"; the full-grant CONTROL and the registered-schema case assert the door's URL instead of `dataSource.delete(sys_comment_reaction, r1)`.
2. `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/affordanceGrantMap-12082.test.tsx` — `EXPECTED_GRANT.feedReactionRemove` is `'create'`; the write-census entry `RecordDetailView > handleToggleReaction > write :: delete` is deleted, since that site no longer calls a `DataSource` write (the census states it does not see a write through its own route, the same as the attachment upload).
3. `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.reactionRecords-12078.test.tsx` — not named in the dispatch; forced because its fake server asserted the take-back as `delete(sys_comment_reaction, id)`. The fake server now also models the unreact door per member (removes the member's own row, `403` on anyone else's), and the two take-back cases assert the removed ids at the door and that `delete` is not called.

## Acceptance notes

- The door authorizes on the row's `created_by`; the chip decides "mine" on the row's `user_id`. Both are stamped server-side from the reacting session at create (the create hook stamps `user_id`, the engine stamps `created_by`), so they name the same member for every row made through the data door. Keying the chip on `created_by` was not done here (it would move the read's grouping too); noted for the seat.
- The `feedReactionRemove` row now asks the same grant as `feedReactionAdd`, and the reaction control is only handed over when `feedReactionAdd` allows it, so on the records store the take-back is in practice decided by ownership alone, as the card asks.

## Verification

Commands and readings are in the os-dev-report on #26346, taken at this PR's head.

</details>

body:
Fixes #5000

Quota Details no longer shows raw epoch milliseconds. Observed, reset and projected-depletion times read as local clock times next to the existing age and reset duration, in the board's local zone (`App.local_zone`).

## What
- `board/local_time.rs` (new, small): `time_in(at_ms, now_ms, &TimeZone)`: the time today, the weekday and date this year, the full date in another year (`2025-10-03 23:30`), so an old date is never read as a recent one. `cronboard::line::time` is a thin name-resolving shim over it, so Cron output is unchanged; Cron and Details no longer depend on each other.
- `home/limits/detail.rs`: the four raw-ms lines use it. The parts of one time are joined with no-break spaces here, so `notes::wrap` (which breaks at ASCII spaces only) wraps before a time and never inside it. An unrepresentable timestamp reads `—`. The trailing raw `(<ms> ms)` duration after `before reset` is dropped (the readable duration is already shown).
- Core's observation and reset timestamps are untouched; only the string changes. No new read, re-dating or forecast rule.

## Oracle
6300 -> 6316 frames: 16 new (`quota-details`, `quota-details-week` at 100 and 40 wide, four looks, Tokyo-pinned), none changed or removed; style table unchanged (111). Decoded delta approved by tmt-tui-lead; recorded in a separate commit from source head `d2c20250300d4dcae6dcd970b5d56e02b891f942`.

## Tests
Same day / other day / other year, the day boundary by zone (23:05Z Sunday is 08:05 Monday in Tokyo), the year by zone (Dec 31 UTC is Jan 1 in Tokyo), a DST instant in New York, an unrepresentable timestamp, no `ms` or long number left in any line, a narrow wrap keeps a time whole and a width below it loses nothing. body:
## Resumo

Primeira (e única) fase da etapa **Marcação pai** (épico `epic/marcacao-pai`, detalhada no `PLAN.md`): com vários itens selecionados, o botão **Envolver** do resumo da seleção múltipla cria uma marcação pai em volta de todos.

- **Modelo** (`src/model/multiSelection.ts`): `canWrapItems`, `wrapRect` e `wrapItems`. Retângulo do conjunto mais 8 px de margem, limitado ao container e ao pai atual do conjunto; a nova entra no array antes da primeira selecionada (ganha o desempate de área igual). O pertencimento sai só do `settleHierarchy`, nada é escolhido à mão.
- **Store**: action `wrapItems`, uma entrada no desfazer, devolve o id.
- **UI**: botão **Envolver** antes de Trancar; a nova fica selecionada sozinha; desabilitado no somente leitura e quando só há notas e setas (dica "Notas e setas não entram numa marcação pai"). Textos em pt-BR e en-US.
- **Testes**: `tests/model/wrapItems.test.ts` (14 casos), action no store, componente.
- **Roteiro**: passo R12.11a no `docs/TESTING.md` (feito pelo agente sozinho; termina com `Ctrl+Z`, então os passos seguintes não mudam).

Sem schema, formato de proposta, especialização nem MCP novos.

## Como testar

O preview do branch é publicado sozinho ao abrir o PR (há um preview só: o do último PR atualizado).

1. Abra o preview no desktop, crie um projeto e um container.
2. Modo **Desenhar**: desenhe duas ou três marcações dentro do container. Modo **Navegar**: clique na primeira e **Shift+clique** nas outras.
3. Nos Detalhes, clique em **Envolver**: nasce uma marcação em volta delas (8 px de margem), selecionada sozinha; na Árvore, as marcações aparecem dentro dela.
4. `Ctrl+Z` uma vez: a nova some e as marcações voltam ao pai de antes.
5. Selecione marcações de dois containers diferentes e **Envolver**: a nova é do canvas e envolve os dois containers inteiros.
6. Selecione só uma nota e uma seta: **Envolver** desabilitado, com a dica.

## Decisões tomadas

As seis decisões estão no `PLAN.md` ("Etapa — Marcação pai"). As que não vinham do pedido:

- Margem de 8 px (`MIN_MARKING_SIZE`), limitada ao container e ao pai atual, para a nova nunca tirar o conjunto de dentro do pai que ele já tinha.
- Setas e notas (marcações flutuantes) são ignoradas, porque ficam fora do pertencimento.
- Com marcações de containers diferentes (ou containers na seleção), a nova é do canvas e cada marcação de container conta pelo **container inteiro**: só o container pode ser filho de uma marcação do canvas.
- Marcações não selecionadas que caem dentro do retângulo também viram filhas (é a geometria).
- O épico `epic/marcacao-pai` foi criado a partir da `main` para este PR.

body:
## Summary

Stacked layer on #2821 (`claude/2560-bag-scroll-arrows-select-swap`); it targets that branch and lands in `dev` with it. SELECT now picks up an item in the Items, Poké Balls and Key Items pockets, in Field and Battle, never on the close row, with a pocket-switch press winning over it and a refused press still consuming the frame (`item_menu.c` `Task_ItemContext`, `BagMenu_SwapItems`). While swapping, input order is SELECT, A, B, Up, Down; SELECT or A puts the item down (A also on the close row), B cancels, and Left, Right, L and R do nothing, so the engine only ever receives Up and Down. The move is upstream's insertion (`item.c` `MoveItemSlotInList`): `to == from` and `to == from + 1` change nothing, and the cursor row steps back whenever the destination is below the item, for put-down and cancel alike, with scroll kept. Because `BagMenu::refresh` cannot set positions and `open` re-centres every pocket, restoration reopens the engine menu from remembered per-pocket positions. The swap line is eight 16-pixel sprites from X 112 with the last pulled in to 216 at Y 9 + 16 × row, sprite 0 from sheet rows 0 to 15 and the rest from rows 16 to 31, hidden until the first non-SELECT swap frame (`menu_helpers.c`); the picked-up row shows a gray cursor only while in the window, the moving cursor is hidden, and the icon and "Move the {item} where?" prompt stay frozen on the item. The host's `&Bag` is never written: the screen keeps its own copy and returns `BagScreenTick::Reordered { bag }` with the pocket packed in list order, so `BagScreenTick` loses `Copy`. The arrow blit moved into a shared `sprite.rs` used by both layers. This layer carries no VERSION bump; #2821 holds the stack's single bump.

Left outside this layer: host persistence of the reordered bag (no caller opens the screen yet, #1765 and #1779), the horizontal pocket-switch arrows, the affine bag shake, and held-direction auto-repeat (#2749).

## Linked issue

- Issue: #2560 (the arrows and the SELECT swap; the pocket-switch animation and horizontal arrows continue in #2832, so this does not close the parent)
- Acceptance ID: C-5

## Test evidence

Twenty-five tests in `bag_menu/tests/swap.rs`: the four move directions, the close-row destination, both no-ops, the cancel cursor cases (12 stacks at 5/3 to 5/2, the 31-stack 2/5 pocket), sparse raw-slot mapping across two moves, pocket and mode gating, input precedence, swap-line positions and visibility timing, other pockets keeping their positions, and the host's bag staying unchanged; replacing the position reopen with the engine's current positions fails `a_swap_leaves_the_other_pockets_where_the_player_put_them`.

- `node ~/.claude/birch/gate-run.mjs <worktree> HEAD` — steps 1 through 18 exit=0
- `cargo test --workspace` — pokeemerald-rs lib `1211 passed; 0 failed; 95 ignored`; every other result line `0 failed`

body:
## Summary

The queued retreat-through-doors fix. C's `do_retreat` picks its escape among directions gated by `CAN_GO` (`src/act.offensive.c:1056-1076`), and **this codebase's `CAN_GO` skips closed doors entirely** (`src/utils.h:565-567`) — the loop never *attempts* a closed exit, so `do_simple_move`, which has no door check of its own (`src/act.movement.c:95-308`; `EX_CLOSED` belongs to `perform_move`, `:321`), can never slip a retreater through one. The port's gate checked only exit presence and destination, so whenever a draw landed on a closed exit Go fired the "gracefully attempts" act and moved the player **through the shut door**.

The gate now skips `ExitClosed` exits like C. `do_flee`'s port already had the clause (`pkg/game/flee.go`) — retreat was the last open door in this class.

## Testing

- **Unit proof / R5h:** `TestCmdRetreatNeverCrossesClosedDoors` fights in a room whose six exits are all closed doors — whichever direction the six draws pick, the command must end cornered with C's line and stay in the room. **Revert control:** without the clause the test fails with exactly the bug — "You make a hasty retreat." through the shut door.
- **Scenario `retreat-closed-door`:** a skilled mortal fights a zookeeper at 8040, whose west gate is closed, and retreats. Green with `--draw-parity` on seeds 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 with the fix; on the **reverted** build it diverges on seeds 2, 3, 5 and 8 (seed 1's draws happen never to land on the gate — which is why the unit test carries the R5h proof).
- Gates: build, vet, `go test -race ./...`, golangci-lint (0), gofumpt, deadcode, gosec — green.
- Targeted census `glm-retreat-doors` @ `81db01710`: `retreat-closed-door, flee-move-failure, flee-combat-forced, flee-audience-success, flee-death-exit, door-lock-pick-depth` — **6/6 CLEAN** (retained under `~/Archives/darkpawns/oracle-runs/2026-10-26/glm-retreat-doors/`).

## Class audit note (R5c)

`CAN_GO` consumers in C: `do_retreat` and `do_flee` (act.offensive.c:394, :1059 — both six-draw escape loops; flee's port already gated), mob wander (`mobact.c:124`; Go's `mobact.go` door draw uses `CAN_GO`-equivalent gating — covered by existing wander scenarios), the death-cry broadcast (`fight.c:522`, `spec_procs2.c:1543` — Go's `deathCry` walks exits and **also lacks the closed-door clause**), falling down (`comm.c:730`), and hunt pathing (`graph.c:245-250`). The death-cry adjacency gap is a separate finding: C muffles a death cry behind a closed door, Go's port broadcasts through it. Not folded into this PR — flagging for a follow-up (Decisions below).

## Decisions for Zach

1. The death-cry-through-closed-doors divergence (fight.c:522 vs Go's `deathCry`): fix as its own PR with a scenario, or ledger first? I did not touch it here — one class member per PR kept this reviewable.
2. `graph.c` hunt pathing's CAN_GO use — I have not yet diffed Go's hunt implementation for the clause; if you want, I'll audit it as part of the death-cry follow-up.

author: cmlarsen
body:
Closes #376 (v1). Restarts and self-corrections follow in a v1.1 PR.

## Summary

This adds an opt-in **drafting** report that finds what dictation and rapid drafting leave behind: placeholders and notes to self (TK, FIXME, `[name]`, `(check this)`), filled pauses (*um*, *uh*) and spoken commands that were transcribed instead of applied (*comma*, *new paragraph*, *open quote … close quote*). It is the one style report allowed to suggest edits. Those edits are mechanical only: deletion, whitespace, punctuation from a fixed table, line breaks, and a first-letter capital. They never generate prose. This exception is an owner decision, recorded in docs/STYLE-REPORTS.md and AGENTS.md.

- **Typed text (default):** every match is flag only. Accepting a suggestion can never change the author's text, and spoken commands aren't detected.
- **`dictated: true`:** the host knows the text came from speech-to-text. Only then:
  - filled pauses get deletion edits in three unambiguous patterns: spaces only, a sentence start found by the tokenizer, or after a discourse word ("Well, um, I");
  - spoken commands get punctuation edits.
- **Conservative by design.** Each case below is flagged with no edit:
  - typed punctuation right next to a command;
  - a dash, bracket or quote edge next to a pause;
  - list commas and introductory clauses;
  - names (*Um Kulthum*);
  - camel-case words;
  - a pause right after a closing quote or a mid-sentence ?/!;
  - *scratch/delete/strike/undo that*.
- **Paired marks are atomic.** A dictated quote, paren or bracket pair is one match carrying both edits, so a host that applies one match at a time can't leave a lone mark. An unpaired command is flag only.
- **Speech:** pauses inside quotes, unclosed quotes and em-dash dialogue are skipped unless `includeDialogue` is on. Inserted marks follow the document's own quote and apostrophe style.
- **Surfaces:**
  - Rust: `drafting::report`, `StyleDocument::drafting`, `drafting::apply`, and `with_*` option builders.
  - WASM: `document.drafting()`, with TypeScript types.
  - Swift: `drafting()`, with Codable records.
  - Python: `document.drafting()`.
- **Options:** `placeholders`, `dictated`, `spokenCommands` (follows `dictated`; `true` without it is `invalidOptions`), `filledPauses`, `er`, `includeDialogue`.
- **Data:** project-written lists in `style/data/drafting/` (commands, fillers, placeholders). No third-party data. The idea comes from [dictation-cleanup-rules](https://github.com/AbhishekBarali/dictation-cleanup-rules) (MIT); none of its code or data is used.

## Measurements

`python3 bench/style/drafting.py --gate`:

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Hand-written fixtures (Dragon-, Apple- and Whisper-style; edit, flag-only and control cases) | 636/636 exact |
| Ordinary-prose negatives (command words and pause words used as words: *Coma patients*, *the Oxford comma*, *delete that file*, *uh-huh*, *um.edu*) | 332/332 silent, with and without `dictated` |
| Edits returned in default mode, across all fixtures and negatives | 0 |
| `--precision` on `bench/public` plus the 13 public-domain books (871,778 words) | 0 matches, 0 edits, both modes |
| Fuzzing (`rvfuzz`, about 100k mixed inputs including U+2028, ZWJ emoji, combining marks, ß/İ/ǆ, CRLF) | 0 default-mode edits, 0 overlapping edits, 0 off-boundary spans |
| Report time on a 50,000-word paragraph dense with *um* | 0.017 s (was 6–8 s before the fix) |
| Report time on `moby150k` | 7 ms |

## Review

Built by Codex and Claude workers. Each step was reviewed with `/code-review`, followed by a final round of three parallel Codex reviews (dictated-mode edits, code quality and API, safety). Review findings drove two design changes, each an owner decision recorded in the doc:
- after four rounds kept finding ordinary prose being rewritten, spoken commands became opt-in;
- after a fifth, edits became dictated-only.

Every review input is now a permanent fixture or negative.

## Known limits (dictated mode)

Dictated mode misses some things on purpose. A missed flag or edit is acceptable; a damaged sentence is not.
- Mid-sentence *scratch that* is flag only. Its referent can't be recovered.
- A command next to a typed mark is flag only or skipped.
- *dot dot dot.* is flag only.
- A pause after a determiner and adjective (*a long uhhhh*) is never edited. Restart detection in v1.1 will handle *the red um the blue one*.

New dictated-mode edge cases should come in as bug reports with the input, and each one becomes a fixture.

## Gates

- `bench/tools/gates.sh`:
  - conformance 6085/6085
  - public recall 60/60
  - private recall 50/50, +0 −0
  - golden 12/12, chunker 6/6
  - style tier 1 runs in CI
- On the merge with `main` (which now includes #375):
  - `cargo test --workspace --exclude writemorebetter-python --all-features --release`: 1,090 passed, 0 failed
  - WASM node tests pass
  - `swift test`: 24/24, with a clean Generated diff
  - name spelling and drafting gates pass

author: harrycordewener
body:
Replaces #2347 with the same change on a linear branch, stacked on #2346 (image roles), which is stacked on #2345 (renderer over TCP).

## What changes

- `deploy/fly/edge.fly.toml`, `server.fly.toml`, `renderer.fly.toml`: one config per role. The launcher fills in the game's name (`{game}`) when it downloads them, so the private addresses (`<game>-server.internal:8080`, `<game>-renderer.internal:5100`, `nats://<game>.internal:4222`) are written into the files and survive a plain `fly deploy`.
- `launch.sh` / `launch.ps1`:
  - The default is now split. It creates `<game>`, `<game>-server` and `<game>-renderer` on a private network of their own (`fly apps create --network <game>`), with `sharpmush_edge` (1 GB) on the edge and `sharpmush_data` (10 GB) on the server. Public IPs go on the edge only.
  - A new game's edge is deployed first, with `--detach`. The server waits for the edge's NATS before it answers, and the edge's `/health` goes through to the server. The server and the renderer follow.
  - On later runs it deploys the server, then the renderer. The edge is left running unless `--update-edge` / `-UpdateEdge` is given, so a rerun drops nobody.
  - `--single` / `-Single` keeps the one-app layout. A game keeps the layout it was launched with, which the launcher reads from the files beside it: an existing `<game>.fly.toml` stays single. It refuses `--single` on a split game, and refuses when both layouts' files are there.
  - The game name must be `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`.
- `deploy/fly/README.md`: launch, updates and cost for both layouts.

author: jeongjaesoon
body:
## 무엇을

Linear 94S-832, 94S-833. 취소가 사람의 거절과 섞이지 않게 감사 기록에 사유를 남기고, 런타임이 답을 어떻게 받았는지(`AnswerResult`)를 receipt에 반영한다.

worker 안쪽은 이미 앞 PR에서 고쳐져 있었다. #808이 취소를 `run.answer({kind: "cancelled", reason})`로 내리게 했고, #849가 `answer()` 결과를 settlement에 반영했다(stale → cancelled, unknown → answered). 이 PR은 그 정보가 worker 밖으로 나가지 않던 부분을 고친다.

- **wire**: worker→gateway settlement에 선택 필드 `reason`과 `answer_result`를 더한다.
- **감사 기록**: `pending_requests`에 `settled_reason`·`settled_answer_result` 칸을 더한다(마이그레이션 0177. main의 0176은 #830이 차지했다). 사람의 거절은 `answered` + `answer.decision = deny`로 남고, 취소는 `cancelled` + 사유로 남는다.
- **receipt**: `unknown`이면 status를 `unknown`으로 둔다. 취소이거나 stale이면 `failed`(`REQUEST_STALE`)이고, 메시지가 이유를 말한다.
- **옛 서버 대비**: 옛 API는 새 필드가 실린 poll 전체를 400으로 거절한다. 이때 worker는 경고를 한 번 남기고 `outcome`만 다시 보낸다.
- **문서**: 배포 순서 표(`docs/operator/images-and-supply-chain.md`), 감사 칸 설명(`observability.md`), 답 API 설명(OpenAPI와 생성물).

## 최종 wire 표

| 필드 | 값 | 함께 오는 `outcome` | 옛 쪽과 섞였을 때 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settled[].reason` | `park` · `shutdown` · `interrupt` · `refused` | `cancelled`에만 | 새 API + 옛 worker: 필드가 없으면 예전과 같다. 새 worker + 옛 API: 400을 받고 `outcome`만 다시 보낸다 |
| `settled[].answer_result` | `applied` · `unknown` | `answered` | 위와 같다 |
| `settled[].answer_result` | `stale` | `cancelled` | 위와 같다 |

만료는 원래 `outcome: expired`라서 `reason`에 넣지 않는다. 엔진이 요청을 스스로 거둔 경우(withdraw), 콜백이 사라진 뒤에 답이 온 경우, `answer()`가 throw한 경우에는 이유를 알 수 없다. 이때는 필드 없이 `cancelled`만 보내서 예전 뜻("콜백이 먼저 사라졌다")을 유지한다.

**배포 순서: API 먼저.** 새 worker가 옛 API를 만나도 receipt 정산은 잃지 않는다. 다만 그 attempt의 감사 칸은 비게 된다.

receipt에 남는 모습:

| settlement | receipt status | error |
|---|---|---|
| `answered` (`applied`이거나 필드 없음) | `succeeded` | null |
| `answered` + `unknown` | `unknown` | `REQUEST_STALE`, "the engine did not know the request …, so it may or may not have acted on it" |
| `cancelled` + `stale` | `failed` | `REQUEST_STALE`, "the engine had already closed the request …" |
| `cancelled` + `reason` | `failed` | `REQUEST_STALE`, 사유별 메시지 |
| `cancelled` (필드 없음) | `failed` | `REQUEST_STALE`, 기존 메시지 |
| `expired` | `failed` | `REQUEST_EXPIRED`, 기존 메시지 |

## 정한 것

- 새 에러 코드는 만들지 않았다. `unknown` receipt는 기존 `lost` 경로(`abandonUndeliveredAnswers`)와 같은 모양이다. 공개 API의 enum은 바뀌지 않는다.
- 감사 칸은 사유와 결과 두 칸으로 나눴다. stale은 취소 사유가 아니고 답의 결과이기 때문이다.
- `cancelAll`이 받는 사유를 `CancelReason`에서 `expired`를 뺀 것으로 넓혔다.
- 94S-858(#850)이 먼저 land해서 main을 merge했다. park가 성립하지 않아 `unpark()`가 정산하는 요청은 `cancelled` + `reason: park`로 보낸다. 성립한 park는 예전처럼 row를 열어 둔다(정산 없음).
- Codex 리뷰 1차에서 P2가 하나 나왔다. `expired`에 `answer_result`를 같이 보내도 통과했다. 99c341b8에서 고쳤다(`stale`은 `cancelled`에만, `applied`·`unknown`은 `answered`에만 허용).
- 832 완료 조건 3("취소된 요청의 `approval.resolved`가 `outcome: cancelled`로 한 번")은 스파이크 계약을 기준으로 쓴 것이다. 지금 계약(design §3)에서 `ApprovalOutcome`은 `withdrawn`뿐이다. 리드 승인을 받아 계약은 넓히지 않았다. 대신 같은 의도를 테스트로 고정했다. 취소 답은 `ApprovalChannel`을 거쳐 정확히 한 번 settle된다. 엔진에는 사유 문구가 간다(park는 `interrupt: true`). `approval.resolved`는 나오지 않는다(`contract.test.ts`).

## 수용 기준 대응

- 832-1 취소 경로마다 `run.answer` 인자 확인: registry 테스트 "tells the run each way a request is cancelled …"가 만료, 사람 거절, hash 불일치, kind 불일치, interrupt를 다룬다. `cancelAll` 사유 넷도 따로 확인한다. worker-host 테스트 "cancels an approval … when it is interrupted"가 `run.answers`와 settlement를 단언한다.
- 832-2 사람이 거절한 경우만 `selected`/`reject_once`: 같은 테스트와 adapter 테스트 "passes a person's deny on as theirs"로 확인한다.
- 832-3: 위 '정한 것'의 마지막 항목대로 대체했다.
- 832-4 gateway에 보내는 settlement `outcome`은 그대로다: 기존 pending-requests와 interrupt 테스트에서 `outcome` 값이 바뀌지 않는다. 필드만 늘었다.
- 833-1 `stale`·`unknown`이면 receipt가 `answered`(succeeded)로 남지 않는다: worker-host 테스트 "reports what the run made of an answer …"와 db 통합 테스트 "an answer … settles its receipt and records why"로 확인한다.
- 833-2 `answer()` 결과 전에는 확정하지 않는다: 기존 "holds an answer's outcome until the run says …"(#849) 테스트가 그대로 통과한다.
- 833-3 Claude 승인 흐름 receipt는 그대로: `applied`/필드 없음은 `succeeded`다(통합 테스트). E2E 결과는 아래에 적는다.

## 검증

bun 1.3.14로 로컬에서 실행했고, pg 통합 테스트는 이 카드 전용 postgres:17-alpine에서 돌렸다.

- 루트 `bun run typecheck`: exit 0
- `bun test tests/architecture.test.ts`: 42 pass
- contracts 190 · runtime-core 125 · runtime-claude 323 · db 878 · platform 1110: 모두 0 fail
- worker: 539 pass / 5 fail, control-host: 1471 pass / 4 fail
  - readiness 2건은 이 PR이 원인이었다. migration head 기대값을 0176으로 고쳤고, 고친 뒤 8 pass다.
  - 나머지(worker `workspace-capture`·`checkpoint-restore`·`session-checkpoints`, control-host Slack outbox)는 5초 timeout이다. 다시 돌릴 때마다 실패하는 테스트가 바뀌었다(load average 42). main의 제품 코드로 돌린 scratch worktree에서는 113 pass였다. 이 PR이 건드리지 않은 코드라 CI 결과를 기준으로 본다.
- `biome check .`: error 0 (warning 15건은 main에도 있다)
- 생성 명령 `openapi:generate`·`api:generate`·`db:generate`를 다시 돌린 뒤 `git diff` 0
- **고친 코드를 끄면 실패하는지**: 제품 파일 4개(`pending-requests.ts`, `worker-host.ts`, `pending-control.ts`, `worker-protocol/index.ts`)만 origin/main으로 되돌리고 새 테스트를 돌렸다. contracts 1, registry 16, worker-host 4, interrupt 1, db 6건이 실패했다. adapter의 `contract.test.ts` 새 테스트는 #808·#849에서 이미 들어간 동작을 고정하는 것이라 되돌려도 통과한다.
- E2E: 아래 댓글에 붙인다.

author: chauvuusvn
body:
- Closes #11480

### Description

PR #11413 introduced the invariant to preserve model responses in history when crossing `UsageLimits`:
> *"Token and cost limits are only known once the response has been billed, so commit it to history first: a run a limit stops keeps it in its messages, and resuming from them doesn't request it again."*

While `_finish_handling()` was updated to append before checking usage limits, the two `except exceptions.ModelRetry as e:` handlers in `_agent_graph.py` (streaming at line 1830 and non-streaming at line 1974) still checked `_enforce_usage_limits()` *before* appending `_handler_response`.

This caused `UsageLimitExceeded` to bypass `_append_response()`, dropping the response from `message_history` / `capture_run_messages()` even though the request had already been recorded in `ctx.state.usage`, leading to data loss and double-billing if resumed.

This PR:
1. Aligns both `except exceptions.ModelRetry:` handlers with `_finish_handling()`: appends `_handler_response` first, and if `UsageLimitExceeded` is raised, marks `state='interrupted'`.
2. Adds a regression test `test_response_over_limit_with_model_retry_is_kept_in_captured_messages` in `tests/test_usage_limits.py`.

### Checklist

- [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md).
- [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration and release note, and an exact API-check waiver if the gate reports it.
- [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

body:
Operator selection previously lacked a tested pretrained multi-view path. This adds source-only box/mask selection, a pinned MVTracker adapter, metric RGB-D trajectories, explicit estimated/predicted/unavailable states, auditable JSON/CSV/NPZ exports, H.264 previews, and reproducible model/data acquisition. Sparse SIFT-LightGlue and person-only pose/OSNet paths integrate with the existing geometry pipeline.

This remains a partial offline prototype: one selected surface cohort is not full arbitrary-object MTMC. Independent object detection/search, long absence/handoff re-ID, complete MOT evaluation and live operation are not established. Destination depth support has false visibility confirmations; MVTracker's root license remains unresolved.

Measured on RTX 3090: 10 DexYCB sequences per main/clean checkpoint and 6 Panoptic/main sequences. DexYCB/main mean sequence RMSE 21.08 mm; Panoptic/main 105.85 mm. The actual browser-selected coffee run now has separate post-hoc source-visible fixed surface evaluation: 34/35 source matches within 10 mm, 7.96 mm RMSE over 706 post-query visible samples; this approximate mesh correspondence protocol is not the official benchmark or object IDF1. Destination projection RMSE 4.84–4.92 px and depth-support visibility precision 47.28–64.32%. PRID OSNet Rank-1/mAP 50.63/47.81%; WILDTRACK selected-person recall remains 33.33%.

Validation: 70 Windows unit/integration tests and Ruff pass; original GPU-host suite 64/64, real CUDA inference, CPU smoke, 1/2/4-view scaling, camera dropout and browser-picker checks. All 13 locally retained MP4s decode fully; 37 PNGs are readable. New confidence preview rerenders frozen predictions on CPU without restarting the GPU VM.

Reports, protocol-specific numerical evidence, limitations, reproduction commands, requirement audit and durable artifact index are in docs/pretrained_bakeoff/. Model binaries, third-party footage and full datasets remain outside Git. Original 314-file remote backup snapshot matches local SHA256/size; local additions are separately indexed.

Stacked on PR #18 / feat/recorded-multicamera-pipeline. No merge. Guest shutdown was accepted and a subsequent SSH probe was unavailable; provider power state and billing cessation are unverified, and the configured deletion timer was preserved.

author: nerdytoddgerdy
body:
Closes #187. It also fixes a bug I introduced in #189, described below.

## What's new
- **Unlocking:** one **land claim** for every 2 residents beyond the founding pair. A fourth resident earns the first, and the top bar shows "1 land claim". You chose this and the strip size.
- **Claiming:**
  - Build menu → **Claim land** outlines a strip along each edge, **8 cells deep**.
  - The one nearest the cursor is on offer, even with the cursor off the map, and the camera can look a few cells past the edge while you do it.
  - A click stakes it.
- **The stakes:** a small blueprint of 4 sticks, with a post at each corner of the strip. A builder plants them like any blueprint. One claim is in progress at a time, and the top bar says "Staking land" meanwhile.
- **New land isn't empty:** each strip gets trees, boulders, berry bushes and up to 3 sheep. They're generated from the game's seed and the claim's number alone, never the live random numbers, so a village always claims the same land. East and west strips keep a 3-wide lane clear to the signpost.
- **Limits:** 64 cells a side. A village that's full in one direction can still grow in the others. The hint explains why a claim is blocked: too few residents, one already staked, at the maximum size, or no open ground for the stakes.
- **Signposts** move out with their edges, since they're derived from the map's size. One that lands on a tree or boulder makes room for itself.

## Growing west or north
That moves the origin, so `SimMap.shift` moves **everything** by the strip's depth in one pass:
- trees, boulders, bushes and animals, including where they're heading;
- stacks, the stockpile and its reservations;
- farm plots, sites and their plots, pens (their built fences too) and gates;
- the residents.

Chest slots from #189 are keyed off the map, so they keep their keys and only their door cells move. Everyone's job ends and is claimed again on the next tick. A traveler still walking in is the exception: his walk is re-planned to the house where it now stands, because ending it would have left him with no home. The camera moves with the land through a new view event, `map_grew`, so the sim never touches the view.

## A bug in #189, fixed here
`_on_site_done` fell through to the house branch for any building without its own case. So **finishing a storehouse counted as a house**: it raised the house count, could make Ada its "owner", could finish the founding's "second house" goal early, and showed "Ada's house is finished". I found it while checking the boundary stakes, which did the same. Now only a house is a house, the storehouse says what to do next, and a test covers both. Villages that built a storehouse on `main` may have an inflated house count; it isn't repaired.

## Two small things I found along the way
- Hints now never run off the right edge of the screen. The claim hint at an edge did.
- The village bot's storehouse step ended with an Esc that opened the game menu. It's fixed.

## Saving (v29)
A save keeps its size, and its claims come from its residents, so an older village with enough residents has claims waiting. The upgrade only records `claims_made = 0`. New fixture `save_v29.save` is a village grown east by one claim. The v29 fixture was generated twice on this branch while it was unmerged.

## Tests
- New `test_land_claims`:
  - unlocking at the fourth resident and not the third;
  - claiming east grows the map and keeps every coordinate;
  - for **north, west and south**: every site, plot, stockpile cell, farm plot, pen and resident moves by exactly the offset, every old cell is as walkable as before, chest slots keep their keys, animals keep their destinations, and hauling still works afterwards;
  - the signposts move;
  - the same seed gives the same land, and another seed gives different land;
  - the size maximum holds;
  - a traveler mid-walk carries on to his house;
  - the stakes don't count as a house;
  - an older save keeps its size.
- `game_test.gd`: the claim chip, the Build entry, picking an edge with the cursor off the map, the click staking it, and the camera staying on the same ground after a west claim.
- `playtest_village.gd`: claim the north edge through the Build menu, watch a builder plant the stakes, then place a house on the new land and see its foundation go down. The issue said `playtest.gd`, but its opening has only 2 residents.

Results:
- Sim tests: 1926 checks, 0 failed.
- `game_test.gd`: passed.
- All five bots: passed, run one at a time.

Docs: `slice-2-spec.md` (the rules, stuck reasons, saving, tuning) and `docs/how-to-play.md`.

author: neuralempowerment
body:
Refs #2107. This is the second slice, after #2110 (newest-only capture delivery).

## Problem
`CaptureRecoveryWorker` re-claims every caught-up, unreleased spool every `retry_seconds` (10s). Each claim reopens the volume and re-sweeps the live native transcript, so every change archives a full new revision. Measured on the VPS: about 10.3 revisions per session, 53GB stored against 3.85GB newest-only. Every older revision is a strict prefix of the newest.

## Change
`PostgresCaptureSpools.claim` skips a spool that is caught up (no envelope or child watermark), unsettled and was claimed within `SYN_SESSION_INVENTORY_LIVE_RESWEEP_SECONDS` (default 900).

These are still claimed as soon as they are due, so terminal capture and crash recovery are unchanged:
- a settled spool, whether the session completed, the run became terminal, or the deadline passed;
- a first claim;
- an unfinished traversal.

For a live session, revisions drop from one per change every 10s to at most one per 15 min, plus the final sweep after settlement.

## Evidence
- New integration test covers the state space: envelope or child traversal in progress, settled, aged past the interval, recently swept live, and constructor validation.
- Three existing tests assumed immediate re-claim of a live caught-up spool, which is the behaviour being removed. They now assert the gate first, then settle or age the last claim.
- Local runs:
  - 17/17 integration across the spool, worker, drain, jobs and release suites;
  - 2711 unit tests in syn-adapters and syn-shared;
  - preflight green.
- `.mutations/`: 5 patches, all killed locally; mutation-evidence dispatch is next.

## Not in this PR (#2107 remainder)
- Supersede older local revisions.
- Compression at rest.
- `SessionArchiveSink.confirm()`, which waits on APSS #154.

author: bradhallett
body:
Incident hotfix for the post-merge sheets orphan failure (merged main @ 540d27b5, `sheets-actions.test.ts:1209`: orphan(actionId) then read('Sales!B2') = [[6]], not [[4]] — the dead activation landed).

## Root cause (lands on #111)
`worker.ts` `claimTestAction` marks the action claimed via a **second ActionJournal over the same DO storage** ("the live one never knew of the apply"), exactly the premise an activation that died mid-apply creates. #111's `#pendingCache` was an instance field cleared only by writes through that instance, so the live journal's cached UNDECIDED view survived the external claim and the next read projected the dead change. Pre-#111, `#scan` always re-walked storage. #113's orphan/adopt semantics are not implicated (verified by A at 5a010e83 pre-#115 as well: single same failure).

## Fix — coherence belongs to the storage namespace
- Every mutation flows through a **guarded kv facade** built in the constructor: `put`/`delete` bump a namespace-scoped `journalVersion:<recordPrefix>` key **first** (fail-closed: a write that throws still invalidates); the bump writes through raw storage so the guard cannot re-enter.
- No mutating path can bypass it: `#write` (allocate/stage/adopt/update/markClaimed/markFailed/markSubmitted), `remove`, `#reserve`, `reserveThrough`, `retire`'s applied-id put, `listRetained`'s stale deletes — all are facade writes.
- A **second journal instance** over the same storage bumps the same version key, so an outside mutation invalidates this journal's cache as surely as its own writes.
- `#scan` reads the version **before** the walk; an entry built under an older version is unreachable, never wrong. M2's amplification win is kept (repeat projections still walk once per view between mutations).

## Verification
- New kit pin: a second journal's `markClaimed` invalidates the live journal's cached `listUndecided` (asserts the re-walk via scan spy).
- google docs-worker: **322/322**, including the two orphan-premise tests `sheets-actions :1209` and `slides-actions :923` (122 in those two files).
- kit: **740 + 136** (both pools). github: **194**. gitlab: **156**. vp lint on touched files: 0 errors.
- Keyspace goldens updated with the new `journalVersion:` key (documented in the golden comments).

Review: @FixGatekeepersA per the incident rule.

body:
## Alcance implementado
Registro adulto/tutor, salas privadas, invitaciones, tablero del profesor, cuestionarios adaptados y ruta de aprendizaje nivel 0→1. Esta PR incorpora ahora una segunda capa de seguridad orientada a privacidad infantil y operación.

### Protección y minimización de datos
- Salas infantiles **DENY por defecto**, incluso con un checkbox de tutor. Una solicitud de verificación queda pendiente y jamás autoriza el ingreso.
- Consentimiento vinculado a UID adulto, sala, rango de edad y versión de política, comprobado por recibo JWS Ed25519 de un proveedor externo. El CLI operativo valida firma, vencimiento, propósito, contexto, evita replay y guarda digest, no documentos ni comprobante completo. **Aún no está contratado/integrado un proveedor real y no hay aprobación legal.**
- Revocación global inmediata y autorización individual caducable; lectura de Firestore revalida permiso.
- Los diagnósticos se califican en el backend; solo se conserva resultado 0–5, no respuestas individuales.
- Retirada atómica de sala elimina índice, membresía, diagnóstico, aprobación y solicitud; borrado de cuenta contempla solicitudes residuales.

### Controles operativos
- Callable Functions v2 con Firebase Auth, rol de coach confiable y App Check exigido en producción (desactivación solo en emulador).
- Cuotas transaccionales: 3 salas/día por profesor, 10 invitaciones/hora, 2 revisiones/día por cuenta, 15 ingresos/día por cuenta y máximo 50 admisiones por sala en su vigencia.
- Auditoría mínima con TTL, cleanup programado con dry-run, índices Firestore y purga recursiva de salas.
- Política de retención propuesta: invitaciones/revisiones 7 días, autorizaciones y membresías infantiles 30 días, adultos 90 días, salas 90 días + 30 días tras cierre; auditoría 90 días. Plazos pendientes de revisión jurídica.

### QA — Sandbox V3 (local/emuladores; no producción)
- 318 unitarios del frontend: PASS (15 suites).
- 14 unitarios de Functions, criptografía y aprobación de release: PASS.
- 12 escenarios adversariales Firestore de salas: PASS.
- 19 regresiones de reglas del sistema anterior de clases: PASS.
- 13 recorridos E2E Playwright con profesor, adulto y tutor, incluyendo firma sintética y revocación: PASS.
- 12 escenarios de cuotas, auditoría y retención con Functions/Auth/Firestore Emulator: PASS.
- 8 recorridos UI de salas y 48 regresiones UI generales: PASS.
- PWA offline, lint, TypeScript, build, accesibilidad automatizada: PASS.

### Refuerzo de gobernanza — commit d48c8ec
- La habilitación global de salas infantiles ya no admite referencias escritas manualmente como aprobación: requiere **dos firmas Ed25519 válidas y claves públicas distintas**, asociadas a un dictamen legal y uno de seguridad.
- El manifiesto firmado queda vinculado a **Firebase project ID, SHA de release, versión de política, jurisdicciones, ticket, URL/versión y SHA-256 del aviso de privacidad**. La activación consume un digest único para impedir reutilización del mismo manifiesto.
- El pipeline de GitHub Actions incorpora el job **rooms-safety**, que instala dependencias bloqueadas y ejecuta pruebas de reglas Firestore, Functions/Auth, cuotas/retención y Playwright con autorizaciones sintéticas. Se creó el job, pero **todavía falta verificar su ejecución en un runner independiente del SHA final**.
- Scripts de E2E operativo implementan **SAFETY_STOP** si no detectan emuladores Firebase locales con puertos esperados; no deben conectarse accidentalmente al proyecto real.
- El gate de release permanece **NO-GO**, incluso con referencias de aprobación ficticias sin el manifiesto firmado. La verificación de configuración no equivale a aceptación legal o despliegue validado.
- Pruebas locales más recientes: **318 frontend, 14 backend, 12 reglas de salas, 19 reglas previas, 13 E2E autenticados, 12 pruebas operativas, 8 UI, 48 regresiones y PWA offline: PASS**. Se observaron timeouts intermitentes de Playwright debido a saturación del workstation compartido; la ejecución completa más reciente pasó 13/13.
### Correcciones de CI y dependencias — commit bb1acea
- GitHub Actions (primera ejecución del SHA d48c8ec): el job general falló porque npm audit detectó 3 avisos (2 moderados, 1 alto) en Vite/Vitest; el job rooms-safety pasó Firestore, cuotas/retención y 13/13 E2E autenticados, pero falló en las pruebas UI estáticas porque faltaba compilar dist/.
- Se actualizaron las versiones fijas a **Vite 8.3.5** y **Vitest 5.0.5**, y el lockfile con npm ci; **npm audit --audit-level=low: 0 vulnerabilidades** tanto en frontend como Functions.
- El job rooms-safety ahora ejecuta **npm run build antes del navegador estático**, valida precondición dist/index.html y audita también el árbol de dependencias Functions sin suprimir errores.
- Verificación local tras upgrade: 318 unitarios, 14 de Functions, 13 E2E autenticados, 8 UI salas, 48 regresiones, PWA y build: PASS.
- **PENDIENTE:** conocer el resultado de GitHub Actions sobre el SHA bb1acea; CI verde no habilita menores reales. PR continúa Draft, sin merge ni despliegue.
### Evidencia y guías
- `progress/evidence/rooms/gates.json`
- `progress/evidence/rooms/safety-release-gate-adults.json` y `safety-release-gate-minors.json`
- `docs/CHILD_SAFETY_DATA_GOVERNANCE.md`
- `docs/ROOMS_PRIVACY_NOTICE_DRAFT_ES.md` (borrador, **NO publicar como definitivo**)
- `docs/ROOMS_SAFETY_RUNBOOK.md`
- `docs/ROOMS_ZERO_TO_ONE.md`

### Release gate — NO-GO
**Adultos:** pendiente de publicar aviso de privacidad aprobado y configurar realmente App Check/reCAPTCHA Enterprise, permisos, infraestructura y smoke test.

**Menores:** además, requieren evaluación legal por jurisdicción, responsable/contacto de privacidad, revisión de seguridad/impacto infantil, contrato e integración de un proveedor real de consentimiento parental verificable, versiones ES/EN/PT aprobadas, DPA, operaciones de retención/backup, IAM, presupuesto y alertas. Los recibos de prueba son sintéticos; no autorizan a menores reales.

El gate estricto `npm run verify:safety` devuelve NO-GO a propósito mientras falten estas condiciones. **Mantener esta PR como Draft; NO merge ni despliegue a producción.**

author: timborovkov
body:
## Agreed issue

Scope approved by the repository owner in this Codex task: reduce API usage across all native integrations, MCP health checks, and Slack/Telegram chat. No separate issue was opened. Builds on the merged Monday changes in #443.

## What changed

Idle integrations previously repeated recovery reads and discovery requests too frequently. Routine native recovery now runs daily with account staggering, saved pagination, completed-resource tracking, and shared quota enforcement across workers and web requests. Monday retains its existing 100-request daily cap and GitHub retains its reserve; other providers gain accounting without a new universal daily cap.

- Add request context, privacy-safe usage telemetry, atomic Redis reservations, shared remaining-capacity observations, and provider retry deadlines.
- Add signed, selected-channel Slack ingestion and migration readiness checks. Pause legacy polling until permissions and a signed delivery are verified. Bound Slack recovery to 48 hours with conservative history/replies pacing.
- Preserve Drive change-feed checkpoints and content progress, renew watches, checkpoint Linear collections, and stop Sentry release pagination at the saved boundary.
- Cache MCP discovery for 24 hours and apply progressive failure backoff without invalidating unrelated server discoveries.
- Defer quota-limited Slack/Telegram delivery durably, coalesce pending Telegram edits, preserve distinct final sends, and avoid automatic replay of ambiguous writes.
- Expose pending work/setup and budget pauses in integration health; document rollout and recovery limitations.

## Verification

Passed with Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 11.8.0:

- `pnpm validate`
- `pnpm run doctor` — score 100, no issues
- `pnpm test:dist-imports`
- `pnpm test:eval`
- `pnpm test:reconciliation-eval`
- `NODE_OPTIONS=--conditions=development TEST_REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379 pnpm --filter @timeline/shared exec vitest run src/integrations --project unit` — 257 tests passed
- Relevant Slack ingress/dispatcher, MCP health/cache, delivery, integration worker, webhook worker, and web integration tests passed. Real Redis tests verified concurrent reservations, pacing, quota observations, encrypted deferred delivery, and edit coalescing.

Documentation was audited manually; the repository's named release skills were unavailable in this environment.

## Privacy, security, and rollout

- Apply migration `0077_mcp_health_schedule.sql` for MCP scheduling state. Existing provider cursors remain readable.
- Deploy the full worker with the new `chat-delivery` consumer alongside the web changes.
- Existing native Slack connections remain paused until reconnect and signed-event verification. Reply recovery requires user `channels:history` and `groups:history` scopes in addition to the documented bot scopes. Chat remains independently available.
- Native rollout controls: `INTEGRATION_REQUEST_GOVERNOR_PROVIDERS` and `INTEGRATION_RECOVERY_PROVIDERS`. Disabling recovery preserves checkpoints and does not restore legacy Slack polling.
- Request telemetry excludes credentials and content. Deferred command payloads and credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM in Redis; completed jobs are removed immediately, failed jobs expire after 24 hours, and quota-delayed jobs remain pending until eligible.

author: hernanwilkinson
body:
## What

A set's `repr` names its type, as CPython's does, everywhere except on an exact set. test_pprint goes from 6 failures to 3, fixing `test_set_reprs`, `test_same_as_repr` and `test_width`. With #1816 as well, it goes to 1.

## Why

CPython's `set_repr` (`Objects/setobject.c:566`) writes the elements in braces and puts any type other than exact `set` around them:

| | Grail | CPython |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{7}` | `{7}` | `{7}` |
| `S({7})` for `class S(set)` | `{7}` | `S({7})` |
| `frozenset({7})` | `frozenset({7})` | `frozenset({7})` |
| `F({7})` for `class F(frozenset)` | `frozenset({7})` | `F({7})` |
| empty `S()` / `F()` | `set()` / `frozenset()` | `S()` / `F()` |

pprint falls back to `repr()` for a small set, so test_pprint read the subclass reprs differently.

## How

`set >> __repr__` and `frozenset >> __repr__` follow `set_repr`. Each takes the type name from `type(self).__name__`. The element loop the two methods repeated is now `Set >> ___elementsRepr___`. No env-1 method is removed (#1727).

## Tests

`tests/python/set_subclass_repr.py` has 5 checks measured against CPython 3.14, passing on both arms. They cover exact and subclass reprs, empty and non-empty sets, `pprint.pformat`, and `str`.

`SetTestCase >> testSetReprNamesAnyTypeButAnExactSet` asserts the fixture's summary.

## Measured

- test_pprint: FAIL, from 6 failures to 3. The three left are the two SimpleNamespace reprs (#1816) and `test_mapping_proxy`.
- test_set: OK, 630 tests, unchanged.
- Tier 1: confined to set and frozenset's `repr`.
- SUnit, full run: `main suite (sharded: 8 of x8): 8412 run, 8412 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors`, with all 8 shards reporting.
- The full CPython suite also ran with this change underneath other pending ones: `0 regression(s), 24 improvement(s)`.

author: p3n1cillin
body:
## Problem and change

PS4 build 56578 (01.33), A Guardian Rises, Fight Through the Wall. In run 2026-10-27-route6 the Guardian reached the mine-corridor junction and the client requested slice set 96. The activity host published region 96 with token 4, its own previous token plus one. The client was waiting for token 5: read natively, a retried transition advances the token without changing the target. So the transition never completed.

- `follow_slice_target` reads the client's token from udt 21 (+0x1F8) and publishes the (target, token) pair whenever it changes. Token 0 is reserved and ignored.
- udt 21 is a replicated delta. The listener keeps each connection's last image and decodes the next one seeded from it (`decode_seeded`), so a target and a token arriving in different deltas are both seen.
- Tests updated for the new rule, including a same-target retry.

## Validation

- d1-activity-host tests: 85 passed, 0 failed (lab tree, which has the eboot the tests need).
- Not yet re-tested natively: the transition into slice set 96. That's the next run.

author: carloshgalves
body:
## Escopo isolado: V7 — plano de Ryūen (800 milhões) e confronto do terraço

**Base:** `main`, após a integração da PR #40. Esta PR é **independente** e não modifica os packs de exames, instituições ou os demais capítulos.

### Fonte
PDF original privado, Seven Seas English, **207 páginas físicas**, SHA-256 `b41f00143f483fa7704bcc6c4bfda03323bd835c77ea1e95e53d27bd859e461b`. Apenas paráfrases e localizadores foram commitados. Ver `data/canon/consolidated/audits/y1-v07-ryuen-plan-rooftop-deepening.json`.

### Alterações
- Um **dossiê estruturado**: o raciocínio e as falhas do plano de Ryūen (pp. 120–150), reação de Kiyotaka, cronologia de confronto e posterior situação na escola (pp. 156–205).
- **18 casos individuais existentes** atualizados in-place com `episode_deepening`: 6 de Ryūen, 6 de Kiyotaka, 2 de Ibuki, 1 de Ishizaki, 1 de Albert, 1 de Manabu e 1 de Chabashira. IDs, arquivos anteriores e índices globais preservados; sem reclassificar habilidades como atributos fixos.
- Quatro confrontos **não simultâneos**: Ishizaki inicia; Albert intervém na mesma fase; Ibuki ataca depois; Ryūen enfrenta Kiyotaka por último. Conservar as diferenças de força/resistência, timing, seleção de golpes e **dor sentida pelo próprio Kiyotaka** (pp. 178–188).
- **Testemunhas contextuais** na fonte: `actor.manabu-horikita` (ex-presidente, posicionado na escadaria, pp. 164–165/191–193/195) e `actor.sae-chiyabashira` (professora conversa e observa contexto prévio/corredor, pp. 156–165/191). Ambos são citados nominalmente como **testemunhas**, mas **nenhum presencia diretamente os golpes**, conduz audiência ou aplica sanção.
- **Plano 800 milhões** (pp. 198–200): documento de três anos visto no celular por Ibuki; ela infere objetivo coletivo de levar a classe A, enquanto Ryūen nega a interpretação. **Não é saldo acumulado, transferência realizada nem confissão de intenção interna comprovada**.
- **Divergência numérica documentada:** a edição V7 registra Ibuki dizendo **2 milhões** para passagem de uma pessoa, enquanto a regra relatada no V2 é **20 milhões**. Mantida `OPEN_NO_SILENT_CORRECTION`; nenhuma fórmula de transferência em massa criada.
- Teste `tools/test_canon_y1_v07_ryuen_rooftop_deepening.py` + workflow: **13 casos**, incluindo **12 mutações adversariais**, para evitar falsa testemunha ocular, confusão sobre Manabu, luta simultânea, negação da dor, falso aceite externo, roteiros determinísticos e reconciliação arbitrária dos pontos.

### Gates
- `verified:false` e `independent_second_reviewer:NOT_PERFORMED`; testes estruturais/semânticos deste mesmo assistente **não equivalem** a revisor independente com o PDF original.
- Sem admissão automática em memória/engine ou ratings universais. **Permanecer Draft até revisão e liberação humana**.

author: cano721
body:
## 배경
v0.43.0 뒤 LLM 단계가 돌기 시작해 자동 sync가 실행됐지만 jobda·jobda-agent·jobda-cms 3건 모두 `left_for_user`로 끝났다. 로그: 작업 worktree의 `.ai-harness/`·`.claude/`·`.agents/` 쓰기가 "denied by your permission settings".

## 원인
- `make_work_tree`가 worktree를 `$HM_DATA_DIR/harvest-auto/worktrees/`에 만든다.
- v0.35.1 보안 강화로 무인 claude는 `--disallowedTools "Edit(/$HM_DATA_DIR/**)" "Write(/$HM_DATA_DIR/**)"`를 받는다(데이터 디렉터리의 config·shim을 transcript 속 지시로 고치지 못하게).
- 그래서 worktree 전체가 쓰기 금지 범위에 들어가 sync·프로젝트 harvest 모두 파일을 고칠 수 없었다(프로젝트 harvest는 지금까지 전부 no-change라 드러나지 않았다).
- 실측: 같은 권한 인자로 `claude -p`를 돌리면 `~/.ai-harness/harvest-auto/worktrees/…`에서는 `DENIED`, `~/.cache/ai-harness/worktrees/…`에서는 `OK`.
