author: pimlock
body:
## Summary

When a retained sandbox's main process exits, the supervisor stays connected so you can still get into the sandbox. SSH, file transfer and port forwarding already worked in that state. Exec and exposed services did not, so `openshell sandbox exec -- cat result.txt` failed on a sandbox you could `download` the same file from. On a gateway with several replicas, the post-exit check also only looked at the replica that received the request, so access worked or failed depending on the load balancer.

This PR applies one rule to every way into a sandbox. A `Ready` sandbox is reachable. A `Completed` or `Error` sandbox is reachable while its supervisor is connected to any replica. Every other phase is refused. The gateway makes the call, and the CLI no longer rejects `Completed` or `Error` on its own. #4949 has the full set of rules and a lifecycle diagram. New ways into a sandbox should use the same check.

## Related Issue

Closes #4949

## Changes

- Exec, SSH sessions, port forwarding and exposed services share one replica-aware reachability check in the gateway.
- The CLI sends exec and service forwards for `Completed` and `Error` sandboxes to the gateway.
- The docs and CLI skill now say what you can still do after a retained sandbox's main process exits, and that `--no-keep` sandboxes are deleted.
- A new `sandbox-retention` conformance scenario checks both cases, for exit codes 0 and 3. A `--no-keep` sandbox is deleted. A retained sandbox records the exit code and still accepts exec.

## Testing

- [x] `mise run pre-commit` passes
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] E2E tests added/updated (if applicable)

The conformance scenarios ran against a local Docker gateway built from this branch. I didn't test Kubernetes, Podman or a real multi-replica gateway live.

Still broken and tracked in #4949: after a Docker gateway restart, `Completed` and `Error` sandboxes lose their supervisor and can't be reached.

## Checklist

- [x] Follows Conventional Commits
- [x] Commits are signed off (DCO)

author: nathsou
body:
Fixes for issues found playing Animal Crossing: New Horizons (each verified in scripted runs; Dread re-checked on save checkpoints: unchanged, 120 fps).

- **Animations too fast**: ACNH runs at 30 fps (present interval 2) and steps per frame; nothing waited the interval out, so it ran at the display's rate (4x too fast at 120 Hz). Presents now wait for their 60 Hz vsync slot, as on the Switch; time-stepped games opt out (`GAME_UNCAPPED_FPS`, Dread). Measured: steady 30 fps.
- **Black rectangular areas** (blurred distance, right and bottom of the screen; blocky shadows on the airport wall): the depth-of-field pass drew into a scaled colour target and an unflagged R8 texture left unscaled; Metal draws a pass only over its smallest attachment. Such textures are now scaled too.
- **Scrambled island flag / custom designs**: `LINEAR_RENDER_TARGET` textures were de-tiled as block-linear; they're packed rows.
- **Dark, near-black sea**: the sky panorama the water reflects samples a cube array (`agl::env::CubeMap`) as a cube; that view was missing, so it got a black dummy.
- **Compute shaders with shared memory** (`LDS`/`STS`) failed to translate; a lighting kernel never ran.
- Draws into targets not drawn the frame before (one-shot renders) wait for their shaders instead of being skipped while they compile.
- Test aids: `LARECOMP_LIVE=<dir>` steers a running game from a command file; debug-frame logs of attachment sizes, rscale, sampler LODs.

- **Audio effects**: I3DL2 reverb (rooms, ACNH and Dread), delay, biquad filter and Aux ported from Ryujinx; the first three were passed through dry, and Aux (ACNH taps its final mix through it) left its output unwritten.

### Testing further into the game: saves made elsewhere
- **Saves from another Switch now load.** A resident belongs to the account that made it: `LARECOMP_USER_ID` sets the account the game sees, and `tools/acnh_save.py <save dir>` decrypts a save (NHSE's scheme) and prints its residents' account IDs. Without it the game moves a new resident in.
- **Upgrading an older save** crashed: the game commits every save mount together through fsp-srv `OpenMultiCommitManager` (1200), now implemented (IPC requests also carry their objects now).
- **A loaded resident aborted the SDK** asking for the controller's colours: `nn::hid::GetNpadControllerColor` is now answered.
- **Camera photos** were garbage: the camera renders into a linear render target and hands that memory to the album; linear targets are now copied back to guest memory, and `caps:su` writes photos as PNGs to `save/<game>/album/`.
- `tools/acnh_saves.sh <dir>`: boots each save folder as its resident's account, day and night, walks, opens the phone and pockets, captures frames. `LARECOMP_LIVE` holds now run one after another (`+NAME n` for simultaneous).
- Checked on a public April 2020 save (github.com/ericlewis/acnh-save-backups) on 2.0.7: the save upgrade, island, house interior, Nook's Cranny, Resident Services and the Nook Stop terminal, the airport and a Nook Miles Ticket flight to a mystery island, night lighting, NookPhone apps (map, camera, custom designs editor), chat and naming keyboards, Save and end, reloading the saved game. No save files are committed.

### Frame generation and 4K
- **`frame_generation = 60 | 120`** (nx.ini): ACNH keeps its real 30 updates a second (so its speed stays right) and the window shows images generated between its frames from GPU optical flow. Capped at the display's refresh rate; off for games that already run faster (Dread). About one display frame of latency; fast limbs can ghost a little.
- **4K internal resolution** (`resolution = 2x`) now really renders ACNH at 3840x2160: its window textures weren't scaled, so the 4K scene was composited into 1080p images.
- **MetalFX frame interpolation** (`frame_generation_method = metalfx`, the default at 60): ACNH draws no motion vectors, so nx draws them - each shader program gets a variant that runs its vertex shader with this frame's and the previous frame's data for the same draw (matched across frames by mesh, shaders and uniform contents) and writes the difference. MetalFX gets them with the game's depth and the HUD as a separate layer, so the HUD stays still. Cleaner than the optical flow on moving limbs and lighter on the GPU; 120 stays on the optical flow (MetalFX makes one image per frame).

### Performance
- **Uniform snapshots shared between draws**: every draw copied its bound uniform buffers (ACNH: the same 40 KB one to each draw, 55 MB a frame). ACNH uncapped: 77 -> 115 fps at 1440p, 98 fps at 4K.

author: sukalov
body:
visitors in russia cannot reach cloudflare, so `ru.mktour.org` is a dns-only record pointing at a proxy in moscow, which forwards to the server past cloudflare. this pr makes one image serve every hostname of its environment, so the mirror needs no build of its own.

## changes

- **websocket**: `getSocketUrl()` connects to `wss://<page host>/ws`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL`, now optional, still replaces it; vercel needs that, since it cannot proxy websockets
- **lichess login**: the client is built per request, and the callback returns to the host login started on if that is the base url's or listed in `MIRROR_HOSTS` (runtime, comma separated). any other host gets `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, as before
- **posthog**: the client sends to `/ingest` unless `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_API_HOST` is set, and nginx proxies `/ingest`. next rewrites would need `skipTrailingSlashRedirect`, which turns off trailing slash redirects for every page. the server's posthog host now uses `||`, so an empty build arg falls back too
- the club link of the team link error (`form.tsx`) is relative
- ci requires only `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, and the pr smoke build no longer sets a socket url
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` stays built in, so canonical urls, open graph and the sitemap keep naming the main domain

also on this branch: `ref: better shape of clubManagers` (12d3ea6e).

## rollout

nothing changes on merge: the `beta` github environment still sets both overrides, and `MIRROR_HOSTS` is unset. to switch beta over:

1. nginx on the server: `location /ws/` and `location /ingest/` in the beta site, the mirror hostname in its `server_name`, the moscow proxy trusted for the visitor address, and `X-Forwarded-Host` set by nginx
2. delete `NEXT_PUBLIC_SOCKET_URL` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_API_HOST` from the `beta` environment
3. set `MIRROR_HOSTS` in `~deploy/mktour-app/beta.env` and redeploy

prod on vercel keeps both variables until it moves to the server.

## testing

- `tsc`, lint and the full suite pass (242 pass, 3 skip). `src/tests/request-origin.test.ts` covers mirror, base, unlisted and missing hosts
- a production build without env files falls back to `wss://${window.location.host}/ws` and `/ingest` in the client bundle, and names neither `ws-beta.mktour.org` nor `data.mktour.org`
- the moscow proxy already serves beta at `ru.mktour.org`: pages, api, static caching and websockets work, including a socket held idle for an hour. login through it needs this pr and the rollout above

The test workflow installs the latest CLI on Linux, Windows and macOS and a pinned version on Linux, and runs weekly. It can only pass once `install.ahwoo.com` serves the install scripts and a CLI release where `ahwoo push --ci` needs only the client ID and secret. After merging, tag `v1.0.0` and `v1`.

author: blackvectra
body:
## Summary

`Invoke-TPAssessment.ps1` and the batch runner take `-ControlId` and `-ExcludeControlId` (wildcard patterns) and assess only the matching controls. Only the collectors those controls need are run, and services no selected control needs are not signed in to. For example, `-ControlId AAD-1.2` never connects to Exchange, Purview or Teams.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking; default runs are unchanged)

## How the selection is worked out

`Lib/Resolve-TPControlSelection.ps1` is a pure, tested helper.

- **Patterns** are matched against `controls.json` with `-like` and validated by `\A[A-Za-z0-9.*?-]{1,40}\z`. The entry point and the batch runner carry copies of the rule, and a test pins them equal. A malformed pattern, a pattern that matches nothing, or an empty result is fatal (exit 4) before any sign-in.
- **Raw-data keys** come from four sources:
  - each selected control's `CollectorDependency`;
  - every `Get-TPRawData -Key` read in its evaluator and in the helper functions it calls, found by parsing the code;
  - the control's baseline evidence keys;
  - `AAD-Inventory`, which license gating always needs.

  Each needed collector's own prerequisites are then added until nothing new turns up. A read that cannot be determined falls back to running every collector, so nothing is under-collected; no shipped evaluator triggers that fallback.
- **Collectors and services:** `Get-TPCollectorCatalog` maps each collector to its keys and service, and a test pins it to every `Set-TPRawData` call. `Connect-TPServices` gains `-SkipExchange`. Selection-driven skips are not recorded as operator skips.
- **Refused combinations:** `-Quick`, `-FromResults`, `-Web`, `-RegisterApp`, `-DistributionListsOnly`, `-DeviceResults`, `-SSPQuestionnaire` and `-MonthlyReport`.

## Unselected controls on every output

| Output | How unselected controls appear |
|---|---|
| Results JSON | `Metadata.ControlSelection` records the selection. Findings an evaluator emits for unselected controls are dropped and listed, never scored. |
| Scope section | New `NotSelected` bucket: "Not assessed: not selected for this run". It is checked before other signals, and the buckets still sum to the unscored count. |
| Baseline view and plan | New reason code `NotSelected`, right after `SkippedByOperator` (Scope Both), counted as evidence not obtained. |
| Maturity | "<tier> (provisional: partial run, N of 243 controls)". |
| Console, HTML report, Markdown summary, report site | "Partial run: N of 243 controls selected (...)" at the top. |
| Baseline regressions, delta report | Controls either run did not select are "not compared (not selected)", never regressions or resolutions. |
| `-FromResults` | Republishing a partial results file keeps it partial. |

## Fixes a partial run exposed

- `Publish-TPRemediationScript` threw under StrictMode on a run with no Gap.
- The delta report's drift check treated a collector missing from the current run as everything removed, which flagged every prior CA policy. It now compares a section only when both runs collected it.

## Test plan

- [x] `./tools/Invoke-TPTestGate.ps1`: 3,937 passed, 0 failed, 134 skipped
- [x] `./tools/Invoke-TPSecurityAnalysis.ps1`: passed, no baseline entries added
- [x] New `TP.ControlSelection.Tests.ps1` (50 tests). It covers:
  - the pattern rule, matching and refusals;
  - key and collector derivation, including TMS-5.6 reading Defender data beyond its declared dependency, and the fallback;
  - the catalog matching the collectors both ways;
  - the scope bucket and its invariant, the reason code, coverage, the plan, maturity, regressions, the delta report and the SSP;
  - the real entry point against stub modules: refusals; `EXO-1.6` signing in to Exchange; `AAD-1.2 -AllFiles` never signing in to Exchange, Purview or Teams, scoring only AAD-1.2, saying it is partial everywhere, and staying partial when republished.

## Security checklist

- [x] Read-only invariant intact
- [x] Input validation: `[ValidatePattern]` on both new parameters, pinned equal to the helper's rule

author: magicdrive
body:
## Problem
On a local macOS machine, a full `go test ./...` under load made plugin tests time out at the 10s plugin timeout: `TestPluginRetryPolicy` / `TestPluginV1` ("the plugin did not finish within its timeout of 10s"), `TestExternalFeatherSend`, `TestCritical_PluginPATHHijack` (commandline), `TestBinarySIGINTCancelsPluginGroup` (e2e, "the plugin never started its child"). Reproduction on main@575d7ca: 16 busy loops + `go test -count=1 ./...`, **4/4 runs failed** (a plugin test in each); with CPU load on `./internal/feather/external` alone, 1/1. CI never showed it.

## Root Cause
Classification: **Test Bug** (the wait is the machine's; the tests put it inside the timeout under test).

Measured with a temporary trace (not committed) of `external.run` (time of `cmd.Start`, of `cmd.Wait`) and of the test plugin (a timestamp on reaching `main`, after reading stdin, at its end), under load, 2 full-suite runs, 101 runs that reached main:

| | n | exec → main median | p90 | max | killed before main |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| first run of a newly written copy | 47 (+8) | 2.956s | 5.565s | 9.895s | **8** |
| later runs of the same copy | 54 | 0.012s | 1.015s | 5.548s | 0 |

- `cmd.Start` returned in ~6ms every time; once in `main`, the plugin answered within ~2ms. No time in pipe I/O, `Wait`, or the process group handling: **all of it is between exec and the plugin's `main`**, and only for a new copy.
- The first exec of an executable just written waits for the system's scan of it (XProtect; on this machine also an Endpoint Security agent, Bitdefender's `com.bitdefender.agentui.sp`), one at a time machine-wide and slowed by load (the suite writes many new binaries at once: test binaries, kjak, plugin copies).
- A copy killed by a short timeout while it is being scanned was followed by a stall of the next new copy: `TestPluginTimeoutAndCancellation` (300ms / 200ms) killed both its copies before main, and the next test's first copy (`TestPluginRetryPolicy`) then waited 9.99s. A standalone probe (no kjak) showed the same: fresh copies 0.33s exec→main idle; after killing a fresh copy at 50ms, 1.0–2.7s; later up to 6.5s.
- kjak counts the plugin's start inside its timeout by design (a wall-clock budget; the outcome "may have delivered" is correct: kjak cannot know). The tests installed a fresh copy per test and ran it straight under a timeout, so the OS scan landed inside the timeout under test.

## Solution
Every new copy of the test plugin is run once to its end, with no deadline, before any test runs it under a timeout (`settle` / `settlePlugin`: an empty request, the plugin exits 8): `internal/feather/external` (`install`, the shared copy), `internal/commandline` (`installPlugin`), `internal/e2e` (`installPlugin`, and `kjak version` once in `TestMain` for the kjak binary). A first run over 1s is logged with its duration. No timeout was changed.

## Security Impact
None: tests only. The settle run gives the plugin no request, no secret, no setting.

## Compatibility
No product change.

## Tests
Same machine, same load (16 busy loops, `go test -count=1 ./...`), with the temporary trace:

- before: 4/4 runs had a plugin timeout; first-run exec→main median 2.956s, 8 killed before main.
- after: **0/4** plugin timeouts; the first kjak run of a copy exec→main median **0.012s**, max **0.024s** (n=116), 0 killed before main. The settle runs themselves took up to 11.6s (logged), i.e. the scan now happens outside every timeout.
- `-race` under the same load, 2 runs: 0 plugin failures, no data race.
- The remaining local failures are unrelated and handled elsewhere: `TestProxyEnvironment` (needs a non-loopback route: separate PR), and the Darwin ACL tests when GNU `chmod` (coreutils) is first on PATH.

## CI
See the checks of this PR.

## Migration
None.

## Risks
One extra exec per installed copy (milliseconds on Linux/Windows). If the plugin did not exit 8 on an empty request, the helper fails loudly rather than hiding it.

author: haseebkhalid1507
body:
Closes #159

review: shady 8/10 APPROVE (https://github.com/HaseebKhalid1507/Axon/pull/161#issuecomment-6434811467)

## What changed
`src/kvsave.rs`: `KvIo for CudaQwen2::kv_ident` now returns `None` for an MLA (deepseek2) net, as `KvIo for Qwen2` (the CPU) already did. A refused identity makes `chat --session` prefill the saved tokens again instead of loading rows. New test: `moe::ds2_tests::ds2_cuda_session_image_refused`.

## 1. Design notes
- **The gap (#159):** the CPU impl refuses deepseek2, whose K-only MLA cache has no image format. The CUDA impl only refused split models (`self.first > 0`). Its save would write no rows under a header that claims a valid image, and a restore would decode from a cache it never wrote.
- **Product reach (CODE):** `chat` saves through `Backend`, and deepseek2 on CUDA is `Inner::Moe`, whose `kv_ident` falls to `_ => None`. So `chat --session` on a CUDA deepseek2 model already re-prefilled and was **not exposed**. The gap is the GPU net's own `KvIo`, reachable by anything driving `CudaQwen2` directly (tests, a future backend arm). The test checks both levels.
- **The `Backend` impl** (~462; Cpu / Cuda arms, `_ => None` for Hybrid / Pipeline / Moe) needs no change.
- **Fix:** `if self.first > 0 || self.mla.is_some() { return None; }`, with the CPU impl's comment.
- **Bits:** no kernel, cache or gen path touched; `kv_ident` is only read by the session code.

## 2. Hardware / environment
| | |
|---|---|
| CPU, RAM | bella: Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX, 32 GB · avante: Intel Core i5-13420H, 15 GB |
| GPU, VRAM | bella: RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (sm_120), 12 GB · avante: RTX 4050 Laptop (sm_89), 6 GB |
| driver, CUDA / NVRTC | bella 615.78.08, NVRTC 13.4.92 · avante 610.43.02, NVRTC 13.3 |
| OS, kernel | CachyOS, Linux 7.2.11 |
| threads / pinning | test defaults, `--test-threads 1`; builds `nice -n 19 taskset -c 22,23` |
| power / thermal | n/a (no timing) |
| base commit | `main` @ d8a296c |
| candidate commit | c19ba6c (code); b01ca2b = + log entry. Test-only commit 050287f = the test on main's code |

## 3. Models
| file | quant | source | sha256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| deepseek2 fixture (in-tree, `ds2_fixture`) | Q8_0 | synthetic | n/a |
| the chat session tests' models (Qwen2.5 0.5B Q4_K_M and the like) | Q4_K_M | CONTRIBUTING | `models/*.sha256` |

## 4. Methodology
```bash
# the bug reproduced: the test on main's code (050287f) must fail with the refusal message
expectfail.sh axon-test-kvmla-050287f moe::ds2_tests::ds2_cuda_session_image_refused 'must refuse a session image'
# the fix, release and debug: kvsave, the chat session tests, the deepseek2 fixture tests (moe:: and model::)
axon-test-b01ca2b     kvsave:: chat::tests::session moe::ds2_tests:: model::deepseek2_tests:: --test-threads 1
axon-test-dbg-b01ca2b kvsave:: chat::tests::session moe::ds2_tests:: model::deepseek2_tests:: --test-threads 1
```
`expectfail.sh` (6 lines) runs the test binary with `--exact` and passes only if it fails with the given message. It is in the raw logs.

## 5. Benchmarks
n/a: a session-identity refusal, no speed claim.

## 6. Correctness
- [x] `rustfmt --check` clean
- [x] clippy `-D warnings` clean, lib and `--test`

| check | where | job | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| the new test on main's code (050287f): must FAIL | bella | 1027-014232-e935 (resubmit of d2f5, which never ran) | PASS: `EXPECTED-FAIL OK (rc 101)`, panicked at ds2_tests.rs:751 (GPU-net assert) |
| kvsave + chat session + deepseek2 fixture tests, release | avante | 1027-003725-9405 | PASS 36/0 |
| same, debug assertions | avante | 1027-003728-e82b | PASS 36/0 |
| `AXON_SIMD=scalar` | — | — | n/a: no CPU kernel touched |
| md5 | — | — | n/a: no gen path touched (`kv_ident` is read only by the session code) |

## 7. Raw logs
Gate logs are posted as a PR comment (9405, e82b, e935). `expectfail.sh`:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
out=$("$1" "$2" --exact --nocapture --test-threads 1 2>&1); rc=$?
echo "$out" | grep -E "panicked|test result|$3" | head -8
if [ $rc != 0 ] && echo "$out" | grep -q "$3"; then echo "EXPECTED-FAIL OK (rc $rc)"; exit 0; fi
echo "EXPECTED-FAIL MISSING (rc $rc)"; exit 1
```

## 8. Risks and what wasn't tested
- No end-to-end `chat --session` run on a real CUDA deepseek2 model (Moonlight). The refusal is checked at the identity level, which decides between load and re-prefill (`Chat::load_session`).
- A future MLA session image format would drop this refusal and need its own restore == recompute test.

## 9. AI disclosure
Spike (Claude), moeres builder under foreman axon. Not human-reviewed.

author: drewstone
body:
On GTM production (2026-10-27) two addressed agents ran in parallel but the viewer saw them one after another: the composite stream read out speaker 1 completely before speaker 2 (its header appeared at 66 s, Research Lead's at 10 s). Both agents also answered every role ("I'll play both roles myself"): nothing told a responder which name it answers as.

- `composeAgentProducers` announces every responder up front (`speaker` events in mention order), then forwards each event as it arrives with `speaker` set to its agent id. A viewer keeps one live block per responder and draws them answering at once. Stored rows keep speaker order.
- A responder's failure (`error` / `session.run.failed`, or a thrown produce) becomes a `notice` under its own name, live and in the stored row; the turn fails only when every responder failed.
- `addressedTurnText`: each responder's `prompt` and `body.content` lose the addressed `@handles` and gain one line naming who it answers as and who else answers separately.
- `chat-stream`: `onSpeakerEvent` hands raw-callback consumers the speaker of every event; the guide documents the live contract.

Proof: `tests/chat-routes/agent-fanout.test.ts` (5 tests: ordering, addressing, one-fails/all-fail, parallel timing). Red/green on beelink1 follows in a comment. GTM adopts the live grouping in tangle-network/gtm-agent (feat/speaker-live).

author: duo-ee
body:
## The gap

`assess_site` answers "is this method defensible here?" from catalogue metadata: span, resolution, variable. That says a record exists, not that it is worth fitting a distribution to. The reconnaissance step (#375) could not tell a complete 60-year series from one with a 14-year hole in the middle.

## What this does

`SiteContext` gains four fields, filled by a new `explore.record_quality_half`:

- `completeness_by_variable`: share of the daily calendar between the first and last observation that carries a value.
- `longest_gap_days`: the longest gap `assess_quality` reports between consecutive observations.
- `flagged_fraction`: share of observations flagged provisional or suspect.
- `change_points`: year of a significant Pettitt shift in the annual means, per variable.

The first three reuse `aquascope.analysis.quality.assess_quality`; the fourth reuses `aquascope.analysis.changepoint.pettitt_test`. Both already exist, so this is one more caller, not another test.

`change_points` moves from one list for the site to a dict by variable, because a shift in discharge is not a reason to mark the precipitation record non-stationary. `assess_method` now demotes only the stationarity methods that read the variable the shift belongs to, plus the site-wide years a caller passes in. A plain list is still accepted and read as those site-wide years, so existing calls keep their meaning.

## Where the record comes from

A local copy of the Archive dataset, pointed at by `AQUASCOPE_ARCHIVE_DIR` (`<dir>/obs/<variable>/<source>/<station_id>.csv.gz`, the dataset's own layout, so an extracted Zenodo snapshot works too). No mirror, no file, or an unreadable file leaves the four fields empty, adds a note that the judgement is metadata-only, and reads nothing from an agency or from Hugging Face. The default path is therefore exactly as fast as before and still makes no network call.

## Tests

- the quality half sees a 14-year hole as completeness < 0.8 and a gap over 14 years;
- a step change in 1991 is reported as `change_points == [1991]`, and only the flood-frequency row is demoted (not the precipitation one);
- without a mirror the four fields are empty and `fetch_archived_series` is never called;
- a mirror that holds no file for the station is a note, not an error.

`pytest tests/test_explore_assess.py tests/test_methods.py -q` -> 25 passed; `ruff check` on the four changed files passes. The wider set (`test_explorer`, `test_playbooks`, `test_advanced_playbooks`, `test_mcp_server`) runs 215 passed, 1 skipped.

## Not in this PR

The CLI/MCP faces do not show the quality half yet (step 4 of the issue); the fields are in the `assess_site` JSON under `context`, so a face can read them without a new call. `change_points` changing type is called out in the CHANGELOG entry.

Part of #375.

author: jelly-raytian
body:
In America/Toronto, a date-only posting value such as 2026-05-25 is parsed at UTC midnight and falls on May 24 locally. This adds a day to posting age and shifts the tooltip and posting-date sort value. Separately, dividing local-midnight elapsed milliseconds by 24 hours undercounts calendar days across the spring DST change. For example, a posting from the preceding calendar day can display today rather than yesterday.

Parse YYYY-MM-DD values at local midnight, format the tooltip from that parsed date, and compare UTC day numbers built from local calendar components. Timestamp parsing and source-relative labels retain their behavior. Includes documentation of the date and freshness rules. This is independent of #787.

Validation (Node 22.22.2):
- Six added regression cases cover local date/tooltip and aging boundaries, sorting, and calendar-day counts around US/European clock changes. Before the fix, the Toronto run has five failures (three added cases and two existing cases); after the fix all 14 tests pass.
- The same 14 tests pass with TZ=UTC, TZ=Europe/London, and TZ=Australia/Sydney.

- All required CI-parity checks pass: Biome CI, shared/orchestrator/Gradcracker/UKVisaJobs typechecks, and client build. git diff --check passes. The build reports its existing large-chunk warning.

author: ravsinghchandan
body:
`determine_feed()` selects feed links with `//link[@rel="alternate"]`, an exact string match. In HTML, `rel` is a case-insensitive list of space-separated keywords, so feeds declared as `<link rel="Alternate" ...>`, `rel="ALTERNATE"`, `rel="alternate feed"` or with surrounding spaces were not found at all, and the `<a href>` backup does not look at `<link>` elements. The `type` attribute is already normalized for case and `; charset=` suffixes; `rel` was not.

Links are now kept when `alternate` is one of their `rel` keywords, compared case-insensitively. Other links, such as stylesheets or `rel="alternative"`, are still ignored. Added a test next to `test_determine_feed_type_normalization`.

author: vietbui1999ru
body:
## Problem
`pueue kill` sends SIGKILL to the whole task, which can't be caught, so `pi-view` never reports its own end. herdr kept showing the viewer pane as `working` forever. This applies to plain and `--live` dispatches alike.

## Fix
- `pi-view` passes its own pid and the pane id to `pi-tail` (`--watch-pid`, `--pane`). `pi-tail` runs in the herdr pane, outside pueue's process group.
- When that pid is gone and herdr still shows the pane `working`, `pi-tail` reports it `blocked` (message `killed`, seq 3).
- A run that ended normally has already reported `idle` or `blocked` at seq 2, so it is left alone.

## Tests
- `node --test scripts/pi-tail.test.mjs scripts/pi-live.test.mjs`: 15 pass, 0 fail, including two new `watchRunner` cases (dies while working → reported; already reported idle/blocked → left alone).
- `zsh -n scripts/pi-view`: clean.
- **Live, against herdr:** a killed run (task #179) went `working` → `blocked`, and pueue showed `Done Killed`. A run that finished on its own (#178) stayed `done`.

author: vij658
body:
Era 8 of the book, stacked on #9 (Era 7).

**What is in it**
- `book/era-08-the-web-the-genome-and-the-ledger/`: plan, reference catalog (57 links, each opened before it was listed, with certainty labels and gaps), the era front page with its time line and map, and 13 topic pages in two editions (GitHub Markdown with SVG figures, and interactive HTML with widgets).
- `code/era-08-the-web-the-genome-and-the-ledger/`: 13 single-file Java programs with expected outputs; 488,910 checks in all. Every number on the pages is parsed from these outputs.
- `code/tools/book/`: `era08.py` and 13 topic modules (`topics/e8_*.py`); READMEs updated.

**Topics**: support vector machines, Goemans and Williamson's MAX CUT, streaming sketches, consistent hashing, MinHash and locality-sensitive hashing, LSTM, PageRank, Paxos, genome assembly with de Bruijn graphs, PRIMES is in P, MapReduce, compressed sensing, Bitcoin's proof-of-work ledger.

**Findings worth a look**
- Nakamoto's Section 11 tables reproduce to 7 decimals, but the race simulated block by block (1,000,000 times per z) lies above his Poisson formula from z = 2 on: at z = 5, 0.00180 against 0.00091. The genesis block's 80-byte header hashes to its published hash, with 43 leading zero bits.
- AKS agrees with a sieve on every n up to 3,000 and rejects the Carmichael numbers, but for the prime 100,003 it needs 266,381,759 coefficient multiplications against 92 for Miller–Rabin.
- Paxos was model-checked exhaustively for 2 proposers and 3 acceptors (192,441 reachable states) with no two different values chosen; breaking one rule breaks it.
- Goemans–Williamson on a 400-node graph: a dual certificate proves the best cut found is at least 94.3% of the best possible.
- MapReduce's widget runs the program's own scheduler and reproduces all four of its schedules entry by entry; without backup tasks a slow machine made the job 133% longer (the paper measured 44% for its sort).
- Compressed sensing: ℓ1 minimization recovered sparse signals exactly where the smallest-squares solution never did (0 of 560).
- Disputed points are marked: Paxos's first submission (1989 or 1990), the soft-margin paper's text (1.5%) against its own table, PageRank iteration counts in secondary sources (52 against 50 to 100).

**Checks run**: `env -u JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS bash code/run-all.sh era-08` (13 passed); `check.py` on the index and all 13 pages (0 problems, desktop light/dark and phone); every widget exercised in headless Chromium. The SVM, Goemans–Williamson, Count-Min, consistent-hashing, MinHash, LSTM, PageRank, Paxos, assembly, AKS, MapReduce, compressed-sensing and Bitcoin widgets reproduce the programs' own numbers.

**Gaps**: video sites could not be opened, so no videos are listed in the catalog; a separate video list is being built on the `video-list` branch. Several papers are described through records and secondary sources, and each topic's gaps line says which.

author: eternaldark949
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"eternaldark949"} -->
_Requested by **ETERNAL** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_012neUuoXczqQejW7TjHGmQ6?thread=cmsg_012neUuoXczqQejW7TjHGmQ6Dq4nVgg2J3QxYQnGH9iY6q)_

## 1. Blade hitboxes and quick hits
- **Hitbox:** the hitbox is now the blade as drawn, from fist to edge tip, the same geometry as the trail. `updateMeleeSwing` sweeps it through the cut each tick, so a body is cut when the blade passes through it, once per swing, and never through walls.
  - Before, Blood Pact's cone reached about 25 px past its drawn tip and missed the sides of its visible sweep.
  - Both blades also used to land at the press, before the blade moved.
- **Quick hits:** cuts (`opts.cut`) and bleed ticks now ignore and don't start i-frames. Gangers' 20-tick i-frames had been eating every other 16-tick Kukri cut.

## 2. New schematics
| Schematic | Cost | Kind | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mirror Blade | 200 | attachment | A blade's cut turns enemy shots back at the shooter |
| Bloodthirsty Muzzle | 275 | attachment | Bullets deal 1.75× |
| Crimson Edge | 300 | attachment | Blade cuts deal 1.5×; bleed stacks to 5 instead of 3 |
| Mirrored Glass | 650 | accessory, needs the Crystal Glass | All damage 1.35×. Turns 90 damage of shots back, then refills over 3 s. Silvered rim, never sold. |
| Clothing Dyer | 1,000 | for the apartment | Recolors outfits (section 7) |

- Any number of attachments can be crafted and kept, and up to two can be worn at once (`equippedAttachments`).
  - Attachments don't count toward the 10-item carry capacity.
  - Older saves load their one attachment into the new list.
- `craftSchematic(id)`: a full bag no longer eats the scrap.

## 3. Crafting window
- The workbench still opens the `#craft-shop` pop-up, now restyled to match Skills and Contacts (`renderCraftingScreen`).
  - The scrap sits in a gold version of the Skills dial.
  - Schematics are calling cards grouped under Attachments, Weapons, Accessories and For the Apartment, each with cost, a scrap bar when short, and Craft.

## 4. Balance pass
**Golden Child**
- Orbs stack: burn ticks (`{type:'burn'}`) skip and don't start i-frames.
- Burn is 8 per tick, down from 10.
- Each orb snapshots its shot's boosts (Hollow Points, Flit-Strike, Quick-Draw, Muzzle, Glass). A crit orb burns ×2.
- At most 4 orbs per target; a 5th replaces the oldest (`stickOrb`).

**Melee**
- Quick Hands and Reflex Sync shorten blade cooldowns the same way they shorten a gun's.
- Each cut heals 4% of its damage.
- While a swing is active, she takes 25% less damage (`swingGuard`).
- A swing inside the Flit-Strike window always crits.
- Bleed dps scales with `playerDamageMult`.

## 5. Frozen shoved NPCs
- `syncHumanoidGait` kept `driven` on forever after any `gaitCommand`.
- After an NPC walked back to its post, a later shove therefore read as speed 0, and the NPC slid without moving its legs.
- `driven` now covers only the ticks whose commands it averages.

## 6. Drink spills and the bar cart (`engine/spills.js`)
- The held glass keeps a level, `cosmetics.drinkLevel`, which is saved. Older saves load with a full glass.
- **What spills:**

  | Cause | Amount |
  |---|---|
  | Hard turn or reversal (step change ≥ 8.5 px/tick; plain stops and right-angle turns don't count) | about 2.5–5% |
  | Flit, on take-off | 3.5% |
  | Hit | 2–7%, scaling with damage |

  At most one spill every 0.35 s.
- **Puddles:** each spill leaves a puddle in the drink's color, with drops thrown the way it flew.
  - Puddles merge when one lands in another, splash underfoot (`materialAt` → water), dry after 75 s and clear on a map change. The cap is 36.
- The held glass draws its level, and an empty glass shows no liquid.
- A brass bar cart beside the kitchen island (`apt_bar_cart`, Pour) refills the glass.
- **Skills:** these fold into existing nodes, so players who already have them need no respec.
  - Arms' **Steady** also cuts spills by 15% per rank.
  - Frame's **Grounded** makes a ganger who steps in a spill slip for 0.4 s + 0.2 s per rank: no step, no shot, a short skid. Each ganger can slip again after 3 s.
  - **POISE** kill bonus: a kill with the glass at least 75% full earns ×1.25 Resonance.

## 7. Clothing Dyer (`engine/dyer.js`)
- Crafted for 1,000 scrap, the most expensive schematic. Once made, it sets `questState.hasClothingDyer` and its station (`apt_dyer`, Dye) stands on the bedroom wall.
- **Furniture layout fix:** `questState.aptLayout` keys moved furniture by prop index.
  - The dyer station and the bar cart are now appended after every existing piece, so a saved layout still fits.
  - The bar cart had been inserted mid-list in section 6, which would have shifted those indices.
- **Window** (`#dye-shop`, styled like the crafting window):
  - Pick any owned outfit, then a piece. `dyeSlots` lists every top, bottom and shoes color, plus trim, lining, accent and stripe where the outfit has one.
  - Choose from 24 palette swatches or a custom color.
  - A top-down preview shows her as she'd look, and nothing changes until you apply.
- **Cost:** 20 scrap per changed piece. Dyeing a piece back to its own color clears that dye. Original colors is free and asks for a confirm tap.
- **Storage:** dyes are saved per outfit in `cosmetics.dyes` and laid over the outfit by `dyedOutfit`, both in the world and on the Neu.Me swatches. The registry data is never modified.

## Testing
- `node tools/build.mjs --check`
- These all pass:
  - `tools/test-clothing-dyer.cjs` (3)
  - `test-drink-spills` (7)
  - `test-npc-gait`
  - `test-crafted-gear` (12)
  - `test-crits-blood-pact`
  - `test-kukri-animation`
  - `test-game-regressions` (0 failed)
  - `test-player-fire`
  - `test-quick-draw`
  - `test-gauntlet-saves`
  - `test-neural-systems`
  - `test-flit-feedback`
  - `test-character-rendering`
- Checked headless Chromium screenshots of the crafting and dyer windows at desktop and phone size, plus renders of the bar cart, the dyer station, the puddles and the glass levels.
- Not playtested on a device.

author: moetemp
body:
## What changed?

This PR refuses a resource that reaches a type parameter through a proto-backed record, as nexgen refuses one that reaches it through a plain record.

- Before planning, a proto-backed record is named by its proto type. `type_parameters` stops there, so the resource checks in `selected_validation.rs` missed such a parameter.
- The new `type_parameters_through_protos` also walks the record behind a proto type. Only the two resource checks use it, so planning and the generated code don't change.

## Why?

nexgen generated generic models for a resource class that isn't generic, so the code didn't compile. In Python, for example, the resource methods took `AppendRecord[EventT]` with no `EventT` in scope. It came up when trying a `Stream[T]` resource in the `stream-service` sample. Generic resources need a design pass first.

## How did you test it?

The new rejection fixture `advanced/samples/invalid/type-parameters/generic-proto-resource/` fails without the fix. Python and TypeScript generate code, and Go fails with another error. The sample output doesn't change.
`cargo validate` passes.

author: csdev19
body:
## Summary

Two owner reports about the camera bubble:

- **A. The bubble could no longer be moved.** Pressing anywhere on the bubble and dragging moves it again, before and during a take, without breaking resize-by-grip.
- **B. No quick way to turn the camera off once it is showing.** A **Turn camera off** button now sits in the bubble's hover chrome (outside a take) and in the control bar (during a take, while the camera is on).

Two commits, one per issue.

## A. Why dragging stopped working

It was not an accident in the grip-drag or sizing fixes (`62ef1329`, `862c8cae`). It was removed on purpose in `96447be3` ("size the camera bubble from its fixed corner", PR #380): the bubble window became `movable: false`, and `099fa524` deleted its `-webkit-app-region: drag` region. That followed the spec's reading of decision 6 ("fixed at the bottom-left corner, not draggable"), which also changed full-screen recordings, where the bubble had been draggable anywhere.

### The fix

- The drag is driven by **pointer events in the renderer**, not by an OS drag region. On pointer down on the bubble, the renderer calls `beginCameraBubbleMove()`. On every move it sends the pointer's offset since the press with `moveCameraBubble(dx, dy)`. `CameraBubbleWindow.moveBy` moves the window and clamps it inside the recorded area, or inside the work area of the display it is dragged onto, so dragging to a second monitor works.
- **Why not `-webkit-app-region: drag`:** a drag region swallows the pointer events the grip and the new close button need, and the OS would let the bubble leave a recorded area. Outside the area it would silently disappear from the video (ADR 0030). The window stays `movable: false` for the OS.
- **Resize still works:** the grip is a sibling of the bubble, not a child, so a grip drag never starts a move. The window's bottom-left corner is the anchor, so a resize (from the grip or from settings) grows the bubble up and to the right from wherever it was dropped, pushed back inside the container if needed.
- **Position is kept in memory, not persisted.** On the display it lasts for the app session, across camera toggles. Inside an area it lasts for the take: each area recording starts at the area's bottom-left corner, where the overlay's placeholder shows it. When the take ends, the bubble goes back to where it was dropped on the display.
- **The overlay placeholder** (frame-box / record-chrome) stays fixed. The real bubble window is hidden while the overlay is up, and making the placeholder draggable would need a remembered offset per area. You drag the real bubble once the take starts. Push back if you want the placeholder to be draggable too.
- No activation-policy change (ADR 0029): same `panel` + `skipTransformProcessType` window.

## B. Where "turn camera off" lives, and why

Both controls write the same global `isCameraEnabled` toggle that the Record page, the tray, the overlay widget and the `toggleCamera` shortcut already use. Whichever one is used, main destroys the bubble window and releases the device, and the camera light turns off.

**Chosen:**

1. **On the bubble, in its hover chrome (outside a take).** A 22 px dark dot with a white ×, opposite the resize grip: at 45° on the top-left of the rim for the circle, and inside the top-left corner for the rounded square, clear of the size label. The bubble is the thing the user wants gone, and the hover chrome already holds its other direct controls (outline, size label, grip). A hover × is also what Loom-style camera bubbles do, and someone who never hovers sees nothing new.
2. **In the control bar (during a take).** The bubble's chrome never renders while recording because it would end up in the video, so the bubble alone would leave no quick way off mid-take. The bar is already the mid-take control surface and is content-protected. The camera-off button appears between the mode chip and Pause only while the camera is on. The bar window grew from 480 to 528 DIP to hold it.

**Considered and rejected:**

- **The overlay's Camera toggle** (Mic · System audio · Camera). It already exists, but it is only on screen while you choose an area, not while the bubble floats over other apps.
- **A right-click menu on the bubble** (already "deferred" in the backlog doc). Not discoverable as the only way off. It can still come later.
- **A permanent indicator or toggle drawn on the bubble.** Anything always drawn on the bubble ends up in every recording.
- **Record page tiles.** These already toggle the camera, but they are in the main window, which is usually hidden while you record.

All new strings go through i18n (`cameraSettings.turnCameraOff`, in English and Spanish).

## Docs

- `backlog/camera-bubble-shape-and-size.md`: new "Moving the bubble" and "Turning the camera off: placement" sections, the control bar bullet, and new validation steps.
- `specs/2026-10-26-record-capture-modes-design.md`: decision 6's implementation note now has an amendment explaining that dragging is back.

## Verification

- `bun run check-types` (node + web): pass.
- `bun run lint`: 0 errors. The 17 warnings are pre-existing and none are in the touched files.
- `oxfmt --check`: clean for the touched files. `CHANGELOG.md` was already flagged on `main`.
- `vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 280 files, 2564 tests pass. `packages/i18n` tests pass.
- New tests:
  - `camera-bubble-anchor.test.ts`: `moveBy` offsets from the press, ignores a move without a press, clamps to the area, grows from the dropped corner, resets per area take, and returns to the dropped spot after the take.
  - `camera-bubble.test.tsx`: dragging sends offsets, also during a recording; a right-click and the grip do not move the bubble; the hover × turns the camera off; the × never appears during a recording; pressing the × does not start a move.
  - `control-bar.test.tsx`: the camera-off button shows only when `onCameraOff` is given, and calls it.

## Needs manual QA (not run in a real app)

- macOS and Windows: press on the bubble and drag. Check that it is smooth enough, since every step is an IPC call plus `setBounds`. Check that it stops at the edges of a recorded area, that it moves across displays outside a take, and that the grip still resizes from the dropped spot.
- First-click behaviour on the inactive always-on-top window: on Windows, does the first press start a drag?
- The hover × outside a take turns the camera off (bubble gone, camera light off). The control bar button does the same mid-take and is not visible in the recorded file.
- The control bar at 528 DIP: nothing is clipped with the Windows `Ctrl+Alt+S` shortcut label and the "WINDOW" chip. The transparent area beside the bar is slightly wider.

author: jacklionheart
body:
The scheduled `release-run` had failed every day while releases were cut by hand. The cron host still ran it as a launchd agent from an older lf, and that agent kept retrying a stale v0.14.13 selection. Rerunning `scripts/bootstrap-cron-host.sh` now removes those launchd agents before it writes the crontab, so one scheduler runs each job and the daily release either publishes or reports no changes.

<!-- loopflow:task-pr-context:start -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Task:** [Fix the scheduled release-run cron that failed its last run · LOO-629](https://linear.app/loopflow/issue/LOO-629/fix-the-scheduled-release-run-cron-that-failed-its-last-run)
> **PR lifecycle:** Merge delivers the code. Record independent later work as Tasks and comments; complete the delivered outcome.
<!-- loopflow:task-pr-context:end -->

## What changes

- In the "install release schedules" step, `scripts/bootstrap-cron-host.sh` now finds every `~/Library/LaunchAgents/loopflow.cron.<wave>.*.plist`. For each one, it runs `launchctl bootout`, deletes the plist and prints `removed launchd job <label>`. This happens after the preflight checks, so a failed check still changes nothing. When no plists exist, as on Linux or a fresh host, the step does nothing.
- `release/CRON_HOST.md` explains the earlier launchd agents and shows how to confirm which scheduler is live.
- `python/tests/test_release_automation.py` checks that the bootstrap runs this cleanup after the publisher preflight and before `crontab -`.

This delivers the host cutover that main's #1708 needed. #1708 replaced `lf wave cron` and its saved-selection accounting with crontab lines, but it never removed the launchd agents. Once an lf containing #1708 is installed, those agents call a command that no longer exists and fail every day, with nothing left to show them. This PR replaces #1711, which patched the saved-selection code that #1708 has since deleted.

## Risks and post-merge checks

The live cron host is still unchanged. As of 2026-10-27 it has both `loopflow.cron.infrastructure.{release-run,telemetry-daily}` launchd agents (last exit 1) and no `loopflow:` crontab lines. After merge:

1. From `~/src/loopflow` on main, run `scripts/bootstrap-cron-host.sh infrastructure`. As its configured-path check it runs `telemetry-daily`, not `release-run`, so it cuts no release.
2. Expected: it prints both removed labels, `launchctl list | grep loopflow.cron` prints nothing, and `crontab -l | grep loopflow:infrastructure` shows both jobs.
3. The next 10:00 `release-run` should exit 0. Its log, `.lf/logs/release-run.log`, should show either a published patch or that nothing changed since the latest tag. The Task completes on that log, not on merge.

The installed lf 0.14.17 can already run the new crontab line, because `lf release run` resolves without a saved selection. The cutover does not need to wait for the next release.

## Checks

- `bash -n scripts/bootstrap-cron-host.sh` passed.
- `uv run pytest python/tests/test_release_automation.py -q`: 10 passed.
- The plist cleanup loop ran successfully against a fake `HOME`.

## Try it

Suggested, not yet performed: on the cron host, run `scripts/bootstrap-cron-host.sh infrastructure`. Under `== install release schedules ==` you should see `removed launchd job loopflow.cron.infrastructure.release-run` and the matching telemetry line, followed by the new crontab entries. Run the bootstrap again and the step prints no removals.

## Current state

- `open_at_rest` returns a value with no `ENC:`, `ENZ:` or `ENB:` marker as is. This is the plaintext dual-read for rows that were written before their store was sealed (disk format v1).
- The status labels `codec_policy.writer_policy` and `at_rest_compression.enabled` read `LASTDB_AT_REST_RAW` and `LASTDB_AT_REST_COMPRESS`. No writer reads these two switches.
- The docs say that the KV seam wraps `atoms`, `tips`, `indexes` and the other collections. `EncryptingNamespacedStore` wraps only `cas_blobs`.

## Change

- `open_at_rest` returns `InvalidFormat` for a value with no marker. Both callers (the old `ENC:` catalog decode and the local CAS blob open) check `is_sealed_at_rest` first, so they see no change. `open_at_rest_bounded` already requires a sealed value. No other repo mirror calls `open_at_rest`.
- The two labels now read the KV seam switches that select the written form: `LASTDB_KV_AT_REST_RAW` and `LASTDB_KV_AT_REST_COMPRESS`. A new function, `kv_at_rest_raw_enabled`, is the one reader of the raw flag. The seam and the label both use it.
- `at_rest_compression_enabled` and `at_rest_raw_enabled` are removed.
- The docs now say that the KV seam wraps only `cas_blobs`.
- `scripts/disk_v2/node_proof.py` no longer sets `LASTDB_AT_REST_RAW`, because the node does not read it.

## Result

- The label strings and the field names do not change. No repo mirror outside lastdb reads `writer_policy`, `codec_policy` or `at_rest_compression`.
- With the primary job settings (both KV switches on), the labels stay `ENB:deflate` and `enabled=true`.
- With no settings, the labels change from `ENC:deflate` and `true` to `ENC` and `false`. That is what the seam writes.
- The primary job still sets `LASTDB_AT_REST_RAW=1`. After this change, the node does not read it.

Part of the disk format v1 removal (wave 3). Tests stay retired; CI builds and checks the change.

author: parazeeknova
body:
The production migration container exited 2 because `prisma db migrate` does not support `--no-advance-ref`. That option belongs to `db sign`; `db migrate` already leaves local refs alone unless `--advance-ref` is requested. Remove the unsupported option so the migration app can apply its committed graph and verify the database before dependent apps roll out.

Add regression tests that read the actual entrypoint commands and run them against the pinned Prisma CLI in offline preview mode. Include the container ID, exit code and OOM status in deployment failures without exposing runtime configuration.

Validation: `bun run check`; 62 script tests, including both real-CLI entrypoint tests. Image build and production migration/rollout will be verified through the main publish workflow.

Production verification: main publish run https://github.com/parazeeknova/brb/actions/runs/40450894589 passed all three image builds and deployment. The migration container exited 0, applied the corpus baseline and verified the schema. author: aarnott
body: Adds an opt-in timing summary for wallet sync so a later concurrency pass has a baseline. Sync behavior, the public uniffi API, and the database schema are unchanged. Timing is off unless `NERDBANK_ZCASH_SYNC_TIMING` is set to `1`, `true`, `on`, or `yes`. When it is off, the new helpers do not read the clock. When it is on, sync records busy time for: - `block_download` — lightwalletd compact-block streaming (`GetBlockRange`), excluding tree-state fetches and channel backpressure - `tree_state` — `GetTreeState` and `GetSubtreeRoots`, including decoding - `scan` — `scan_cached_blocks`, excluding commitment-tree persistence - `db_write` — `put_blocks` (note commitment trees) and subtree-root writes - `transparent_txids` — transparent address txid fetches and local apply - `tx_enhance` — full transaction fetch and decrypt-and-store - `db_open` — wallet database open/load `scan_cached_blocks` both scans and then persists trees through `WalletWrite::put_blocks`. That method is already a `tracing` span named `put_blocks`. A timed scan installs a thread-local subscriber around that call, records only that span, and restores the callsite cache afterward. Per-block scan spans stay disabled. If the span is not observed, the summary says so and scan time includes the write. The summary is printed to stderr and emitted as a `tracing` info event when `sync` returns. In continual mode it is also printed at the end of each pass, before the mempool wait. Wall time used for blocks/sec omits that wait. Download and scanning overlap, so `wall%` can sum past 100. `busy%` is each phase's share of measured busy time. Scan-range lines are a breakdown of the totals, not extra time. ## How to collect numbers From `src/nerdbank-zcash-rust`, the existing `test_sync` syncs a fresh wallet against testnet lightwalletd (`https://testnet.zec.rocks/`). The account birthday is 100 blocks before the tip: ```bash NERDBANK_ZCASH_SYNC_TIMING=1 cargo test -r --lib sync::tests::test_sync -- --nocapture ``` The same variable works for any process that calls the uniffi `sync` entry point, including the C# light wallet, with no API change. A wallet whose birthday is far below the tip spends much more time in block download and scanning than the short run below. ## Sample output This is a real run of that test in this environment (testnet tip around height 4,546,313, two fresh accounts, 101 blocks). Transparent gap-limit fetches dominate because each address is its own lightwalletd round trip. The shielded scan of those 101 blocks is the `ChainTip` range, about 1,100 blocks/sec, with `put_blocks` separated from scan: ``` zcash sync timing (sync finished): wall 2.431s, blocks 101, 41.55 blocks/sec phase busy wall% busy% calls block_download 0.021s 0.9% 0.9% 1 tree_state 0.035s 1.4% 1.5% 3 scan 0.021s 0.8% 0.9% 1 db_write 0.036s 1.5% 1.6% 3 transparent_txids 2.196s 90.4% 95.1% 90 tx_enhance 0.001s 0.0% 0.0% 1 db_open 0.000s 0.0% 0.0% 2 scan ranges (included in the totals above): [4546213,4546314) ChainTip blocks=101 wall=0.088s 1142.48 blocks/sec block_download=0.021s tree_state=0.012s scan=0.021s db_write=0.033s transparent_txids=0.000s tx_enhance=0.001s db_open=0.000s ``` `db_write` on that range is the `put_blocks` span. The other two `db_write` calls are the sapling and orchard subtree-root writes before scanning. `db_open` ran twice and rounded to `0.000s` on this tiny database.

author: cliffhall
body:
Closes #5197

## Description

`check_may_autonomously_fetch_url` refused on a 401 or 403 robots.txt response and allowed on any other 4xx, but a 5xx fell through and the server's error page was parsed as robots.txt rules. An error page holds no rules, so the parser allowed everything and the autonomous fetch went ahead while the site's robots.txt could not be read.

RFC 9309 section 2.3.1.4 treats a robots.txt that is unreachable because of a server error as complete disallow. A 5xx (any status >= 500, after redirects are followed) now refuses with the same message and guidance as 401 and 403, and the response body is never read. Nothing else in the robots.txt check changes: 401/403 still refuse, other 4xx still mean "no rules", a connection failure still refuses, and the private-address guard on the robots.txt request from #5239 is untouched.

## Server Details

- Server: fetch
- Changed: the robots.txt status handling of the `fetch` tool (`server.py`, one condition), its tests, and the robots.txt section of `src/fetch/README.md`.

## Motivation and Context

See #5197. Prior prototypes, closed in the backlog triage: #4482 by `isheng-eqi` and #3547 by `ElliotJLT`; thank you to both. The timeout half of #4482 is out of scope here.

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Unit / protocol tests.** New `src/fetch/tests/test_robots_status.py` drives the real server through an MCP `ClientSession` with HTTP served by `FakeWeb`:

- 500, 502, 503, 504 and 599 each refuse with the 401/403 message, and only robots.txt is requested. The 5xx body is an allow-all rule set, so a parsed body would have let the fetch through.
- A robots.txt that redirects to a 503 refuses.
- The `fetch` prompt (the path the refusal points the user to) still fetches the page when robots.txt answers 503.

All seven fail against `v2/main` but one (the prompt test, which pins behavior that was already right). `test_protocol.py`'s "Characterizes" test `test_robots_5xx_body_is_parsed_as_rules`, which pinned the old behavior, is removed, as its module header says the fixing PR does. `npm run local:gate` exits 0.

**Client evidence.** A local stub (`127.0.0.1:58197`) answers `/robots.txt` with `503` and the body `User-agent: *\nAllow: /`, and `/page` with `200 stub page body for 5197`. The server runs with `--allow-private-ips` so it can reach the stub. "Before" is `origin/v2/main`'s `server.py`, run with the same environment.

Inspector CLI 2.9.0, `--method tools/call --tool-name fetch --tool-arg url=http://127.0.0.1:58197/page --format json`:

| Era | Before (`v2/main`) | After (this branch) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--protocol-era legacy` (2025-11-25) | exit 0, `isError: false`, `...Contents of http://127.0.0.1:58197/page:\nstub page body for 5197` | exit 5, `isError: true`, `Error executing tool fetch: When fetching robots.txt (http://127.0.0.1:58197/robots.txt), received status 503 so assuming that autonomous fetching is not allowed, the user can try manually fetching by using the fetch prompt` |
| `--protocol-era modern` (2026-07-28, `_meta` carries `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`) | exit 0, `isError: false`, same page text | exit 5, `isError: true`, same refusal |

`--method prompts/get --prompt-name fetch --prompt-args url=http://127.0.0.1:58197/page` on the branch, both eras: exit 0, the message text is `stub page body for 5197` (a user-initiated fetch does not consult robots.txt).

LLM client: Claude Code 2.1.311, headless, `--strict-mcp-config` with a config naming the local build (before and after), `--allowedTools mcp__fetch__fetch`. Prompt: "Use the fetch tool to fetch http://127.0.0.1:58197/page. Reply with one line: either the page text, or the exact error the tool returned."

- Before: `stub page body for 5197`
- After: `Error executing tool fetch: When fetching robots.txt (http://127.0.0.1:58197/robots.txt), received status 503 so assuming that autonomous fetching is not allowed, the user can try manually fetching by using the fetch prompt`

Claude Code gives no way to choose the protocol era and does not print the one it negotiated, so the LLM-client run is recorded without an era (the client-smoke skill notes this version line negotiates 2026-07-28 against these servers).

## Breaking Changes

None for configuration. Behavior: a tool fetch from a site whose robots.txt answers 5xx is now refused instead of proceeding; `--ignore-robots-txt` and the `fetch` prompt are unchanged.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] Documentation update

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [MCP Protocol Documentation](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
- [x] My changes follow MCP security best practices
- [x] I have updated the server's README accordingly
- [x] I have added a changeset (`npm run changeset`) if this changes what a TypeScript server publishes (not applicable: fetch is a Python server; its CalVer is stamped by the release PR)
- [x] I have tested this with an LLM client
- [x] My code follows the repository's style guidelines
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] I have added appropriate error handling
- [x] I have documented all environment variables and configuration options (not applicable: no new environment variable or option)

## Additional context

Part of the fetch v2.2.0 tracker #5265. The change is confined to the status-code branch of `check_may_autonomously_fetch_url`, so it merges cleanly with the other #5265 PRs.

author: azchohfi
body:
## Summary

Fixes gaps in the diagnostics and source-map reporting that inspectors such as winapp DevTools rely on. All of them were found while testing DevTools against `main` (`6a4b8bd9b`).

- **Events**
  - New `ReactorEventSource.CommitError` (EventId 41: phase, host root component, exception type) when a commit-phase or deferred-retirement failure puts up the error screen.
  - `WindowOpened` / `WindowClosed` are now raised for windows opened through `ReactorApp`. A failed open reports neither.
- **Source map**
  - `UseElementRef<T>()` is counted as one hook slot, so later hooks keep their `hooks=` index.
  - `MenuItem(…)` / `AppBarButton(…)` and the other menu and command-bar item factories are intercepted. They get a new equality-ignored `CallSite` on `MenuFlyoutItemBase` / `AppBarItemBase`.
  - Items created by a MenuFlyout, CommandBarFlyout, MenuBar or CommandBar publish `ReactorSource` (owner, kind, call site), and `ReactorSourceMap.GetSource` resolves each item to its own exact call site. When a host swaps its root over kept content, retained menu and command items are re-attributed to the new root too.
- **Keyed lists**
  - `ListView<T>` / `GridView<T>` / `FlipView<T>` rows carry their `KeySelector` key. On FlipView this is for diagnostics only; pages are still matched by position, and when a different item renders identical content at the same position the page takes the new key without replacing the element the control is tagged with (a keyed `Memo` output, a forwarding `RegisterType` child, or a legacy `ModifiedElement`'s inner element), so its callbacks keep working.
  - Null and duplicate keys are reported at mount as well as on update.
  - A null key is matched by position and reported once per diff, on every list binding. Some paths used to reset the whole list on every render; none do now.
  - Duplicate `.WithKey` panel siblings are reported, both at mount and whenever the key sequence changes.
  - `KeyedListDiagnostic` gains `ComponentName` and `CallSite`, including for descriptor lists on the typed `TemplatedItems` strategy. A repeated warning updates its own control's entry with the latest attribution and key summary. Log lines carry a short call site and a capped list of keys.
- **API**
  - New `int selectedIndex` overloads for `TabView`, `Pivot`, `ListView`, `GridView` and `FlipView`. A plain `int` used to be CS0121.
  - New `XamlHost(factory, updater, typeKey)` / `XamlPage(type, parameter)` factories, so the source map records a call site for hosted XAML.

The "bare render error reported twice" report did not reproduce in-process: one event on click, on `ReactorDiagnostics.TrySetState`, and under Errors-only and inspector listeners. It is left out of the fix and pinned by a regression selftest; see the issue.

## Linked issue / spec

Fixes #1421. Related specs: 044 (diagnostics), 010 (source map), 042 (keyed lists).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: `KeyedListAttributionTests` (including per-control dedup, latest attribution and overflow summary, sorted duplicate samples), `ReactorSourcePublisherTests` (`WithKey` / `HasKey` against `Format`), `SourceMapStaticInfoGeneratorTests` (UseElementRef, both surface shapes), `HookSlotTableTests` row, `DslFactoryOptionalTests` (int overloads, XamlHost/XamlPage), `ReactorEventSourceCoverageTests` (CommitError), and the rewritten null-key `KeyedListDiffTests` case.
- [x] SourceMap tests (`SourceMapInterceptorTests`): call sites for XamlHost/XamlPage and MenuItem/ToggleMenuItem/AppBarButton/AppBarSeparator.
- [x] Selftests:
  - `DiagnosticEvents_*`: RenderError reported once on all three paths; CommitError Reconcile and Cleanup phases on ReactorHost and ReactorHostControl, and a function root that remounts and then throws; window open/close and failed open.
  - `KeyedListDiagnostics_RowsKeysAndWarnings`: row keys; LazyVStack, ListView and ItemsView null and duplicate keys reported with attribution; no collection Reset on a null-key update (mutation-checked: reverting the sentinel makes it fail); FlipView prepend updates in place; FlipView same-content, keyed-Memo, forwarded-`RegisterType` and `ModifiedElement` pages keep their tag and click after a key change or re-render (each mutation-checked); typed `TemplatedItems` seed and diff warnings name the list's call site (mutation-checked); in Native AOT tag-skip mode a forwarded callback-free child keeps its own published identity and carries the item key.
  - `FlyoutItemIdentity_Published`: MenuFlyout, CommandBarFlyout, MenuBar, CommandBar and submenu items; republish when an item is patched in place or replaced; items with identical published `at=` text resolve to their own files. `ReactorSource_RootRemountRenamesOwner`: retained menu and command items (including collapsed, never-templated bars) and a hosted `AppBarButton`'s Reactor tooltip follow a root swap on both hosts (mutation-checked).
- [x] `dotnet test tests/Reactor.Tests -p:Platform=x64`: **passed** (15224 total, 0 failed, 64 skipped, after merging current `main`).
- [x] `dotnet test tests/Reactor.SourceMap.Tests -p:Platform=x64`: **passed** (114/114).
- [x] `dotnet run --project tests/Reactor.AppTests.Host -c Debug -p:Platform=x64 -- --self-test --filter <DiagnosticEvents|KeyedListDiagnostics|FlyoutItemIdentity|ReactorSource|RegisterTypeTag|RBC_PrivateUpdateHotPaths|FlipView|ListView|Menu|CommandBar|XamlHost>`: **passed**. The only failure is the pre-existing flaky `ReactorSource_LiveDialog_*_ClosedDialogStopsDescribingItsElement`.
- [x] Full `--self-test` run: the new fixtures pass. The only failures are `AnchorReset_*`, `Issue487_*`, `ItemsView_Parking_VariableHeightReset` and the flaky `ReactorSource_LiveDialog_*_ClosedDialogStopsDescribingItsElement`, and they fail the same way on an unmodified `6a4b8bd9b` checkout on this machine.
- [x] `dotnet restore Reactor.slnx` then `dotnet build Reactor.slnx --no-restore -c Release`: no C# errors or warnings. The run still failed for environment reasons only:
  - `NU1301` restoring `src/vs-reactor` straight from api.nuget.org, which fails TLS on this machine.
  - The nested ARM64 `Reactor.SignaturesGen` build that `Reactor.Cli` triggers.
  
  CI's `Build solution` job is the authoritative gate.
- [x] Docs compiled with `dotnet run --project tools/Reactor.DocPipeline -- compile --topic <diagnostics|xaml-developers|collections|reconciliation>`; the new `XamlPage`/`XamlHost` guide example is a compiled doc-app snippet (`dotnet test tests/Reactor.DocPipeline.Tests`: **passed**, 493/493). API index regenerated through `Reactor.SignaturesGen`; both copies are identical.
- [x] Ran the repo's `pr-review` skill until clean (6 rounds, including a cross-check by a different model family).

## Risk / breaking changes

- **Additive public API.** New factory overloads; new init properties on `KeyedListDiagnostic`, `MenuFlyoutItemBase` and `AppBarItemBase` (`CallSite` is excluded from equality); a new internal ETW event.
- **Behaviour changes:**
  - **Null list keys.** A null key is now matched by position everywhere. Before, the ItemsRepeater, ItemsView and strategy ListView paths reset the whole list on every render, so this only removes resets.
  - **Templated ListView/GridView rows carry their key.** Their containers follow items through the keyed diff, so identity is unchanged. FlipView matching is unchanged.
  - **ItemsView keyed diagnostics** are now recorded against the ItemsView, not its inner repeater.
- **Hot path.** `ChildReconciler.Reconcile` runs the duplicate-sibling scan only when a keyed panel's key sequence changed. A stable keyed panel pays one key compare per child.

body: ### Description Fixes code-scan finding **sfind-9af33a88** (critical): `GET /rest/track-order/:id` concatenated the path segment into a MarsDB `$where` string. MarsDB compiles that string with `Function('obj', 'return ' + selector)`, so an anonymous caller could dump every order (`' || true || '`) or run commands (`'||(global.m=process.mainModule)||'` then `'||m.require('child_process').execSync('id')||'`). The only input processing when `reflectedXssChallenge` was enabled was `utils.trunc(id, 60)`. Changes in `routes/trackOrder.ts`: - The `[^\w-]` allow-list now always applies, whether or not the challenge is enabled. - The query is now a plain equality selector, `db.ordersCollection.find({ orderId: id })`. No JavaScript is evaluated. - The Reflected XSS `solveIf` checks the raw `req.params.id` and only fires when the challenge is enabled, so the detection still works. The `noSqlOrdersChallenge` `solveIf` is removed because it can no longer be solved. - Tests: in `test/api/track-result.test.ts` the injection case now expects one placeholder row `{ orderId: 'true' }`, and there is a new case for stripping the XSS payload. The "NoSQL Exfiltration" block is removed from `test/cypress/e2e/noSql.spec.ts`. Retiring the challenge in `data/static/challenges.yml` is left to maintainers. RSN is not affected because the route is not part of a coding-challenge snippet. **Duplicates:** this PR is the same fix as #1679, #1570, #1405, #1321 and #1288, which came from earlier tickets for the same finding. Only one of them should land. It is opened separately because each new ticket gets its own PR. #### Verification `juice-shop` has no `node_modules` on the VM and the npm registry is blocked, so I couldn't run `npm run lint` or the api/cypress suites locally. author: quadseven
body:
## Why

A slot on cluster runners takes public repos only: a run's inputs and logs live in this public repo's Actions, so the runner dispatch refuses a private repo and parks the brief. The factory's tier filter (`lanes_of`, `_rung_lanes`) knew only `PUBLIC_ONLY`, so it kept giving free-gemma private tickets, and the final claim step never checked `needs_public_repo`. Each such ticket cost a claim, a park and a retry: on 2026-10-27 at 04:00Z the factory gave free-gemma tickets from two private repos, and a third private repo's ticket was claimed for it at 23:23Z on 10-26, parked, then retried on codex-2. Nothing private was dispatched; the cost is lost passes and free-gemma capacity.

## Summary

- `factory.public_only(lane)`: `PUBLIC_ONLY` or a slot in `LOOM_RUNNER_SLOTS`. `lanes_of` and `_rung_lanes` use it, so the factory never gives a private ticket a runner slot.
- The final claim step in bus/station.py refuses a lane where `needs_public_repo(lane, model)` holds and the repo is not public, and puts the ticket back to `loom:queued` with no lane, where the factory gives it a lane that takes private repos. A log line, no comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A factory test shows `lanes_of("medium", True)` drops free-gemma when it is a runner slot and keeps it when it is not; fails on main.
- [x] A station test with a private ticket labeled for a runner slot writes no brief for that slot and puts the ticket back in the queue with no lane; fails on main.
- [x] A station test shows a public ticket labeled for the same slot is still claimed there.
- [x] A station test shows a private ticket for free-gemma is still claimed when free-gemma is not a runner slot.
- [x] The full suite passes locally (.github/unittest_parallel.py: 4131 tests, OK).

## Size

S: about 25 lines in bus/factory.py and bus/station.py, four tests.

## Out of scope

- Which slots run on cluster runners (an operator setting).

Closes quadseven/loom#1917

This pull request introduces several improvements and refactors to the artifact delivery and group file upload system in the runtime, focusing on making group file uploads more robust, idempotent, and observable. It also enhances the tool interface for artifact management, adds new tests, and updates documentation and dependencies.

**Artifact Delivery and Group File Upload Improvements:**

* Refactored artifact delivery to use a unified `ChannelOperationResult` type, and introduced the `inspectArtifactDelivery` function for robust, idempotent inspection of delivery receipts, ensuring uploads are not repeated and results are consistent across restarts. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-523bca7741052d3ab1c31f9111252954f32ad3a1b66d73f3cb1f47a3304a1bc2L2-R4) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-523bca7741052d3ab1c31f9111252954f32ad3a1b66d73f3cb1f47a3304a1bc2R20-R39) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-523bca7741052d3ab1c31f9111252954f32ad3a1b66d73f3cb1f47a3304a1bc2L30-R64)
* Added the `canUploadGroupFile` and `deliverGroupArtifact` functions in `channel-delivery.ts` to centralize capability checks and the group file upload process, ensuring consistent behavior and proper capability enforcement.
* Updated the container tool registration to support artifact selection and discard operations, not just uploads, and to enforce that only "selected" artifacts can be uploaded. Improved input validation and error handling for these operations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-af8e6775125740e7bc4b1cc6fa8b9a0f086b14f93da26e8abec7d435d784955aR13-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-af8e6775125740e7bc4b1cc6fa8b9a0f086b14f93da26e8abec7d435d784955aL51-R94)
* Enhanced capability checks for group file uploads, ensuring that only channels with proper support allow uploads, and refactored the destination resolution logic.

**Testing and Quality Assurance:**

* Added comprehensive tests for the group file upload system (`channel-delivery.test.ts`), covering idempotency, error handling, capability enforcement, and edge cases to ensure robust behavior.
* Updated the CI workflow to install Playwright and run WebUI acceptance tests, improving test coverage for the WebUI.

**Dependency and Documentation Updates:**

* Updated dependencies in `package.json` files to include new modules and CLI entry points. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-85abf4ce3f1bc379456ec2b7b8ded1ab79966394876813a229c464b89dfa6d05R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-85abf4ce3f1bc379456ec2b7b8ded1ab79966394876813a229c464b89dfa6d05R47)
* Updated the README to clarify the product's roadmap and current capabilities, including references to the new features and documentation.

**Other Code Quality Improvements:**

* Improved configuration handling in `agent-factory.ts` by supporting additional parameters such as `maxInputChars`, `maxOutputTokens`, `timeoutMs`, and `maxRequestChars`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-39697286a75bf65c6f5e811a75aba1709d1da6a594e0cc82e9ed2905831b9579R34-R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-39697286a75bf65c6f5e811a75aba1709d1da6a594e0cc82e9ed2905831b9579R51-R52)

These changes collectively make the runtime's group artifact delivery more reliable, observable, and easier to manage, while also improving test coverage and developer experience.
