Saved VPN profiles currently provide no gateway reachability information. This change adds a Servers menu for automatic selection by lowest direct TCP connection latency, manual probe-and-select, and local city/IP JSON import. Probes are bounded, asynchronous, and send no application data or credentials. Existing certificate validation and interactive authentication remain in place. Automatic selection defaults off and does not switch an active connection or retry credentials across profiles.

The Windows portable build bundles Python for owned route/DNS cleanup, including a watchdog for GUI process exit. It supports direct AnyConnect over IPv4/TLS, preserves RFC1918 routing and detected internal DNS suffixes, and rejects conflicting VPN/DNS configuration. The GUI does not invoke Windows Script Host. No provider inventory or account data is included in the public package.

Validation: complete Windows build, gateway-probe tests, and portable packaging passed for b484851 and 1747042. The Windows GUI launches and probes real gateways. Local route-manager preparation, explicit cleanup, and owner-process-exit cleanup passed. An authenticated b484851 connection, with the redundant profile DTLS flag cleared, returned Google HTTP 204 and Cloudflare HTTP 200 with HTTP proxy inheritance disabled; socket and routing inspection confirmed direct VPN transport and preserved office routing/DNS. Commit 1747042 removes the duplicate DTLS call exposed by this test and passed Linux and Windows builds. Final 1747042 authentication also passed against a second gateway, with Google HTTP 204 and Cloudflare HTTP 200 and preserved office routing/DNS. The preceding packaged version passed a real disconnect check: no VPN routes, tagged DNS rules, or tunnel adapter remained. The final change affects only duplicate DTLS initialization; its network cleanup code is unchanged.

This remains a draft. The package is unsigned. Build fixes also cover upstream qt-solutions dependency ordering, current MinGW headers, and dependency DLL version discovery.

author: johnolafenwa
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"johnolafenwa"} -->
_Requested by **John** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01JQSf4RAkdgWS9xJ2iPpMi4?thread=cmsg_01JQSf4RAkdgWS9xJ2iPpMi43jsWCP5NLPFX3KVjSSXfrd)_

Step 2d of Phase 2 (typed native layouts) of the Rust-speed plan. Details: `work/2026-10-26-rust-speed-2d-list-buffers.md`.

## Summary

- `ListElements::Float32` keeps a `list[float32]` in 4-byte elements, and generated code reads, writes, and appends them in place. A `list[float32]` prints its elements with `float32` digits, and `aura run` rounds a float literal written where a `float32` is expected, as native code does (fixes the `float32-list-literal-append-parity` repro).
- `ListElements::Boxes` (`native_element_boxes.rs`) keeps each element of a list of class instances, enums, lists, dicts, or other boxed values in a box of its own. `native_codegen_elements.rs` finds element reads whose local is only read (each element of a `for` loop that reads its fields, `items[i].field`), and generated code borrows the box instead of copying the element into a new one. Before an instruction that changes, frees, or passes on the list while the local is still read, the local takes its own copy.
- Lending stays on one thread: generated code reads a box only while its list is confined and shares its storage with no other list. A list whose boxes another list shares, or that a closure, a task, or a mutable loan reaches, goes through the runtime, which lends only once the list owns its boxes. A list converts to boxes only after native code has copied out an eighth of its length, so a list read a few times keeps its form.
- Changelog: #159 merged after the 0.8.0 release preparation (#160), and its entry landed in the 0.8.0 section. `v0.8.0-preview` tags `f3b19e0f`, which does not include it, so this moves the entry to Unreleased.

## Measurements

Callgrind instruction counts, Linux container, release builds, cross-language suite at the check size. Before is step 2c.

| Program | Before | After | Change | After vs Rust |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `interpreter` | 368.8M | 238.3M | -35.4% | 29.7x |
| `mini_browser` | 1,392.1M | 1,153.8M | -17.1% | 35.5x |
| `sort_records` | 75.2M | 67.1M | -10.8% | 16.1x |
| `sql_engine` | 2,809.7M | 2,616.8M | -6.9% | 55.2x |
| `nbody` | 16.2M | 16.0M | -1.7% | 19.6x |
| `text_diff` | 10.6M | 10.4M | -1.6% | 8.3x |

No program regresses by more than 1.1% (`order_book`). The step's gate (`heap[i]` in `graph_paths` in at most 10 instructions) was already met by 2c, at about 9.

## Verification

- Runtime tests: the list model's edit sequence covers lends, writes through a lent element, and snapshots after edits; box identity, copy-on-write sharing, sort and conversion of shared lists; `ElementBox` copies an element another reference holds before a change.

author: samoylenkodmitry
body:
Part of #902. Stacked on #1922 (and so on #1921, #1916 and #1914): its own commits are the last two.

A picture keeps where each item of its scene can draw in the frame (its reach list), and the damage of an update is where a changed pair of items reaches: both are an item's bounds in the frame. An update in place worked the bounds out three times for each changed item (the old item's and the new item's for the damage, the new item's again for the reach list) and once more for each item it pushed again unchanged.

- The damage reads an old item's bounds from the reach list. An update in place writes each changed item's bounds into the list in its old item's place where a subtree of the same extent puts it; an item drawn as before keeps its entry. The full rebuild reads the old items' bounds from the list too. The list goes stale only after a splice, which measures it all again, as before.
- The damage list merges each area with every area it touches, so no two of its areas touch. An area inside the last one touches that one only, and the merge loop took it out and put it back unchanged after a scan of all the areas: the scan goes for such an area. Consecutive changed items of one card land in the area the first ones made.

The damage areas are the same, in the same order. The framebuffer bench draws the same checksums as the branch below: the dashboard in 16-bit strips (339076777; 360602623 redrawn whole), in RGBA (64803609), and the default screen (25967595). A stale reach list fails `the_dashboard_drawn_by_changed_areas_matches_whole_redraws` (checked by turning the write off).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| x86 dashboard, 100 frames (callgrind) | 183,952,904 | 179,475,462 (-2.4%) |
| `item_bounds` calls in a bench frame (1.6 updates) | 351 (56K instructions) | 144 (23K) |
| ES3C35P dashboard frame (reach commit alone, on #1921) | 31.96 ms, 2,769K instructions | 31.70 ms, 2,716K instructions |

author: ege-bulut
body:
**Paste a copied image** (web, desktop, Android). A screenshot or an image copied in another app goes into the message with Ctrl+V / ⌘V in the message box. The paste handler takes the clipboard's files when the paste has no text with it, because a range copied from a sheet also carries a picture of itself. A pasted image has no name of its own: browsers call it `image.png`, and Android's are named after a number. So each one is named `image-<local date and time>.png`.

On Android the WebView's text box offers no Paste when the clipboard holds only an image, and the page may not read the clipboard (`navigator.clipboard.read()` is denied). A small plugin, `ClipboardImagePlugin.java`, does the reading:
- `has()` looks only at the clip's description, because reading the clip itself makes Android show its "pasted" notice.
- `read()` returns the image's type and bytes.

Tapping 📎 with an image on the clipboard asks "You copied an image — Paste it / Choose a file". Without an image, 📎 opens the file picker as before. A keyboard's Ctrl+V works there too.

**Drag and drop** (web, desktop). Files dropped on a chat join the message, and a dashed "Drop to add to your message" shows while dragging. A file dropped anywhere else is ignored, so the browser or Electron doesn't open it in place of the app.

**Tests**
- `test/app.e2e.mjs files`:
  - a pasted image is added and renamed
  - a paste with text pastes the text
  - the drop hint shows
  - a drop adds the file
  - a drop outside a chat is not opened
  - both files are sent
- `test/android/paste.mjs`, on an emulator. The app runs in a chat against the in-memory GitHub, with its requests caught through DevTools so none leave the machine. Chrome copies a real image from a page the test serves. Then:
  - 📎 offers Paste and adds the image
  - Ctrl+V adds it
  - both are sent and arrive as PNGs
  - the chat stays open after switching to Chrome and back

The usage guide (EN+TR) and the changelog (EN+TR) are updated.

Establishes a reproducible evaluation capacity model across every registered rule type and every stage of the poller pipeline:

author: paragmore
body:
## Problem

`rebates.addresses` now carries one address per site phase (phase 1 and phase 1.5 on Ivinhema), and the finance layer attributes rebates to phases by the row's `receiver` (tetherto/miningos-app-node#320). The one-wallet reading from #25 breaks that: a transaction paying several configured addresses collapses into a single row for the full amount, credited to whichever address received the largest share — one phase's rebate would land on another phase's books, invisibly (the site total stays right, only the per-phase split is wrong).

No prod data is affected yet: every rebate tx so far pays a single address, and the second address has no transactions. This makes the split correct before it starts mattering.

## Change

- `extractRebates` emits **one row per (txid, receiving address)**, each with that address's own summed share. Both #25 fixes survive: no address's amount is dropped (the shares sum to what the old single row held), and a transaction spending from any configured address is still internal — never a rebate, at any of them.
- Rows are stored under `txid:receiver`; rows written before this change stay readable under their bare-txid keys and block their transaction from being retro-split.
- Deleting a txid removes every row of the transaction and the tombstone keeps covering it whole.
- Updates address one row by txid + receiver, falling back to the transaction's single stored row when the receiver itself is the field being corrected.

## Companion

app-node's `combinePoolRebates` dedupes synced rows by txid alone, which would drop the second address's row of a shared transaction — fixed on tetherto/miningos-app-node#320.

## Tests

Per-address extraction on a shared tx; sync stores both halves; delete removes both and blocks re-sync; update touches only the addressed half; receiver-correction fallback; all existing single-address and internal-transfer cases unchanged. 86/86 pass.

## 무엇
「법카 결제 한 번에 올리기」 목록 — 대표 요청 「최신 것부터 나오는게 좋지 않아? 금액이나 날짜로 검색할 수 있으면」.

- **최신순**: `ORDER BY expense_date DESC, expense_time DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC`. 목록은 200건 상한이라 예전(오래된 순)엔 200건이 넘으면 **가장 최근 결제가 잘렸다**. 이제 잘리는 쪽은 오래된 결제, 안내 문구도 맞춤. 기본 선택(앞에서부터 최대 건수)도 최근 결제부터가 된다.
- **검색**(화면에서, 불러온 목록 안): 금액(쉼표·원 무시, 부분 일치), 날짜(10.24 · 10/24 · 1024 · 2026.10.24 · 20261024), 가맹점·제목. 띄어 쓰면 모두 만족(AND). 순수 함수 `matchesPendingQuery` + 테스트.
- **가려진 선택**: 검색에 가려진 선택도 제출되므로 버튼 「5건 올리기 · 가려진 4건 포함」, 주황 안내 + 「가려진 N건 선택 해제」. 검색 중 전체 선택은 「보이는 N건 선택/해제」.
- 바뀌지 않는 것: 제출 내용·금액(서버가 고위드에서 읽음)·claim·회사/카테고리/제목 기본값·「아직 안 올린 결제 N건」 요약·법카 한 건 폼.

## 검증
- `npx tsc --noEmit` 0 · `npm run lint` 오류 0 · 단위 테스트 476/476
- 로컬 운영 빌드(가짜 결제 5건, 390px): 순서 10.27→10.15, 검색 6가지(금액·날짜·가맹점·AND·없는 값), 가려진 선택 버튼·해제 확인.

## 배포
DB 변경 없음. 비용계획 창 대상은 아니지만(계획 「법카 연결」 창도 같은 목록을 쓴다) 배포마다 열린 앱이 새로고침되므로 07:00~08:30 창에 #21과 함께 권장.

author: movieholic-plex
body:
## What leaked

The exported player shipped the workshop object-gen kit, including an `api.openai.com` host list (the `objectShape` chunk). The import chain was:

`player.html → exportEntry → project/io → io/migration → io/shape → project/gameDesignBrief → harnesses/_core/registry → interior-props/harness → interior-props/editor/runner → _core/workshop/referencePrompt → … → genKits/object-gen.json`

`gameDesignBrief` imported the full harness registry only to normalise the one saved harness contract (romance-scene). The registry pulls every harness's editor runner, so all of them came along.

## Fix

- **`src/harnesses/_core/contracts.ts`** is a new contracts-only index; the schema now reads contracts from it.
  - `test/harnessContracts.test.ts` checks that it lists exactly the registry harnesses that declare a contract, with the same normaliser.
- **`scripts/lib/playerBundleGuard.mjs`** is a new build plugin, wired into `vite.player.config.ts` and `vite.standalone.config.ts`. The build fails when either of these reaches the player:
  - Modules: `src/ai/`, the harness registry, harness `editor/` runners, `_core/workshop/`, `src/editor/workshop/`, or the legacy DB client. The failure message prints the import chain.
  - Text in any `.js`/`.css`/`.html` artifact: an AI-provider host (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini `generativelanguage`/`cloudcode-pa`/`aiplatform`, OpenRouter, xAI, Mistral, Groq, Together, Cohere, DeepSeek). Only the label and file name are reported.
- **`test/playerBuild.test.ts`** now uses the guard's module and host lists. It adds a case proving the lists catch the known leaks and do not flag `contracts.ts`.
  - The in-test build now runs with `NODE_ENV=production`. Under vitest's `NODE_ENV=test`, vite kept `import.meta.env.DEV` true, which pulled the dev-only flagship demo builders and the editor tool registry into the graph. The shipped build never includes those.
- **`openwiki/licensing.md`**: the "미수정" (not fixed) note about this edge is replaced with the fix and the guard.

## Verification

- **Local `vite build`, player and standalone configs:** both succeed with the guard. With the old `gameDesignBrief`, the player build fails and prints the registry chain. After the fix, the player output contains no provider host.
- **CI, `ci-vitest-files` run 40463234067:** passes for `test/playerBuild.test.ts`, `test/harnessContracts.test.ts` and `test/playerEditorOnlyAssets.test.ts`.
- **`.omo`:** `test/playerBuild.test.ts` is removed from the gates baseline and the fix list.

author: mlloyd5
body:
## Why

A disc only became a double feature when the case barcode's product title, the disc label or the disc's own metadata named several films. A generic label (`DVD_VIDEO`) or a barcode naming only one film left the second film filed as an extra, with no way to fix it in the UI. A title fix couldn't undo a wrong double feature either: the film rows stayed, so `file_collection` still split the rip. And with `MAINFEATURE: true` only one title was ripped, so a double feature's other films were lost.

## What changed

**Double Feature page** (`/doublefeature`, `arm/ui/jobs/double_feature.py`)
- A **Double Feature** button sits next to Bonus Disc on the home-page card and the job page. Title Search and Custom Title link to the page too, or show "Change" when the disc is already marked.
- Search for each film and click **Add as film N**. Each film's runtime comes from TMDB or OMDb. Films can be moved up or removed, and **Not a double feature** clears them all.
- Films are stored as the job's `film` rows, the same rows `identify_collection` writes, so filing after the rip is unchanged.
- Once there are two films, the job takes the first film's title, year, IMDb id and poster, as a title fix would. This also ends the manual wait.
- Refused for finished jobs, bonus discs, and anything other than DVD or Blu-ray.

**Title fixes**: Title Search and Custom Title now remove the job's films, unless the new title is the first film. The comparison ignores the ripper's hyphens versus the UI's spaces. A finished job keeps its films, which record where each film was filed.

**MAINFEATURE**: `apply_collection_settings` turns `MAINFEATURE` off for a double feature's job when its rip starts, so every title is ripped and matched to its film. `file_collection` then leaves the unclaimed titles out, as `MAINFEATURE` would have. A disc marked after its rip has started still rips with `MAINFEATURE` on, so only one title is ripped. The wiki says to mark it during the manual wait.

**Docs**: new `arm_wiki/Double-Features.md`, linked from the sidebar and from Bonus Discs.

## Testing

Run in Docker (`arm-labels-test` image), each module in a separate pytest invocation:

Before: the manual control window used solid flat buttons in many colours (green ON, red 닫기/후진, orange 실행, purple 배기 ON). Disabled buttons looked the same as enabled ones, so with EtherCAT disconnected every button still looked pressable. Status text used LimeGreen and Yellow, which are hard to read on a light background.

After: groups are plates like the main screen. Buttons are white and raised with a small dot showing the kind of action: green for ON/켜기/진공 ON, blue for 열기/전진/서보 ON/배기 ON/티칭, amber for 실행/원점복귀, grey for OFF/닫기/후진. Painting only: every button keeps its position, size, click handler and Enabled logic, and no I/O call or interlock changed. The E-stop keeps its place in the bottom bar.

Groups use `AttachPlate`, the E-stop uses `AttachEmergency`, and status `ForeColor` assignments map LimeGreen/Red/Orange/Yellow to `UiTheme.Success/Danger/Warning`.

Not changed here: the bottom bar with the E-stop sits below the scrolling content, so the window has to be scrolled down to reach it (also true before this PR). Moving it needs the owner's OK.

author: iroqi
body:
## 背景

对 `main` 做格式塔式深度 review（整体行为 > 单点语法）。全仓已有的结构性门禁（`lint` / `Layout` / `Contrast` / `check_svg` / 成片时长契约）覆盖得很扎实，**唯一还在看像素的**只有 `scripts/perceptual.py`。review 的结论是：这道门禁本身有三处"失效模式"——它不会误报太多，而是在特定条件下**静默失效**，或**会被使用者亲手关掉**。

三条都用可复现的合成场景固定成测试，并在回退版上逐条验证过"测试确实会红"。

## 改动

### 1. 缺 Pillow 抛 `SystemExit`，把已出片的 run 判成失败

`_load_pil()` 抛 `SystemExit`，违反 `run_gate` 自己声明的"不阻断、不 sys.exit"契约。`SystemExit` 不是 `Exception` 子类，`run.py` 的 `except Exception` 接不住它：成片已渲染完、`production_report.json` 写了一半，进程以"Pillow 没装"的码收场。

→ 改为 `PillowMissing(RuntimeError)`，被现有 `except RuntimeError` 收成 `{"error": ...}`，走"门禁未完成"那条路，退出码不动。

### 2. `snapshot` 失败被上一次的帧掩盖

判据原是 `returncode != 0 and not isdir(outdir)`：只要上一轮跑过、帧目录还在，这次取帧全失败也照样往下判——量的是**上一次**的编排，报告里写着"帧数正常、无判词"。

→ 取帧前清空目录；`and not isdir` 改成无条件判非 0 退出。`--project` 取回帧数少于采样点数时另打一条 warn：判词变少不等于通过。

### 3. `--strict` 口径与文档不符

帮助文本与 `references/perceptual.md` 都承诺"有 error 级判词才退出 5"，实现是"有任何判词就 5"，而判词此前根本没有 severity。后果不是"多报几条"，是：节奏舒缓的合格片子被 CI 判红 → 人不改画面、删掉 `--strict` → 这道门禁整体失效。

→ 每条判词带 `severity`（真源 `ISSUE_SEVERITY`，未登记的按 error 从严）；`temporal_budget` 归 warn；`--strict` 只让 error 判非零。登记表注明了"为什么只有这一档是 warn"。

### 4. 顺带修一处误报

换页读数早于首段口播起点时（开屏页还挂着），"最近 span"恒为第一段，旧判据会写成"第一段声画不同步"——那一刻第一段一秒都还没开始。读数落在 `[首段起点, 末段起点]` 之外时不再归属任何段。

## 验证

| 检查 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `python -m unittest discover -s tests` | **1478 passed**（基线 1473，新增 5） |
| `tests/check_docs.py` | 0 条悬空引用 |
| `tests/check_numbers.py` | 40 条决策阈值全部对得上 |
| `tests/check_examples.py` | 4 个示例全跑通 |
| `tests/check_image_snippets.py` | 2 个片段全过 |
| 回退验证 | 三条新测试在回退版上均 **FAIL**、修复版上 PASS |

改动只在 `scripts/perceptual.py` / `tests/test_perceptual.py` / `references/perceptual.md`，不碰渲染、模板与数据契约。

## 未做（留给后续）

- `html_renderer.py`（2946 行）与 `gen_hyperframes.py`（2349 行）是两个巨型模块，`pipeline.py` 已 1463 行；拆分是重构，不在本次 review 的止血范围内。
- `temporal_budget`（"这一页一共变了多少次"）只登记了严重度、还没有判据实现——它是 `dead_seconds` 之外真正拉近 3b1b 的那个量，需要先有实测基线才敢定阈值。

author: windroc-bot[bot]
body:
WDRC-248 PRD "WDRC-248 安装器 v0.5.0 实测问题回归防护" (`Product Design/2026-10-27-0437-WDRC-248-installer-v050-regression-tests.md`): FR-4, FR-6, FR-7, FR-8 (U1a, CL2).

## What changed

**U1a: a failed egress fetch leaves nothing** (`scripts/install.sh`)
- The `egress_download` subshell has no `local`. Its EXIT trap holds the `%q`-quoted literal temp path, so it reads no variable when it fires. That holds whether it fires after a `die` from a nested function or after a bash has left the function's scope. Correct by construction, whatever the shell.
- Every egress step removes `~/.egress/versions/.download.*` left by an earlier failed run (v0.5.0's leftover on the test mini).

**CL2: cleanup removes the egress the installer created and keeps the rest** (`scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install-cleanup.sh`)
- New ledger kinds `docker-container egress-proxy` and `docker-image egress-proxy`. A new shared helper `egress_absent` writes them only when Docker reports `No such container|image`, so a Docker hiccup never claims a container or image that was there before.
- `~/.egress` is recorded when install creates it. When it was there before, install records only what it adds: `versions/`, `config.local.yaml`, `compose.networks.yaml` (rendered by start.sh), and the version dir plus `current` when install owns the link. A pre-existing `current` keeps the version it now points to.
- Cleanup:
  - a preflight stops with `Docker is not running: start Docker Desktop, then rerun; nothing removed` when a `docker-*` record exists and Docker does not answer;
  - a new `egress proxy` step runs `docker rm -f egress-proxy`, then `docker image rm egress-proxy`, before Docker Desktop is removed, and drops each record only once Docker reports it gone;
  - a `worker images and volumes` step lists `ensemble-worker` images and `ensemble-ws-*` volumes as kept, noting when the Docker Desktop removal will delete them with Docker's data;
  - the no-`--yes` listing shows the new records and a "keeps worker images … volumes" line.
- `egress-*` networks are kept: worker containers attach to them.
- `docs/docker-host.md` now says what cleanup removes and keeps.

**Related defect** (both scripts' `sudo_once`): the keep-alive's TERM trap read `nap` before its first assignment under `set -u`. `nap` is now initialized.

**Tests** (`tests/integration/install_integration_test.py`, `install_fakes.py`):
- 9 new `test_u1a_*` / `test_cl2_*` integration tests.
- `run_install`/`fresh` take `shell=` (U1a runs `/bin/bash`).
- The docker fake models the egress container and image, Docker's `No such …` errors, Docker quitting mid-cleanup (`docker_stops_at`) and the list filters.
- `test_cleanup_round_trip` and `test_cleanup_removes_only_what_was_added` now expect `~/.egress` removed.

## Root cause and U1a status: please verify on the test mini

The trap read `tmp`, a function-local of a subshell function. A bash that unwinds function scope before running the subshell's EXIT trap prints `tmp: unbound variable` under `set -u` and skips the `rm`.

**The `unbound variable` trigger was not reproduced on Linux.** Probes tried:
- shells: stock GNU bash 3.2.57 (built from source) and 5.2;
- script modes: file and piped (`bash -s`);
- paths: the success path, errexit, `die` from a nested function, `die` after a failing pipeline, and a parent `on_exit` trap.

All of them cleaned up. So `test_u1a_failed_egress_fetch_leaves_nothing` passes before the fix on Linux, and the trigger is probably specific to Apple's `/bin/bash` 3.2.57. The fix does not depend on it. `test_u1a_failed_egress_fetch_removes_earlier_leftovers` fails before the fix on Linux. To verify live: on the test mini, make the tarball fetch fail (for example, no repository access) and run `curl … | bash -s -- --docker`. stderr should show `cannot fetch pinned windroc/egress-proxy` and no `unbound variable`, and `~/.egress/versions/` should hold no `.download.*`.

## Regression evidence (NFR-1)

Each test ran on Linux with this PR's tests and fakes over a `git archive` of the scripts at the commit before its fix, then on the head.

| Test | Base e10a8f8 | 3dc0f79 (before review fix r1) | Head 1a05757 (and 1fe0d09) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test_u1a_failed_egress_fetch_leaves_nothing` | pass (trigger not reproduced, above) | pass | pass |
| `test_u1a_failed_egress_fetch_removes_earlier_leftovers` | FAIL `[.egress/versions/.download.stale] != []` | pass | pass |
| `test_cl2_cleanup_removes_installed_egress` | FAIL `dir ~/.egress not found in ledger` | pass | pass |
| `test_cl2_cleanup_keeps_preexisting_egress` | FAIL `dir versions/<sha> not found in ledger` | pass | pass |
| `test_cl2_cleanup_keeps_the_version_a_preexisting_current_needs` | FAIL `file config.local.yaml not found in ledger` | pass | pass |
| `test_cl2_cleanup_keeps_preexisting_egress_container` | FAIL `kept ensemble-worker:abc123 not found` | FAIL same | pass |
| `test_cl2_install_records_only_what_docker_reports_missing` | FAIL `docker-image not found in ledger` | FAIL `docker-container unexpectedly found` | pass |
| `test_cl2_cleanup_keeps_a_failed_egress_removal` | FAIL `0 != 1` | FAIL `0 != 1` (record dropped while Docker was down) | pass |
| `test_cl2_cleanup_needs_docker_for_egress_records` | FAIL (cleanup went on to sudo: hung) | pass | pass |

CI on 1fe0d09 (after the base merge): all checks pass. `Repository tests 1-6` run the installer suite on ubuntu whenever `scripts/` or these tests change (NFR-4).

## Without an in-repo integration test (NFR-5)

- **FR-5** (the pinned egress commit fetchable by every installing user): needs a real network and real account access. Out of scope per the ticket; mini-op verifies it with a test account (`--docker`).
- **U1a's `unbound variable` trigger**: not reproducible on Linux (above). The fix is by construction, and the leftover half has a red-to-green test.
- **`nap` initialization**: the failure is a TERM race inside a background subshell whose stderr is `/dev/null`, so no deterministic test exists. `test_cleanup_helpers_match` keeps both copies identical.

## Decisions

- This PR adds no macOS workflow. Since the base merge (#108, c53ea4b), the base ships `installer-macos.yml`, so `Installer macos-15` runs the installer suite, U1a's test included, under `/bin/bash` 3.2. Per the manager's ruling it is extra coverage, not evidence.
- The base was merged in (1fe0d09), keeping both sides. The only conflicts were `install-cleanup.sh`'s listing kinds and step order: `plugin-root`/`plugin_root` from the base, then `worker_data`, then `egress_proxy`. A final review round on the whole change against c53ea4b passed.
- The listing of worker images and `ensemble-ws-*` volumes runs whenever Docker was chosen (manager decision), not only when install created the proxy.

## How to verify

```
export PYTHONPATH=.:.github:src
python3 .github/run_tests.py Integration tests/integration/install_integration_test.py
grep -n "_u1a_\|_cl2_" tests/integration/install_integration_test.py
```

## Deferred non-blocking review items (verbatim, for the manager or user)

- code-quality: "scripts/install-cleanup.sh egress_proxy (about lines 692-700): the container and image branches repeat the same rm-or-inspect-then-die shape. A small helper taking the rm command and inspect command would shorten it." The fix reduced this to a two-way `case` plus one shared `egress_absent` check.
- code-quality: "tests/integration/install_integration_test.py (test_u1a_failed_egress_fetch_leaves_nothing and ..._removes_earlier_leftovers): both repeat the same failing-fetch setup and `fresh(...)` call. Pull it into a helper or fold the first test's asserts into the second."
- test: "scripts/install.sh egress_download: the `%q`-quoted trap path is only exercised with a plain mktemp path. A HOME containing a space or quote would test the quoting that replaced the local variable."
- test: "scripts/install-cleanup.sh egress_proxy: the error paths are untested (`cannot remove container/image

author: lugabeeee
body:
## Summary

A fullscreen right panel was clipped to its docked track on tablets.

The stock `sidebar-right` paints its panel at `width: 100vw` once it enters fullscreen (`data-sidebar-right-panel="fullscreen"`), but the dedicated Mobile layout mounts that panel inside the docked overlay (`.dshm-details`: `width: min(94vw, 460px)` with `overflow: hidden`). On a wide viewport with a docked panel, `layout.openRightbar(track, true)` therefore dimmed the conversation, hid the navigation drawer and showed only the right ~460px of a viewport-wide panel: its header slid off-canvas and the body rendered clipped line tails. Phones were unaffected because their overlay is already 100% wide below 900px.

- Track the fullscreen state DSH reports through the layout service as `data-rightbar-fullscreen` on the shell, and let the overlay span the viewport while a fullscreen panel is mounted.
- Treat that state like the existing phone overlay: the conversation behind it is `inert` and needs no scrim.
- Phones derive fullscreen from their width, so their rendering is unchanged.

## Compatibility

- DSH 0.1.7-alpha.2 through 0.2.1-rc.2 all call `layout.openRightbar(track, fullscreen)` and expose `data-sidebar-right-panel`; the new attribute stays false on any page that never reports fullscreen, so surfaces without the feature keep their current layout.
- No `:has()` or other new selector is required; the added rule uses attribute selectors and `inset`, which the layout already uses.
- Docked (`push`) mode, the narrow overlay, the wide default sidebar and the phone layout are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `npm test` 2496 passed / 27 platform skips, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm run build`.
- A 390x844 phone view of the shipped CSS is pixel-identical before and after.
- A 1369x914 tablet harness built from the shipped Mobile and `sidebar-right` CSS shows the panel clipped to 460px before and full width after.
- The reporting user confirmed fullscreen entry and exit on a physical Android tablet. That run used an equivalent `mobile.css` override, because the released plugin predates this change; the packaged fix itself was not exercised on the device.

## Notes

The temporary CSS override will be removed from the reporter's installation once a release contains this fix.

author: alessbarb
body:
## Scope / phase and gate
Construction: Enterprise phase 2 implementation/blockage-escalation protocols and phase 4 §14 pilot continuity. No new protocol engine, authority, provider activation or integrator enablement.

A high-priority child that reaches its attempt/no-progress limit no longer starves independent eligible work assigned to the same agent. Reuse existing admission/staging gates; persist the blockage and try the next child. Preserve the first blocked result if every candidate is blocked. Revalidate grants and assignment before recording a staging conflict. Non-409 errors still propagate.

## Evidence (candidate 73e3dee)
- RED before implementation: both new ATTEMPT_LIMIT / NO_PROGRESS cases failed because dispatch selected the blocked first child; QUEUED/RUNNING cases passed.
- GREEN on final candidate: focused PostgreSQL dispatch integration: **6 passed**, including all-blocked, deduplicated block reporting and deterministic grant revocation between staging conflict and block write (403, no additional block event or attempt).
- Full backend using repository `.venv/bin/python`, explicitly disposable `aao-disposable-pg`, warnings as errors: **763 passed, zero skipped**, 79.06s.
- Ruff: all checks passed; pip check: no broken requirements; git diff --check passed.
- Frontend in candidate worktree: npm ci, TypeScript, **230 tests / 26 files**, production build passed. Existing bundle-size warnings remain.
- Read-only construction second-line review: no blocking findings; not independent audit.

## Limits / authority
No actual model task, operational PM deployment, W2 App push or B-2 acceptance is claimed by this change. No concurrent two-dispatch race test added; revocation test is deterministic interleaving. No migration, grant changes, secret access, public endpoint or integrator activation. Ordinary external-construction authorization only.

body:
[94S-1043](https://linear.app/94soon/issue/94S-1043)

## 왜

오너 피드백(2026-10-27): "프로필의 상세내용확인이나 편집 등도 못하는거 같은데?". /profiles에서는 표의 요약만 보이고, 한 프로필의 모델·도구·버전 기록이나 그 프로필을 실제로 쓰는 에이전트를 볼 곳이 없었습니다.

## 범위

- 워크스페이스·운영자 프로필 행 어디를 눌러도 상세 화면 `/profiles/$profileId`가 열립니다(`GridTableRowOpener`, 키보드는 행마다 Tab 한 번). 이전 버전 펼치기·수정·사용 중지 버튼은 행 위에 올려 그대로 동작합니다.
- 상세 화면:
  - 설정: id, 바탕 프로필(링크), 기본 모델, 고를 수 있는 모델, 도구, 권한 모드, 실행 환경, 만든 때·사용 중지한 때
  - 버전 기록: 같은 이름의 vN·상태·만든 때, 지금 보는 버전 표시. 행을 누르면 그 버전으로 갑니다.
  - 이 프로필을 쓰는 에이전트: 활성 release가 이 버전을 쓰는 에이전트와 그 에이전트 버전. 누르면 에이전트의 release 탭으로 갑니다.
- 소유자·관리자: 상세의 **수정**(바탕이 바뀐 버전은 **다시 만들기**)이 지금 값이 채워진 편집 화면을 엽니다. 저장 버튼은 "새 버전으로 저장", 안내는 "새 버전으로 저장합니다…"이고, 저장하면 새 버전의 상세로 옮겨 갑니다. 운영자 프로필 상세에는 **이 프로필로 만들기**가 있습니다.
- 구성원: 읽기만 합니다. 에이전트 목록은 서버가 `agent.manage`를 요구하므로 요청하지 않고 "에이전트를 관리할 수 있는 사람만 봅니다"를 보입니다.

author: mr-karan
body:
## Description

Adds a stack for [Logchef](https://logchef.app), a log analytics interface for logs that already live in ClickHouse or VictoriaLogs. It queries them with LogchefQL or SQL and keeps its teams, sources and saved queries in a local SQLite file.

One application container behind the Tailscale sidecar, no deviations from the standard setup. The log backend stays outside the stack on purpose: Logchef never stores or copies logs, and bundling an empty ClickHouse would still need a separate shipper before anything was queryable. The README says what to point it at.

Built-in email and password login is enabled, so the stack needs no identity provider. Two secrets are required and use the `${VAR:?}` pattern, so Compose stops until they are set:

- `API_TOKEN_SECRET`, at least 32 characters
- `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, at least 10 characters

Settings come from the config file in the image and are overridden with `LOGCHEF_` variables, where a double underscore is one level of TOML nesting.

Disclosure: I maintain Logchef.

## Related Issues

- Closes #402

## Verification

- [x] `docker compose config --quiet` from each changed service directory, with dummy values for required variables
- [x] The stack started, Tailscale is healthy, and the service is reachable through the Tailnet
- [x] The main function of the service works, and its data survives a restart
- [x] `rumdl check --config .markdownlint.yml .` on the whole repository, and `git diff --check`

Against the published image, which is Alpine based and ships BusyBox `wget` but no `curl`:

- Starts clean from the stack's environment variables with no errors or warnings, and `/api/v1/health` returns `{"status":"success","data":{"status":"ok",...}}`. That is the health check command in `compose.yaml`, run inside the container.
- Signed in with the bootstrap administrator, added a ClickHouse source (`is_connected: true`), linked it to a team, and ran `SELECT ... WHERE severity_text = 'error'` against a seeded table of 5 rows. It returned exactly the 2 matching rows in 5 ms.
- The source and its data survived a restart, reconnected, and queried again.
- With `./logchef-data/app` owned by root, the container stops with `unable to open database file (14)`. After `chown 1000:1000` it starts and writes `local.db` plus its `-wal` and `-shm` files to the host. That is why "Before you start" has the `chown` step, and why the exact message is in "Troubleshooting": it never mentions permissions.

On a live Tailnet the sidecar joined as `logchef-test.dove-climb.ts.net`, Tailscale Serve issued the certificate, and `https://<name>/api/v1/health` answered. Signing in, adding the source, the query and a full `docker compose down && up` all pass over that address. Details are in a comment below.

## Impact on existing users

- None. New service.

## Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code and followed the [templates](https://github.com/tailscale-dev/ScaleTail/tree/main/templates/service-template) structure.
- [x] I did not commit a working auth key, password, token, or other credential.
- [x] The service README uses the headings of the template, in the same order, and is up to date.
- [x] I added, removed, or renamed the service in the [root README.md](https://github.com/tailscale-dev/ScaleTail/blob/main/README.md), in alphabetical order, or this PR does not change the list of services.

## Additional Context

ClickHouse uses its native protocol port, `9000`, for a source, not the HTTP port `8123`. Mixing them up is the most likely setup mistake, so it is called out in "Troubleshooting".

Anyone who pulled `ghcr.io/mr-karan/logchef:latest` before v2.5.0 should run `docker compose pull`. Older images shipped a config file that pointed at a path only present in a source checkout, so they exited at startup. Fixed upstream in v2.5.0, which is what `latest` now resolves to.

author: ramanareddychamakura
body:
A file opened by HTTP range requests now shows its first page without first reading every page dictionary. This was the "lazy page tree" item in the docs' Planned list, and it follows up on #120.

## Design
- **`PdfPageTree.IsLazy`** (used by ranged documents only):
  - The page count is the root's `/Count`. It is checked before anything is sized by it: it must be at least the number of kids and at most the file's xref entries and `MaxObjectsCount`.
  - A page is found when it is first needed. The tree descends from the root to the kid whose `/Count` holds the page. The descent is a loop bounded by `MaxPageTreeDepth`, with a visited set for the path.
  - A node with as many kids as pages goes straight to the kid. In any other node, every kid is read, and the kids' pages must add up to the node's `/Count`.
  - When a kid's bytes are missing, up to 64 more kids are read in the same pass, so one round fetches them all.
  - Any mismatch (loop, too deep, missing or wrong `/Count`) throws an internal `PdfPageTreeMismatchException`.
- **`PdfRangedDocument`:**
  - The structure walk stops at the root of the tree (`PdfObjectClosure.FollowKids = false`).
  - `EnsurePageFoundAsync` fetches the path to a page, one level per round, with a small read-ahead. Opening resolves page 1.
  - A mismatch, a damaged node, or a page not found within `MaxRounds` turns the lazy tree off (`PageTreeFallbackReason`). The document is then opened again with the full tree walk, still by ranges.
  - New public API: `FindPageAsync` (a page's node without its contents) and `PdfRangedOptions.LazyPageTree` (default true).
- **`ViewerDocument`:**
  - Pages not read yet are laid out at page 1's size.
  - `EnsurePageSizeAsync` runs before strip rendering, and each ranged render or text call updates that page's size.
  - On completion, every size comes from the full parse. The page count is replaced if a lying tree changed it.
  - A `PagesChanged` event tells the viewer to lay out again (`Viewer.razor.cs` handles it).
- **Not changed:** files opened from memory or a file, and the desktop app. They use the eager walk. It was refactored into shared `Inherit`/`MakePage` helpers with the same behaviour, and the full suites pass.

## Measured
The same generated 46.2 MB, 320-page file as #120, with page objects spread through it. Headless Chrome, `large-file.html?url=`, release build, 3 runs after a warm-up (cached viewer), time to first page:

| Network | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 50 Mbit/s + 40 ms, `serve.mjs --rate 6104 --latency 40` | 21.4–21.6 s, 2.4 MB in 318 requests | **2.4–2.7 s, 1.2 MB in 6 requests** |
| 50 Mbit/s + 40 ms simulated in the page (`large-file.html` default) | 5.1–5.4 s, 2.4 MB in 316 requests | **1.5–1.6 s, 1.2 MB in 4 requests** |
| loopback | 2.5–2.9 s, 318 requests | **1.6–1.7 s, 6 requests** |
| whole file, 50 Mbit/s + 40 ms (`serve.mjs`) | | 10.7–10.9 s |

Through `serve.mjs`, my "before" runs took 21 s, not the 5.8–7.4 s in #120, even though the bytes and requests were identical. Chrome seemed to send the 318 requests for the same URL almost one at a time. The in-page simulation gives numbers close to #120's. With 6 requests, the difference no longer matters.

## Tests
- PdfEngine.Vector.Tests: 1343 passed, 1 skipped. This includes the new `LazyPageTreeTests` (15 tests, 17 cases), which use a fake `MemoryRangeReader` to count requests and bytes:
  - Spread-out file, page 1: 6 or fewer requests and less than 5 % of the bytes. Without the lazy tree: 150 or more requests.
  - Balanced tree: every page's boxes, rotation, object number and ancestors match the full walk.
  - Hostile trees: root `/Count` too high, negative, or huge (2e9); a lying intermediate `/Count`; kids that do not add up; cyclic kids; a node that is its own kid; a chain past the round limit; a tree deeper than `MaxPageTreeDepth` (fails as the in-memory open does); a kid without `/Count`.
  - One `RangeLoadingTests` test now takes the image object number from the in-memory document. Before, it found page 15 through the tree, which now costs one more round.
- PdfEngine.Vector.Skia.Tests: 447 passed, 2 skipped (+2 `EmbedRangeTests`: placeholder sizes and `PagesChanged`, and a corrected page count for a lying tree).
- PdfViewer.Tests: 827 passed. One run had a `Direct2DPageHostTests` failure under load. It passed alone and in a full rerun.
- `tests/sdk/*.test.mjs`: 14 passed, 1 skipped.

## Limitations
- A node whose kid count equals its `/Count` is trusted without reading every kid. In other nodes, only the nodes on a page's path are checked. So a wrong `/Count` beside the path can put pages in the wrong order until the whole file is read. Then the full parse corrects it, and `PagesChanged` fires.
- A deep tree takes one round per level. Past 12 rounds, the whole tree is read, as before.

Docs: `docs/sdk/index.md` (Large files: intro, how it works, fallbacks, Measured; the Planned item is removed) and the web README's next steps.

author: marcin-wosinek
body:
## Summary

Closes #2059

- Notification takeover, data upgrades, worker start-up and history cleanup scheduling move from `plugins_loaded` to `init` priority 11. That is after Action Scheduler (priority 1) and translations (priority 10), and before Connectors (priority 15).
- The Telegram connector hooks and the REST routes are still registered on `plugins_loaded`. The connector's callbacks (registry, setting, autoload, credential check) now check ownership when they run, so a failed or locked migration never exposes the connector early.
- The migration sequence, markers, locks, delivery claims and scheduling deduplication are unchanged. There are no schema, option-name or translation-policy changes.

## Notes

- The new opt-in mu-plugin `e2e/mu-plugins/fair-e2e-notification-startup.php` loads before all plugins. It stands in for Hostinger's option observer (notices on option writes before `init`:1) and for translated `cron_schedules` labels (notices before `init`:10). It flags notices raised while Fair Events notification code is on the call stack. These stand-ins are the documented equivalent fixtures; the real third-party plugins are not installed.
- With main's bootstrap, these stand-ins raise both notices from notification code on a WP-CLI startup. With this branch, they raise none.
- **Follow-up (out of scope):** `fair-audience/src/Hooks/PaymentHooks.php:52-55` calls `wp_schedule_event()` at plugin load with its custom interval registered afterwards. The event never gets scheduled, so every request builds `cron_schedules` early. This still triggers the stand-in translation notice, but not from notification code.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run test:php -- --filter Notifications`: 213 tests pass, including a new connector ownership-gate test
- [x] `e2e/notification-startup.spec.js` (new): 5/5 pass. It covers fresh install (WP-CLI), pending upgrade (page request plus both REST controllers), interrupted import, WP-Cron (cleanup handler runs) and migration-lock contention. Each scenario checks that there are no notification-originated notices, markers complete once, no duplicate cron events or imported history, unchanged settings and claims, and no mail or Telegram sends.
- [x] `e2e/user-flows/weekly-telegram-notifications.spec.js` passes. The first two runs failed at login with the password typed into the username field; the next two runs passed.
- [x] `e2e/user-flows/individual-email-notifications.spec.js` (scheduled delivery) passes
- [x] `NotificationHistoryController.api.spec.js`: 14/14 pass
- [x] phpcs clean; `npm run format` in fair-events is clean; no JS/CSS changes, so no build

author: nicogarrr
body:
## Hallazgo
Revisión GerarAI (27-10-2026), hallazgo **B1**: las actions de GitHub se fijaban de forma mixta. Unas iban por SHA (`actions/checkout@3d3c42e… # v7`) y otras por tag mutable (`actions/checkout@v7`, `aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.36.0`, `docker/build-push-action@v7.4.0`…). Un tag se puede mover: si una action se compromete (como pasó con `tj-actions/changed-files` en 2025), el CI ejecuta código ajeno con el token del repo.

## Cambio
- 56 referencias en `ci.yml`, `qa-e2e.yml` y `sbom-scan.yml` pasan a SHA completo con el tag como comentario (`@<sha> # v7`), resuelto con `git ls-remote` contra cada repo de la action (tags anotados desreferenciados al commit). Mismas versiones que hoy: no cambia ninguna versión.
- Actions afectadas: `actions/cache@v6`, `actions/checkout@v7`, `actions/download-artifact@v8`, `actions/setup-node@v7`, `actions/setup-python@v7.1.0`, `actions/upload-artifact@v7`, `anchore/scan-action@v7.4.2`, `aquasecurity/trivy-action@v0.36.0`, `docker/build-push-action@v7.4.0`, `docker/setup-buildx-action@v4.4.1`.
- Guard nuevo `data-engine/tests/test_workflow_actions_pinned.py`: falla si alguna `uses:` de terceros no va por SHA de 40 caracteres (las locales `./` y `docker://` quedan fuera).
- Dependabot ya cubre `github-actions` y sabe actualizar SHA + comentario, así que no se pierde el mantenimiento.

## Pruebas
- Guard nuevo: verde con el cambio; **rojo en main** (verificado con `git stash`).
- Los 9 workflows se parsean como YAML válido.
- `ruff` y `pyright` sobre el test → 0 errores.

Nota: otra PR de Tab (gitleaks en CI) puede añadir una action nueva; si se mergea después, este guard pedirá fijarla por SHA también.

author: jhrozek
body:
## Summary

- **Why:** the configured delegate client fields from the previous PR were validated but never reached the running server, so a pre-provisioned broker could not use `private_key_jwt` or log users in. Once a configured client can hold grants other than token exchange, two checks that assumed delegates were back-channel-only have to change.
- **What:**
  - The runner reads each `jwks_file` next to the client secret handling and passes keys, auth method, grant types and redirect URIs to the client constructor.
  - Discovery advertises `private_key_jwt` when a configured client uses it, and the `client_secret_*` methods only when a client or DCR actually uses a secret.
  - `/authorize` treats every client without `authorization_code` as back-channel only and answers `invalid_client`, as for an unknown client, so a client's existence cannot be probed.
  - Delegate clients are registered before the consent-exempt IDs are checked, so a configured login client can be listed there.
  - `/authorize` checks the requested resource against the client's own audiences (its resource allowlist for SPIFFE clients), and ID-JAG redemption does the same, both with `invalid_target`. The check uses fosite's audience matching strategy, the rule the authorization code callback and the refresh grant already apply, so a request it accepts cannot fail the callback later. It applies to every client, DCR and CIMD included.
  - A client that sets `grant_types` explicitly must list `jwt-bearer` to redeem an ID-JAG, or it gets `unauthorized_client`. A client that omits `grant_types` keeps redeeming ID-JAGs for backward compatibility.
  - The removal test harness gets a configured login client, so removing one is covered.
  - The delegate client integration tests share one embedded auth server helper.

Stacked on #6952. Review only the last four commits.

Refs #6893

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests (`task test`) — run on the packages this PR touches, not the whole repository (see below)
- [x] Linting (`task lint-fix`) — `golangci-lint` on the same packages, no findings

Tests, lint and vet were run on the touched packages at this tip, and `task docs-verify` reports no drift. The integration tests in `pkg/authserver` cover a configured client logging in, `private_key_jwt` authentication through the runner, the audience checks, and the removal harness for a configured login client. E2E tests were not run.

## Does this introduce a user-facing change?

Yes.

- **Before:** configured delegate client fields were ignored at runtime. `/authorize` did not enforce a client's declared audiences.
- **After:**
  - `/authorize` enforces a client's declared audiences with the same path-prefix rule as the callback. A client with no audiences, which could never complete the callback, now gets `invalid_target` at `/authorize` instead of failing after the upstream login.
  - ID-JAG redemption checks the `resource` against the client's audiences too. A client that keeps no resource allowlist and has no audiences is not narrowed there, as before, so embedder clients registered without audiences keep working. This exception fails open and exists only for backward compatibility. Clients with a resource allowlist, such as SPIFFE clients, are always checked.
  - Delegate clients that omit `grant_types` keep today's ID-JAG behaviour, but their ID-JAG `resource` must now be in their audiences.
  - A client without `authorization_code` gets `invalid_client` from `/authorize`.
  - Discovery no longer advertises `client_secret_*` methods unless a client or DCR uses a secret.

## Special notes for reviewers

- The client audience check matches like fosite does: scheme and host exactly, and a path that equals the client's audience path or extends it at a segment boundary. The server-level check that runs before it still requires an exact match, and the RFC 8693 `resource` check uses the same strategy as this check.
- The plain JWT-bearer grant is not gated by the new `jwt-bearer` rule, because it can run without client authentication.
- Commit by commit: the helper move first (no behaviour change), then the runner wiring, then audience binding, then the test coverage.

body:
## Scope: fix unintended over-strictness after #183, independently classify exact runway delay

Owner reiterated **scientifically justified tolerances**, fast work before Wednesday, and exact f.8 runway label. This is **OFFLINE source/test only** after successful paid WSSS Gate05c (already two GETs, four units, 33+33 rows, scheduled/revised 33/33, runway 0/33 per variant), not another provider trial.

### Concrete post-#183 flaw
Previous `materializePreSnapshotsForCutoff` used a single batch-wallclock `cutoffUtc` for all flights and exact `T-cutoff=h`. Almost all independently scheduled flights at different minutes would be blocked even when their population was legitimately observed before their own (T_i-h). It also required `flight_population.cutoff_utc <= C`, although that census column is the query/service-window cutoff, **not** an evidence receipt clock. This confuses scheduler timing with scientific as-of timing and is more restrictive than the plan.

### Changes
- Move materializer to `PRE_SNAPSHOT_BUILDER_VERSION=1.3.0`: interpret passed `cutoffUtc` as a **processing-as-of watermark** only, use first durably observed provider-native schedule per analytic identity (unchanged by later schedule revisions), derive each flight's own nominal (C_{i,h}=T_i-h) in SQL for T−24h/T−6h/T−90m, and use a latest-available-before-C LATERAL population observation per flight+horizon. Query rows missing earlier population explicitly produce `population_unobserved_at_cutoff` counter, not a fake snapshot. The restricted `verifiedProviderNativeSchedule` and source semantics evidence config in #183 still gates using actual observed T; caller-side source evidence is NOT independently certified by this local code.
- Drop the incorrect extra `flight_population.cutoff_utc <= C` filter; enforce **`available_at<=C`** for every included row and **`available_at<=processing watermark`** for all retrieved source.
- Add pure `gate05RunwayDelayLabelAudit_v39.ts`: exact runway target `(verified actual wheels-off - independently verified scheduled wheels-off)/60,000` minutes, supports negative early-delay outcomes, does NOT transform `runwayTime` estimated into actual or generic `scheduledTime` into scheduled wheels-off, uses `PENDING` before frozen target grace and `MISSING` after. Other independent targets and snapshot eligibility remain unaffected. No provider I/O.
- Test heterogeneous per-flight cutoffs, late source exclusion, T−90m, SQL source path, no manufactured labels, negative delay, explicit missingness and identity ambiguity.

### Proportional rigor and unresolved scientific evidence
- Source semantics/identity, data availability, unauthorized cost/STOP and raw-before-2xx are P0 invariants; **partial callback observations, small measured gaps, and optional feature missingness are NOT binary study rejection**. Tier B observed-only and prospective MCAR/MNAR sensitivity remain available as documented Oct12–14; do not turn two billed units into two missing legs.
- FIDS Gate05c returned **zero runway UTC values** for that measured sample and no independent true scheduled wheels-off source; full original runway label, first as-of feed/schedule certification, live adequately sampled trajectory pilot, end-to-end provider SEND reconciliation **remain NOT PROVEN**.
- `analytic_identity_id` may still drift on a large retime; the query freezes T within an identity, not an unauthenticated physical-leg link. Do not claim that flaw resolved; keep retime-linkage review as the next separate source/identity gate. No change to a historical hash-frozen plan/log.
- Current [scientific tolerance + 2-target checkpoint](https://github.com/HKcode22/ReplitTranvr/blob/docs/gate05-science-tolerance-yssy-current-evidence-20261027/data-collection/phase3/2026-10-26_PRE_SCALE_GATE05_YSSY_48H_SPRINT.md) and issues #173/#38.

Adds Sparkle 2.10.0 to the Mac host with signed HTTPS appcasts/archive verification, Check for Updates and automatic-check controls. A paired iPhone can explicitly request download/install/relaunch and monitor progress using the frozen `pocketdesk-maintenance/1` ALPN, independently of the exact streaming protocol. Stream protocol is now 25.

Maintenance requires existing trust, respects Face ID and the Mac's connection-approval policy, and cannot start capture/input/file access. Update URLs come only from the bundled signed feed. The updater serializes work and cleans up host sessions/workspaces before relaunch; reconnects do not replay ambiguous install requests. Older pre-Sparkle hosts require one manual bootstrap update.

Validation: signed Mac/iPhone builds; 79 Swift regression tests plus one additional real-QUIC phone-client test; six publication-tool tests; website tests/build; Mac deep signature verification; signed bootstrap feed verification and tampered-feed rejection. Build 87 is installed on the paired iPhone 14 Pro and matching Mac; user confirmed the maintenance screen reports Mac 1.1 (87).

Release tooling emits a notarized updater ZIP and signs/version-checks appcast entries while retaining previous builds. Private signing material stays in Keychain. Initial feed is signed and empty; publishing the next notarized release and verifying a real Sparkle replacement/relaunch remain release acceptance steps. See docs/evidence/host-updates.md and docs/RELEASING.md.

author: jackspiering
body:
Design question DQ11, plan v3.13 item 17.

Docker's `on-failure` policy restarts only on a non-zero exit while retries remain (moby `restartmanager`: `exitCode != 0` and `MaximumRetryCount == 0 || restartCount < MaximumRetryCount`; the manager is seeded from the container's `RestartCount` at boot restore — read from moby master). A container stopped by the host under `on-failure` that exited 0, or whose `on-failure:N` retries are spent, is now `exited-host-stopped` like `restart: "no"`: one `NotifyOnly` ("left down by policy"), its `network_mode` dependents stay down with it (the existing `adjust` path), only `heal-exited=always` starts it. A non-zero exit with retries left, `always` and `unless-stopped` are unchanged.

Verification: `TestHostStoppedOnFailureContainerDockerWillNotRestore` (boundaries RC = max−1, RC = max, max = 0, heal-exited modes) fails before the change; `TestAnOnFailureParentDockerWillNotRestoreStaysDownWithItsDependents` (daemon: nothing started, one NotifyOnly naming the sidecar; none when Docker restores). Fresh review: no defects. Docs (running.md, troubleshooting.md), CHANGELOG and CLAUDE.md updated.

Stack s10-rules, 7 of 7.

author: nicogarrr
body:
## Bug
Cuando el motor (FastAPI) rechaza una petición con un **422 de validación**, la UI mostraba literalmente **«[object Object]»**. Ejemplo reproducido como usuario real en `/screeners`: ejecutar un filtro ad-hoc con una métrica muy larga (`/screeners?left=<5000 caracteres>&operator=%3E&right=1`) pinta el banner «No se pudo ejecutar el screener. [object Object]». Afecta a todas las acciones de `lib/actions/research-tools.actions.ts` (screeners, filtros guardados, métricas personalizadas, supuestos de drivers…) y a `researchRequest` de `lib/research/client.ts`.

## Causa
`apiError` (research-tools) y `responseError` (research client) hacían `payload.detail ?? payload.message`. En los 422 FastAPI devuelve `detail` como **lista de objetos** `{loc, msg, type}`; esa lista acababa como `message` del `AppError` y se convertía a texto como «[object Object]».

## Fix
- Nuevo helper puro `lib/research/error-detail.ts` → `researchErrorDetail(payload, fallback)`:
  - `detail` texto → tal cual (sin cambios para los errores de negocio, p. ej. «Sintaxis de fórmula no válida»).
  - `detail` lista (422) → «Datos no válidos en: left, operator. Revisa esos campos y vuelve a intentarlo.» (campos deduplicados a partir de `loc`), o un aviso genérico en español si no hay `loc`.
  - `detail` objeto con `message`/`detail` anidado → ese texto; si no, `message` o el status HTTP.
  - Nunca devuelve un no-texto.
- `apiError` y `responseError` usan el helper.
- `scripts/research-client-contract.loader.mjs` mapea el nuevo alias para que los guards con loader sigan resolviendo `client.ts`.

## Test
`scripts/research-error-detail.test.ts` (node --test, entra en `run-guards`):
- casos del helper (lista 422, lista sin `loc`, texto, objeto anidado, fallbacks);
- **contrato de cableado**: `researchRequest` con un `fetch` stub que responde 422 con lista → el error lanzado es texto, no contiene «[object Object]» y dice «Datos no válidos en: left».
- Con el cableado antiguo de `client.ts` el test falla (`The input was expected to not match /\[object Object\]/`); con el fix pasa (6/6).

## Gates ejecutados
- `node scripts/run-guards.mjs` → 2268/2269; el único fallo (`E6/H6 .gitignore…`) es de entorno (git no puede evaluar `node_modules` enlazado por symlink en el worktree de QA) y falla igual sin este cambio.
- `npx eslint` sobre los ficheros tocados → 0 errores.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → 0 errores.

PR abierta por Tab (asistente de Nico) en nombre de Nico, como parte del QA de la zona «Descubrir».

author: cipher813
body:
## What

This PR promotes the D20 EOD spine-window guard (`data_spine_window`) from OBSERVE to ENFORCE, on its codified per-guard criterion.

- `validators/expectations.py::SPINE_WINDOW_GUARD` is now `GuardMode.ENFORCE`.
- `data_gate/guard_promotion.py` sets the entry's `mode` to `"enforce"`, in lockstep. Its `blast_radius` now describes the new raise site.
- `collectors/metron_market_data.py::collect` handles a window verdict other than `ok`, `unmeasurable` included. On a successful write it returns `status: degraded`, with a `detail` that names the window finding.
- `weekly_collector.py::_DEGRADED_DEFECT_REGISTRY` gains a `metron_market_data` entry, so a degraded D20 page names `alpha-engine-config-I10780` and the clearing condition instead of `UNTRACKED`.
- `registry.d/units/D20-metron-eod-closes-fx.yaml`: one note no longer says "also OBSERVE".
- `.debug-swallow-allowlist.yaml`: three `weekly_collector.py` line numbers move +13, following the file's usual shift-note convention. No swallow site changed.

## Why

Tracker: alpha-engine-config-I10780, phase 2 ("promotes to enforcing"). The data gate row `data.guard_promotion.data_spine_window` read **READY TO PROMOTE: the codified criterion holds** on every `data-phase2` gate read from 2026-10-20 through 2026-10-26 (code SHAs `1df8b32`..`8582f45`). It is the one phase-2 clause that can move without an operator (alpha-engine-config-I10870 re-exam).

Verified read-only:
- Every scheduled D20 run manifest from 2026-10-07 through 2026-10-26 (14 sessions) recorded `data_spine_window` verdict `ok`.
- Each of those runs had all 5 window sessions published, non-empty and dated to their session, and full coverage on the symbol axis.

The criterion is Brian's 2026-10-04 option (c) on alpha-engine-config-I11973: per-guard and risk-based, with at least one scheduled observe execution, and promotion by a deliberate PR. This is that PR.

## What ENFORCE does, and what it does not do

On a window verdict other than `ok`, **D20's own run is degraded. The process is not failed.**

**What changes on a breach:**
- `_phase_collect` raises `_DegradedRun`, so D20's run manifest records `failed`, with the window finding as its reason.
- The phase marker is not `ok`, so a retry recomputes D20.
- The page is a DEGRADED page naming I10780.

**What does not change:**
- The EOD aggregate reads `degraded`, so the process still exits 0. The Step Function still runs the ArcticDB append and EODReconcile.
- The day's closes are still published.

This matches the codified blast radius ("the EOD spine's (D20) own run", moderate risk). Returning `error` instead would have halted the whole EOD Step Function. That is a wider blast radius than the one the criterion was graded against, so it is not done here. `tests/test_d20_cardinality_wiring.py::test_an_enforcing_spine_window_degrades_d20_and_never_the_process` asserts this through the real `_phase_collect` and `_aggregate_daily_status`.

The write-failure path already returns `error` and is unchanged.

**For review: two things become load-bearing with this promotion.**
1. **The window grades the session's symbol axis too.** An undeclared missing symbol on D20 now degrades D20's run through `data_spine_window`. `data_cardinality` itself stays OBSERVE and unchanged. That symbol axis read 57/57 on all 14 sessions above.
2. **The thresholds are now enforced.** `D20_SPINE_WINDOW_SESSIONS = 5` and `D20_MAX_BAR_LAG_SESSIONS = 1` were proposed on #2068, which said it would stay draft until Brian ruled on them. Brian marked #2068 ready and merged it on 2026-10-07. Their code comments still read "PROPOSED, not ratified", so this PR leaves both comments and values untouched. Changing a value is a separate threshold decision.

## Red line?

No. This tightens a guard: observe becomes a degraded run on breach. It does not touch IAM, trading risk or sizing, data deletion or spend.

## Deploy and weekly paths

- `Deploy-mechanism:` the EOD collector runs `main` on its next scheduled data-spot run, so the first enforcing run is the next EOD after merge. `data-gate.yml` (push on `data_gate/**`) re-reads the gate, and the row should then read PROMOTED. `deploy-data-spot-dispatcher.yml` and `deploy-collection-readiness-probe.yml` fire on the `registry.d/units/**` note edit. Each repackages its Lambda, and neither Lambda's code changes.
- `Deploys-after:` N/A
- **Weekly SF:** no Step Function definition changes. `weekly_collector.py` and `validators/expectations.py` are weekly-run files. The only behaviour change is in `metron_market_data.collect`, which runs only in daily (EOD) mode.

## Tests

- Run locally: the full `pytest tests/` suite, `validators/ssm_log_capture_contract.py` and `validators/sf_entrypoint_lint.py` (0 new findings). The hard-coded env refs check shows no new finding in any touched file.
- New tests:
  - a stale bar degrades the run;
  - a missing earlier session degrades the run and names the session, and the closes are still written;
  - rolling the staging back to OBSERVE leaves the run `ok`;
  - the end-to-end `_phase_collect` degraded path;
  - the degraded page names I10780.

Tracker: alpha-engine-config-I10780

author: theomeunier
body:
## Summary

Shows the version of the running API in the sidebar footer, next to the Documentation link, so the first question in a bug report ("which version are you on?") has an obvious answer.

The version comes from the API rather than from the front build. That way the sidebar shows what really runs on the server, even when the front and the API run from separate images.

## Changes

### API
- New `GET /api/version` endpoint, which returns `{"version": "1.5.0"}`.
  - Only signed-in users can call it: a public version number would help someone look for a known flaw.
  - The images get the version from the git tag (`v1.5.0`), so the endpoint removes the leading `v`. An empty value becomes `dev`.
- `ShowVersionResourceTest`: a signed-in user gets the version (200), a signed-out request gets 401, and the `v` is removed.

### Front
- `SidebarVersion`: a small rounded badge on the right of the Documentation row.
  - It links to the GitHub release notes (`/releases/tag/vX.Y.Z`), or to the list of releases for a `dev` build.
  - It is fetched once per session and stays hidden if the request fails.
  - It is hidden when the sidebar is collapsed to icons.
- New `release_notes` label in fr, en, de and es.

### Images
- `build-push-docker` now passes `APP_VERSION` to the build: the tag name on a tag, `dev` otherwise.
- `backend/api/src/main/docker/Dockerfile.native` now sets `UPTIME_VERSION` from it, as the all-in-one and worker images already do.
- Before this change, the standalone `api` image published by `backend-docker-build.yml` always reported `dev`, both in the sidebar and in `uptime_build_info`.

author: kimptoc
body:
## Why
With NordVPN on, every announcement used on-device TTS, and Gemini was never called. Before a cloud announcement, `NetworkQualityChecker` times a HEAD request to google.com, and anything over 200ms counted as a poor network. Through the VPN that request took 530-884ms, so the app skipped every cloud voice. The wifi itself was fine.

200ms is too strict: the request can include a new HTTPS handshake, and any VPN or ordinary mobile connection goes over it. Cloud announcements take about 3s to make anyway, and outros are made 30s ahead of time.

## Change
- `GOOD_LATENCY_THRESHOLD_MS` goes from 200ms to 2s. A ping that fails, or a network that isn't validated, still counts as poor.

## Tests
- `NetworkQualityCheckerTest`: 900ms (VPN-like) now counts as good, and 2.5s still counts as poor.
- Full `./gradlew assembleDebug test`: 516 tests, 0 failures.
- On the phone with NordVPN on, the ping took 753ms and then 626ms. Both outros were made with the Gemini API voice, line by Gemini.

body:
﻿## Summary

- Package the existing synthetic workbench as unsigned Windows, macOS, and Linux Electron installers, with a hardened renderer and packaged-app smoke checks.
- Add a Linux Electron container with Xvfb, password-protected VNC, and noVNC, plus local run instructions and multi-architecture build support.
- Keep the synthetic provenance visible and retain the current plots and calculations.

## Validation

- Frontend lint, type checking, unit tests, production build, desktop static-server tests, and Python checks passed.
- The Windows packaged app smoke test loaded all four plots and reported 277 paired valid pixels.
- The amd64 container smoke check confirmed password enforcement, the packaged synthetic preview and plots, and HTTP 200 from noVNC on a loopback-bound port.
- The six-project browser suite passed 178 cases before hitting its 15-minute suite timeout; 26 narrow WebKit cases did not run. No completed assertion failed.
- The arm64 image build is being checked locally; CI will also package and launch the native app on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Container note

Docker's default seccomp profile blocks the Linux namespace operation Chromium needs in this setup. The documented run command relaxes that host filter so Chromium can start its renderer sandbox. The app remains non-root, and the Electron renderer keeps sandboxing, context isolation, and disabled Node integration.

This preview contains synthetic data only and makes no claims about observed Louisiana flooding or flooded area.

author: greatv
body:
Adds native execution of TierFlow/LoopVL's recurrent language model, text input only. Weights are loaded in their published BF16 form, with nothing converted or written. The model has:
- 32 physical layer weight sets (an L stack and an H stack of 16 layers each), run in the order (L, L, L, H) × 2, which makes 128 layer applications per token;
- 128 application-indexed KV slots, one per layer application;
- weightless layer and stack-final RMSNorms (a typed weightless variant chosen from the spec at setup);
- a sigmoid-gated attention output;
- YaRN RoPE with the model definition's BF16-quantized `inv_freq`;
- scaled token embeddings and a learned initial L state.

Text prefill and cached decode run in eager and CUDA-graph modes. The full 580-tensor manifest is validated; the 259 text tensors are loaded, and media input is rejected until the vision path lands.

## How the text prefix is attended
The model uses a prefix-LM mask: prefix rows attend to the whole prefix, and response rows are causal. For each layer application, the K/V of the whole prefix are written first. Rows are then queried through the existing owned decode-attention kernels: prefix rows with length P, response row r with length r+1.

This row-wise path is a correctness stopgap. It costs 256·P attention launches per prefill and is capped at `ROWWISE_PREFIX_LIMIT = 64` rows; a 65-row prefill errors before mutating any state. It will be **replaced, not kept alongside**, when the native Rust flash-attention prefix-LM mode lands. No FA2 code is changed or called for this model.

Decode-attention eligibility is now derived from head_dim 128 and the GQA ratio instead of fixed 16/2 and 32/4 head counts. KV capacity is admitted from device memory with a named `KV_CAPACITY_LIMIT`.

## Correctness
Reference: the publisher's model definition (Tier-Flow/LoopVL @ 6c14bed1 with transformers' `hrm_text` 5.15.1), clean load of 580 tensors, full recompute per step.
- `loopvl_text_gpu`:
  - 3 fixtures (21-, 42- and 64-row prefill), 32 teacher-forced steps each, eager and graph.
  - Logit error over each 32-step trajectory, max / p99 / RMS, worst case 0.305 / 0.109 / 0.039; frozen limits 0.60 / 0.20 / 0.06, set from measured reference noise.
  - Prefill and all 8 stack taps within their frozen limits.
  - Graph and eager are bit-identical. All 168 argmax comparisons with margin ≥ 0.35 agree.
  - Controls detected: prefix bidirectionality and response causality, omitted final norm, bypassed output gate, KV slots aliased by weight index instead of application.
- `recurrent_decode_shapes_gpu`: decode attention exact at 12:12, 16:2 and 32:4.
- Manifest gate: 580 tensors, 0 missing / unexpected.
- Existing models unchanged against main, each side built from its own commit with pinned calibration:
  - MiniCPM-V-4.7 BF16 graph decode: 256/256 ids, logit and state dumps byte-identical;
  - Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 `q38_engine_capture_gpu` passes;
  - Flint engine controls pass (graph NLL = eager NLL).
- Five checks: CUDA 365 passed / 164 ignored, no-CUDA 259 passed / 33 ignored.

GPU gates ran on sm_86. No timing; timing is paused pending a unified regression.

## Counted cost
- Weights: 61,341,696 B per layer; 8.05 GB of weight operands per decode token (128 applications plus lm_head).
- KV: 786,432 B per token, so 6 GiB at 8192 tokens.
- Launches: 1,421 kernels per eager decode token, confirmed by nsys, including 264 fused residual+norm kernels in place of 528 separate add and norm launches.

## Purpose
Add an isolated Go 1.27 Linux research journal to persist an **already dual-signature-verified** Nexus permit for crash-safe retries, without trusting on-disk content for authentication. Fsync file + atomic rename + fsync directory; exact envelope bytes and digest; private directory and flock; fail closed on corrupt/conflicting records and changed owner-approved request.

## Tests
Go race tests: idempotent retries, parallel requests, post-crash reload (with re-verification), expiry, tampered/corrupt journal, insecure directories/symlink rejection.

## Hard safety limits
No vault or epoch activation; no durable protected anti-rollback floor, no ACK generation, no signed receipt, no KMS key provisioning or Nexus DB transaction. A filesystem journal alone is NOT a rollback-resistant security boundary. This is staging PoC only, NOT imported by production node, `strict-pq` OFF. Pending CI and security review.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Report prior and posterior sampling progress through an optional callback.

Fitting a model can take hours, yet `sample_posterior` gives no sign of life
until a whole chain batch has been sampled, because NUTS runs as one compiled
XLA computation. Neither notebook users nor services that show a live training
status can tell how far along a fit is or when it will finish.

`Meridian.sample_prior`, `sample_posterior` and `Meridian.sample_posterior_and_review`
accept a keyword-only `progress_callback`. It receives `PriorSamplingProgress`
snapshots as each prior sampling stage completes, and
`PosteriorSamplingProgress` snapshots when a chain batch starts and finishes,
after each posterior reconstruction batch and, on the JAX backend, after every
MCMC draw, adaptation included, together with the running count of divergent
transitions among the kept draws. Snapshots are frozen dataclasses in the new
`meridian.model.progress` module. A failing callback is reported as a warning
and never interrupts sampling.

author: albabit
body:
## Problem

With ComfyUI frontend 1.57 (bundled with ComfyUI 0.43.0), typing a number in a widget of a node can fail: the field goes back to the old value a moment later, and only the "-" / "+" buttons work. Seen on the "Write" node's "version" field.

It happens when one of the node's widgets is linked, for example the Write's "fps" fed by "Resolution". Frontend 1.57 keeps a linked widget hidden whatever is written to `widget.hidden`. The Write's 250 ms poll asked to show "fps" again on every pass, `setWidgetVisible` read the frontend's "hidden" as a hidden-to-visible change each time and reinserted the widget, so Nodes 2.0 redrew the node and dropped the number being typed.

## Change

`js/radiance_widget_utils.js`: `setWidgetVisible` returns `false` without touching a widget whose input is linked, and leaves it to the frontend. A widget the helper hid itself (type "hidden") before it was linked can still be shown again. Every node that shows and hides widgets on a poll goes through this helper ("Write", "Sampler", "Loader", "Prompt", "Resolution", upscale, VAE widgets), so all of them get it. The "Prompt" already left its linked "text_to_video" alone on the caller side.

A linked widget keeps its row as before: in Nodes 2.0 the visible rows are the same with and without this change.

## Tests

- Browser, Nodes 2.0, frontend 1.57.4, a workflow with the Write's "fps" linked to "Resolution": typing "1" in "version", then Enter.
  - Before: the field goes back to 5 within 300 ms, the value stays 5.
  - After: "1" stays and is saved.
  - Switching the format to an EXR sequence still hides "quality" and shows "exr_compression" and "start_frame". The visible rows are the same before and after.
- Checked by hand in the ComfyUI UI.
- `js/tests/widget_utils.test.mjs`: two new cases, a linked widget the frontend keeps hidden is left alone, and a widget hidden by the helper then linked can still be shown (this one fails on the first version of the guard).
- `node --test js/tests/*.test.mjs`: 633 pass, 0 fail.
- `pytest`: 5683 pass. The 5 failures are the known Windows-only ones (import blocker, write streaming memory), not touched here.

author: charlietolleson
body:
## Problem
`merge_chunked` calls `merge_checked(current, ...)`, and the shrink guard's floor is computed from `current`, the previous chunk's output. The floor therefore compounds across chunks. On an 80-claim wiki under the cap, a 4-chunk run (60 items) has per-chunk floors of 60, 46, 35 and 27, so a model that cuts about 24% per chunk ends the run at about 27 of 80 claims with every chunk accepted. That is the 2026-10-02 failure (47 to 21 claims) the guard was added for, and chunking (2026-10-22) reopened it.

## Evidence
`ingest/ai_research.py` `merge_chunked`: the only floor applied is inside `merge_checked`, against the chunk's input. The new test feeds 4 chunks to a fake merge that keeps 80% each time; on main all 4 are accepted and the run ends far below `claim_floor(start)`.

## Fix
`merge_chunked` computes `claim_floor(index_md)` once for the run and skips any chunk whose result falls under it, logged and counted like any other rejected chunk (its items stay archived and unreviewed). `merge_checked` and its retry are unchanged.

## Risk
Low. A run can now reject a chunk that its own guard would have passed, but only when the run as a whole would keep under 75% of the starting claims (scaled by cap/words, as before). Prune is separate and keeps its own floor.

## Testing
- `python -m pytest -q tests` in a cloud venv: 57 passed. The new test fails on main and passes here.
- `python -m py_compile ingest/ai_research.py`.
- No CI in this repo; no real ingest was run (it calls paid APIs).
