author: hugoxk
body:
fix(issue-ref): read a bare #1234 only when the number stands alone

Fixes #1391
Owner: Dev2
Reviewer: Reviewer
Written-by: Dev-2
Tip SHA: `0a0887327804685aae28a977fde7a26d0833f894`
Base: `10884b8b` (`main`, `#1385`)
Tree: `cfee808d8b6e9deeac63b16c54abb5b8ea92274c`

## What changed

`core/src/shared/issue-ref.js` guarded only the character *after* the digits (`#(\d{1,7})(?![0-9])`), so a `#` glued to anything counted as a reference: `#3366ff` → `#3366`, `C#7` → `#7`, `1.2#3` → `#3`, `abc#12` → `#12`, `#1360abc` → `#1360`, and a URL fragment `help/#123` → `#123`. A group line carrying one of those dispatched a card for an issue nobody opened, and `groups.js` empties `speakers` once a card is written, so the line got no answer.

The matcher now keeps three separate shapes.

- A **bare** `#N` counts only with a separator in front — `(?<![\w./-])`, so a word character, `.`, `-` or `/` glues it to something else — and a non-word character behind (`(?![\w])`, which also refuses `#1360abc`).
- **`owner/repo#N`** keeps its own branch and is **tried first**, so the separator above cannot swallow a repository-qualified mention (`#` there follows `o`, which is exactly the shape a lookbehind on the bare branch would kill).
- **`github.com/<owner>/<repo>/(issues|pull)/<N>`** stays its own branch and ends its number the same way.

`MENTION` (`cardMentions`, and `withoutMentions` in `work-dispatch.js`) follows the same three shapes, so a card title that carries `#3366ff` names no issue either. `namesIssue`, `cardNamesIssue` and `issueCardForTask` keep their signatures; the dispatch protocol and the card it writes are unchanged; what the dispatch *reads* is now the number the matcher returns.

The three shapes that must keep resolving are pinned in the new test and are green in both halves: bare `#1360`, `owner/repo#1360` (repository-qualified, tried before the bare branch), and `https://github.com/o/r/issues/1360`.

`core/src/host/work-dispatch.js` took the id from the raw match (`'#' + (match[1] ?? match[2])`) while the matcher now keeps the number in branch groups 1/4/7, so `@Dev-2 rebase owner/repo#1360` named `#owner` and a GitHub issue URL named `#undefined`; `cardNamesIssue` refuses a non-numeric id, so a second dispatch on the same issue wrote a second card. Both `issueRefs` and `workDispatch` now call one `refOf(match)` helper, and the test pins `#1360` for both shapes plus **one** card for two dispatches.

**Deliberate behaviour change — a URL fragment stops parsing, and so does the tail of a `#55/#198` shorthand.** `…/help/#123` used to be read as `#123` and is now not a reference at all, because `#` follows `/` there and `/` is one of the gluing characters. The same boundary ends the copy-editing shorthand the repo itself writes: in `#55/#198` only `#55` is read now (it named both before), because that `#` also follows `/`; the spaced form is untouched — `'#876 / #892'` → `["#876","#892"]` — and so is `'#55, #198'` → `["#55","#198"]`, so write `#55, #198` where two ids must both be read from a card title or a dispatch line. Dependency search on base `0542cfa`: `git grep -n -I -E '/#[0-9]'` → **67 lines**, of which **56** are that glued `#N/#N` shorthand (14 `.github/**`, 14 `docs/**`, 12 `plugins/**`, 4 `core/src`, 3 `core/test`, 2 root `*.md`, plus 7 more in the generated `patches/` + `ds-bot/` mirrors) and **11** are JS regex literals inside assertions that each name one id (`/#812/`, `/#3B5BFD/`, `/#1281/`, …), all still parsed; no line in that output is a `…/#<n>` URL fragment reference. Two readers, not one: `.github/**` never imports `issue-ref.js` — `enqueue-rules.mjs` carries its own `const ISSUE_REF = /^[\s>#-]*(?:fixes|closes)…/im` (`:30`), and `merge-gate.mjs` / `enqueue-guard.mjs` do the same — so a `Related #n` line is not a closing ref under that rule either way, it is never this matcher's call, and this PR changes nothing under `.github/`. No test imports `core/src/shared/issue-ref.js`; the only consumer under test is `core/test/work-dispatch.test.js`, which imports `workDispatch` and asserts that a bare `#1234` still parses (65 lines there carry a `#[0-9]`, 43 of them `#1234`). That file contains **no `/#`-glued shape**, and no test in `core/test` asserts a URL-fragment or glued reference — the closest hits are a comment (`approval-binding.test.js:5`, `#49/#48`) and colour literals (`branding.test.js:40-41`, `/#3B5BFD/`). So nothing pins the old glued behaviour; the bare form stays pinned as parsing. The prose that does use the shorthand — `docs/subsystems/core-host.md:267` (`#55/#198`), `docs/autonomous-dev.md:255` (`#1094/#1095/#1108/#1115`), `docs/subsystems/core-client.md:145` (`#51/#149/#55/#57`), `CHANGELOG.md:389` (`#499/#504`), `AGENTS.md:192` (`#711/#713`) — is not read by the matcher, so it changes no behaviour. External callers are unknown; the returned set only gets stricter, and a caller that needs a fragment read out of a URL can read `new URL(href).hash` itself.

## Red first, same command in both halves

`cd core && TZ=UTC node --import ./test/harness-resolve.mjs --test test/issue-ref.test.js`

Half (a): this tree with the new test but the old `issue-ref.js` (base `0542cfa`):

```
not ok 1 - a hex colour is not an issue reference
  error: |-
    @Dev-2 set the accent colour to #3366ff
    + actual - expected
    + [ '#3366' ]
    - []
not ok 2 - a language version is not an issue reference          C#7       -> [ '#7' ]
not ok 3 - a version string is not an issue reference            1.2#3     -> [ '#3' ]
not ok 4 - an identifier is not an issue reference               abc#12    -> [ '#12' ]
not ok 5 - a number running into letters is not an issue ref     #1360abc  -> [ '#1360' ]
not ok 6 - a URL fragment is not an issue reference              help/#123 -> [ '#123' ]
not ok 14 - namesIssue answers the same question, so a colour cannot name an issue
not ok 15 - a card whose title only carries a colour names no issue
# tests 15
# pass 7
# fail 8
```

Half (b): the same command on this tip — the same 8 green, plus the 7 that must keep working:

```
ok 7 - a bare number still names the issue: #1360
ok 8 - a repository-qualified number still names the issue: owner/repo#1360
ok 9 - a github issue URL still names the issue: https://github.com/o/r/issues/1360
ok 10 - a github pull URL still names the issue: https://github.com/o/r/pull/1360
ok 11 - a number after a Bot mention still names the issue: @Dev-2 rebase #1360
ok 12 - a number in a sentence still names the issue: please rebase #1360 onto main
ok 13 - numbers in brackets and punctuation still names the issue: (#1360), #1361.
# tests 15
# pass 15
# fail 0
```

### The dispatch consumer, same command, two states

`cd core && TZ=UTC node --import ./test/harness-resolve.mjs --test test/work-dispatch.test.js`

At this tip (`0a088732`): **19/19 green**. With `core/src/shared/issue-ref.js` and `core/src/host/work-dispatch.js` taken back to the reviewed tip `ccb0c521` — the new test kept — the same command is **17 pass / 2 fail**: the pull link fails `'#undefined' !== '#1234'`, the repository-qualified mention on the next line reads `#owner` (its own assertion, `'#owner' !== '#1234'`, is reached once the pull link passes), and the two-dispatch case fails `2 !== 1`.

```
not ok 1 - the dispatch shape is an issue id and an imperative, never any @ (#1254)
  error: |-
    a pull link names its number, not undefined
    + '#undefined'
    - '#1234'
not ok 4 - two dispatches on one issue through a qualified or URL id write one card (#1254, #1331)
  error: |-
    the same issue through a URL id reuses that card, so the id is the number
    2 !== 1
# tests 19
# pass 17
# fail 2
```

## Knife

Removing only the bare branch's left separator (keeping the right-hand rule) on this same tree: **5 red / 10 green** — `C#7`, `1.2#3`, `abc#12`, `help/#123` and the `namesIssue` case go red, while `#3366ff` and `#1360abc` stay green. Each half of the rule carries a different class of false positive,

author: novoj
body:
Consolidates the open Dependabot bump PRs. There are no open Dependabot security alerts, so there is no `fix(security)` commit this time. Unlike earlier consolidations, this one carries production code: byte-buddy 1.18 needs a one-line change in `AbstractInterruptionTransformer`, which ends its five-consolidation hold. A third commit fixes a flaky test that the verification run surfaced.

## Landed (6)

### `chore: bump Maven and GitHub Actions dependencies`

**Maven**
- `jackson.version` 2.22.3 -> 2.22.4 (#1813)
- `prometheus.version` 1.8.0 -> 1.10.0 (#1814)
- `org.codehaus.mojo:versions-maven-plugin` 2.21.0 -> 2.23.0 (#1811)

**GitHub Actions**
- `docker/login-action` 4.6.0 -> 4.7.0 (#1815)
- `anthropics/claude-code-action` 1.0.252 -> 1.0.261 (#1816)

The diff is the exact sum of the five PRs. All 19 action pins in `.github/workflows` verify against their release tags.

- **jackson 2.22.4** fixes CVE-2026-110879: `PolymorphicTypeValidator` now also checks type parameters and array element types of polymorphic type ids. Our only polymorphic type, `CaptureSiteDto`, uses `Id.NAME` with explicit `@JsonSubTypes`, which never consults the validator.
- **prometheus 1.10.0.** `micrometer-registry-prometheus` 1.17.1 asks for `prometheus-metrics-exposition-formats` and `-tracer-common` at 1.7.0. It wins the nearest-wins tie in `evita_server`, so the server ships those two at 1.7.0 next to 1.10.0. **dev already does the same next to 1.8.0** (`dependency:tree` on both). The 1.7.0 protobuf writer implements the 1.10.0 `ExpositionFormatWriter` interface. A probe on the `evita-server.jar` classpath scraped a counter, gauge, histogram, summary and the JVM metrics in protobuf, Prometheus text and OpenMetrics without error.
- **versions-maven-plugin 2.23.0** changes `versions:set` only for `-pl` selections, and `ci-release.yml` runs it without `-pl`. Run with 2.21.0 and with 2.23.0 against two copies of the tree, it rewrote the same 33 poms identically.

### `chore: bump byte-buddy 1.17.8 -> 1.18.16` (#1812)

Byte Buddy 1.18 hands `module-info` to build plugins as a type of its own. `AbstractInterruptionTransformer#matches` accepted every type, so the `evita_engine` transform failed with `Illegal modifiers 32768 for class module-info` (`ACC_MODULE`). That error held 1.18.x back since #1623. The transformer now declines the module descriptor via `TypeDescription#isModuleType()`, which is absent from 1.17.8 and so lands together with the bump.

A module descriptor declares no methods, so nothing goes unwoven:
- `InterruptionAdviceWovenTest` still finds the poll in all three woven modules.
- Each jar still describes its module.
- In `evita-server.jar` the 1.18.16 classes win over the `byte-buddy-dep` 1.13.0 that `proxycian_bytebuddy` brings, as the 1.17.8 ones did.

### `test: close the subscribe-vs-trigger race in the system capture tests`

The full functional run had one error, `SystemGraphQLSubscriptionsFunctionalTest.shouldReceiveSystemCaptureWithoutBody`, which received only `connection_ack`. It and its Untyped twin subscribe without `sinceVersion`, and `ChangeSystemCapturePublisher#subscribe` then starts the stream after the version current *at registration*. The ack doesn't prove the `subscribe` message was registered, so the single catalog they create can commit first and is never delivered. That is the same race `64d006eab1` closed for the host-event tests. Both tests now create a fresh catalog per attempt until one's envelopes arrive.

Proven by counterfactual: with `subscribe` delayed by 3 s, the old tests fail exactly as in the full run, while the `sinceVersion` controls pass. The fixed tests pass under the same delay.

## Held back (1)

- **`com.graphql-java:graphql-java` 26.1 (#1481): ninth consecutive hold.** #1422 is still open and untouched since 2026-08-15.

## Verification

- `mvn -T 1C -P full clean install -DskipTests`: all 33 modules, including `evita_long_running_tests`, `evita_documentation_tests` and `evita_performance_tests`, build from clean.
- Full functional suite (`-P unitAndFunctional -am`, before the test fix): **29,923 tests, 0 failures, 1 error**. The error is the race above; the test passed 3/3 isolated reruns. After the fix, all 44 subscription tests pass.
- The surefire classpath holds byte-buddy and byte-buddy-agent 1.18.16, jackson-core and jackson-databind 2.22.4, and prometheus 1.10.0 (tracer-common 1.7.0).

Closes #1811
Closes #1812
Closes #1813
Closes #1814
Closes #1815
Closes #1816

body:
## Summary

Add **Actions > Renovate now > Run workflow**, which runs the real Renovate CLI and creates bot-authored update PRs for BentoPDF and cloudflared immediately. It uses the repository's built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not a PAT or custom App key. This supersedes the earlier manually authored image bumps in this PR; **both workload image pins are unchanged from main**.

- `workflow_dispatch` only, allowlisted to this repository and trusted `main`; no cron and no arbitrary inputs.
- Pinned native Renovate `44.186.6` on `ubuntu-slim`, 15-minute timeout, serialized manual runs.
- CLI force-overrides ignore schedule and PR-creation limits for this run, limit managers to the Kubernetes image manager, and **force automerge and Dependency Dashboard off**. The workflow creates PRs; it does not approve, merge, or deploy.
- `renovate-manual/` branches keep manual-run writes separate from the optional hosted App's `renovate/` branches. Review for duplicate proposals before merging either path.
- Job-scoped Contents/Pull requests write and Issues read. No checkout, custom secrets, Docker socket, scripts/plugins or post-upgrade commands.
- Keep the tunnel image line single-line for extraction with a scoped YAML length exception so a longer Renovate-generated tag does not fail lint.
- Document the exact UI/CLI invocation, bot-PR CI approval tradeoff, repository creation permission, hosted separation and downstream Argo acceptance.

## Required activation

1. Merge this source after review and green CI. GitHub exposes workflow_dispatch only after the workflow exists on the default branch.
2. Enable **Settings > Actions > General > Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests**. This combined GitHub setting is needed for PR creation; no self-approval command is added. Keep default workflow permissions read-only.
3. Click **Actions > Renovate now > Run workflow > main** or run:

   ```sh
   gh workflow run renovate-manual.yml --repo KostaGorod/kubernetes-talos-apps --ref main
   ```

4. Verify the actual workflow run and generated bot PRs. GitHub requires approval before workflows on GITHUB_TOKEN-created PRs execute. Approve that run, check green validation and review/merge the generated dependency PR. No privileged workflow bypass is introduced.

The manual run never merges, regardless of the existing scoped hosted-automerge config. Required-check protection remains separately recommended for main and mandatory before activating unattended hosted merging. No live repository settings, merge or deployment performed here.

## Verification

<details>
<summary>Executed source and native Renovate checks</summary>

- `mise run validate` passed, including YAML/action lint and the maintained Helm/Kubernetes/Argo schema checks. The new manual workflow is included in actionlint.
- Strict native Renovate repository-config validation passed.
- Executed the same manual CLI override arguments with credential-free local registry lookup: only the Kubernetes image manager ran. It resolved BentoPDF `2.8.10` and cloudflared `2026.10.4`, including immutable digests and `renovate-manual/` branch names.
- Exercised Renovate's native CLI config parser and package-rule application. All eight minor/patch/digest/major image cases keep `automerge=false` despite the repository's non-major automerge package rule; schedule, limits, manager scope, prefix and disabled dashboard overrides verified.
- `git diff --check` and redacted Gitleaks directory scan passed.
- Optional native RE2 is absent with install scripts disabled; the CLI reports its JavaScript RegExp fallback and completes validation/lookup successfully.
- The real Actions-token PR creation path cannot run on trusted main until this workflow is merged and the repository PR-creation setting is enabled. Local lookup is not claimed as a real bot update or end-to-end delivery.

</details>

author: anthonyturner
body:
## Summary

The match-upload function now keeps each player's Final Hits (killing blows) instead of silently dropping them. Final Hits are permitted for every player, the same as kills, deaths and assists ([RivalsPulse ADR-0017](https://github.com/anthonyturner/rivals_pulse/blob/main/docs/decisions/0017-count-and-keep-final-hits-for-every-player.md)). A player whose figure was not counted stays null, never 0.

- **Accept.** `parseParticipants` reads an optional per-player `final_hits` through the same `readCount(..., MAX_STAT)` as kills, deaths and assists. `storableMatch` does the same for the recorder's own `match_player` line.
- **Absent is not zero.** Absent, null or invalid (negative, fractional, over 999, text, boolean, object) becomes null, exactly as an invalid kills value does today. Nothing is coerced to 0, and the upload is not refused for it.
- **Store.** New migration `20261027000000_participants_final_hits.sql` adds a nullable `participants.final_hits integer`. Existing rows stay null.
- **RPC.** `record_match_participants` keeps its signature and grants, and writes `final_hits` on insert. On a repeat upload of the same match it now fills a blank `final_hits` as it already fills a blank `is_win`; a value already set is never changed.
- `index.ts` needs no change: it already passes the parsed rows and the recorder's performance straight through.
- `docs/supabase.md` lists the new migration.

Older app versions keep working unchanged: they never send the key, so their rows store null.

Related: https://github.com/anthonyturner/rivals_pulse/issues/1102

## Type

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Chore
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Content/data update

## Verification

- [x] `npm run build`: passes (needed `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` locally; the first run hit a Node out-of-memory abort before the change was involved).
- [x] `npm test`: 73 of 73 pass (run headless with Edge as `CHROME_BIN`, since Chrome is not installed on this machine). These tests do not cover the Supabase functions.
- [x] Focused tests: `npm run test:functions`: 45 of 45 pass. New cases cover a valid integer on both teams, zero, absent, null, each invalid shape (`-1`, `1.5`, `1e9`, `'three'`, `''`, `true`, `{}`, `[2]`), and the recorder's own line.
- [ ] Manual UI check
- [ ] Not applicable

The migration SQL was **not executed** anywhere: no local Postgres or Docker is available, and nothing was applied to the live project.

## Changelog

- [ ] Not user-visible yet because: nothing reads or displays the column until the overlay sends `final_hits` and a read path exists.

## Manual testing

- After the migration and function are deployed by hand (see Risks), upload a match from an overlay build that sends `final_hits` and check `select name, kills, final_hits from participants order by id desc limit 12;`.

## Risks

- **Deploy is manual.** Nothing in CI applies migrations or deploys functions (`docs/supabase.md`; CI only builds and runs `test:functions`). Order: `npx supabase migration list --linked`, then `npx supabase db push`, then `npx supabase functions deploy track-match-history`. The migration must go first: a function deployed before it sends `final_hits` to the old RPC, which ignores the key, so nothing breaks but nothing is stored either. The new RPC with the old function also works (null figures).
- **No read path exists yet (acceptance criterion 5).** Nothing in this repo or the overlay reads `participants`: RLS is on and anon/authenticated have no grant ("Nothing reads these rows yet", initial participants migration). So there is no Global-view query to extend. Whatever read function is added later must select `final_hits`.

## Escalation signals

- None.

## Notes

- Assumption: "rejected the same way other invalid numeric fields are" means stored as null, which is how kills/deaths/assists are handled, not a 400 for the whole upload.
- Follow-up: the read path for participants, when it is built.

Closes #119

author: irichard00
body:
Root cause: opening any HeadlessUI Dialog marks the app container inert + aria-hidden until close, removing <main> from the accessibility tree. boardMain() used getByRole('main'), so every board locator resolved to nothing for the whole modal-open duration and the header-create waiter starved on unbounded header reads.

Fix: scope boardMain() to CSS `page.locator('main')` (ignores inert state). Verified on the oracle stack: header reads resolve in ~10ms behind the open modal (were unresolvable for 120s+ pre-fix); nested route/layout <main> twins dedupe to one column set either way.

Regression pin: ISS-036 project-context step now asserts columns still resolve while the create modal is open (fails deterministically pre-fix, passes post-fix; new-leg safe via getByTestId reads).

Validation: ISS-036 oracle spec 4x green post-fix; typecheck/lint/test:changed(222)/boundaries/headers/deps/coexistence/similarity/paths all green. Temp probe code fully reverted.

author: bobikenobi12
body:
Part of #6129 — the first half: **members, teams, roles, access**. SSO, classification and activity follow in a second PR.

## What changed

**Reads over GET (ADR 0005 D1).** The bodies of `getMembers`, `getMembersPage`, `getInviteContext`, `getTeamsPage`, `listCustomRoles`, `getRolesBootstrap`, `listRoles`, `getAccessGrantsPage` and `getGrantOptions` moved (not wrapped) into `lib/rpc/procedures/members.ts`: `members.page`, `members.list`, `members.gate`, `members.inviteContext`, `members.teams`, `members.roles`, `members.roleCatalog`, `members.grants`, `members.grantOptions`. Each read keeps the authorization it had as an action: member/team lists answer any member of the addressed org; roles answer `member:view` (`authorizeQuiet`); grants answer `member:view` (`authorize`, denial recorded). Every predicate is on the actor the address resolved. `getInvitations` (no caller) is deleted. `artifact-shares.ts` now imports `listRoles` from the procedure module (outside scope; widened by name on the issue).

**Routes prefetch exactly what the client asks for (B1).** Members, teams, roles and access prefetch the pristine key and the link's filtered key in-process through `serverOrpc()` and dehydrate only `members.*` reads. Roles and access render their **forbidden** state on the server when the prefetch is refused (a viewer without `member:view`), as their own render, not as an empty list or an error (B4). Skeletons now have the real layout: toolbar, filter bar and table column count, and the roles master/detail (B2). A failed first load renders `RegionError`, never the empty state.

**Writes (ADR 0005 D4).** `setMemberSuspended`, `createRole`/`updateRole`/`deleteRole` and `assignGrant`/`revokeGrant` are `defineAction`s. The checks run in the same order as before: the PDP gate, the entitlement, the org binding (#6226), the privilege ceiling, and the active-membership refusal. Only input-shape validation now comes first. The organization-plugin writes (invite, role change, remove, cancel invitation, create/delete team, roster add/remove) stay browser calls to `/api/auth/organization/*`, so the route's guards and plugin hooks run exactly as before. A small adapter (`components/settings/members/auth-action.ts`) turns their `{ error }` into an `ActionResult`. This also fixes the role change, removal and cancellation, which used to drop `error` silently. Every write goes through `useActionMutation`: per-row pending state that disables the row's controls (the double-submit guard), one toast policy, and invalidation of every `members.*` read. The role sheet tracks dirty state: Save is disabled until something changes, and closing with unsaved changes asks first. The invite dialog puts a refused address's reason under that address and keeps only the refused rows.

**Gates on the server (F017, F049/F057).** `members.gate` returns `canInvite` from the same predicate `beforeCreateInvitation` enforces. It also returns the effective plan, derived the way the switcher badge derives it (billing plan while the status is live, else community), and a reason. Invite member and Create team are no longer enabled buttons that open an upsell. They are the same buttons, disabled, with their reason (`DisabledReason`), and the reason names the plan the badge shows. The teams filter bar is not drawn when the upsell is the page body. The teams entitlement comes from the route, so there is no unknown-state flash.

**Live (ADR 0005 §7 Q3).** New topics `members` (member, invitation, team, team_member) and `access` (grants, role, role_permission), with triggers in `programmables.sql`. The triggers have explicit `IS DISTINCT FROM` column lists and carry ids only. Routing: `members` goes to the org arm, unfiltered (every member reads those lists). `access` goes to a new `oaccess:<org>` key that a stream holds only with `can(view, member)`. Operators do not hold that permission, so they never hear grant or role hints. `capabilitiesOf` asks for it, and the 60 s re-authorisation refreshes it. Both topics invalidate `orpc.members.key()`. These pages had no polls to delete.

**Tests.** Tenancy fixtures for all nine procedures, through both entry points, with new team, role and team-grant markers per org. `realtime-notify-members.test.ts` covers each trigger both ways, plus who hears each hint. Routing unit tests cover the new keys. Action tests are ported to `ActionResult`. `grant-org-binding` still asserts the exact binding reason, read through a pass-through spy on the real check. The component tests are ported to the GET reads, and new teams-gate tests cover disabled-with-reason and the hidden filter bar. Three e2e titles in `flows/rbac.spec.ts` changed with the gate behaviour, and `gate-baseline.json` is renamed to match.

## Verification
Local runs were stopped partway through because the machine was overloaded: the action, list-read, filter-hook, url-search, realtime, members, access and teams component suites passed locally before the last batch of edits. The roles component tests, activity tests, tenancy fixtures and the new trigger integration test are verified by CI only.

## Not verified without a running app
- CLS of the new skeletons (B2) and the visual of the disabled-with-reason buttons.
- Hints arriving within ~1 s through the live bus.
- The members skeleton draws 5 columns; an org with the `organizations` entitlement renders 7.


## Review follow-ups (rebased on #6219)

**Fixed:**
- **Clock-dependent dates.** `members.grants` now returns `asOf`, and "Granted …" is computed against it, so the server render and the hydrating client print the same text.
- **Skeletons follow the entitlement.** The loading skeletons resolve the entitlement from the request-cached actor:
  - members draws 7 columns when the org may manage members, 5 when it may not;
  - teams and access without the plan draw the upsell's shape instead of a filter bar and a table (F021).
- **The `members` topic** now also invalidates `overview.usage` and `billing.summary`, which both show the seat count.
- **One denial per forbidden Access view.** The Access route prefetches the unfiltered grants read alone, first. A viewer without `member:view` is refused there once, and the filtered list and the builder options are not asked.
- **No-access state.** Access has its own `AccessNoAccess` component.
- **Tenancy suite clock fields.** `withoutClock` now nulls only the personal scope's synthesized owner.
- **Comments.** The ones the review named are corrected: `projectId` in the procedures header, zod-first in the `grants.ts` header, the binding refusal now named only on the server, and the stale `qk.*` and stat-strip mentions.
- **Trigger documentation.** The `member` trigger now says that name, email and avatar changes are not hinted.

**Skipped, with reasons:**
- **`members.gate` as an org-scoped fixture.** Both seeded orgs share one live Team plan, and the billing and usage fixtures (#6127/#6118) depend on that. Giving Y another plan means re-deriving their markers in a file several lanes share; it stays `not-org-scoped`, and the fixture's comment says why.
- **A server-key = client-key assertion.** The route tests run through the fake client, which cannot prove the two keys are equal. The tenancy suite does call `serverOrpc()` as shipped, but proving equality needs the real browser client in a test environment, which I have not built. Left for the second PR.
- **`StreamCapabilities.memberView` required.** That would mean editing other lanes' realtime test files (bus, events-route, support notify). The field stays optional and fails closed (absent means no `access` key), and a routing test pins that.
- **`[project]/settings/access` prefetch (B1).** That route is outside this unit's scope, so its project-scoped Access list is still fetched on the client.
- **The deleted `getInvitations` tests.** The inviter-name fallback is covered for `queryMembersPage` in `tests/lib/queries/members-list.test.ts`. Ordering is not: `q

author: usirin
body:
Every pull request ran the same 7-minute check twice, and 5 min 40 s of it was the tests on one machine.

**What changes** (`.github/workflows/check.yaml`, `vitest.config.ts`):
- **Once.** `push` runs only on `main`; `pull_request` runs on every pull request. A newer push to a pull request cancels the run it replaces.
- **Only what it can reach.** A pull request runs `vitest --changed` against its base: the tests that import what it changed. A change to a file tests read without importing (lockfile, workspace, tsconfig, biome and its plugins, `layer-rules.json`, `fixtures/`, `.github/`) runs every test (`forceRerunTriggers`). Two tests read the whole repo themselves, so they always run: the app's bundles and the law that every machine has laws.
- **Main runs every test**, so whatever a pull request's run could not see shows up one merge later.
- **Three machines.** The tests run as 3 shards (`--shard`), beside one job for typecheck, lint, promises and build.

**Numbers.** On five recent merges, `--changed` picked 55, 100, 230 (it touched a package.json), 83 and 0 (docs only) of 234 test files. Locally, the full suite takes 212 s, the 100-file set 132 s, and the 55-file set 30 s.

**Doubt.** A test that reads a file at run time without importing it, and is not on the trigger list, can be skipped on a pull request. Main's full run is the backstop. Main has no merge queue, so a red main is found after the merge, not before.

**What it cannot tell us.** This PR touches `.github/` and the vitest config, so its own run is a full one over three machines. The first ordinary PR after it shows the `--changed` time on CI.

body: # Narrow-pane layout fixes, themes and animated backdrops for REVamp **TL;DR** - Fixes cropped/clipped UI in narrow Hermes Desktop panes (docked player, control page, EQ presets menu, library toolbar, Focus view). - Fixes bugs that only show inside Hermes: skins/playlists failing on the control page, the theme differing between the two pages, no way back after "Bring the player here". - Adds pane scaling for big screens, and a theme system (8 Looks, 13 animated backdrops, 4 original scenes, custom colours/image). Default look is **Lantern night**. Found while testing REVamp inside **Hermes Desktop**: the UI was cropped and clipped in narrow docked panes, and the docked player stayed tiny on large screens. This PR fixes those and adds a theme system. Everything below was checked in headless Chrome at 240-1000px (and the layout fixes by hand in Hermes Desktop after a full restart). ## 1. Problems fixed (before / after) | Problem | Before | After | |---|---|---| | **Docked pane (~300px):** the 275px classic stack was centered in a stage narrower than itself, so the left side was cut off. Nav rail is now a top row; the stack scales to fit. | | | | **Control page (~400px):** the queue was drawn on top of the "Playing in the frame" label, the Artist/Album columns collapsed to a few pixels, and five toolbar buttons wrapped over three rows. Status row is one line, queue below, secondary actions in a "More" dropdown, narrow tables keep Title + Time. | | | | **EQ presets menu (275px overlay):** the preset list fit neither right (25px free) nor left (137px free) and was clipped. It now falls back to an overlay aligned with the stack; menus fit to the player windows and the reported frame grows to include them. | | | | **Focus view:** oversized Start button, misaligned sliders, unequal timer chips. | | | Also fixed (no screenshot): - **Skins and Playlists on the control page:** clicking a skin threw `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'setSkin')` because the control page has no player (audio lives in the other frame); Playlists had the same problem with `loadTracks`/`playIndex`. They now send the server commands the live player already handles. - **Theme differed between pages:** Hermes iframes are sandboxed (opaque origin, no `localStorage`), so each page kept its own theme. The plugin host now stores it and relays it to both frames (plain-browser use falls back to `localStorage` + a `storage` listener). - **No way back after "Bring the player here":** the page toolbar now shows a "Return to frame / pop-out / desktop" button with the green status dot. - **Skin museum previews** cropped each skin's title bar (`object-fit: cover`); now `contain`. - EQ-off white band, bottom ticker floor/ceiling, scrolling sidebar, desktop page toolbar wraps instead of overflowing, and `ensureClassicOpen()` read the wrong state path so the pop-out never reopened a closed EQ/playlist. ## 2. Features added - **Pane scaling:** the docked player scales up in whole-number steps (up to 4x, so the pixel art stays crisp) to fill wide panes. The scale comes from the three player windows only (not an open menu), and a new scale commits only after it has held ~400ms, so a skin load/change can't make the player jump. *(Hermes-only; needs a plugin reinstall/restart, so no browser screenshot.)* - **"Return to frame" button:** after "Bring the player here" there was no way back without opening settings. The page toolbar now shows a button with the green status dot ("Return to frame / pop-out / desktop"). *(Hermes-only.)* - **Theme picker** (palette button labeled "Theme" in the panel header): - 8 one-tap **Looks**: Default, Moonlit girl, Sakura shrine, Neon city, Lantern night, Campfire, Aurora, Paper, in a sideways-scrolling row. - **Animation** row with 13 backdrops: embers & sparks, fire, sakura petals, snowfall, fireflies, rain, thunderstorm, aurora, stars & shooting star, warp speed, matrix code, bubbles. Half-resolution canvas, ~30fps, paused when the tab is hidden, off by default, respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **Customize** (opens as a panel to the left on wide panes, below on narrow): 7 colour schemes, 4 original anime-style SVG scenes (`web/img/bg/`) or your own image, gradients with custom colours, accent colour, intensity. - Default look is **Lantern night** (the plain original is "Classic"); kept in sync across the control page and the player page, so nothing flips after "Bring the player here". ## 3. Final result: the Looks | Sakura shrine + petals | Neon city + rain | Lantern night + embers | Campfire + fire | |---|---|---|---| | | | | | Library "More" dropdown (narrow panes): ## 4. Verification - `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: 25/25; web/contract pytest subset passes. (Unrelated pre-existing failures: `ffprobe` missing, a Python 3.14 `TypeError` in `test_plugin_api`.) - Overflow sweep: 112 view/width combinations (240-1000px, every nav view, control and embed pages), no horizontal overflow. - Presets menu verified with real mouse hover, and with a frame wider than the stack (menu and list stay inside the 275px stack). - All 13 animations run without errors. Skin click on the control page verified (applies, no error). - **Not run end to end:** the host-relayed theme sync and the pane scaling only execute inside Hermes; the page side was exercised in a normal browser, the plugin side is covered by syntax checks and the desktop test subset. - New tests/probes: `eq_layout`, `shell_layout`, `focus_view` (node tests), plus `probe_*.mjs` scripts used for the sweeps. ## 5. body:
## Summary

Send to CMS, phase 2 (#1331): **WordPress**, part 5, the docs. It covers what #1569–#1572 built.

**Stacked on #1507** (the Webflow docs), since both change `send-to-cms.mdx`. This PR's own change is its last commit, docs only. Merge it after #1507 and the WordPress chain.

`guides/send-to-cms.mdx`:
- **Intro.** Three ways now: Webflow, WordPress, your workflow.
- **Connect WordPress** (new). It covers:
  - making an Application Password (Users → Profile; a separate Author user is enough, as Ansvisor writes drafts only);
  - the Settings → Integrations card, and how the site address is read (https added, `/wp-admin` and `/wp-json` taken off, a folder kept, https and the standard port only);
  - what's checked before anything is kept, and when the password goes to the site: once it answers as WordPress, or when it keeps its REST API from visitors;
  - a table of what the toast says when the check fails, and what to do: the user or password refused, Plain permalinks, Application Passwords off, the `Authorization` header dropped (with the `.htaccess` line), users hidden, a firewall, a redirect, a user who can't write posts;
  - Change sign-in (a new password, user or site; the old password revoked where the site allows), Disconnect, and Sign-in refused;
  - a self-hosting note on `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIALS_KEY`.
- **Choose where pages go.** Webflow, WordPress, then your workflow. With nothing remembered, or the remembered one no longer connected, the first one ready is picked. A remembered CMS that isn't ready sends to your workflow, never the other CMS (#1572).
- **To WordPress** (under Send one page). It covers:
  - what goes: title, slug, content, and the meta description as the excerpt;
  - what doesn't: the meta title (set it in the SEO plugin), and JSON-LD (WordPress would keep it as text for users without unfiltered HTML);
  - tables, images, no featured image or category, and how WordPress adjusts the slug;
  - when a send updates the post (a draft or pending review), and when it makes a new draft (the post published, scheduled or private; trashed or deleted);
  - the toast;
  - when the page becomes Published, with the 60-day check, what happens after it, and "Removed in WordPress".
- **Send several pages and See how a send went.** WordPress counts toward the 200 a day. A page already on its way can't go twice. The Library's paper plane covers a draft post.

`api-reference/webhooks.mdx`: pages sent to WordPress don't fire `content_draft.sent` either. `guides/content-editor.mdx`: the Send to CMS line names WordPress.

## Related issue

Part of #1331 (phase 2, WordPress). Stacked on #1507; documents #1569, #1570, #1571 and #1572.

## Type of change

- [ ] `feat` — New feature
- [ ] `fix` — Bug fix
- [ ] `chore` — Maintenance / dependencies
- [x] `docs` — Documentation only
- [ ] `refactor` — Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
- [ ] `test` — Adding or updating tests

## How to test

Read `docs/guides/send-to-cms.mdx`, or run `mint dev` in `docs/` and open **Send to CMS**. Each statement can be checked against the code:
- the address and the check: `server/src/lib/cms/wordpress.js` (`siteAddress`, `checkSite`);
- what goes and when a new draft is made: `wordpress-delivery.js`;
- the published check: `wordpress-status.js`;
- the card's messages: `settings.wordpress` in `web/messages/en.json`;
- where pages go: `web/src/components/content/cms-target.tsx`.

## Checklist

- [x] Branch follows the naming convention (`feature/`, `fix/`, `chore/`, `docs/`) — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/ansvisor/ansvisor/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Commits follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [ ] `yarn lint` passes (run from `web/`)
- [ ] `yarn typecheck` passes (run from `web/`)
- [ ] `yarn format:check` passes (run from `web/`)
- [x] Changes are focused — one concern per PR

Docs only: no web or server code changed, so the web checks don't apply. A pre-push review checked each statement against #1569–#1572's code. Its findings are folded in: the check's messages are toasts, the refused sign-in row, when the password is sent, the dialog leaving out a CMS it can't check, Change sign-in, http and ports, where the password is kept, Application Passwords off behind a proxy, a remembered CMS no longer connected, a post published after the 60 days, and no featured image.

author: daniil4545
body:
## Consequences

Two new make targets for sessions; the app, the CLI and the installer do not change. Agents get a live check that cannot touch the user's running Tarn, and new task worktrees build without copying the core by hand. The profile now says how acceptance goes: a stand check per PR before the merge, a hand check by the user per batch on a `dev` build.

## What and why

- `make -f tarn.mk live [STAND_APP=...]` runs `tools/stand/stand.sh`: a copy of a built `Tarn.app` with its own bundle id, re-signed ad hoc, started with a test-only interpose (`fakehome.c`) that gives it its own home. Its control socket, settings and AppleScript target are separate from the user's Tarn. It prints `HOME` and `TARN_SURFACE` for `cli/tarn`; `stand.sh stop` ends it. On 2026-10-27 an acceptance session built this by hand and found two defects of `tarn ls` with it (#55); every session needs it.
- `make -f tarn.mk worktree NAME=<branch>` creates `.worktrees/<branch>` from `origin/dev` and links `GhosttyKit.xcframework` and `zig-out` of the main checkout. Three sessions on 2026-10-27 solved the missing core in a worktree three different ways, one by asking the user to build.

## Decisions

- Interpose instead of a socket path setting in the app: the stand stays test tooling and adds no option to the product.
- AppleScript by bundle id is asked only while the stand process lives and its socket exists: otherwise it would launch a fresh copy with the real home.
- `release` keeps refusing a linked core, so a release is still built only in the main checkout.

## How it was checked

- Stand from the t203 Debug build: `stand up`, `cli/tarn ls` answered from the stand socket; restart left one process; `stop` left none; the user's Tarn kept running with its socket.
- `worktree` from the main checkout created the worktree with both links; inside a worktree it refuses.
- `shellcheck tools/stand/stand.sh` (now part of `check`), `typos`, `gitleaks`: ok.
- Review: no must-fix; three should-fix fixed in e290a8a9b.

## Where to look

`tools/stand/stand.sh`, the `worktree` and `live` targets in `tarn.mk`, the acceptance line in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

author: varis-variden
body:
Closes #13

## Summary

Makes goods-receipt confirmation idempotent and confirmed receipts final (GR-04, GR-05).

Before this change, a repeated idempotency key was rejected with `CONFLICT` (ticket #12's behaviour). #13 changes that: a retry of the same action now **returns the original receipt** and never double-counts stock, while a genuinely new receipt with a fresh key still posts.

- **GR-04 (idempotent replay).** `confirm` looks up the idempotency key **before** the status and over-receipt checks. If a receipt already exists for the key, the original is returned unchanged — whatever the order has become since (it may now be `COMPLETED`). The looking-up-first matters: a post-hoc catch would re-run the over-receipt cap and wrongly reject a retry of the receipt that completed the order (e.g. resend 20-of-20 → `20 + 20 > 20`). The unique-constraint catch is kept as a concurrency safety net: two identical requests racing each other both pass the lookup, one commits, and the loser replays the winner's receipt instead of failing.
- **Store scope on replay.** `replayReceipt` enforces `assertStoreScope`, so a replay can never hand one store's receipt to another (NFR-01).
- **GR-05 (finality).** A confirmed receipt cannot be edited or cancelled because no such route exists on the contract. A contract test guards this: `goodsReceiptsContract` exposes exactly `listOrders` and `confirm`, so a future edit/cancel/delete route can't quietly make receipts mutable.
- The `GoodsReceipt` response is now assembled by one shared `toGoodsReceipt` mapper, used by both a fresh confirmation and a replay, so the two can't drift.

No schema or contract shape change: `idempotencyKey` was already `@unique` and the receipt already stores every field the response needs.

## What was tested

- **Contract** (`goods-receipts.test.ts`): GR-05 finality guard — the contract exposes only `listOrders` and `confirm`.
- **API controller spec** (`goods-receipts.controller.spec.ts`): a repeated key replays the original receipt and runs no second stock movement; a replay of the receipt that completed the order is returned (never reaches the transaction); a replay is refused across store scope (`FORBIDDEN`); a key clash with no readable receipt falls back to `CONFLICT` without leaking database detail.
- **Postgres integration spec** (`goods-receipts.integration.spec.ts`): AC-02 — receive 8, resend the identical request → original receipt returned, stock stays 18, cumulative received stays 8, one receipt/one movement; a fresh key still posts; resending the receipt that completed the order replays rather than hitting the over-receipt cap.
- **Playwright e2e** (`goods-receipt-idempotency.e2e.ts`): walks the Demo line through the API the browser uses — receive 8, resend the identical request (same key) returns the original and counts once, a confirmed receipt has no edit/cancel/delete route (404), a fresh key posts a new receipt.

`pnpm check` (lint, typecheck, test incl. integration, build) and `pnpm format` pass from the repo root.

## Evidence

- `pnpm check`: green — 171 api unit tests, 12 api integration tests, all web and contract tests.
- `pnpm e2e`: Chromium installed locally; the new `goods-receipt-idempotency.e2e.ts` passes, as do 12 of the 13 others.
- The one local e2e failure is the pre-existing `goods-receipts.e2e.ts` (#11), which asserts the seeded `PO-DEMO-001` shows 0 received. That singleton had been partially received by repeated local runs against a database that was not reset (the `db:reset` guard reserves the reset for a human), so the assertion saw stale data. It is unrelated to this change — which touches neither that test, its page, nor PO-DEMO-001's behaviour — and CI runs each suite against a freshly seeded database, where it passes.

author: muscles4817
body:
Closes audit item **C4 (Negotiation)** in `docs/34-promoter-audit-execution-plan.md`. **Stacked on #52 (C3), which is stacked on #51 (C2).** Retarget it as those merge.

## The audit evidence, and what changed

| Finding | Now |
|---|---|
| "Offer a deal" signed a free agent on the spot, on hard-coded terms (4 fights, no matching rights) | The roster button opens the fighter's page, where the deal is negotiated |
| No re-sign action, even for a #1 contender whose tab says "This deal is now an insult" | Your own fighters get a **Re-sign** button in the header |
| Managers, the champion's clause and matching rights never reached promoter mode | All of them are on the terms sheet. The manager is the counterparty, and their `negotiationMultiplier` sets the price |
| Bout offers were answered the same day, with a single money counter | Answers arrive 2–7 days later. A counter can ask for money, a better slot, five rounds or a different opponent |

## Engine
**`business/negotiation.ts` (new), all pure:**
- `preferredFights`: ambitious fighters want short deals, loyal ones will sign long.
- `termsValue`: prices every term using the existing `TERM_PRICING`.
- `reservation`: what the fighter will take. It is their asking price, adjusted by:
  - the manager's negotiation skill;
  - the loyalty discount on a re-sign;
  - being broke (they take less);
  - **the relationship ledger**. This is the deferred C3 item: the player's own re-sign now reads it.
- `readTerms` gives the acceptance meter: a label and the main concern, never a number.
- `makeOffer` / `takeCounter`: the fighter agrees, counters (once or twice depending on temperament), or walks.
  - The counter is shaped by personality. Everyone wants the money up to what they are worth. The ambitious also want the length they prefer and no champion's clause. Stars with ego ask for PPV points where the promotion can grant them. The money-minded ask for a signing bonus.
- `isHoldingOut`: resentment ≥ 65, with enough ego or ambition. `acceptanceOf` then returns chance 0 with `holdout: true` for any bout, title fights included. Only a new deal ends it.

**`business/boutAgreements.ts`:**
- The `BoutCounter` union: money, a better slot, five rounds, or a different opponent.
- `replyDelayDays`: 2–7 days, deterministic per offer.
- `shapeBoutCounter`: checks for an opponent request first, then slot, then rounds, then money.
- `describeCounter`: the counter as a sentence.

**`business/eventPlans.ts`** (additive only):
- `CornerAnswer` gains `counter?` and `quote?`.
- `PlannedBout` gains `replyDay?` and `pending?`.

## App
- **`game/plans.ts`:**
  - `sendOffer` leaves the bout `offered`, with the answers in `pending` until `replyDay`.
  - **`settleReplies(db, day)`** reveals the answers and raises the inbox item. The clock runs it every simulated day, so a counter can stop the clock when it lands, and once more on the day the clock stops, fight night included.
  - `missPlans` runs after it. An offer still pending on a missed card simply lapses: nobody had camped for it yet, so there is no ledger entry.
  - `acceptCounter` meets each counter kind: pays money, grants five rounds, or moves the bout into the requested slot if that slot is free. A different opponent can't be granted here; it needs a re-booking.
- **`game/contracts.ts`:**
  - `tableFor` and `canNegotiate`: open to your own fighters, free agents, and fighters whose deal elsewhere has expired.
  - **Rival-bid hook for B4:** `rivalBidsFor(db, fighter, incumbent)` and `matchBid`. For now the bids are read off the free-agency market (`offersOnTheTable`) during the last `BID_WINDOW_DAYS` (90) of a deal. B4 can swap the source without touching any caller.
- **`screens/ContractTable.tsx`** (new): the terms sheet (show, win, signing bonus, PPV points, fights, champion's clause, matching rights), the meter, their counter with a quote, "Accept their terms" / "Start from their terms" / "Make a revised offer", a notice when they walk, and rival bids with **Match it**.
- **`FighterView`** gains `negotiation` and `negotiationLabel` props: a header button opens the Contract tab, where the table sits at the top. The Contract tab also shows a **Holding out** notice when it applies. `FighterScreen` builds the table and commits after signing.

## Cross-lane touches (named, minimal)
- **`screens/PlanScreen.tsx` (Lane A):** the counter button reads "Accept: <describeCounter…>" for a non-money counter instead of "Pay £0", and is hidden for an opponent counter. A4 will do the full treatment.
- **`game/clock.ts` (Lane A):** two calls to `settleReplies`.
- **`game/inbox.ts` (Lane A):** a counter's title uses `describeCounter` for non-money counters.
- **`tests/integration/planning.test.ts`:** the three offer tests now expect `offered`, then settle on `replyDay`. They also check the replies still can't be re-rolled.
- **`tests/ui/promoter.test.tsx`:** a `waitAWeekForAnswers` helper, used in "sending the card out" and "fight night".
- **`screens/PromoterRosterScreen.tsx`:** "Offer a deal" navigates to the fighter instead of signing on fixed terms.

## Tests
- `engine/src/business/negotiation.test.ts`:
  - length pricing;
  - a generous offer reads as a yes and a lowball as no;
  - agree, counter and walk, with the counter landing at a yes;
  - the ambitious counter drops the clause;
  - counter limit by temperament;
  - the ledger raises a re-sign price;
  - a holdout refuses a title fight;
  - reply delay is 2–7 days and deterministic;
  - counter kinds in order.
- `tests/integration/negotiation.test.ts`: `canNegotiate` modes, signing on exactly the agreed terms, rival bids only inside the window (and matched when allowed), five rounds granted, opponent counter not grantable.
- `tests/ui/contract-table.test.tsx`: the header button opens the table with its meter and toggles; an offer gets an answer; a generous offer signs.
- Playwright screenshots of the table and a counter at 390px: `scratchpad/laneC/c4-contract-390.png` and `c4-contract-answer-390.png`.
- Typecheck and lint are clean. Results for the full `npm test` and `test:long` on this head will be posted as a PR comment.

author: m-moravcik
body:
## Intent

The user took screenshots (⇧⌘4) on 2026-10-27 at 07:21:53 and 07:22:16 and "nothing happened": no file, nothing on the clipboard, no ClipShot preview. They asked where it failed, then said "fix it" (ano oprav to) after I proposed the fix below. After the fix passed the pipeline, they asked "ok, so are you going to make a release?" (ok cize ides spravit release?).

Diagnosis (from the unified log, file timestamps and ~/Library/Logs/clipshot.log):
1. macOS: screencapture wrote each capture to its hidden temporary file in the screenshot folder (birth 07:21:58 and 07:22:19), then blocked 69 s and 48 s in MDItemSetAttributes waiting on Spotlight (mds), and only at 07:23:07 renamed both files into place (ctime 07:23:07). Not ClipShot's fault and not fixable by ClipShot.
2. ClipShot: when the files appeared at 07:23:07, CopyDecider.isFresh rejected them because birth and modification time were 69 s / 48 s old, outside the 30 s copy window. They were dropped silently: no copy, no preview, not recorded in the ledger (so not in the popover list), and no log line.

Fix 1 (commit "Copy a capture that macOS renames into place late"), as agreed with the user:
- Detect late captures by inode, not by ctime. Each pass also lstats the dot-files in the folder; StagedCaptures remembers the resourceID (device+inode) and birth time of each hidden file the first time it is seen while fresh. A rename keeps inode and birth time, so when a visible file appears with that inode and birth time within 10 minutes (StagedCaptures.limit), it is judged from the moment it appeared: CopyDecider.isFresh(file, now:, hiddenFor:) shifts "now" back by how long the file sat hidden. The delay is fixed at the first visible listing so the rescans after it count the window from the same moment.
- ctime was deliberately rejected: it also changes on xattr writes, Put Back from the Trash, ClipShot's own Undo of a Trash move and renames, so old screenshots would be copied again. A file never seen hidden (put back from the Trash, moved in) is judged by its own times exactly as before.
- A sync tool that writes a hidden file, sets an old modification date and renames it is still rejected, because freshness is judged with the file's own modification time at the moment of the hidden sighting.
- CopyDecider now prunes its memory of a copy by max(modified, time of the copy) instead of by modified, otherwise the 1 s poll would forget a late copy right away and the rescans would copy it again. seed() now takes `now` explicitly.
- Hidden files present when watching starts are never staged (the user decided an in-flight capture at launch must not be copied), consistent with "files present when watching starts are never copied".
- Logging: a late copy logs "copied late ext=png, macOS held it back N s"; a new screenshot (with the marker) that is not fresh logs "not copied, created N s before it appeared ext=png", also when the marker lands after the first pass, so a silent drop can be diagnosed next time. The existing "N ms after the file appeared" metric for normal captures is unchanged.
- DEVELOPMENT.md documents the rule.
- Tests: CopyDecider unit tests, StagedCaptures unit tests, and CopyCoordinatorTests on a real folder with a real kqueue watch and an OffsetClock that failed before the fix; logged seconds are checked as a range. Verified end to end on a Release build with the real ~/Pictures/Screenshots folder: hidden file held 86 s, then renamed and marked; the log said "copied late ... held it back 86 s" and the clipboard held the PNG.

Fix 2 (commit "Quit when another ClipShot is already running"), offered by me and accepted by the user as a separate small commit:
- During diagnosis I accidentally started a second ClipShot by running /Applications/ClipShot.app/Contents/MacOS/clipshot (on case-insensitive APFS that is the GUI binary, not the CLI in Contents/Helpers). Two instances meant two menu bar icons and every screenshot copied twice. Launch Services only prevents a second instance per bundle, not per bundle identifier (also a copy opened from a disk image).
- At launch, before the model is created, ClipShot looks for another process with its bundle identifier, waits up to 2 s for it to exit (a relaunch can overlap the old instance's exit), and if it still runs, logs "another ClipShot is running (pid N), quitting" and exit(0)s. Skipped under XCTest; Debug builds have their own bundle identifier so a dev build next to the installed app is unaffected. Verified end to end: the new Release binary run next to the installed app exited with 0 after 2.7 s.

Pipeline history: run 01M5Y3G1NK4WARX6BVVRQ1FD56 (cancelled at CI, which never runs) and run 01M5Y9NNA87FX0A67WJGTM69JF (passed) validated everything up to 9493827; their Test, Review and Document fixes are on the branch (StagedCaptures(present:), the marker-late log, test badge 566).

This run adds one commit, "Prepare 0.9.3: release notes and version", because the user asked for a release. Following the repo's precedent (0.9.1 and 0.9.2 had their notes and version bump on the feature branch before merge): MARKETING_VERSION 0.9.2 -> 0.9.3 and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 3 -> 4 in project.yml (above the appcast's highest sparkle:version 3), and release-notes/0.9.3.md, which is both the GitHub release body and Sparkle's update window text (paragraphs, "- " bullets, backtick code only), written for end users in the style of 0.9.2.md. The log lines are deliberately left out of the notes as not user facing. After merge, scripts/release.sh runs locally from main. CI is skipped because GitHub Actions never run on the user's account; `make guards` passes on this head.

User preferences: prefer quality, simplicity, robustness and long-term maintainability over development cost. Comments and commit messages in English, no em dashes, no agent co-author line in commits.

## What Changed

- Late captures are now detected by inode. Each pass also lstats hidden files in the screenshot folder, and the new `StagedCaptures` remembers the device+inode and birth time of every fresh hidden file. When a visible file shows up within 10 minutes with the same inode and birth time, `CopyDecider.isFresh(_:now:hiddenFor:)` judges it from the moment it appeared, so a screenshot that macOS held back (for example while Spotlight was blocked) is still copied. Files never seen hidden, such as ones put back from the Trash or moved in, are still judged by their own times. Hidden files that were already there when watching started, or that appeared while copying was off, are never staged and never copied under their final name. Markup edits of such files are still copied. `CopyDecider` now forgets a copy based on max(modified, copy time), and `seed()` takes `now`, so the rescans after a late copy do not copy it again. New log lines: "copied late ... macOS held it back N s", "not copied, created N s before it appeared" and "not copied, saved while ClipShot was not copying".
- New `SingleInstance`: at launch, before the model is created, ClipShot looks for another process with its bundle identifier, waits up to 2 s for it to exit, and quits if it is still running. This stops two menu bar icons from both copying every screenshot. The check is skipped under XCTest.
- New unit tests for `StagedCaptures`, `SingleInstance` and the `CopyDecider` freshness/pruning changes, plus `CopyCoordinator` tests that run on a real folder with a kqueue watch and an offset clock. `DEVELOPMENT.md` documents the late-capture rule, the README test badge is updated, and the release is prepared for 0.9.3 (`project.yml` version 0.9.3, build 4, and `release-notes/0.9.3.md`).

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The latest fix round is a one-line guard (`!editing`). It does what the recorded decision asks, and the regression test fails without it. The excluded-capture rule, late-capture staging, decider pruning, single-instance exit, version bump and release notes all match the intent and the recorded user decisions.

author: takeisan24
body:
## Summary

Moves invites to a database-free architecture on Vercel Blob.

- **Short links:** an invite config is stored as an immutable JSON blob and served at `/i/<id>` (id = `YYMM` expiry + 10 CSPRNG chars).
- **Fallback link:** `/invite#c=…` carries only the delta from a frozen default snapshot (`lib/invite-baseline.ts`), and the fragment never reaches the server. Default invites shrink from ~2,700 to ~95 characters, so Vietnamese invites get a scannable QR code again.
- **Legacy links:** `/invite?c=` and `/invite?id=` still open. `?id=` redirects to `/i/<id>`.
- **Answers are no longer stored on a server.** The ticket share message carries a `/reply#r=…` link. Opening it on the sender's device saves the answers into the local archive, now with question labels.
- **Uploads:** background and music files go straight from the browser to Blob with a short-lived token limited by type and size, so large songs no longer hit the function body limit. Images are re-encoded to WebP first.
- **Cleanup:** a weekly cron removes expired month folders (30 days after the date, or 90 days after creation; 180 days max).

Also:
- sanitize every config read from a URL or request body (`sanitizeInviteConfig`)
- show option titles instead of ids in the share message
- return the LAN address only in development
- add vitest with codec and share message tests
- add a one-off script to copy existing invitations into Blob
- add `AGENTS.md` as the source of truth for agents, and ignore local agent tooling dirs

## Deployment notes

Before this goes to production, the Vercel project needs:
- a Blob store connected (provides `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN`)
- `CRON_SECRET` set for `/api/cron/cleanup`
- the cron in `vercel.json` registered

`scripts/migrate-legacy-invitations.mjs` is optional and run by hand.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npm run lint`

- [x] `npm run build`
- [ ] Manual QA on a preview deploy: create an invite, open `/i/<id>` on mobile, answer, send the `/reply#r=` link back, check the archive
- [ ] `#c=` fallback link opens with Blob disabled
- [ ] Legacy `?c=` and `?id=` links still open
- [ ] Image and music upload on a preview deploy

author: orastorelk-cell
body:
## Cause
Packing PDF generation and the separate server download-status save are different operations. `markInvoiceBatchDownloaded` returned immediately after enqueueing the receipt, before the `/api/orders/invoice-download-status` request finished. Operators could download a PDF and still see the batch in Need Download with no nearby explanation or retry control. A mixed single/multi-page batch is only done once all orders have download receipts.

## Fix
- Await the existing idempotent download-receipt queue flush and refuse to report success until the affected order IDs are no longer pending acknowledgment.
- If server acknowledgment fails, keep the durable client receipt in the retry queue; surface a useful error in the PDF download flow. Do **not** download the PDF again.
- Add the existing Retry Status Save control and queue status inside the Packing Invoice Downloads tab, plus the number of invoices in a batch still pending.
- Mark batch badge STATUS SAVE PENDING while saved PDF metadata is in the queue.
- Add test assertions that pending receipts remain until the server acknowledges, then disappear.

## Safety
No change to invoice PDFs, stock, courier data, financial fields, authentication, or server writes. Uses existing authenticated R2 endpoint and original invoice identity checks. A mixed single/multi-page batch still requires both PDF groups to be downloaded. Source review performed; full npm/TypeScript/browser tests and live deployment not available from this connector session.

author: larsbx
body:
Complete all actual first/run/last children of H3,J,K,L and their orientation reversals throughout the minus boundary chamber, with a 76-label outgoing union and selected typed-coincidence exits of length at most five. The alpha=1/2 split is resolved by exact polynomial sign cones, including its two small diagonal exceptions. Stacked on #357 while its fresh hosted gates remain pending. Independent human review pending.

## Work shown

### Assumptions and hypotheses
k,t>=0, n=k+3+t, d=2n-1-k, A=n+d and N=n-1, with exactly the ordered class-A minus words and all bottom-minus-top integer Parikh coordinates. Sources H3=(x,y,0,-1,3), J=(y,x,1,2,-4), K=(y,x,-1,-2,5), L=(y,x,0,3,-4), plus each real orientation reversal. Retain actual occurrence ordinals, strict physical overlap and typed target compatibility.

The same three-source review and non-unit/all-source firewalls are recorded in docs/class-a-boundary-h3-stopgo-2026-10-27.md. The new table explicitly replays the inherited alpha+2/beta<1 certificate, in addition to alpha+1/beta<1. No spectral or internal-space transfer is introduced.

### Derivation / reduction
Writing alpha=beta-(n+2), the exact identity 8f(n+5/2)=4k^2+20k-4t^2-24t+5 and four positive-coefficient cone/diagonal cases prove alpha>1/2 iff t>k or t=k>=2. Equality cannot occur; (0,0),(1,1) are low, not high. This is symbolic chamber-wide algebra.

All nine child kinds of all eight oriented sources are completely resolved with actual word clips. O(n+d) synthesis uses at most two run/run strips and bounded endpoint ranges. Polynomial identities bind the full transport, constant-space predicates bind the exact 76-label image, and actual witnesses attain every envelope label. The full proof and tables are in docs/class-a-boundary-h3-carrier-2026-10-27.md.

The uniform path H3 -> J -> K -> L -> H1 -> C=(y,y,0,0,0) uses actual pairs (2n+2,0),(t+2,0),(k+1,0),(0,n-2),(1,2). Other sources use suffixes, and reversals swap the same actual indices. Rank 5..0 is restricted to eleven selected labels; it is not assigned to the full outgoing carrier.

### Evidence and replay
Canonical kernel kernel/psc/class_a_boundary_h3_children.mojo, regression kernel/tests/test_class_a_boundary_h3_children.mojo and driver kernel/class_a_boundary_h3_children.mojo. Local locked Mojo 1.1.0.dev2026090805 passed 56 members / 132,384 ordered pairs / 5,824 accepted / 1,568 selected path edges, including all 76 labels and every reversed edge. native-local.txt pins source bytes and preserves full output.

The independent literal-prefix integer-polynomial/Fraction oracle covers 117 members / 936 source cells / 490,464 pairs / 15,912 accepted / 3,276 selected edges. It independently tests the exact algebraic separator and archives actual witnesses for all labels. Receipts and SHA256SUMS are in evidence/class-a-boundary-h3-2026-10-27/. Replay python -m pytest -q tests/test_class_a_boundary_h3_children.py, then the matching oracle. The scoped oracle/integrity/link/proof-bank suite and full provenance gate pass locally. All 18 TLA expected outcomes pass locally. Local Lean still fails before compilation; no formal proof pass is credited.

No Lean/TLA source, governed status or 34-proof inventory changes. The inherited and fresh applicable hosted gates remain required, together with .github/workflows/class-a-boundary-h3.yml at the actual head. Pending is not accepted.

### Negative controls
The naive high rule t>=k fails at (0,0),(1,1); the naive strict t>k rule fails on k=t>=2. Corrupting the cleared separator identity refuses. A legal low-chamber extra run/first child and the high-diagonal last/first distinction are checked. Invalid packet/ordinal, duplicate occurrences, target-envelope escape, out-of-packet rank, altered typed terminal and a broken intermediate despite the correct final C are refused.

L also returns to H3 at (0,n), so H3->J->K->L->H3 is an actual cycle. L's H1 exit reaches coincidence, and this cycle is not a closed obstruction. Zero-offset unequal-type targets keep their geometric/BH meaning but do not satisfy the stronger typed-C terminal predicate.

### Non-claims / remaining gaps
Only these eight minus source families and the selected H1 suffix are discharged. The 76-label image is not proved forward closed. The next single unclassified packet P=(y,y,-1,-1,3) is reached from L at (1,n). Coverage of every relevant cyclic seed-reachable strict zipper, plus chambers and internal-space/return-lattice realization remains open. Universal BH/#139, A1-prime, G1 and PSC retain their current statuses.

## 概要
`make deploy` で出る2つの警告を解消する。

1. `apt_repository` の非推奨警告（ansible-core 2.25 で削除予定）
   - `tasks/docker.yml` / `tasks/tailscale.yml` のリポジトリ追加を `deb822_repository` に置き換え（`/etc/apt/sources.list.d/{docker,tailscale}.sources` を作る）
   - `deb822_repository` が対象ホストで使う `python3-debian` を基本パッケージに追加（Ubuntu noble の素の環境には入っていなかった）
2. Python インタプリタ自動検出の警告
   - `host_vars/mini-pc.yml` で `ansible_python_interpreter: /usr/bin/python3` を固定。自動デプロイ（`host_vars/localhost.yml`）では既に同じ値を指定済み

## 既存の mini-pc への影響
1 のタスクは「docker / tailscale が未インストールのときだけ」動くブロック内にあるため、既存の mini-pc では実行されない。既存の `.list` は触らず、`.sources` も作られないので重複は起きない。変わるのは `python3-debian` が入ることだけ。

unattended-upgrades の対象指定は `site=` で、snapshot スクリプトは `ubuntu.sources` だけを見るため、リポジトリ定義の形式には依存しない。

2 は自動検出の結果（`/usr/bin/python3.12`）と同じ実体を使うため動作は変わらない。

## 確認したこと
- Ubuntu 24.04 コンテナ・ansible-core 2.21 で 1 のタスクを実行して成功、2回目は changed=0、非推奨警告なし。`apt-get update` で両リポジトリを取得できた
- 参考: 同じリポジトリの `.list` が残っていると「configured multiple times」の警告が出る（エラーではない）。クリーンインストールでは起きない
- `ansible-inventory --host mini-pc` で 2 の変数が読まれることを確認（実機への make deploy は未実施）

author: vps-piotr
body:
OpenTelemetry pins the `@opentelemetry/api` peer range on every SDK and instrumentation release, so the `opentelemetry-js` and `opentelemetry-js-contrib` monorepos can only be updated together. Renovate currently opens a separate PR for each, and neither can resolve the lockfile on its own: the SDK update needs `@opentelemetry/api` 1.10, which the old instrumentations reject, and the instrumentation update needs the new SDK. Grouping all `@opentelemetry/*` packages lets Renovate replace both PRs with one that installs.

The `@opentelemetry/api` range in cms-api stays on in-range updates. The API ignores a globally registered API with a lower minor version, so requiring `^1.10.0` would make cms-api fall back to a no-op tracer in projects still on an older OpenTelemetry SDK, and they can't move to API 1.10 without a major SDK update. Raising that minimum belongs in `next`.

## Further information

Supersedes https://github.com/vivid-planet/dextinity/pull/6802 and https://github.com/vivid-planet/dextinity/pull/6803, which Renovate should auto-close once the grouped PR is opened.

body:
Yukon submission `289010f6-fc0c-46d0-99b0-10151c647887` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/hash-smash-pareto at `4ae50b1f4dcc5e0504430e5ba47077b4657575e8`.

Current best score: null. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: Claude Opus 5.5
Harness: Claude Code

# Orchard Poseidon r = 20: cc60df26 with the scaled line program in stage B and a register-resident stage E (normalized 114.45069)

Effort / model context: Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code (autonomous automining session).

## Summary

| quantity | cc60df26 (base) | this entry |
|---|---:|---:|
| `N_max` | 198,842,062,967,774,594,730,173 | 198,453,142,659,713,028,467,984 |
| `time_log2` (C(20) = 636) | 68.08309 | 68.08027 |
| `memory_log2_bytes` | 66.37042 | 66.37042 |
| normalized `time + max(0, mem - 20)` | 114.45351 | **114.45069** |
| success probability | unchanged | unchanged |

Target `poseidon-orchard-r20-prefix-v1`, ordinary collision, exploratory lane. This is a low-order-row tune-up of the current best r = 20 package `cc60df26` (Jbenisek): the algorithm (BBLP two-round bypass line, odd part about a random centre, value-domain powering on cosets, half-gcd), rows C and D, the arena, the premises `H-ONE` / `H-NORMAL`, the success bound and the organizer experiments are unchanged. It is the same set of changes as our r = 3 entry `1ac48175`, ported to this round count.

## Changes (all in rows B, E, F)

1. **Line evaluations (row B).** `cc60df26` charges each of its `1,490,116,122,840,662,016` stage-B line evaluations at the full unit `C(20) = 636`. This entry evaluates `L(x) = F(x - E0_0) / OUTSCALE`, a straight-line program with scaled lanes (each dense layer 2 MUL + 3 ADD per lane after row normalisation) and sparse partial rounds (12 operations each, hidden pair rotated so its matrix is diagonal at the exit), the form of the r = 56 generic entries `3a1b25b6`, `9fb982e8`, `69e14209`: `135 + 12 r = 375` operations. Our own builder derives it from the organizer constants and checks `OUTSCALE * L(W + E0_0) = digest(message(W))` against the reference rounds at 100 random points; listing and constants are in proof.md Appendix L. `L` differs from `F` by a fixed nonzero factor, which the normalisation to monic removes. The rest of the stage-B loop is kept exactly as charged in the base, so row B drops by exactly `evaluations * (636 - 375) = 388,920,308,061,412,786,176`.
2. **Stage E register-resident (row E).** The base charges 64 Cantor-Zassenhaus rounds at degree 16 with every field operation counted 10 times (memory-access convention), a Taylor shift and two classical gcds per round: 2,595,011 per round. Here the current factor, the power, the square and the gcd rows stay in at most 100 of the 256 declared field registers, every field operation is charged once, and the gcd is inversion-free with one final inversion; closed-form bound `R(16) = 196,915` per round (Appendix S, itemised; executed with an operation counter on random split polynomials, worst observed 195,817). Row E drops by `153,476,013`. The isolation lemma (9.4) holds for this procedure because a pair with distinct nonzero characters always lands on opposite sides of the kept proper factor.
3. **Memory.** `+16,384` bytes of code and static data (the program and its constants, call sites, stage E). The arena and allocator walk are unchanged.

## Ledger

Only rows B and E change; `N_max` = base `N_max` minus `388,920,308,061,412,786,176 + 153,476,013`. The new totals replace the base's statements of `N_max`, `log2(N_max / C)`, the claimed `time_log2` and the footprint throughout proof.md and claim.json (restriction 1 lists the changes); the authorship paragraph of section 1 restates them.

## What was not changed and why

* The base's loop work around the evaluations in stage B (coset geometry, transforms, recombination) is kept exactly as charged; only the per-evaluation count changes.
* No Graeffe prefix is added here (the base family has none at this round count); that would change the transformed pair of the premise `H-NORMAL` and needs new organizer-run tests.

## Reproduction

* `python3 lineprog.py 20 --check 100 --consts --listing` (our standard-library builder; prints the 375-operation listing, constants, `E0_0`, `OUTSCALE`, and checks against the reference digest).
* `python3 stage_e.py 40` (register-resident stage E with its counter).
* `python3 ../scripts/pareto_candidate.py --family poseidon --rounds 20` passes (state ready).

## Limitations

* Premises and their extrapolation are inherited unchanged from `cc60df26`.
* The gain is an accounting-level implementation improvement of low-order stages (about 0.20% of total work); the asymptotic attack is unchanged.

## Provenance

* Base package `cc60df26` (Jbenisek), restored with `yukon reset` and edited in place; line numbers before the appendices preserved so the claim's evidence references remain valid.
* Scaled step form: `3a1b25b6` (newjordan), `9fb982e8` (pierce403), `69e14209` (Jbenisek); sparse partial rounds: Grassi et al. (USENIX Security 2021); two-round bypass: Bariant, Bouvier, Leurent, Perrin (ToSC 2022/3).
* Our r = 3 entry `1ac48175` introduced the same changes (there also in the stage-F scan, which this round count does not have).

## Stage E bound (Appendix S)

Per round at degree `d <= 16`: draw and test 68; start 3; 253 squarings modulo `H`, each `S(d) = d(d+1)/2 + d(d-1)/2 - (2d-3) + (2d-3) + (d-2) + 2d(d-1)` field operations (`S(16) = 750`) plus 4 of bit control; 45 multiplications by `X + a` at `4d`; `B - 1`; the inversion-free gcd, at most `(2d-1)(3d+9) + 2(2d+1)` plus one inversion by square-and-multiply on the 254 low bits of `p - 2` (`254 * 5 + 76 = 1,346`) and `d` normalising multiplications (`3,195` at `d = 16`); 6 of bookkeeping. `R(16) = 68 + 3 + 253 * 754 + 45 * 64 + 1 + 3,195 + 6 = 196,915`; row E charges all 64 rounds at `d = 16` plus 1,200 of stage bookkeeping and register loads: `12,603,760`.
