body:
Sin issue: estas son las candidatas 1, 2, 5 y 7 de la retro de la etapa 0. Las otras (3, 4 y 6) van en #27.

## Qué cambia
- **El presupuesto de Opus incluye las sesiones interactivas** (candidata 5). `consumo_semanal("opus")` suma también los tokens ponderados de las sesiones de Claude Code de este repo y de sus worktrees, que lee de `~/.claude/projects/` (o de `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`). Cada mensaje cuenta una sola vez. `--informe` muestra esa parte por separado. Las corridas `claude -p` del despachador usan `--no-session-persistence`, así que no se cuentan dos veces. ADR 0011 queda actualizado.
- **El despachador no corre `--hasta-vaciar` dentro de una sesión de Claude** (candidata 2). Si `CLAUDECODE` está definida, sale con código 2 y pide usar una terminal aparte. En la etapa 0 se gastaron 68 comandos y 6 avisos vigilando el despachador desde una sesión con unos 240k tokens de contexto.
- **El protocolo pasa a `docs/protocolo-agentes.md`** (candidata 7). Etiquetas, Opus o Codex, revisión cruzada, bloqueos y una sección nueva, "Sesiones de Claude", salen de `AGENTS.md`, que baja de 113 a 66 líneas. Queda un puntero en la sección "Protocolo".
- **Las sesiones cortas quedan escritas** (candidata 1): planificar termina al crear los issues, el despachador lanza a Opus con `claude -p` limpio, `--solo-codex` se usa solo mientras haya una sesión abierta a mano, y se vuelve a Claude solo ante `bloqueado` o `necesita-criterio`.

## Cómo se prueba
- `pruebas/test_despachador_presupuesto.py`, nuevo, con 4 pruebas. Las 3 del presupuesto fallan contra `main`. La de `CLAUDECODE` reemplaza `ciclo` con un `pytest.fail`, así que si falta la protección, falla y no lanza nada.
- A mano: `--informe` da 8.766.439 ponderados esta semana (438%). `--hasta-vaciar` desde Claude sale con código 2.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format` y `pytest` (272 pasan, 24 se saltan sin MySQL) en verde en local. `mapa_capacidades --verificar` también da bien.

## Rutas sensibles
- [x] No toca `reglas/`, `migraciones/`, `comun/migrar.py`, `sincronizacion/`, `permisos/` ni `salud/`
- [ ] Toca rutas sensibles: necesita revisión de Opus

Toca `scripts/despachador*`, `AGENTS.md` y un ADR, que según AGENTS.md le corresponden a Opus.

## Definición de terminado
- [ ] CI en verde (ruff, pytest, migraciones, secretos)
- [x] `docs/capacidades.toml` y el mapa actualizados, si cambia una capacidad (no cambia ninguna)
- [x] `INDICADORES.md` actualizado, si se movió código citado (no cita estos archivos)
- [x] ADR provisional o `necesita-criterio`, si se decidió algo no cubierto (ADR 0011 actualizado)

## Notas para el próximo agente
- **Al fusionar, Opus queda al 438% esta semana.** Según ADR 0011, los issues `ejecutor:opus` que no son sensibles pasan a Codex (`pasar-a-codex`) hasta el lunes, empezando por #20. Si 2 M es poco para la cuota real, hay que recalibrar `semanal_opus` en el cierre de la etapa 0. Lo decide el usuario.
- Se cuentan todos los modelos de Claude, no solo Opus, porque comparten la cuota.
- La carpeta de sesiones de Claude Code sale de reemplazar en la ruta todo lo que no es letra ni número por `-`. Se compara por prefijo sin distinguir mayúsculas, así que `gimnasio-pro-trabajo-issue-N` también cuenta.
- Trampa: una prueba que llame a `main()` tiene que reemplazar `ciclo`. Mientras escribía este PR, una versión sin ese reemplazo corrió contra `main`, lanzó el despachador real y dejó #20 en `bloqueado` (`claude -p` falló por falta de login y no gastó tokens).

author: buddhika75
body:
## Summary
- **#24806:** a Pharmacy Direct Issue got a bill number with an empty prefix (leading `/`) under the prefix-based Transfer Issue numbering strategies, because `Bill Number Suffix for PHARMACY_DIRECT_ISSUE` defaults to blank. When it is blank, `TransferIssueDirectController.saveBill()` now stores the default `DI` before numbering. This is the same pattern already used for GRN (`GRN`) and purchase orders (`POA`, `POR`). A prefix set by a hospital is left as is.
- **#24807:** `TransferReceiveNativeSqlService` and `TransferIssueNativeSqlService` tried to `INSERT IGNORE` into a `BILL_FORWARDREFERENCEBILLS` join table that does not exist. `Bill.forwardReferenceBills` is `mappedBy = "backwardReferenceBill"`, so the `backwardReferenceBill_ID` both services already set *is* the link. The insert always failed and logged "Could not insert forwardReferenceBill link" on every settle. It is removed.

## Testing (local Payara, Playwright, copy of a hospital DB)

author: henrikogaard
body:
Linear: OCT-750

## What

A Code Project can now store a disposable-desktop recipe. The recipe is journaled, only a local window can set it, the server validates it, and the lease service reads it. Before this change the lease service's recipe lookup always returned nothing, so every lease command was refused.

- **Contracts** (`packages/contracts/src/projects.ts`, `desktopLease.ts`):
  - Optional `desktopRecipe` on a Code Project and its summary.
  - Command `change-code-project-desktop-recipe` (`recipe: null` removes the recipe), its result, and event `project.code-desktop-recipe-changed@1`.
  - Desktop pane request `recipe-providers` and its answer.
  - `decodeLeasableDesktopProvider`.
- **Domain** (`packages/domain/src/projectPolicy.ts`): `changeCodeProjectDesktopRecipe`.
  - Only a Code Project can hold a recipe.
  - The provider must be one this host offers for leasing now.
  - A host-local recipe cannot allow network.
  - A save that changes nothing is refused.
  - Removing a recipe is always allowed.
- **Server:**
  - `projectService.ts` handles the command; `runtimeRegistry.ts` and `projectProjection.ts` register and project the event.
  - `projectRoutes.ts` returns 403 to a paired device.
  - New `computerUse/projectDesktopRecipe.ts` is the lease service's lookup: the thread's Code Project, only while it is active. It is wired in `wiring/computerUse.ts`, `wiring/workspace.ts` and `server.ts`.
  - `desktopPaneRoutes.ts` answers `recipe-providers`.
  - **Review fix:** `desktopLeaseService.ts` now checks a running desktop's frames against the screen it was acquired with, not the recipe's current screen.
- **Web:**
  - New `projects/ProjectDesktopRecipeSection.tsx`, shown under **Disposable desktop** in the Code Project overview. It sets, saves and removes a recipe, and asks before removing.
  - Plumbing through `useProjectController.ts`, `shellActions.ts`, `App.tsx`, `ThreadPaneContainer.tsx` and `WorkspaceView.tsx`.
  - The pane's "no recipe" message now points to the Project's settings.
- **Docs:** `docs/design/disposable-desktops.md` (new "Built: recipe storage" section, delivery state), `docs/architecture.md` summary, and `apps/docs/advanced/browser-and-computer-use.md` ("Setting a desktop recipe").

## How to verify

All results below were run fresh on head `6548d651a` (branch merged with `origin/main` `2a694a803`), in a Linux container.

| Acceptance | Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stored and journaled; survives a restart | `projectDesktopRecipe.test.ts`: saves through `ProjectService` on a real journal and reads the recipe back after a restart | pass |
| Set only from a local window | `projectRoutes.test.ts`: a paired device gets 403 and nothing runs; a local window gets 200. The remote route policy already gives a paired device no action for Project POSTs | pass |
| Validated on the server | `projectService.test.ts`: recipes the schema refuses are refused and nothing is journaled. The fixture offers the recipe's provider, so only the schema can refuse, and a valid save is the control (this review tightened the test). `projectPolicy.test.ts`: provider and network refusals, Work and Chat Projects, no-op saves | pass |
| Editor offers only providers the host has ready | `ProjectDesktopRecipeSection.test.tsx` (4 cases); `desktopPaneRoutes.test.ts` (provider list) | pass |
| Lease service reads the stored recipe, end to end | `projectDesktopRecipe.test.ts` acquires from the stored recipe; the screen and limits reach the driver. Removing the recipe makes the sweep release the desktop as `recipe-removed`, and the next start is refused. **Red before:** the builder reports that with the old always-empty lookup, the acquire was refused | pass |
| Editing a recipe applies to the next desktop (spec) | `desktopLeaseService.test.ts`, "bounds a running desktop's frames by the screen it started with…". **Red before the fix:** it failed with `no-frame` after the screen shrank | pass |
| Rendered editor | Builder's Playwright run, not repeated in this review: light and dark themes, 1280px and 390px wide, 4 states, no console errors, no horizontal overflow | builder evidence |

### Checks

- Focused tests:
  - domain `projectPolicy` (32)
  - contracts `projects` and `desktopLease` (91)
  - server `src/computerUse` plus the persistence registry and projection (178)
  - server Project service and routes, pane routes, recipe test (64)
  - web `ProjectDesktopRecipeSection` and `src/desktop` (14)
- Typecheck run one package at a time: server and web clean after the merge. The builder reported contracts, domain and client-runtime clean; those packages had no changes after the merge.
- `bun run fmt:check`, `bun run lint` (exit 0; the warnings are in untouched files), `bun run style:check`, `git diff --check` all pass.
- Not run locally: `bun run verify` and the full server and web suites (hosted CI covers them).

## Rules resolved in the spec (please confirm)

- Only a Code Project holds a recipe. Work gets one when Work leasing is delivered.
- A recipe must name a provider the host offers **now**. So on a host where no provider is ready, a save is refused, but removing still works.
- A host-local recipe cannot set `network: "allow"`. A cloud provider's recipe could store it until the cloud slice sets its own rule.
- Removing the recipe, changing its provider or credential reference, or archiving the Project ends running desktops as `recipe-removed` at the next sweep. A new screen size or new limits apply only to the next desktop.

## Remaining

- **Likely merge conflict with `feature/disposable-desktop-cloud-driver`.** Both branches edit the same areas:
  - `wiring/computerUse.ts`: the `providers:` and `recipe:` lines sit next to each other.
  - The decode exports in `packages/contracts/src/desktopLease.ts`.
  - `desktopPaneRoutes.ts`, `desktopLeaseService.ts` (this PR's frame fix touches `LiveLease`, the acquire entry and `frame`), and the docs.
  - Whichever lands second has to merge both sides.
- **Follow-ups:**
  - The server does not check that a recipe's `credentialRef` exists in a credential store. The cloud slice should check it.
  - `OctantNumberStepper` is styled only by `settings.css`, so it may be unstyled outside Settings (`AgentRunSettingsPanel`).
- **Maintainer:** nothing new beyond confirming the rules above.

## Checklist

- [x] Existing or new coverage and applicable acceptance checks prove the changed behavior; omissions are explained
- [x] Applicable local checks pass under AGENTS.md; required exact-head CI must pass before merge
- [x] Current specification and affected user docs describe the resulting behavior; conflicting summaries are reconciled
- [x] No unrelated changes

author: dericknor
body:
## Ringkasan

Mengganti Access Point bawaan HomeSpan dengan **provisioning WiFi lewat
Bluetooth**, memakai protokol provisioning Espressif. Berpasangan dengan app
iOS **DapurSetup** yang memakai SDK ESPProvision.

Pengguna tidak lagi perlu berpindah jaringan WiFi atau membuka halaman web:
buka app, pindai QR di badan perangkat, pilih WiFi, selesai.

Bertumpu di atas `feat/homekit-homespan`.

## Cara kerja

`homeSpan.setApFunction()` mengarahkan HomeSpan ke `bleProvisioning()`,
sehingga alur ini jalan saat kredensial WiFi belum ada, atau saat `A` diketik
di Serial Monitor. Kredensial hasil provisioning disimpan lewat
`setWifiCredentials()`, lalu board menyala ulang dan masuk mode HomeKit.

`NETWORK_PROV_SCHEME_HANDLER_FREE_BTDM` melepas memori Bluetooth begitu
provisioning selesai, jadi BLE tidak membebani RAM saat HomeKit berjalan.

## PoP unik per perangkat

PoP (PIN provisioning) **tidak di-hardcode**. Diacak 8 karakter saat boot
pertama dan disimpan di NVS, jadi setiap board punya PIN sendiri — tidak ada
satu PIN yang sama untuk semua unit, dan PIN tidak ikut terkompilasi ke
dalam app.

Kamus karakternya tanpa `0 O 1 l I` supaya tidak salah baca kalau ditulis
tangan. PoP disampaikan ke app lewat QR yang dicetak ke Serial Monitor
memakai generator QR bawaan ESP-IDF.

⚠️ Kunci `"security":1` **wajib ada** di JSON QR. Tanpa itu SDK iOS
menganggap Security 2 dan pemasangan gagal tanpa pesan yang jelas.

## Perubahan lain

**Nama BLE** diberi akhiran 6 digit MAC (`DAPUR_xxxxxx`) agar beberapa board
bisa dibedakan di daftar app.

**Timeout 5 menit** — kalau tidak ada app yang menghubungi, board menyala
ulang dan masuk mode provisioning lagi, bukan menggantung selamanya.

**Perintah Serial Monitor baru:** `@Q` menampilkan ulang PoP + QR, `@R`
membuat PoP baru (QR lama jadi tidak berlaku).

## ⚠️ Partition Scheme naik ke Huge APP

**Tools → Partition Scheme → `Huge APP (3MB No OTA)`.**

Stack Bluetooth menambah sekitar 320 KB. Hasil akhir 1.760.893 byte — masih
muat di Minimal SPIFFS tapi hanya menyisakan ~10%, terlalu mepet untuk
pengembangan lanjutan.

```
Sketch uses 1760893 bytes (55%) of program storage space. Maximum is 3145728 bytes.
Global variables use 64036 bytes (19%) of dynamic memory.
```

## Pengujian

Diuji di perangkat, bukan hanya compile: provisioning berhasil, board
tersambung WiFi di 2,4 GHz, dan ter-pair dengan Apple Home
(`Database Validation: Warnings=0, Errors=0`).

## Catatan untuk reviewer

- **Firmware dan app harus sinkron.** Prefiks `DAPUR_`, format JSON QR, dan
  kode pairing HomeKit dipakai di kedua sisi. Mengubah salah satu tanpa yang
  lain akan mematahkan provisioning.
- Kode pairing HomeKit masih di-hardcode. Dari tiga identitas perangkat,
  baru PoP yang jadi unik per unit; kode HomeKit menyusul.
- **Jangan squash saat merge** kalau PR `feat/homekit-homespan` di-merge
  terpisah — branch ini bertumpu di atasnya dan akan perlu rebase.

author: lorancdaniel
body:
## Podsumowanie

Poprawki błędów i porządki w scraperze przepisów oraz w skryptach bazy danych. Frontend (`front/`) bez zmian.

### Naprawione błędy
- **Parsowanie czasu przygotowania** – wartość w formacie ISO 8601 (np. `PT1H30M`) dawała `int("P")` → nieobsłużony `ValueError`, który przerywał program. Teraz czas jest poprawnie zamieniany na minuty (`PT1H30M` → 90; obsługiwana jest też sama liczba minut).
- **Duplikaty** – każde uruchomienie dodawało ten sam przepis od nowa. Teraz przepis z tym samym `zrodlo_url` jest aktualizowany.
- **Brakujące elementy strony** – `<li>` bez `<span>` przerywał przetwarzanie całego przepisu; przepis bez nazwy kończył się `IntegrityError` (kolumna `nazwa NOT NULL`). Teraz składnik bez `<span>` jest brany z całego `<li>`, a przepis bez nazwy jest pomijany z komunikatem.
- **Pobieranie strony** – dodany `timeout` i nagłówek `User-Agent` (wcześniej zawieszony serwer blokował program bez końca).
- **Sesja bazy** – przy błędzie zmiany są wycofywane, a sesja zamykana; błędy bazy dają czytelny komunikat i kod wyjścia 1.
- Opis i instrukcja zachowują podział na akapity zamiast sklejania kroków w jeden ciąg.

### Porządki
- Jeden model `Przepis` w `database/models.py` i jedna konfiguracja połączenia w `database/session.py` zamiast trzech kopii. `create_database.py` tworzy tabelę z modelu; **schemat tabeli się nie zmienił**, więc istniejąca baza działa bez migracji.
- Dane połączenia czytane ze zmiennych środowiskowych (`DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_NAME`) zamiast zapisanego w kodzie hasła.
- Adres przepisu można podać jako argument wiersza poleceń.
- `README.md` przekonwertowany z UTF-16 do UTF-8 (wcześniej wyświetlał się na GitHubie jako krzaczki) i uzupełniony o instrukcję uruchomienia.
- Dodane `requirements.txt` i `.gitignore`.

### Zmiany w uruchamianiu
- Przed uruchomieniem trzeba ustawić hasło: `export DB_PASSWORD=...`
- Skrypty uruchamia się z katalogu głównego repozytorium:
  - `python -m database.create_database`
  - `python -m scraper.recipe_scraper <url>`

## Testy
Na lokalnym PostgreSQL 16:
- `create_database` – utworzenie bazy oraz ponowne uruchomienie, gdy baza już istnieje,
- scraper na stronie testowej – dodanie przepisu, a przy drugim uruchomieniu aktualizacja zamiast duplikatu,
- strona bez przepisu, odpowiedź 404 i błędne hasło do bazy – czytelny komunikat i kod wyjścia 1,
- `parse_duration` dla `PT30M`, `PT1H30M`, `P1DT2H`, `45`, małych liter i niepoprawnych wartości.

Nie testowane na prawdziwej stronie aniagotuje.pl (niedostępna ze środowiska testowego) – selektory HTML są takie same jak wcześniej.

author: m33ch1384
body:
## Tonk "Play again" recap flake: a test-timing bug, not an app bug

**Symptom:** in the offline Tonk e2e, after `mode-again` the recap stays visible and `waitFor({ state: 'hidden' })` times out at 20 s. It was seen on live and in 3D runs, and it reproduced on the V10d branch (both 3D and 2D runs).

**Root cause:** Play again correctly deals a **new** game, but a new 4-seat Tonk game can end on the deal.
- The test uses 7 cards with jokers wild. An instant win (dealt 49/50) is worth +2 from each player, so +6 points, which reaches the 5-point target. The new game is therefore over immediately and its own recap appears ("Hand 1 · instant win on the deal").
- Engine simulation with the test options: **1,069 of 4,000 seeds (26.7%)** end at `newGame`.
- The app behaves correctly (recap state, rules and scoring are untouched). The test's assumption that the recap always hides was wrong.

**Fix (test only):**
- After Play again, wait for either the table to return or a fresh one-hand "instant win on the deal" recap.
- Allow up to 6 games to see the between-hands flow.

**Verified:** with this test, the V10d branch mode-play passes in forced 2D (71 ✓, exit 0) and clears the Tonk section in 3D.

**Possible UX follow-up (not in this PR, needs Demetrius):** when a rematch ends on the deal, the recap looks unchanged, so players may think the button did nothing. A short "New game: X won on the deal" cue would make it clear. No rule change needed.

author: onurtuncer
body:
core: one worker pool per Context (M10, part two; ADR-0007)

ADR-0007's review decided that the worker threads of a parallel Context
belong to a pool the Context owns, created on first use with its thread
count, shared by copies made with With..., another thread count making
another pool, and no operation creating threads of its own. ParallelFor
built a static_thread_pool per call.

Stereon/Core/Parallel.hpp now declares an opaque WorkerPool and a
PoolHandle (Parallel.cpp starts the pool on the first Get(), from any
thread, once, with std::call_once, so the header still includes no
stdexec). The Context holds the handle through a shared_ptr: copies share
it, WithThreadCount with another count makes a fresh handle, and
GetWorkerPool() returns the pool, or nothing for the serial scheduler, so
that ParallelFor, which now takes the pool, runs on the calling thread.
The four callers (ProjectAll on curves and surfaces, the Booleans' face
pairs and region seeds) pass ctx.GetWorkerPool(). A body on the pool must
not wait on it; the Booleans already run nested work with a serial copy.

tests/core/ParallelTests.cpp: chunks independent of the thread count at
three grains; no pool, the calling thread; a Context's copies share its
pool, the serial scheduler keeps and ignores it, another count is another
pool of at most that many threads; eight threads asking at once start one
pool. The drilled slab's speed-up holds on the shared pool: 5.7x at 100
holes, 8 threads on a 6-core machine.

## What changed

author: yanglebupt
body: ### 🔗 Linked issue #111 #24 ### 🧭 Context When using non-`:` delimiters (`-` / `--`), icon completion behaves inconsistently with what the user typed: - The suggestion detail always uses `config.delimiters[0]`, so typing `mp--` shows `mp:arrow` instead of `mp--arrow`. - The replace range starts right after the prefix. Since `-` is also matched by `[\w-]`, the range covers `collection + delimiter`, so VS Code filters by `mp--arr` rather than `arr`, and accepting an item replaces the whole text. In addition, when a project provides a custom collection (via `iconify.customCollectionJsonPaths`) whose prefix is the same as a built-in one (e.g. `weui`), the built-in collection always wins. Completion, inline annotations and hover previews then show the wrong icons. This PR: - **Completion**: keeps the delimiter the user typed. The suggestion detail shows `mp--arrow` / `mp-arrow` / `mp:arrow` to match the input, and accepting an item only completes the icon name after the delimiter. - **Custom collections**: when a custom collection has the same prefix as a built-in one, the custom collection is used for completion, icon loading and previews. Cached previews are cleared when a custom collection is (re)loaded, so icons already rendered from the built-in set get refreshed. ### 📚 Description #### 1. Icon completion keeps the delimiter the user typed Previously: - The completion `detail` always used `config.delimiters[0]`, so typing `mp--` showed `mp:arrow` in the suggestion list. - The replace range started right after the prefix. With `-` / `--` delimiters (matched by `[\\w-]`), the range covered `collection + delimiter`, so VS Code filtered by `mp--arr` instead of `arr` and accepting an item replaced the whole text. Now `REGEX_NAMESPACE` captures the partial icon name after the delimiter. Icon items only replace that part, and the detail uses the typed delimiter. | Input | Detail | After accepting `arrow` | |---|---|---| | `mp--` | `mp--arrow` | `mp--arrow` | | `mp-` | `mp-arrow` | `mp-arrow` | | `mp:` | `mp:arrow` | `mp:arrow` | #### 2. Custom collections take priority over built-in ones with the same prefix When a custom collection (`iconify.customCollectionJsonPaths`) uses the same prefix as a built-in one (e.g. `weui`), the built-in set was always used for completion and preview. - `enabledCollections`: custom collections come first and override built-in ones with the same id; `enabledCollectionIds` is deduped. - `LoadIconSet`: look up custom collections before loaded/cached built-in sets. - `deleteTask`: clear `dataURLCache` when a custom collection is (re)loaded, so icons rendered from the built-in set before the custom one finished loading are refreshed. ### 🎯 Result ### ⚙️ VSCode Setting ```json { "iconify.customCollectionJsonPaths": ["./icons.json"], "iconify.delimiters": ["--"], "editor.quickSuggestions": { "strings": "on" }, "editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters": true, "editor.suggest.showInlineDetails": true, "iconify.inplace": true, "iconify.annotations": true, } ```

**Describe your changes**

Fix S3 output with both default and explicit client options. On current main, `to_json(filepath="s3://...")` fails because the writer requires `s3_options`; supplying that keyword instead sends it to the JSON encoder and raises another `TypeError`.

Remove the transport-only keyword before encoding and normalize omitted/None options to an empty mapping at S3 dispatch, matching the input path. Serializer options such as `indent` and `sort_keys` still reach the serializer, and the caller's options are preserved. The change adds no dependency or public method.

**Related issue**

Fixes #649.

**Validation**

- Final new regressions on unchanged Git base `e910141`: **13 errors** across two test methods; fixed source: all **13 subcases pass**.

- Independent real-boto3 localhost HTTP checks: original source **six TypeErrors and zero uploads**; fixed source **six successful PUTs**, verifying exact bytes, default/None/empty/custom configuration, JSON/YAML/TOML output, and existing success-path cleanup. author: willem-jaap
body:
A user's agent kept opening in a project they'd picked earlier for the same address, not the one they were looking at.

Two bugs in `ProjectResolver` caused it together:

- **A saved pick never expired.** `resolve()` checked `origins.json` first and trusted the folder as long as it existed, ahead of the loader's repository root and the process on the port. Ports get reused (5173 is every Vite app's default), so a later app on the same address went to the old folder. Picks now come last: they only cover addresses that can't be traced to a project, like containers without compose labels. The overlay only asks when detection fails, so this doesn't override anything the user chose deliberately.
- **On Windows, the port lookup missed IPv6.** `netstat -ano -p TCP` lists IPv4 sockets only, and Vite on `localhost` listens on `[::1]`. The lookup found nothing, the overlay asked, and the first bug kept that answer. Now it runs `netstat -ano`. `parseNetstat` already skips UDP rows and matches `[::1]:5173`.

Workaround for anyone on the current release: delete the address's entry from `~/.config/tencil/origins.json`.

## Tests

- Replaced "still prefers what the user picked for the address" with tests showing the port lookup and the loader's root both beat an earlier pick, and the pick is still used when neither finds anything.
- The same holds for a pick that's an Ensemble thread: the port lookup beats it, and it's used when nothing is found. (A thread whose dev server is on the port still comes first, as on master.)
- Added a Windows test with a `[::1]` listener.
- All three new tests fail against the old resolver. `pnpm check` passes.

Fixes PIX-2399

author: mrgoonie
body:
Closes #315

Ports the extra `fal tts` checks from the unmerged branch `claude/gracious-heisenberg-fm8nzl` onto the current structure (`speech-input.ts`, `speech-output.ts`, `speech-models.ts`).

## What changes
1. **Gemini dialogue is checked before submit**, against fal's live schema (`SpeakerConfig`, `SpeechTurn`). It needs exactly 2 `speakers` with distinct `speaker_id`s and voices from the list (spelling is canonicalised), plus at least one `turns` entry that names one of them and has non-empty `text`. A text or `--voice` given alongside a dialogue is refused, as are `speakers` without `turns` and fields the schema does not list. A malformed dialogue therefore costs nothing. A well-formed one still gets HTTP 422 from fal (#310); the docs now say so.
2. **`--input` values get the same checks as the flags**: text length in code points, the voice list, the `output_format` enum and the language code. The language code is now also checked on `--language`. `null` counts as unset, because fal's schemas allow it and playground payloads include it.
3. **A WAV with a header but no samples is refused** ("header but no audio samples"). This applies to `fal tts` and to `fal result --download`. Streamed WAVs with a data size of 0 are still accepted when samples follow the header.
4. **fal catalog paging stops on an empty page or a repeated cursor**, in both `fal voices --live` and `multix models --live`. The latter marks the list as `truncated`.

Docs: `docs-site` fal page (English and Vietnamese) and `skill/SKILL.md`.

## Evidence
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` are clean.
- `npm test`: 2145 passed, 22 skipped.
- `npm run check:mcp`: worker typecheck, tests and bundle check are clean.
- `npm run verify:docs`: 8/8.
- 9 new or changed tests fail on `dev` without the `src/` changes and pass with them.
- CLI run with no key; every case is refused before any request:
```
$ multix fal tts --input '{"turns":[{"speaker_id":"A","text":"Hi"}]}'
Error: --input turns needs "speakers": two {speaker_id, voice} entries
$ multix fal tts --input '{"speakers":[{"speaker_id":"A","voice":"Kore"},{"speaker_id":"A","voice":"Puck"}],"turns":[...]}'
Error: speakers[1].speaker_id "A" is repeated
$ multix fal tts -m elevenlabs/tts/eleven-v4 --input '{"text":"hi","language_code":"english!"}'
Error: --input language_code must be a language code such as en or vi, got "english!"
$ multix fal tts --input '{"prompt":"Hi","speakers":null,"turns":null}'
Error: FAL_KEY is not set ...   # null fields pass validation
```
- An isolated review is in `plans/reports/code-reviewer-261027-1004-fal-tts-input-checks.md`. It found one medium issue (`null` was refused), fixed in 4bf524b. Low findings 2–4 are fixed too. Finding 5 (an empty `data` chunk followed by a trailing `LIST` chunk) is lenient on purpose and is not changed.

body:
Lane network-accounting

`wipe_gate.sh` wrote the gate's `fetch RUN` under the lane's own key, which includes `witness/` (the cells' salts, the certified heads and the prompts), to `$OUT/bundle.tgz`, and custody uploads all of `$OUT`. This is INF-271's leak again. Three records in the store hold such a bundle:

- r20261026-172344-585d (the 17:23Z rehearsal, 9.8 MB);
- r20261026-180728-eda7 (Demo B session 1, about 106 MB);
- r20261027-044345-3b89 (Demo B session 2, about 106 MB).

The `wipe-egress/v1` arts and the `wipe_egress.py` runs hold public fields only.

The fix:

- The lane's fetch goes to `KEEP/RUN/fetch.tar.gz`. `KEEP` is 0700, by default `/workspace/research/lanes/network-accounting/gate` (the chain records' gate directory on cpu-2). A `KEEP` inside the run dir is refused before anything is sent.
- `$OUT/bundle.tgz` is now only what `fetch` gives any other key: the bundle less `witness/`. `wipe_egress.py` reads it unchanged.

NET-103's whole-node wipe (T = 16:05Z) runs this script. This PR touches no line that #5160 changes, and it merges cleanly onto both #5160 and #5218.

Tests: `benchmarks/network_traces/tests/test_wipe_gate.py` runs the whole script against a stub gate. It fails on main's script and passes here.

body: ## 问题 AFK 的 `implement-prd.ts`（以及另外六个 runner）在 GitHub Actions 里刷屏。 `verbose: true` 是 1.6.5 加的，目的是让 Read / Edit / MCP 这些 sandcastle 类型化 `toolCall` 事件不认识的工具调用可见。它的实现是照写每一行原始 stdout，于是把 Claude Code 在模型思考期间持续发出的心跳帧也写了进来： ```json {"type":"system","subtype":"thinking_tokens","estimated_tokens":42,"estimated_tokens_delta":4,…} ``` ## 实测（2026-10-27，Claude Code 2.1.311，本机中继 profile，一条真实 prompt） | 帧类型 | 条数 | 字节占比 | |---|---|---| | `system/thinking_tokens` | 227–342 | **58%** | | `system/hook_response` | 4 | 18% | | `system/init` | 1 | 11% | | `assistant` | 2 | 7% | | `result` | 1 | 3% | 真正的工具调用只有几行，其余是整个可见运行的心跳。用录下来的真实流做回放： **292 行 → 12 行，280 个心跳被丢弃，真实输出零损失。** ## 为什么不在 CLI 侧关 两条路都实测过，都不行： - `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_THINKING=1` → 仍发 232 帧 - `CLAUDE_CODE_THINKING_DISPLAY_UPDATES=0` → 仍发 342 帧 该帧属于 stream-json 的契约（交互式客户端拿它当 spinner），CLI 没有理由省略。 ## 改动 - **`quiet-heartbeats.ts`（新）**：包一层 `process.stdout.write`，按**解析后的** `type`/`subtype` 丢弃。不用子串——agent 可能在回答里引用这一行（本模块自己的 注释就是这种引用），子串匹配会把它一起吃掉。 - **`claudeProfile()` 里装一次**：七个 runner 都通过它拿 `run()` 参数，一处覆盖全部， 将来新增的 runner 自动继承。 - **退出时打印 `dropped N`**：帧名是外部产品的契约，改名会让过滤器**静默失效**； 这是唯一能区分「改名了」和「这轮确实没思考」的信号。 - **`quiet-heartbeats.check.ts`（新）+ CI 接线**：两种失效都无声（太宽吃掉输出 / 太窄放回刷屏），所以匹配本身要被钉住。 - **`upgrade-afk.sh` 1.7.30 步骤**：补丁位门控、幂等（重复执行不装第二次）， 锚点缺失时报告而不是半改。 - **`test/smoke.sh` 1.7.30 段**：新脚手架 / 1.7.29 升级 / 二次升级幂等 / 无锚点报告 / filter 自身 check 共 5 组断言。 - **ADR 0014**记录被否的三个方案（去掉 verbose、CLI 侧关、workflow 里 grep）和代价。 ## 验证 - `test/smoke.sh node` / `python` 全绿（含新增 1.7.30 段） - `python3 test/workflows.py` → 10 files passed - `node scaffold/.sandcastle/adr.check.mjs --base origin/main --all` → ok - `shellcheck -S warning bootstrap-afk.sh upgrade-afk.sh test/smoke.sh` → 0 - `tsc --strict` 对 `quiet-heartbeats.ts` + check → 0 - 真实流回放：292 → 12 行 - 对真实的 AI-Ops / Auto-Test 副本跑升级：profile.ts 与 afk-policy.yml 正确改动， 二次升级为 no-op Consumer 升级后需要按惯例重建镜像（Dockerfile 未变，但 `.sandcastle/` 变了）。 ---

author: letur
body:
Fixes #1604

## Intent

Callers that hand a session its first prompt must know whether the agent can take input yet, and thurbox owns the agent runtimes. Until now a caller pieced that together from `state`, and for a fresh agent that fires no hook before its first turn (Codex) it had to carry its own screen probe per agent. Fleet's `initial_codex_ready` is the example. This PR adds one agent-agnostic `ready` field so callers no longer need per-agent knowledge.

## What Changed

- `session get` and `session list` now carry `ready` (`Assessment::ready`):
  - `true`: the hook's last report is `idle` or `done`; or no hook has reported, an agent holds the pane, and its input line shows a drawn, empty composer (one prompt glyph left of the cursor).
  - `false`: `working`, `blocked` or `background`; parked; a pane with no agent; a contradicted report; or a fresh agent whose composer is not drawn yet.
  - `null`: nothing can say, for example the pane was not probed or its input line was unreadable. Callers should ask again.
- The input line is read only for a `running` session with no hook report, and only by a verb that probes the pane. A reported session costs no extra read.
- `composer::shows_prompt` is the stricter twin of `classify`'s `Empty`: a blank line, which is what a booting pane shows, is not a prompt.
- The contract is documented in `docs/ORCHESTRATION.md` → Readiness, the `session get` help and the `thurbox-session-status` skill.

## Risk Assessment

- The field is additive; existing fields keep their values. A peer reading the mirror shape ignores it.
- The pre-hook answer is a screen reading. Holding text, a dialog with a hidden cursor (Codex's update and folder-trust prompts) and a blank booting screen all read `false`. An agent whose composer prompt is not one of the known glyphs (`❯ › > → » $ % #`) would stay `false` until its first hook.
- `session list` without `--verify` answers `null` for a never-reported session, because it does not probe panes.

## Testing

- New end-to-end regression `cli_session_hook_state::a_session_is_ready_once_its_composer_is_drawn_and_then_as_its_hooks_say`. A stand-in Codex runs on a real tmux server: it boots (`ready: false`), then draws `› ` with a placeholder right of the cursor (`ready: true`, `hook_reported: false`); then `working` gives `false` and `idle` gives `true`. On `origin/main` it failed with `ready: null` (no such answer). A unit test pins `shows_prompt`.
- Checked live against the installed CLIs on a private tmux socket, with no input sent: Claude's empty composer reads `❯` left of the cursor, which counts as ready. Codex's update and folder-trust dialogs (hidden cursor, nothing left of it) read not ready. Codex's composer itself was not reached, because every folder tried needed a trust decision that would have saved config. author: cristianonescu
body:
Fill track (TRACKS.md). Calibrates plain fill against the PE-DESIGN 11.50 round-1 reference files (PR #34), measured black-box from their stitch data. The full analysis is in the shared notes (`fill-analysis.md`).

Rebased on main at 33f03aa (gui #37 and #41, pes-io #39, satin #40). This PR leaves those tracks' specs as they made them.

## What PE-DESIGN does (measured)
- **Under sewing (default on, Medium)** has two layers:
  - an edge run 1.0 mm inside the outline (holes included), each side split into equal stitches of ≤ 2.5 mm;
  - tatami rows across the fill direction (angle + 90°), 2.0 mm apart, 4.0 mm stitches, 1.2 mm (30 %) shift per row, 1.0 mm inside the outline.
  - It starts and ends at the shape's start point, and the top fill follows with running stitches (no jump).
- **Top fill:** 4.5 lines/mm, with the first and last rows on the outline (181 rows for 40 mm). Frequency shifts the grid Frequency × step pitch per row (0 / 1.0 / 2.0 mm for 0 / 25 / 50 %), so the specs' semantics are right.

## Changes
- `RegionSewing::new`, fill fields only: Fill density 2.5 → 4.5. Fill and Programmable fill now have under sewing on, with the new `UnderlayStyle::EdgeFill` (also available in the inspector and in `object.setRegion`).
  - Programmable fill density is unchanged (not measured).
  - The Frequency default stays ⅓, because `fill-frequency-default` pins it. PE's UI default is 30 %.
- `region.rs`: `fill_underlay` and `join_layers` make the under sewing run on into the top fill (in compile.rs). Fill has its own `FILL_UNDERLAY_INSET` (1.0 mm); satin's 0.5 mm `UNDERLAY_INSET` is untouched.
- `generate.rs`: `fill_edge_to_edge` places plain fill rows from edge to edge, as PE does.
- `openstitch-compat` measures, approved by the coordinator, with synthetic unit tests:
  - `rowShift` counts only fill rows (two consecutive interior needle points one stitch length apart), so under sewing and travel are skipped.
  - `stitchedArea` sums each row's needle extent, including the stitches into and out of the row from ≤ 0.5 mm away, and multiplies by the mean row gap. Re-measured: PE 839.9 mm², OpenStitch 839.9 mm², spec 833.5 mm².
  - Both changes are documented in COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md.
- Docs: the audit's "Uncalibrated numeric defaults" and the status table.

## Specs passing with their PE references (added here)
fill-frequency-0, fill-frequency-25, fill-frequency-50, region-travel-u-fill, region-travel-u-along-outline, region-travel-u-on-outline, hole-sewing-pentagon-star. No expected value was changed.

## Still out (references not included)
- **programmable-fill-45:** PE's angles turn counter-clockwise on screen (y up), so its default 45° measures 135° in the file. OpenStitch's turn clockwise. Per the coordinator's decision, a follow-up PR adopts PE's convention, with an .osd migration.
- **region-travel-u-gradation:** 619 stitches in PE against 1088 in OpenStitch. PE's default gradation pattern runs from about 50 % density at one side to about 11 % at the other. OpenStitch's `gradation: 50` runs from 100 % to 50 %. Matching it needs PE's max/min gradation model.

## Follow-up fixes (after the first CI runs)
- `join_layers` joins only the boundary between layers, follows the region's Running Stitch Path (as PE's U files do), and runs only when the region travels. A region with travel unset still jumps between its parts.
- The fill under sewing starts at the region's entry point on the outline. Edge-to-edge rows chain from the row end nearest the entry, and skip end rows shorter than 0.3 mm (a near-zero stitch at an ellipse's tip). They are sampled just past their line, so a row on a notch's edge doesn't run across the gap.
- Tests that check the top layer or Optimize's entry/exit set under sewing off explicitly, without loosening any assertion. The outline-path test uses 45° rows: at 0° the rows end on the notch edge, where inside and on-outline travel coincide, as they do in PE's own files.
- Golden values re-recorded with dated notes: `golden_badge` 3068 (main's 3071 minus 3 from the edge-to-edge rows) and `badge-golden.pes`.

## Checks
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: passes.
- `compat --status`: 23 of 23 specs pass; the status table is regenerated.
- `cargo test --workspace --locked --no-fail-fast`: passes locally on the rebased tree (main at 33f03aa).

author: bruceliubeiru
body:
## Failure reproduced
An Evidence Envelope with an unresolved material conflict could be transformed into `Needs verification` by deleting both the contradictory evidence and its conflict record. `evaluateDecisionDelta(resolve_conflict)` incorrectly reported `realized=true` even though no resolution basis was recorded.

## Minimal repair
Require each previously unresolved conflict to have a distinct after-state `resolved` or `not_material` disposition matching the original issue and at least one original evidence ID. Continue to reject still-acquired undispositioned contradictions. This is an Evidence Engine/control-state refinement, not a new collaboration gate.

## Challenge and counterexamples
- Silent deletion of contradiction and conflict: must fail.
- Genuine invalidation recorded with an auditable retained context pointer and `resolution_basis`: still passes.
- Unrelated resolved issue: fails.
- Unlinked evidence rekeys: fail closed until identity mapping exists.
- Two prior unresolved conflicts with only one disposition: fails.

## Validation
Isolated V8 execution of actual module function bodies: 19 semantic Evidence Envelope fixtures and five targeted conflict cases passed. Added tests to `scripts/validate-research-decision-delta.mjs` for full Node CI. No permission expansion, browser write, credential handling, or cross-surface reopen.

## Remaining limitations
`resolution_basis` is still an asserted explanation; the validator does not independently verify external evidence or guarantee independent execution snapshots.

author: waldekmastykarz
body:
Closes #1334

Adds a Dev Container Feature that installs Dev Proxy and trusts a per-container root certificate, following the spec in https://github.com/dotnet/dev-proxy/issues/1334#issuecomment-3967872434.

## Usage

```json
"features": {
  "ghcr.io/dotnet/dev-proxy/dev-proxy:1": {}
}
```

## What's included

- `features/src/dev-proxy`: the Feature (version `1.0.0`, versioned separately from Dev Proxy).
  - Options: `version` (`latest`, `beta`, `2.2.0` or `v2.2.0`) and `trustCertificate` (default `true`).
  - `install.sh` runs at build time as root. It installs dependencies (curl, unzip, ca-certificates, openssl, ICU) and resolves the version. It downloads the x64/arm64 Linux release into `/opt/devproxy`, symlinks `/usr/local/bin/devproxy` (plus `devproxy-beta` for betas) and creates `~/.config/dev-proxy` for the remote user. It also installs a root-owned cert-trust helper that the remote user can run with `sudo` and no password, then verifies `devproxy --version`. It's idempotent and non-interactive, and fails clearly on Alpine/musl and non-apt distros.
  - **No certificate is generated at build time**, so no CA private key ends up in image layers or prebuilds. In `postCreateCommand`, the remote user runs `devproxy cert ensure`, then the helper validates the certificate (`CA:TRUE`) and adds it to `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates` + `update-ca-certificates`.
  - `containerEnv`: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and `SSL_CERT_FILE`, all pointing to the system CA bundle.
  - The Feature doesn't auto-start Dev Proxy, set `HTTP(S)_PROXY` or support Java.
- `features/test/dev-proxy`: tests for `devcontainer features test`.
  - Autogenerated tests on debian, ubuntu and devcontainers/base:ubuntu. The duplicate test installs the Feature twice.
  - Scenarios: non-root user without sudo, specific versions (with and without `v`), beta, `trustCertificate: false` (verifies no cert is generated or trusted), and end-to-end trust through Dev Proxy for curl, Node.js, Python urllib and requests, and .NET.
  - Every test checks that no certificate exists outside the user's profile.
- Workflows:
  - `devcontainer-feature-test.yml`: runs on PRs/pushes touching `features/**`, on x64 and arm64 runners, plus metadata validation.
  - `devcontainer-feature-release.yml`: publishes to GHCR with `devcontainers/action` on pushes to `main` that touch `features/src/**`, or manually.
- Docs: the Feature README, a mention in the root README and the skill's installation reference, and a note in copilot-instructions.

## Design decisions and notes for reviewers

- **`installToolkit` option dropped.** Feature `customizations` are static metadata and can't depend on option values. The Feature always adds `garrytrinder.dev-proxy-toolkit`, and users can opt out with `"-garrytrinder.dev-proxy-toolkit"` in their `devcontainer.json` (documented).
- **Python 3.13+ and Dev Proxy v3:** Python 3.13 enables `VERIFY_X509_STRICT`, which rejects v3's leaf certificates because they lack an Authority Key Identifier. v4 (the Kestrel engine on `main`) already adds it. The runtimes scenario uses `beta` for this reason, and the limitation is documented in the Feature README.
- **Beta resolution** picks the newest beta tag whose Linux asset exists. v4.0.0-beta.13 currently has a tag but no assets.
- v4 creates the root certificate on any command, even `--version`. The install-time check runs in an isolated temporary HOME so no certificate is left in the image.

## After merging

- Make the `dev-proxy` GHCR package (`ghcr.io/dotnet/dev-proxy/dev-proxy`) public after the first publish.
- Optionally add the Feature to the [containers.dev index](https://github.com/devcontainers/devcontainers.github.io).

## Open questions from the spec

- Documenting a sidecar setup (Dev Proxy in a separate container) isn't covered here.
- The API port (8897) isn't forwarded or configured by the Feature.

## Testing

Ran `devcontainer features test` (CLI 0.89.0) locally with Docker on arm64. All autogenerated tests (debian, ubuntu, devcontainers/base:ubuntu, including the duplicate install) and all scenarios pass.

author: f1l1ph
body:
Wallets warn on any transaction sent to the private rollup, because they simulate it against Solana mainnet. A deposit asked for two wallet signatures, the second of them on the rollup. Now it asks for one, on mainnet only.

How:
- One long-lived deposit key per owner, random, wrapped under a non-exportable key in IndexedDB (the order-seed store, with storage persistence requested), created before any wallet prompt.
- One mainnet transaction: create the key's token account, transfer the amount to it, delegate it into the rollup under the key (plus the permission instruction on a sealed first deposit). The wallet signs and pays first, its returned transaction is checked unchanged, then the key co-signs. Worst case 1,175 of 1,232 bytes.
- The key signs in to the rollup itself, waits for its balance, and signs and pays deposit_tokens crediting the owner's account. No rollup transaction needs the wallet.
- Leftovers on the key (a refused or interrupted deposit) are credited automatically once when the terminal opens, and by hand from the transfers section. A refused recovery leaves no record and can be retried.
- Records begun by the old flow are refused on resume and returned with the existing Return flow.
- The first broadcast error is carried into the outcome instead of a silent wait, with addresses and tokens removed.

Builds on #19 (browser Buffer 64-bit methods); merge that first.

Checks: typecheck, eslint, prettier clean; vitest 1050/1050. Reviewed adversarially; the two valid findings (funds at rest under the key, signing order) are addressed. Not yet proven on mainnet: a real 1 USDC deposit is the release test.

author: petalas
body:
## Summary

Scoped mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. Every downset generated by three or more sunflower facets has an explicit nonsingular, symmetric, nonnegative integer disjointness-supported matrix whose number of positive eigenvalues equals its largest star size. The construction also gives the exact determinant. This resolves the disjoint-petal first case left by merged #5247, extending its two-facet result to any finite number of petals and any common core.

The new step chooses the leaf cross blocks simultaneously:

```text
B_ij = u_i u_j^T + 4 E_i^T E_j = H_i^T J_0 H_j
all off-diagonal leaf Schur blocks = 0
leaf diagonal blocks = diagonal(-1 on odd subsets, -3 on nonempty even subsets)
```

Credit Ellis, Filmus and Friedgut for [spectral Conjecture I](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.28404v1#S4), David Ganz's #2849 for atlas C070, and Nick Petalas's #5247 for the two-facet zeta/Schur construction and explicit open question. Classical zeta inversion and Sylvester's law retain their credit. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Predecessor files and credit lines are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before: #5247 leaves three disjoint facets open. For three two-element petals, keeping the dominant cross weights 3,3 and a leaf cross weight 1 gives inertia `(3,7,0)` and determinant -7.
- After: the new cross weights 3,3,5 give inertia `(2,8,0)` and determinant 9, attaining largest-star size 2. The written proof covers every sunflower size and petal count. The determinant is `(-1)^(N-s) 3^e`, where `e=2^c sum_(i>=1)(2^(a_i-1)-1)`.
- The standalone checker enumerates all 50 nonincreasing positive petal/core tuples with at least three petals and at most seven ground elements. It checks 23,333 actual matrix entries, literal largest stars, exact rational inertia and determinants, integer zeta congruences, all 785 leaf Schur entries and 13 named controls. Largest matrix order is 64. No predecessor verifier or two-facet case is replayed.
- Local CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass in 0.182 s and 0.184 s. The registered runner passes in 0.656 s. Both direct receipts agree exactly. Each registered command has a 120-second cap. These are verification durations.
- At head `b59f9c29bedfb3e2e227f63afb5f630e73a3cd6a`, committed-byte/source-history validation passes for all five files and canonical base `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`. Official export integrity and both read-only Git-free empty-PATH replays pass, with receipts identical to local execution. AST inspection and staged whitespace checks pass; the longest function is 44 lines.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -B research/sunflower-downset-inertia/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -W error -O -B research/sunflower-downset-inertia/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sunflower-downset-inertia
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/sunflower-downset-inertia --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 executable may replace that local path. Expected markers are `PASS_SUNFLOWER_DOWNSET_INERTIA`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Generated stdout receipts bind the five package files by SHA256; no receipt is handwritten or committed.

The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19214425) states the delivered scope. Live open/account PRs, active Discussions, local reservations, main README searches and merged topic searches were refreshed before committing. The cached search covered 416 open PRs and 5,309 Discussion records; sparse local-note coverage is incomplete. No literature-priority guarantee is claimed.

## Limitations

The universal theorem rests on the written informal proof; finite execution corroborates it. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. General overlapping-facet downsets and weighted-Hoffman certificates remain open here. No physical supplier, caller, precision, stock, full multiplication theorem, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. Lean, Docker and the selected cold replay were not run. No local registered check was left solely to CI. The verifier's fixed finite domains and managed-runtime/callback deviations are documented in the README.

## Open next questions

1. Extend the certificate to three facets with distinct nonempty pairwise intersections, starting with `{1,2}`, `{2,3}`, `{1,3}`. Cross-block entries must respect intersecting-pair zeros, so the present free cross-block prescription does not apply.
2. Determine whether smaller integer weights give sharp certificates for arbitrary sunflowers. The three-petal pairwise-weight control retains sharp inertia with determinant 5; no general minimum-weight assertion is made.

## Related open work

No matching open PR studying sunflower-downset inertia or this determinant appeared in the refreshed topic/body searches. #5247 is the merged mathematical predecessor. Shared atlas provenance alone does not identify the same object or quantity. Unpublished work remains outside this overlap check.

The completion refresh read the titles and bodies of this account's nine other open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-27T10:02:18Z: #5865, #5866, #5867, #5868, #5869, #5871, #5872, #5873 and #5874. None studies the sunflower-downset inertia or determinant proved here. #5867 mentions this PR as adjacent matrix work but counts finite-field connector repair ranks, a different quantity. No extra computations were run to validate those contributions or compare unrelated numbers.

## CI notes

At exact head `b59f9c29bedfb3e2e227f63afb5f630e73a3cd6a`, [run 40486899975](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40486899975) finished with **plan failed; replay skipped**. The only failed step is [Onboarding helper tests](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40486899975/job/122130841622). Its ten failure/error entries are all in unchanged `tests/test_research_current_assignment.py`, ending `FAILED (failures=8, errors=2, skipped=22)`, exit code 1.

The two errors are `KeyError: 'follow_up_steps'` and `KeyError: 'catalog_first_step'`. The eight assertion failures concern frozen-card transformation counts, missing-reference rejection and sparse omission lists. All ten failure/error headers and the final counts match the failed log of [PR #5862, run 40479932917](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40479932917). This is the reported shared onboarding failure on main `de5ec2e7a`; no shared test or implementation was changed to bypass it. Maintainer repair remains outstanding.

The [replay job](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40486899975/job/122132300822) was **skipped**. **Hosted replay has not certified this package; only the local scientific checks listed above have run.** Independent human and formal proof-kernel review remain unclaimed. The contribution commit and package are unchanged.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door. Blast radius: one isolated research package. Five new files; no shared implementation, frozen evidence, predecessor credit or selected record is changed.

author: dailyxplorer
body:
## Summary

Port to main of the "markers first" delete fix from #281.

If deleting the local models stops halfway (macOS refuses to remove a file, for example on a permissions problem), Murmur shows the delete error as before. The models now show as not downloaded, with Download and Delete available, and dictation goes to Codex. Before, the models stayed "Ready" with some files gone, and every local dictation failed until the next delete.

A delete that succeeds behaves exactly as before. Only the failure path changes. No visible UI change, so there are no screenshots.

## Changes

- `src-tauri/src/local_models/mod.rs`, `delete()`: removes `.murmur-optional`, then `.murmur-ready`, then the folder. If removing the folder fails, the state still becomes `Missing` and the error is returned. Before, the error was returned before the state changed.
- `src-tauri/src/local_models/tests.rs`: new test `a_delete_stopped_halfway_is_reported_and_leaves_no_ready_models`, adapted from #281.

## Design

- **Markers before files**, as in #281. Without the ready marker, the models are not ready, now and after a restart. `kept_bytes` then shows what is left, and the row already offers Download and Delete for it.
- **The optional marker too.** #281 removes only `.murmur-ready`. On main, `.murmur-optional` says the custom-word (CTC) model is in place. If it outlives a partial delete, the next download skips the CTC fetch because the marker matches (`fetch_optional`), and the helper starts with boosting on while the CTC files are gone. The test proved this: with #281's change alone it failed on `!optional_ready(&path)`.
- **Order: optional, then ready.** If the second removal fails, the models stay Ready with their files intact, and the next launch fetches the optional model again. The reverse order could leave the models not ready on disk but still Ready in memory.
- **Test adapted for main.** #281's `Undeletable` has a Windows branch behind `target_os`. Main allows no `target_os` cfg, so the test keeps only the Unix version: the folder of a model file becomes read-only (`0o555`) until the guard is dropped.

## Testing

Red first, on the Mac (arm64):

- Main's `delete()`: `a_delete_stopped_halfway_is_reported_and_leaves_no_ready_models ... FAILED` at `assert_eq!(ready.status().state, LocalModelState::Missing)`: `left: Ready, right: Missing`.
- #281's change only (ready marker first): `... FAILED`, `assertion failed: !optional_ready(&path)`.

Green, at `8f417e88`:

- `cargo test --locked --lib -- local_models commands::local_models`: `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored`, including `a_delete_stopped_halfway_is_reported_and_leaves_no_ready_models ... ok` and `delete_removes_everything_and_reports_missing ... ok`.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` (aarch64): clean.
- `cargo check --locked --target x86_64-apple-darwin --all-targets`: builds. It shows 2 dead-code warnings, both already on main (`meetings/calls.rs` `parse_mic_users`, `meetings/capture/system.rs` `OsTooOld`).
- `bun run lint`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run check:translations` ("All 5 languages have complete translations!"), and `bun run format:check` (Prettier and `cargo fmt --check`) pass.

## Known limits

- When the delete fails, `delete_local_model` returns before `LocalEngine::release`. A model that dictation loaded stays in memory until the 10-minute idle release. Dictation does not use it in the meantime, because the models are not ready. This is unchanged from main.
- On macOS a delete fails only in rare cases: permissions, a read-only volume, or a disk error. So this path is hard to reproduce by hand.

## Manual checks for the owner

1. Normal path: download the local models, dictate once with the local engine, then Settings → Delete. Check that there is no error, the row shows Download, and the models folder is gone.
2. Optional, failure path: with the models downloaded and the app closed, run `chmod 555` on one folder inside the app's `meetings/models` folder, for example the ASR model's `weights` folder. Open the app and click Delete. Check that an error toast appears, the row shows Download and Delete, and a dictation goes to Codex (History shows the cloud engine). Run `chmod 755` on the same folder and click Delete again: it succeeds. Then download again and check that the row reaches Ready and a local dictation works.

## Added beyond the request

- The custom-word marker `.murmur-optional` is also removed first. #281 removes only `.murmur-ready`. Without this, a partial delete could leave the custom-word model marked present with its files gone, and the next download would not fetch it again. The red run above shows this.

## Questions for the owner

None.

## Owner decisions

- Applied as approved: the "ready marker first" fix from #281, ported to main with #281's test adapted for macOS. The `target_os` branch is dropped.

author: besermenji
body:
Closes #67. Refs #17.

Two items on the #17 hardware checklist were manual. They are now e2e scenarios:

- **t25 flash holds no plaintext**: stores a canary note, dumps the `cvtvault` and NVS partitions over USB with PlatformIO's esptool, and searches both for every secret (passphrases, TOTP secret, every string of 4+ characters the run typed, case-folded). It also checks that the dump matches the device's own vault-header count, that the vault partition has no printable run of 24+ bytes, and a positive control: `cvt_guard` must be found in the NVS dump. The canary note is always removed. The scenario skips when no Python here can run esptool.
- **t26 serial output is silent**: every serial line that is not a reply to the harness (boot output, stray prints, driver errors) is checked against the same secrets. The scenario reboots and unlocks the device itself and fails if the boot output was not captured. Allows at most 20 stray lines per boot.

Harness changes:
- Boot output printed before the first reply is kept (it used to be discarded), and the port is read empty before it closes. Reply tails cut by a reconnect are kept apart from device output.
- Partition offsets come from `partitions_test.csv`.
- `unlock()` wakes a dimmed screen first. The waking key is swallowed by design, so after the device sat idle the harness typed a wrong passphrase and lost an attempt.

## Testing
On hardware (Cardputer ADV, no SD card): full suite 24 passed, 2 skipped (t20 and t21 need `--sd`); t25 and t26 also pass run alone. With a FAT32 card (`--sd`): 25 passed, 1 skipped (t19 needs the card removed); t26 checked 130 device lines.

author: bloxster
body:
Adds `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml`.

- Runs only on Dependabot PRs. Reads the update with `dependabot/fetch-metadata` (pinned to the v3.1.0 commit).
- Only **npm** PRs for this repo's site directory, with a **patch or minor** update, are merged. Major updates, GitHub Actions updates and anything else stay open for the weekly review.
- Waits until every other check on the PR has finished. If any check fails, if the checks never start, or if the PR gets a newer commit, it does nothing. The merge uses `--match-head-commit`, so it only merges the commit that was checked.
- A merge made with the `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger the push-based deploy, so the workflow dispatches the deploy workflow on the base branch after merging.
- Token permissions are granted per job (`contents`, `pull-requests`, `actions: write`, `checks: read`); the workflow default is `{}`. No checkout, so no PR code runs. `zizmor`: no findings.

1. **Discover** — request-local pending lookup dedup across featured campaigns/merchant cards: `findBySlug` **11 → 5** for the current overlap; no cross-request merchant-state cache.

## Ce qui change
- **0. Séparation avec l'appli d'Aaron** : toutes les clés de stockage, la synchro et les caches du service worker sont préfixés `celia-`. Le service worker ne supprime que les caches `celia-`. Les deux applis sont sur le même site (`xazouille.github.io`), elles ne peuvent donc plus se marcher dessus.
- **1. Identité** : nom « Glow Up · Célia », textes au féminin (titres, identités « Je suis… », rangs, badges), ton doux.
- **2. Ses 16 cases** : Culture et Lecture séparées, Yoga et Activité créative ajoutées, listes Alimentation et Hygiène adaptées, journée parfaite à 12 cases sur 16. Échecs et Argent retirés (les badges d'épargne n'apparaissent que s'il existe une case argent).
- **3. Cartes** : Winx Club (fées avec 10 transformations, Spécialistes, pixies, Trix, grands méchants), Monster High (ghouls principales en G1 → G2 → G3, la bande, les rivales, les animaux), Hello Kitty & ses amis. 16 albums. Les surprises (petite pochette, coffret, grand coffret) sont redessinées en pastel, avec un nœud. Les images viennent des wikis Fandom grâce au workflow « Images des cartes » (`tools/gen_cards.py`), avec un rapport et des planches d'aperçu sur la branche `apercu-cartes`.
- **4. Sa PP** : le personnage choisi devient la photo de profil. La complicité 💗 ne redescend jamais. Chaque palier débloque la forme suivante, puis des halos. 2 cœurs sont offerts à chaque palier (Nunes & Drèze 2006). Chaque dimanche, la PP écrit un petit mot dans le bilan.
- **5. Duels magiques** : les boss sont adoucis (Trix, Valtor, Kuromi, Toralei…) et l'énergie remplace les PV.
- **6. 12 thèmes clean girl / zen** :
  - 3 dès le départ : Lin, Sauge, Nuage ;
  - à débloquer : Rose poudré, Lavande, Pêche, Matcha, Nacre, Nuit douce, Winx, Hello Kitty, Monster High.
  - S'y ajoutent de nouvelles icônes (étincelle), des cadres doux, une PP ronde et des couleurs douces partout.
- **7. Documentation et tests** : NOTES.md, CLAUDE.md et README réécrits ; tests Playwright adaptés (le test spécifique à Aaron a été retiré).

## Tests
Toute la suite `tools/tests` passe (smoke en mobile, ordinateur et sombre, motiv, growthtest, flows, summon, midclose, demo, mergechk, icontest, uitest). Il n'y a ni erreur console ni défilement horizontal à 390 px.

## Après la fusion

author: besufkadmenji
body:
## Summary
Two fixes found while checking the forgot-password email:

- **Request language follows the page:** an `/en` page sent `accept-language: ar` to the API whenever there was no `lang` cookie, because the cookie is only written by the language menu. So emails and API messages came in Arabic; the forgot-password email arrived in Arabic for an English visitor. The Apollo HTTP and WebSocket links and the multipart uploader now use the page's locale first, then the cookie, then Arabic.
- **Forgot-password resend:** "Resend" on the reset-code screen always requested a phone-verification code, so an email target answered "user not found" and nothing was sent. Even when sent, that code could not reset a password. It now requests the password-reset code again for the same email or phone, and the 60-second countdown restarts only after a successful send.

## Testing
- Vitest: 81 tests pass (new spec for the request language).
- Checked locally: a cookie-less browser on `/en/auth/forgot-password` sends `accept-language: en`. On the English reset-code screen, Resend now sends `forgotPassword` for the same email, in English.

author: tmorius-eng
body:
The owner wants readers who have not installed the app to be reminded, and an installed app never to be nagged.

## Changes
- **Re-ask every 5 min** (was 14 days after a ✕), across pages and reloads. An ignored strip slides away after 20 s and counts as a ✕. It shows only in a visible tab and waits while a dialog, menu (`[data-popover]` on the mobile menu) or input is active. The rules are in `src/lib/install-ask.ts`, with unit tests.
- **Installed = never:**
  - Android Chrome stops firing `beforeinstallprompt` once the app is installed, so the strip is no longer eligible.
  - Standalone never shows it.
  - A cancelled Android prompt counts as a ✕.
  - Safari cannot see a home-screen install, so the iPhone steps sheet gets "✓ Нүүр дэлгэцэнд нэмчихсэн". Opening the steps rests the strip for a day.
- **Early install offer:** an inline `<head>` script keeps a `beforeinstallprompt` that fires before the page's chunks run (`window.__iltodBip`).
- **CSS fix:** `:where(p) { text-wrap: pretty }` moves into `@layer base`. Unlayered, it beat Tailwind's `truncate`, so every truncated paragraph wrapped onto several lines.

## Verification
- `npm run check`: 382 tests pass.
- Demo build, then Playwright with `page.clock`:
  - **iPhone 13:**
    - The strip shows at 4 s, hides on ✕, is still hidden at 4:50 and is back at 5:00.
    - Ignored, it slides away after 20 s.
    - A reload within 5 min waits the remainder: it was shown 309 s after the ✕.
    - "Нэмчихсэн" means never, including after 25 h and a reload.
    - Steps opened and then closed: hidden at 10 min, back after a day.
    - Standalone: never shown.
    - Menu open: it waits, then shows once the menu closes.
  - **Desktop:** never shown.
  - **Pixel 7:**
    - The strip shows on the first and the repeat visit.
    - With JS chunks delayed 4 s, the early offer is kept and the strip shows.
    - After `appinstalled` it is hidden.

body:
## Goal
Continue the merged dual-site Authentik work with one **source-only**, default-off server composition instead of individually unmounted adapters.

## Implementation
- Add `createPublicLoginRuntime` to wire one distinct signed OIDC code+PKCE flow, encrypted atomic PostgreSQL transaction backend, scoped website-session store, cookie binding, branded site and pinned Node HTTP handler for **each** of `family` and `techtactics`.
- Reject missing/overlapping site IDs, origins, OIDC client IDs/secrets, 32-byte signing/encryption keys or shared query function references. No browser input chooses a site or identity issuer; handlers are returned only to trusted bootstrap.
- Test first: synthetic signed RS256 tokens, both loopback HTTP vhosts, site separation, encrypted database state, replay denial, independently revoked website sessions and invalid configuration.
- Update operator documentation and finish queue to distinguish source completion from live activation.

## Strict boundaries
**Not deployed.** No real Authentik applications, DNS, TLS, Cloudflare settings, runtime listeners, Supabase migrations, database credentials, operator/home-lab rights or production login replacement. Does not import from `server/index.mjs`; Friday production Access remains in force.

## Review gates
- Run exact-head GitHub CI including Node unit tests and `make verify`; resolve any failures before review.
- Real PostgreSQL role isolation (distinct LOGIN principals), Authentik providers/flows/MFA, approved public vhosts and TLS, ingress header stripping, rate limits, retention and account offboarding, and end-to-end browser acceptance remain separate requirements.
- Do not merge/deploy without final owner authorization and a staged cutover plan.

author: thiva-k
body:
### Purpose
Adds the Rich Authorization Requests runtime to the backend, on top of the authorization detail type registry from #6009, with `client_credentials` as the first grant that uses it. A client can request `authorization_details` at the token endpoint, the type processors decide them, and the granted details are carried into the access token, the token response and introspection.

User-facing grants (`authorization_code`, PAR, CIBA and `refresh_token`), where the user approves the details on the consent screen, follow in a separate pull request: #6134. Until then those grants ignore `authorization_details`, as they do today.

### Approach
- **Request validation:** requested details are validated against their type's schema and field policies, and `multipleOf` is checked exactly rather than with floating-point division. Unknown fields and processor-supplied fields are refused, and so is a number with more precision than a 64-bit float holds, since the schema checks numbers at that precision while tokens carry them as sent.
- **Processor:**
  - Calls are batched per endpoint and credential. The timeout is set by `oauth.authorization_details.processor_timeout`, in seconds (default 5).
  - A processor can approve a detail, refuse it with a reason, or fill in fields its type leaves to the processor. Its changes are checked against the type's field policies. A refused detail is dropped while the others remain, and a request whose details are all refused fails.
  - Authentication reuses the outbound authentication module. The processor contract is in `api/extensions/authorization-details-processor.yaml`.
- **Grants:**
  - `client_credentials` decides the details with the client as the subject. Every requested type must declare a processor, since no user is there to consent (RAR-1024).
  - `authorization_code`, CIBA and `refresh_token` ignore the parameter until the follow-up, and the other grants refuse it.
- **Tokens:** granted details are issued in the access token's `authorization_details` claim, returned in the token response, and reported by introspection.
- **Metadata:** `/oauth2/authorization-details-types[/{type}]` publishes the types with an ETag. Discovery advertises `authorization_details_types_supported`. Both are controlled by `oauth.authorization_details.type_metadata_enabled`.
- **Engine:** the `WithAuthorizationDetailProvider` option replaces the authorization details runtime (validation, preparation and processing). A replacement must refuse types without a processor on `client_credentials` (RAR-1024) and return only requested and admitted details. Without it, the engine uses the built-in runtime, which calls each type's processor.
- **Docs:** the configuration reference and the Helm chart cover the `oauth.authorization_details` keys.

### Related Issues
- #5155

### Related PRs
- #6009 (management layer, merged)
- #6134 (user-facing grants)
- #5691 (specification)
- #5692 (threat model)
- Design discussion: #5604

- [x] Documentation provided. (Add links if there are any)

- [x] Tests provided. (Add links if there are any)

body:
As the title says. A minor fix I had to make was to turn off whole-program optimization for zlib and iconv, because those builds select the VS2022 toolset while the pyreadstat extension selects VS2026, and LTCG can only be completed by the exact same compiler version that built the initial libraries/objects. Whole-program optimization is still enabled for pyreadstat; I changed this for both Windows builds because we would hit the same issue on x64 as well if we update the runner, and the new runner image has multiple VS toolsets installed.

In reality, turning this off actually reduced the size of the wheels (by a few kb) and I do not expect there to be any measurable difference in performance.

author: carlo-codes
body:
Closes #38

## Summary

Select mode in the Plan editor. **Select** puts a tick box on every row, and on each Superset header, which ticks the whole Superset. A bottom bar then offers **Create Superset**, **Ungroup** and **Remove**.

- The "Superset with next" link and the header's Ungroup link are gone.
- The up/down buttons stay until 8/9.
- The Round Rest stepper is disabled while selecting.

```diff
 core blockService
+  createSuperset(workoutId, { blockIds?, exerciseEntryIds? })   # any rows, not only neighbours (lifter)
+  ungroupExerciseEntries(workoutId, exerciseEntryIds)            # take ticked entries out of their Superset
   groupBlocks(...)    # AI contract unchanged: neighbouring Blocks only, keeps the first Block
   ungroupBlock(id)    # AI contract unchanged: a Block of straight sets writes and records nothing
 core exerciseEntryService
+  deleteExerciseEntries(ids)       -> ExerciseEntryRemoval[]     # validated, all or none
+  restoreExerciseEntries(removals)                               # Undo for the whole batch
```

```text
createSuperset(ticked)
  entries = ticked entries, in Workout order (a ticked Block counts as all of its entries)
  target  = first wholly ticked Superset   -> rows it takes in get its Round Rest
          | top-most Block, if wholly ticked
          | a new Block                     -> each entry keeps its own rest
  move the entries into the target
  delete the wholly ticked Blocks that are now empty
  renumber what is left of any Superset that lost entries
  place the target where the top-most ticked row was
    (just after that row's Superset, if the Superset keeps some of its entries)
```

```diff
 <PlanEditor>
+  useRowSelection(blocks, plan/workout)   # Select mode ends with its Plan or Workout, or when the Workout has no rows left
+  <EntryListContext value={useMemo({ unit, editing, selecting })}>
     <BlockItem>  -> <SupersetGroup> / <ExerciseEntryRow>   # both tick through the shared <TickButton>
+  <SelectionBar>   # Create Superset (2+ ticked) · Ungroup (a ticked row is in a Superset) · Remove
   <Snackbar>       # Undo restores the whole removed batch
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** `selectMode.test.ts` failed to import `createSuperset`.
- **After:** `selectMode.test.ts` passes. It covers:
  - grouping rows that aren't neighbours
  - a ticked Superset taking in rows, which get its Round Rest
  - a new Superset, where each entry keeps its own rest
  - renumbering after entries leave a Superset
  - partial and full Ungroup, and Ungroup that changes nothing
  - batch Remove with Undo, and validation
  - AI `groupBlocks` with a single Block plus a Superset: it keeps the first Block's id, and Changes by AI Undo restores the exact rows
  - AI `ungroup_block` on a plain Block records no Change by AI
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` all pass: core 201, mobile 62, debug 5.

## Judgement calls

- **Ungroup** takes only the ticked entries out of their Superset, each placed just after it. To split a whole Superset, tick its header.
- **Rest when grouping (owner decision):** if a ticked existing Superset survives, the rows it takes in get its Round Rest. A brand-new Superset keeps each entry's own rest.
- **AI tools keep their old behaviour.** `groupBlocks` and `ungroupBlock` keep their exact AI behaviour. The Superset-survives and Round Rest rules apply only to the lifter's `createSuperset`.
- **Undo order:** removed entries come back last-removed first, so a Superset removed row by row comes back intact. If the Superset is reordered while Undo is showing, positions stay unique but the order is best-effort.
- **No new AI tool.** The spec doesn't ask for one. A possible follow-up is an AI tool for grouping Blocks that aren't neighbours.
- **After an action, Select mode closes.** If the action fails, an alert says why and the rows stay ticked. Switching Workout tabs also leaves Select mode, and Add exercise is hidden while it's on.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

No schema or migration changes. AI Access behaviour is unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** Plan editor
