author: jongtae
body:
## User outcome

When Codex or Claude Code updates itself, Still keeps judging and working. It does not wait for a code change, a restart or a manual Settings requalification. Still checks the installed binary on this machine. A binary that passes is used. A binary that fails, or that cannot be checked, is refused as before, and the owner is told in plain words which check failed.

## Runtime impact

- **Strict Work route and Codex Judgment route:** a new binary identity (path, size, mtime_ns, inode, device of the launcher and native binary) is qualified locally on first use. The check runs the sandbox denial probe and feature plan `qualify_strict` already ran, plus the instruction-file and bridge/tool-surface checks that were run by hand. It uses a loopback scripted model, a synthetic home and `CODEX_HOME`, no provider and no owner credentials. Only passes are memoized, per identity and scope. A failed identity is not re-probed for 60 s (it stays refused during that time).
- **Judgment route:** when the CLI fingerprint or cloud profile identity changes, the existing `decision_qualification_jobs` machinery starts one background requalification with the same `decision-qualification/4` suite (every case must pass). Judgments stay fail-closed until it passes. A failure is shown on the existing Settings status and is not retried automatically for the same identity.
- **Claude Code turns:** stream-json input (#308 S2) is used by capability. If the installed CLI rejects `--input-format stream-json` / `--replay-user-messages` with a fast usage error and no work record, the turn reruns once as the plain `-p` turn. That observation is remembered per binary identity, and steers go through S1.
- `cli_fingerprint` now uses mtime_ns, inode and device. **Every stored Judgment route therefore re-qualifies once in the background after this deploys.**

## Goal / authority

#346, substep `CLI-UPDATE-01` of `RESPONSIVE-01` (#332), added by the owner on 2026-10-26 (plan PR #356). Files are within the program's `allowed_authority` for #346.

## Constitution / specification alignment

- **C16:** this removes a blocker. An exact-version list stopped every judgment after a CLI self-update (#344). No owner request is scripted, and there are no site, provider or category branches.
- **C15:** the existing manual harness is adapted into a runtime qualifier, with one implementation shared by runtime and tests.
- **#616 isolation:** every property the manual procedure covered is still observed. A property that cannot be observed refuses the binary.

## What changed

- `cli_qualification.py` (new): the loopback scripted model and synthetic `CODEX_HOME` population moved from the tests. It holds the runtime surface checks:
  - Codex instruction-file states 0–2;
  - the strict Work bridge round trip and tool surface, where Claude's offered tools must be a subset of the strict bridge allowlist and include `list_notes`;
  - no canary leak;
  - plain-words failure messages.
  - The bridge round trip gets up to three attempts, because Codex 0.164.0 sometimes builds its first request before the bridge MCP server is ready. Security properties are checked on every attempt, and any defect refuses at once.
- `bounded_execution.py`:
  - admission by local result for the current identity and binding, replacing the version-list gate; platform and runtime-root gates stay;
  - pass memo per identity and scope (a Judgment pass never authorizes Work);
  - failure backoff;
  - a re-check of identity before strict launch;
  - per-identity Claude stream-input capability with the plain-turn fallback.
  - `tested_versions` stays as the record of hand-run checks.
- `decision_routes.py`: `CODEX_INSTRUCTION_FILES_QUALIFIED` is a record, not the gate. Automatic background requalification goes through the existing job machinery: coalesced, bound to the target identity and route revision, and a failure is retained across restarts.
- `decision_adapters.py`: stronger `cli_fingerprint`.
- `quickstart_service.py`:
  - Settings reads the current local Work record without probing.
  - An unrecognised saved profile passes `qualification_allowed=False`, so it is still refused before any probe or launch.
- `messages.json`, `web/app.js`: plain failure reasons; the Settings text explains the automatic check.
- `docs/decision-layer.en.md`: the changed procedure.
- Tests:
  - unit and fixture tests for every negative case below;
  - the opt-in process tests import the shared harness and warn "not observed on version X" instead of skipping or pinning a version.

## Existing solutions review (Adopt / Adapt / Build)

- problem/boundary: admission of an installed subscription CLI binary to the strict Work and Judgment routes after it changes, without an in-code version list
- internal repository candidates: `qualify_strict`, `strict_observation`, `_strict_binary_identity` and the L7 per-identity memo (#333); the opt-in harness `_ScriptedModel` / `populate_codex_home` in `tests/test_strict_isolation.py`; `decision_qualification_jobs` and `decision_qualification.qualify`; `bounded_run`; `ClaudeSteerSession` S1 release
- search evidence (paths/symbols/docs checked): `src/personal_agent/bounded_execution.py`, `decision_routes.py`, `decision_qualification.py`, `decision_adapters.py`, `tests/test_strict_isolation.py`, `tests/test_steer_cli_qualification.py`, `docs/decision-layer.en.md`
- standard-library/platform candidates: `http.server`, `tempfile`, `subprocess`, `threading`, `time.monotonic` (used)
- official SDK/reference/standard candidates: Codex `mcp_servers.<name>.required` / `startup_timeout_sec` config (not adopted in this PR; follow-up for production launches)
- mature open-source/framework candidates: none needed; the existing harness already observes the properties
- maintenance/security/supply-chain fit: no new dependency
- licence fit: AGPL-3.0-only repository code only
- runtime/deployment/compatibility fit: macOS (the tested platform gate is unchanged)
- decision: Adapt
- why rejected candidates are insufficient: an exact-version list cannot admit an update that has not been observed yet. A new framework would duplicate the existing harness.
- Still-owned policy/authority boundary kept outside the dependency: admission, binding, failure retention and owner notice stay in Still; the CLIs only run under the synthetic probe
- N/A reason:

## Authority / threat model

Trigger: the #616 isolation qualification changes from a reviewed exact-version list to an automatic local check.

- **Data:** the probe uses only a synthetic store, home, `CODEX_HOME` and canaries under the engine runtime root. It never touches the owner store, Memory or credentials. Raw request bodies die with the temporary fixture.
- **Network:** a loopback scripted model only. The production sandbox flags are unchanged and the probe runs under them.
- **Abuse/failure paths:**
  - a new CLI version adds an instruction source, tool or network use, which the instruction-file, tool-surface and canary checks catch;
  - the binary is replaced during the check, which the identity and digest are re-checked before and after;
  - a check crashes, times out or cannot bind loopback, which refuses;
  - a pass recorded for another identity or scope is never used;
  - a failure is never cached as a pass;
  - an unknown saved profile is refused before any probe.
- **Background Judgment requalification:** this intentionally calls the owner's selected engine (owner direction). It is coalesced, runs at most once per identity, and is not retried after a failure.
- **Residual (accepted in #309 L7):** an in-place replacement that preserves every stat field goes undetected until restart.

## AgentPackage / runtime delta

- exact package/runtime/schema revision or digest: none (CLI identity is now bound by local check; `decision-qualification/4` unchanged)
- permission / owner-data scope delta: none
- external network / data-destination delta: none (the probe is loopback on

author: stuffbucket
body:
## What was wrong

- **The config file was never applied.** `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml` existed, but `codeql.yml` didn't pass it via `config-file:`, so its `paths-ignore` did nothing. Tests made up 178 of the 632 files extracted on every run, and two of the open alerts are in `tests/`.
- **Every change ran a full JS/TS scan**, including docs-only PRs. The desktop app's Rust code (`shell/src-tauri`) was never analyzed. Workflow files were not analyzed with CodeQL's `actions` queries.
- **No cache helped.** Both PR and `main` runs logged `overlay database mode: none without caching`. The JS TRAP cache is skipped as "too small" for this codebase.

## What this changes

- **Config file is wired in** (`config-file:` with `build-mode: none`):
  - `paths-ignore`: tests, broker tests, Storybook, vendored and minified code.
  - Queries move from `security-and-quality` to `security-extended`.
- **A scope job picks the languages for each change.** `scripts/codeql-languages.ts` (17 tests) reads the same `paths-ignore`, so the scan scope and analysis scope come from one list.
  - A docs-only or test-only change runs **no** analysis.
  - A TS change runs JS/TS only, a Rust change Rust only, a workflow change Actions only.
  - The weekly schedule, manual dispatch, changes to the CodeQL setup itself, and anything ambiguous run **all** languages. Ambiguous means a new branch, a compare-API failure, or a diff at the API's 300-file cap.
- **New languages:** `rust` (the Tauri shell) and `actions`.
- **Rust's Cargo registry is cached**, keyed on `Cargo.lock`. The extractor downloads crates to resolve dependencies; the first run saved 34 MB.
- **A new push to a PR cancels its in-flight scan.** `main` and scheduled scans always finish.

CodeQL isn't a required check (only `test` is), so skipping a language never blocks a merge.

## Deliberate trade-off: no incremental PR analysis

CodeQL's incremental PR analysis only runs with the default query suite (the action disables it whenever `queries`, `packs` or `query-filters` are set). But 4 of the 5 rules currently alerting here are medium-precision `security-extended` rules:
- `js/file-access-to-http`
- `js/http-to-file-access`
- `js/file-system-race`
- `js/remote-property-injection`

They watch exactly how this proxy moves tokens between disk and HTTP. Keeping them costs the incremental speedup; diff-informed alert filtering on PRs still applies.

## Measured on this PR's run (all languages, since it changes the CodeQL setup)

| Job | Time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pick languages | 8s | |
| Analyze (actions) | 48s | new |
| Analyze (javascript-typescript) | 74s | 419 files (was 632), 105 queries (was 203); analysis step 52s (was 55s) |
| Analyze (rust) | 467s | new; about 3.5 min extracting the dependency tree, about 3.5 min of queries; runs only when Rust changes, plus weekly |

After merge, the two alerts in `tests/` should close on the next `main` analysis, because those files are no longer scanned.

| Area | Cosa fissa |
|---|---|
| Allocazione iniziale | pesi esatti; con fee `f` il controvalore investito è `V/(1+f)` e i pesi non cambiano; asset assente dai prezzi ignorato |
| PMC | media ponderata su due acquisti; invariato dopo vendita parziale; invariato dopo i costi di detenzione |
| Vendite | imposta solo sul guadagno (`units × (prezzo − PMC) × aliquota`); perdita → imposta 0, nessun credito; oltre le quote → `ValueError`; entro la tolleranza `×1,0001` → quantità tagliata |
| Uscita | `cash_out_costs` = commissioni + imposte, **e non muta il portafoglio** |
| Ribilanciamento | sotto soglia nessun trade; sopra soglia pesi a target; **conservazione del valore**: `V_dopo = V_prima − costi − imposte`; imposta solo sull'asset in guadagno |

### `tests/test_backtest_end_to_end.py` — 17 test sul `Timeseries.csv` reale

| Proprietà | Perché |
|---|---|
| Determinismo | due run identici danno gli stessi numeri |
| `gross > broker > net` | nessun livello di costo può creare valore |
| Lordo indipendente dall'aliquota | il portafoglio ideale non paga imposte (0%, 26%, 50% → stesso lordo) |
| Netto decrescente nell'aliquota | monotonia fiscale |
| Aliquota 0 → colonne `Tax_*` a zero | l'imposta non è applicata "di nascosto" |
| Summary = ultima riga del log | `final_net` è il `Net` finale, non un altro calcolo |
| Anni dallo span reale | `years` viene dai dati, non dalle date richieste |
| Drawdown riconciliato | `max_drawdown` = ribasso della serie `Net` rispetto al massimo cumulato |
| Finestra non coperta → `ValueError` | regressione #51 |
| Output solo con `save_outputs=True` | in una `tmp_path`: i file ci sono oppure la cartella resta intatta |

## Difetto trovato dai test

**Pesi che non sommano a 1 azzerano il capitale senza errore.** Con `{"VTSIM": 0.5}` su 2020-2023: 4.985,54 al giorno 0 → **1e-230** a fine periodo, CAGR −100%, drawdown −100%. Il ribilanciamento vende la quota non investita e il ricavato sparisce, perché il portafoglio non ha un conto liquidità: ogni ribilanciamento dimezza il capitale.

Documentato in `test_pesi_che_non_sommano_a_uno_non_azzerano_il_capitale` marcato `xfail`, e aperto come **issue #62** con riproduzione, causa e fix proposto (una validazione di 3 righe in `backtest()`). La validazione sta in una PR a parte: qui c'è solo la rete che la verificherà.

## Verifica

```
60 passed, 1 xfailed in 35 s
```

Base: `fix/test-engine`. Nessuna modifica al codice di produzione: solo `tests/`.

author: julientinguely-da
body:
fixes https://github.com/DACH-NY/cn-test-failures/issues/10676

When a package-config vote executes, the validator's vetting trigger sees the vote request disappear before its cached AmuletRules shows the new config. For that moment it treats the newly voted-in packages as unsupported and unvets them, then re-vets them later with the wrong validFrom, which is what fails BootstrapPackageConfigIntegrationTest. The fix keeps those configs pending until a new AmuletRules contract is seen, so unvetting never runs in that window.

## Purpose / Description
When disabling the review timebox toggle, the collection timebox limit is set to 0. Previously, when re-enabling the toggle or leaving and re-entering the screen while disabled, the duration defaulted back to 20 minutes (`DEFAULT_TIMEBOX_MINUTES`), losing any custom duration (e.g. 45 minutes) the user had configured.
This PR persists the user's customized timebox limit in Android preferences (`Prefs.customTimeboxLimit`), so that:
1. When the toggle is re-enabled, the customized limit is restored and written to collection preferences.
2. When the user re-enters the screen while timeboxing is disabled, the previously configured duration is preserved and displayed.
3. If an existing non-zero limit is present in the collection (e.g., from desktop sync), it updates the local preference so it is remembered if subsequently disabled.

## Fixes
* Fixes #22720 

## Approach
- Added `custom_timebox_limit_key` in `preferences.xml`.
- Added `customTimeboxLimit` property delegate in `Prefs.kt` with a default of 20 (`DEFAULT_TIMEBOX_MINUTES`).
- In `TimeboxSettingsViewModel`:
  - Injected `PrefsRepository = Prefs`.
  - In `loadSettings()`: if disabled, initialize with `prefs.customTimeboxLimit`; if enabled, record the limit in `prefs.customTimeboxLimit`.
  - In `setMinutes()`: update `prefs.customTimeboxLimit`.
  - In `toggleEnabled()`: restore `_uiState.value.minutes` when enabled, or set 0 to collection when disabled while keeping the minutes in state/prefs.
- Added comprehensive unit tests in `TimeboxSettingsViewModelTest`.

body:
## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip manages work for AI agents.
> - Monitoring creates issues for alerts and closes them on recovery.
> - A blocker root can hold many dependent tasks.
> - The root fan-out evaluator needs a live graph input and a periodic caller.
> - This change connects the SQL loader to the evaluator and the alert service.
> - Persistent root identity prevents duplicate issues between collection periods.

## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Refs #1878. Task: [OPE-9165](http://10.10.10.2:3100/OPE/issues/OPE-9165).

A root that holds more tasks than the configured limit must create one alert. Repeated collection must not create duplicates. Recovery must close the alert.

## What Changed

- Add a separate root fan-out collector and a one-minute worker sweep.
- Use the unchanged SQL loader from #1878 and the existing evaluator.
- Use the monitoring alert service and persistent dedup store.
- Serialize collectors and skip recovery when the bounded graph is full.
- Add a real PostgreSQL test without skip or mocked loader and issue service.

## Architecture Decisions

None. This change connects existing graph and monitoring services. It adds no API, schema, shared registry, or foreign metric changes. Worker registration is next to the existing alert sweep. Registration was coordinated with the loader owner.

## Verification

| Acceptance criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| B3 loader feeds B5 evaluation | root-fanout.ts calls loadBlockedGraph, computeRootFanout, and evaluateRootFanoutAlerts |
| OPE-8079-shaped root with 20 dependents opens one alert | root-fanout.db.myrmidon.test.ts uses real PostgreSQL and persisted monitoring issues |
| Repeated periods do not duplicate | Same test runs two concurrent collectors and checks one alert and no repeated comments |
| Root removal closes alert | Same test changes root to done and checks issue status and dedup recovery |
| Text includes root identifier and task count | Same test checks OPE-8079 and 20 tasks in the stored title |
| Configured threshold and new firing period | Same test checks reopen and recovery at limit 20 |

Tests and build run in PR CI only. CI execution is pending, not claimed as passed. The test has no embedded PostgreSQL skip. git diff --check passed. Deployment and :3100 acceptance belong to ADM after release.

## Risks

- The loader limits the graph to 1000 edges. A full snapshot cannot prove recovery, so it does not close alerts.
- Collection locks shared settings while it writes alert state.
- The unchanged loader and tests from #1878 are included as dependency commits. Merge after #1878.
- CI and independent review must pass before merge. Production is unchanged.

## Model Used

OpenAI GPT-6.1 via Hermes Agent, runtime model ID chatgpt-pool/gpt-6.1-sol. Tool use and code editing enabled. Context window size is not exposed.

body:
Task: [Fix] Session stays running after Claude usage limit is hit (https://maskin.io/e2877e32-2c11-489e-96c8-a76200908ed4/objects/cd7a1036-4621-4942-9688-12ae475dc3f4)

**What was asked**
When the CLI prints "You've hit your limit" as its final error, the session should end as failed with the limit as the reason, not stay running.

**Cause**
Interactive sessions do not exit after a failed turn. The limit reason was only worked out in classifySessionExit, which runs on process exit, so a live CLI that printed the banner was never settled. In the interactive-turn-finalizer, a non-helper session with a limit error either posted the chat message and stopped only if a subscription failover moved, or (no conversation attached) dropped the turn. Helper sessions already ended as failed, but with classification unknown and no failure reason or retry time.

**Changes**
- credit-classifier: new classifyBannerResult (result text must open with a CLI banner), extracted from classifySessionExit, which now calls it. No second classifier.
- interactive-turn-finalizer: new onLimitResult option and failOnLimitResult. For a non-helper session whose final result is an error opening with a banner, it ends the session after the chat has been told. Acts only on the newest turn (the agent-server replays old stdout after a restart). Helpers keep their existing path.
- session-manager: onLimitResult reuses finishHelperSession, which already settles through settleSession and stops the sandbox. author: petitan
body:
## Summary

Phase 3 of the property-based testing plan: P6 (B+ tree), P7 (aggregation) and P8 (MCP authorization and JSON-RPC), plus fixes for the faults they found. The P8 properties use a seeded generator and add no new dependency.

### Security (P8)

1. **Vacuous ACL pass.**
   - *Bug:* a tool that names no collection (`transaction_begin`/`commit`/`rollback`, `embed_job_cancel`) was checked against an empty collection list, so the check always passed. A read-only external caller could therefore start, commit or roll back transactions and cancel embedding jobs.
   - *Fix:* such calls are now checked against the catch-all `*` rule.
2. **Built-in `_system.*` rules could be overridden.**
   - *Bug:* exact-name ACL rules were checked first. So an exact rule on a `_system` collection beat the built-in localhost-only rule. `acl_set` accepts `_system.api_keys`, for example.
   - *Fix:* built-in rules are now checked first.
3. **`prefix.*` ACL patterns ignored the dot.**
   - *Bug:* `team.*` also matched `teammates`.
   - *Fix:* the dot is now required.
4. **HTTP cancellation was not scoped per client.**
   - *Bug:* `notifications/cancelled` worked on the JSON-RPC id alone. Any caller could cancel another client's in-flight request by guessing its id, and two clients using the same id overwrote each other's cancel flag.
   - *Fix:* in-flight requests are tracked per client (`tracked_request_id`).
5. **Requests left unanswered.**
   - *Bug:* three paths left a request without a reply:
     - `initialized` or `notifications/*` sent with an id got no answer, on both the stdio and HTTP handlers;
     - the bridge read `"id": null` as a missing id, so it forwarded the request as a notification;
     - when the server answered a request with 204 or an empty body, the bridge sent nothing back.
   - *Fix:* each of these now returns a JSON-RPC error carrying the request id.

### B+ tree (P6)
- **Descending scan with `limit: Some(0)`.** It returned one entry because the limit was checked after the push. It now checks before collecting, like the ascending scan.
- **`OrderedFloat` equality.** Equality compared bits while ordering compared values, which breaks the `Ord`/`Eq` contract for `-0.0` vs `0.0`. Equality now follows the order, and the hash is canonicalised to match.

### Aggregation (P7)
The aggregation pipelines agree with the oracle with and without indexes. Covered: `$match` vs `find`, `$group` with `$sum`/count/`$avg`/`$min`/`$max` (grouped by scalar and by array fields), `$count`, `$unwind` row counts, top-K, and skip/limit windows. No fault found.

## Validation
- clippy `-D warnings` (core, mcp-server, bridge): clean
- `cargo test -p ironbase-core`: green
- `mcp-server` tests: green
- bridge tests: green
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: green
- release perf tests: green
- Properties at 3000 cases (P6, P7, bridge) and 30000 cases (stdio JSON-RPC): green
- Each fix has a test that fails without it.
- Versions bumped to 0.3.444 / 1.0.642; CHANGELOG updated.

body:
## What changed

Owner decision 2 (spec 50 feature 05): the storage traits are async-only, so their methods drop the `_async` suffix. Each new name is the old name less `_async` (`get_async` → `get`, `query_async` → `query`, …).

| Crate | Traits |
|---|---|
| `foundation_db` | `QueryStore`, `KeyValueStore`, `BlobStore`, `RateLimiterStore`, `DocumentStore`, `PasskeyStore`, `TosStore`, `AuthStore` |
| `foundation_vectors` | `VectorStore` (`insert`, `delete`, `search`, `get`, `len`, `is_empty`) |
| `foundation_auth` | `CredentialStore` |
| `foundation_ai` | `MemoryStore` (`get`, `set`, `hydrate`, `clear`) |

Every implementation and caller is updated (foundation_db, vectors, auth, ai, cedar, cronjobs, keychain, nativeapis `FjallDocumentStore`, the tests, `examples/cf-login-app` docs), and so are the doc comments and `backends/*/docs`.

**Not renamed:** the async VFS traits (`AsyncVfsFileSystem` etc., e.g. `inode_async`). Decision 1 keeps a sync twin with the plain names for each one (`MemoryFs`/`MemoryDelta` implement both, `SyncFs` bridges). Dropping the suffix there would make calls ambiguous and hide which face a caller uses. Section 7 of the feature file gives the reason.

## Clash check (per type)

| Type | Clash | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| `D1Store`, `LibsqlStore` | Implement `KeyValueStore` + `StateStore`, which now both have `get`/`set`/`delete` | Names kept. A call with both traits in scope is a compile error (E0034), so the wrong method can't be picked silently. No such caller exists; use `KeyValueStore::get(&s, ..)` if needed |
| `D1WasmStorage`, `KVWasmStorage`, `R2WasmStorage` | Public inherent `*_async` mirrors of the trait methods (they used to shadow the trait methods) | Kept. The names now differ, so no call changes target (`StorageProvider`, `WasmCredentialStore`, cf-login-app still reach the inherent ones). Backlog entry to fold them into the traits |
| `D1WasmStorage` | `KeyValueStore` + `CredentialStore` share names | Unchanged: they already shared the names before (both `*_async`). The impls use qualified paths |
| Vector stores vs `VectorIndex`/`Bm25Index` (`insert`/`search`/`len`) | — | No type implements both; no inherent method with the new names |
| `KvMemoryStore` vs `SessionMemory::get/set`, `MemoryCoordinator::hydrate_async` | — | Different types. `MemoryCoordinator`'s inherent `_async` names are left (backlog) |

Method: a script renamed only the definitions inside the trait / `impl Trait for` blocks. Then each `no method named X_async` compiler error was fixed at its exact line and column. Code that the normal build does not compile was built separately (wasm32, features).

## Verification

- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --profile dev`: pass, except `foundation_ai` / `answerme-agent` / `bin/platform`. Those need the `tools/llama.cpp` submodule, which is not in the local checkout
- `cargo check -p foundation_ai --no-default-features --features testing --all-targets`: pass. The llama dev-dep was disabled locally for this check only
- Feature builds: foundation_db (`libsql`), foundation_vectors (`sql-store,turbopuffer,fjall-store,sqlite-vec`), foundation_auth (`server-test,server-native`), foundation_cedar (`db`), foundation_nativeapis (`vfs-fjall`): pass
- `ci.py run <crate> --step wasm` for foundation_db, foundation_vectors, foundation_ai, foundation_auth: pass. foundation_auth `wasm,wasm-bindgen-session` on wasm32: pass. `examples/cf-login-app` on wasm32: pass
- fmt step for every changed crate: pass
- The local build/clippy/test steps were not run: the local disk had under 1 GB free. CI runs them on this PR

author: antruly
body:
Fixes the direct TLS hang: libuvcpp's HTTP/2 response builder rejects uppercase header names, and uvscope set `Cache-Control`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Content-Security-Policy`, etc. in mixed case. The h2 stream was dropped after a successful ALPN h2 handshake, so browsers waited forever.

## Changes

- Lowercase every response header name in the application, auth and preview/download response paths.
- Lowercase custom request header names in the HTTP probe (h2 request headers have the same rule).
- Keep the built-in TLS listener on HTTP/2 with an HTTP/1.1 fallback.
- Add `scripts/tls-smoke.sh`, which starts a self-signed TLS daemon and asserts HTTP/2 200, ALPN h2 and HTTP/1.1 fallback; run it in Linux CI and the release pipeline.
- Document that the libuvcpp webapp still cannot serve HTTP/3 responses (TCP-bound response path); h3 needs nginx 1.25+/Cloudflare or the HTTP/3 probe client.

## Verification

- `./scripts/build.sh`
- `--self-check` 0 failures
- `bash ./scripts/tls-smoke.sh ./build/uvscope 18830` → HTTP/2 + h1 fallback
- Full `smoke-test.sh` suite
- Direct TLS HTTP/2 verified against a libuvcpp 1.8.8 build (UI, setup, authenticated API, WebSocket upgrade over h1)

author: matthias-ennen
body:
## Ergebnis aus dem echten Deploy #40509144868

Der vorherige Doppel-Darsteller-Batch #658 hat funktional korrekt reagiert, aber die **hypothetischen Positivtests nannten versehentlich den falschen TMDB-Film als realen Beispielsieger**. Die aktuelle PRIVATE QA aus dem tatsächlichen Deploy belegt:

- Quelle: `Der Außenseiter 4K Brendan Fraser & Matt Damon Ganzer Film auf Deutsch`, 99 Minuten
- TMDB **movie:14684** hat als **einziger** Kandidat beide tatsächlich genannten Schauspieler; Score nach Castbeweis **50**, Laufzeitdelta **7 Minuten**
- Die zuvor als Besetzungsgewinner angenommene movie:12504 hat **keinen** solchen Zwei-Schauspieler-Beleg; Score **20**, aber Laufzeitdelta 1 Minute
- **Kein Link** wurde zurecht freigegeben: der echte Film liegt 7 Minuten statt der erlaubten <=2 Minuten von der Video-Laufzeit entfernt. Einen möglichen anderen Schnitt prüfen wir nicht automatisch.

## Änderung
Reine **Regressionstest-Korrektur**:
- Reale QA-Paarung (Film 14684 vor 12504) und **fail-closed** wegen Schnitt-/Laufzeitkonflikt in Unit- und vollständiger Katalog-Reconciliation
- Synthetische Positivfälle behalten die technische Abdeckung, aber verwenden klar fiktive Konkurrenz-IDs
- Die bereits erfolgreich verlinkte `Marvins Töchter`-Identität (movie:9819) ist positives Beispiel für die generische zweifache Schauspieler-Evidenz
- Keine Änderung am Matcher oder an beiden Playlists, Video-/Anbieter-Badges, Freigabe-Schwellen oder Datenwrites

**Bisheriger Stand aus Deploy #40509144868:** 131 Videos, 61 veröffentlichte Playlist-Direktlinks, 70 offen. Der Anstieg um vier Links gegenüber 57 erklärt sich durch **15 neu hinzugekommene Playlist-Videos**; nicht als Erfolg der Doppel-Darsteller-Regel verbuchen. Bezug #388.

author: dykamino-coder
body:
## Task

Fix the main regression from #451 (ADR3 A06): `css/css-writing-modes/text-baseline-vrl-002.xht` and `text-baseline-vlr-003.xht` (both against `text-baseline-vrl-002-ref.xht`) have failed since A06 kept the paragraph line height at the computed root value.

## PR type and scope

- [x] Change/Fix: code, tests, CI/config or corrective documentation

- Execution role: maintainer (worker branch, gated)
- Authorized scope: a06fix; no release

- [x] Change/Fix: code, tests, CI/config or corrective documentation

Engine text layout only (`crates/html`: paragraph baseline and the native paragraph route). No style/computed changes, no vendor changes, no release changes.

## Summary

- Root cause: a turned vertical line with a central dominant baseline (`text-orientation: mixed`/`upright`) shifts each run by its central offset from the strut (`shift_spans`), but words were placed on the whole-line shaping baseline (`base_of`), which the tallest run moves. Before #451 the paragraph line height was `k x largest run`, and the resulting oversized line box hid the mismatch by coincidence; with the computed 90px root line height (CSS 2 §10.8, A06 model) the text sat 18px off the line box centre.
- Add `Paragraph::shared_base`: for turned central lines it returns the root inline box baseline (half-leading from the paragraph line height plus strut ascent, including the `::first-line` strut via `root_line_box`), otherwise the existing whole-line baseline. `line_base`, `paint_words` and the clamp/ellipsis mark use it; the per-word correction for where shaping puts each word is unchanged.
- Measure the strut metrics (`strut_run` -> `strut_box`, the existing root-box mechanism) for turned central lines too, and pass the strut font from the native route for them.
- Unit tests: a turned central line with 60px/1.5 strut and 120px/30px runs shares baseline 63 (central baseline = line height / 2, matching reported vertical content baselines); a non-turned paragraph keeps the whole-line baseline 81.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `cargo clippy -p kamin-html --all-targets --features wpt-harness -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo html-test --features wpt-harness`: 1753 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored.
- `check_conventions.py origin/main`, `check_layer_imports.py --base origin/main`, `check_transitional.py --base origin/main` (no new entries), `check_computed.py`: all clean.
- WPT against an exact-main runner (8cbf3631): both target pairs green; narrow gate over css-writing-modes, css-fonts and css-inline baseline greens plus controls-broad (2054 pairs): 0 losses, 3 singleton flakes green 2/2 in isolation.

## Risks and limitations

- Affects only paragraphs whose lines are turned with a central baseline (vertical `mixed`/`upright`); horizontal and sideways lines keep the previous baseline.
- Pre-existing, not addressed here: line padding still treats the dominant-baseline offset in `shift_spans` like a `vertical-align` shift, which can over-grow a turned central line whose runs share one fixed line height; the shift-free flat path still uses the whole-line baseline (runs then have equal central offsets).

## Versioning

- [x] Release versions: unchanged

- [x] Release versions: unchanged

No dependency or lockfile changes.

## Evidence and acceptance

Private diagnostics (`agents/a06fix`): before/after screenshots, temporary instrumentation output from exact main and from the pre-#451 commit (line height 180 vs 90, baseline 126/81 vs root 63), gate reports. No live Windows UI gate is required by this task.

## Dependencies and handoff

Based on main 8cbf3631. Fixes the two inherited #451 losses recorded by the integ-55 acceptance. The lead opens and merges the PR.

author: nielsfranke
body:
Wide-gamut exports embedded the correct profile but always wrote EXIF ColorSpace=1, falsely declaring sRGB. Pass the selected output space into the shared metadata builder: sRGB remains 1; Display P3, Adobe RGB and ProPhoto use 65535 (Uncalibrated). When a source Interop IFD is retained, replace its index with R98 for sRGB or R03 for Adobe RGB and remove it for the other spaces.

Affected outputs: kept-metadata JPEG, PNG, TIFF (8/16-bit), WebP, AVIF and JPEG XL. PNG now stores EXIF in the standard eXIf chunk instead of the previous compressed text chunk (including sRGB/rights-only packets); the existing PNG chunk insertion code is shared with XMP. TIFF still omits the Interop IFD. HEIF/HEIC export is unsupported. Export XMP is rebuilt from catalog fields and writes neither photoshop:ICCProfile nor exif:ColorSpace. Metadata stripping and AI-marking policy are unchanged.

Validation: seven format/depth read-back tests cover all four output spaces and sources with no DCF index, R98 or R03 (84 combinations), checking the tags, decoded pixels and exact embedded ICC bytes. Independent ExifTool read-back of all 84 confirms the tags and identical encoded ImageDataHash / ICC bytes against same-encoder outputs carrying the old declarations. AVIF sRGB and JPEG XL use native colour declarations rather than embedded ICC. This is synthetic encoder/metadata coverage, not a new RAW-render parity measurement; rendering and colour/profile generation code are untouched. Full scripts/check.sh and Claude review are required by ship.sh.

## Second-model review

Verdict on 78919930db589d43798e14c6d849696be8f9e957 by claude (author: codex): **approve**. The fix is correct. EXIF ColorSpace is now 1 only for sRGB and 0xFFFF (Uncalibrated) for Display P3, Adobe RGB and ProPhoto, which is the DCF/EXIF convention. A copied Interop index is replaced with R98 for sRGB or R03 for Adobe RGB, and dropped for P3 and ProPhoto. An index is only written when the source already had an Interop IFD. The output space is passed in explicitly from `export_settings.color_space`, with no special cases. The vendored little_exif sorts tags after every insert (`vendor/little_exif/src/ifd/set.rs:29`), so removing and re-setting the index does not reorder the IFD. sRGB exports from sources without an R03 index should keep the same EXIF bytes as before. Originals are not touched, and the engine crates do not reach into Tauri. The new integration test is solid. It covers every format, both TIFF bit depths and three kinds of source index, and checks the ICC profile is unchanged and decoded pixels are identical. The main gap: the change also moves PNG EXIF from little_exif's zTXt 'Raw profile type exif' chunk to the standard eXIf chunk. That alters every PNG export, sRGB ones included, and the commit message doesn't mention or justify it. Below are that and a few smaller test points; none of them blocks the merge.
- [should_fix] `crates/export/src/exif_processing.rs:1652` PNG exports now carry EXIF in an eXIf chunk instead of the zTXt 'Raw profile type exif' chunk that little_exif wrote before. eXIf is the better choice (it is the PNG 1.5 / 3rd-edition standard and what ImageIO, browsers and exiftool read). But this change is separate from the colour fix: every PNG export changes bytes, sRGB ones included, and readers that only knew the raw-profile text chunk lose the EXIF. The commit has only a title and says nothing about this. Under AGENTS.md, an output byte change has to be stated and explained. Add a commit body that names the container switch and the reason (presumably that the colour declaration was not visible to standard readers in zTXt), or split it into its own commit.
- [should_fix] `crates/export/tests/output_color_metadata.rs:94` For PNG the test reads EXIF back with little_exif, which accepts both eXIf and zTXt. It then only checks that the four bytes `eXIf` appear somewhere in the file (line 130), and those bytes could also turn up inside compressed IDAT/iCCP data. So nothing independently proves the eXIf chunk is well formed (a bare TIFF header, placed before IDAT) or that the old zTXt chunk is gone. Read the PNG with `exif::Reader::read_from_container`, as the AVIF branch already does (kamadak supports PNG eXIf), or walk the chunk list, and assert that there is exactly one EXIF chunk and no 'Raw profile type exif' chunk.
- [nit] `crates/export/src/exif_processing.rs:1604` For Display P3 or ProPhoto, if the source's Interop IFD held only InteroperabilityIndex, removing it leaves an empty Interop IFD. Depending on how little_exif encodes that, the output may contain an InteropOffset pointing at a zero-entry IFD. Every test fixture also sets InteroperabilityVersion, so this case is never exercised. Either drop the empty IFD or add a fixture that has only the index.
- [nit] `crates/export/tests/output_color_metadata.rs:146` The `RAWTONIC_COLOR_METADATA_OUT` dump writes files with plain `std::fs::write`, overwriting whatever is there. That is acceptable for a manual-inspection hook in a test, but it is undocumented. Add a one-line comment saying what it is for, or remove it before merging.
- [nit] `crates/export/src/exif_processing.rs:1590` The `if` inside `vec![...]` is harder to read than a named local such as `let color_space_tag = if color_space == OutputColorSpace::Srgb { 1 } else { 0xffff };`. A short comment that 0xFFFF means 'Uncalibrated' and that the ICC profile is the real declaration would explain why the other three spaces share one value.

author: townsendmerino
body:
MM6's night profile (docs/tasks/task-subsystems-2026-10.md, "MM6's night profile"), built to Francis's option B of 2026-10-27 05:56. It replaces 1b's idle profile after the replay found the Mac's nights are not idle. Gates registered in 78c65806a before the code.

## What changes
- **Every job start records the fit guard's available reading** (cmd/hostmem). It goes in the `=== START` line and in the box's `~/goinfer-logs/night/memory.jsonl`, marked night or day by `--not-before`. Until now the runner logged only the load average at a start.
- **The night profile** is the 25th percentile (linear interpolation) of the night-job readings over the last 14 nights. A reading at 02:00 counts with the evening before. The profile records its percentile, window, reading and night counts, and dates.
- **Where it lives:** `~/goinfer-logs/night/profile-night.json`, per box and not committed. `testdata/machines/*.json` is the census's machine zoo, so a profile rewritten nightly there would churn the census golden. Each box's file is that box's own data.
- **Pricing:** night jobs price against it, and day jobs keep the apps-open profile. With fewer than 5 readings or 3 nights in the window, a night job falls back to apps-open, and `add` warns, naming the counts.
- **`night.py profile [--backfill]`** prints the profile. `--backfill` seeds the history once from the fit guard's own "currently has X GB of memory available" lines in night logs. That sample is biased low, since those lines come from refusals and warnings, so it is marked `backfill`.
- **nobara:** its night logs hold no such lines (no refusals there), so its night profile builds from the START readings. Until then its night jobs price on `nobara-desktop`, with the warning.

## Gates
- **G-NP-1 (pass)** a fake history: the profile equals a hand computation over exactly the in-window night readings; older and day readings are excluded.
- **G-NP-2 (pass)** too few readings fall back to apps-open with the warning.
- **G-NP-3 (pass)** a job through the real runner records `available N MB` in its START line and in `memory.jsonl`.
- **G-NP-4 (follows)** the Mac's replay, with commands handed to mac-vk01.
  - **Expected, stated before running: 7 of 8 refused.** The in-window readings (2.9–7.7 GB) give a 25th percentile near 4.4 GB, a 3.1 GB budget. Rows 1–7 need 5.0–12.6 GB, and row 8 (the 1.5B) needs 2.7 GB.
  - **Pass rule:** at least 7 refused. VOID if too few readings.
- **G-NP-5 (pass)** `test_night.py` (74 tests), `touched.py` and the citation lint.

### [`v1.85.0`](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/releases/tag/v1.85.0): Release 1.85.0

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/compare/v1.84.0...v1.85.0)

### New Features

- stats: Expose the effective client authority (sent on the wire as the HTTP/2 `:authority` header) in client `stats.OutHeader` events. ([#​9296](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9296))
  - Special Thanks: [@​aryansk](https://redirect.github.com/aryansk)
- metadata: Add `ValueFromOutgoingContext`, which reads a single metadata value from outgoing context without copying the entire outgoing metadata into a new map. ([#​9282](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9282))
  - Special Thanks: [@​yuyangguo42](https://redirect.github.com/yuyangguo42)

### Bug Fixes

- transport: Refine control buffer throttling to only count peer-induced control frames, raise the default `GRPC_GO_EXPERIMENTAL_CONTROL_BUFFER_THROTTLE_LIMIT` from 100 to 10,000, and close client connections if reads remain throttled for `10s`. ([#​9563](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9563))
- server: Ensure `Stop()` forcefully terminates the server while `GracefulStop()` is waiting for active handlers to complete. ([#​9394](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9394))
  - Special Thanks: [@​stanhu](https://redirect.github.com/stanhu)
- server: Unconditionally increment the highest-seen stream ID on when handling `HEADERS` frames to comply with [RFC 7540 §5.1.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7540.html#section-5.1.1). Previously, truncated `HEADERS` frames left the connection in an inconsistent state and allowed stream IDs to be reused by clients without resulting in a protocol error. ([#​9414](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9414))
- server: Terminate streams immediately when a `HEADERS` frame includes the `EndStream` bit. Previously, this caused server handlers to hang when reading a message. ([#​9391](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9391))
- server: Reject requests missing both `:authority` and `Host` headers with HTTP 400 and status `Internal`. ([#​9365](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9365))
- xds: Fix a bug where route header matchers with non-lowercase names failed to match routes. ([#​9353](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9353))
  - Special Thanks: [@​winklemad](https://redirect.github.com/winklemad)
- client: Ensure retried RPCs use the correct `:authority` value specified by the LB policy instead of inheriting it from a previous attempt. ([#​9277](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9277))
  - Special Thanks: [@​nvxbug](https://redirect.github.com/nvxbug)
- transport: Fail streams with `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF` instead of `io.EOF` upon receiving truncated  message headers or bodies after partial data has already been received. ([#​9204](https://redirect.github.com/grpc/grpc-go/issues/9204))

author: arenukvern
body: ## Summary Fixes the broken pub.dev release path: release-please tags with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and tag pushes from that token do not trigger other workflows, so `pub_publish.yml` never ran its publish step. Adopts the pattern from [UA PR #14](https://github.com/Arenukvern/universal_automation_ai_device_use/pull/14) (merged `42a9f192`): - **`pub_publish.yml`**: `workflow_dispatch` only; refuse refs other than `refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` with recovery command `gh workflow run pub_publish.yml --ref vX.Y.Z`. Validate job (VERSION sync + train dry-run) then publish job with `id-token: write`. - **`release-please.yml`**: `actions: write`, `id: release`, dispatch `pub_publish.yml` when `steps.release.outputs.release_created == 'true'`, passing `TAG` via env to `gh workflow run` (no shell interpolation of secrets). Does **not** touch VERSION, manifest, changelogs, or tags (RP #11 remains separate). ## Design: train script vs reusable `publish.yml` **Chosen:** `tool/release/publish_packages.sh --publish` after `dart-lang/setup-dart` in a single job with `permissions.id-token: write`. **Not chosen:** chained per-package `dart-lang/setup-dart/.github/workflows/publish.yml` calls. **Why:** oka ships a **12-package train** in strict dependency order with propagation waits and **idempotent skip** when a version already exists on pub.dev (`published_version` check). The train script already encodes that; twelve reusable workflow invocations would duplicate ordering, waiting, and skip logic across jobs, add failure-mode complexity, and still need the same OIDC token minting per package. One `setup-dart` step mints OIDC for each `dart pub publish` in the script, matching pub.dev’s documented GitHub Actions flow. ## release-please output key Root component (path `.` in `release-please-config.json`): - **Gate:** `steps.release.outputs.release_created == 'true'` - **Tag:** `steps.release.outputs.tag_name` (e.g. `v0.9.0`) ## Train packages (`dart tool/release/train.dart list --publish`) Excludes manual-only `oka_process`. 1. `resource_composition` 2. `oka_artifacts` 3. `oka_core` 4. `oka_supervisor` 5. `oka_conformance` 6. `oka_android` 7. `oka_huawei` 8. `oka_play` 9. `oka_rustore` 10. `oka_web` 11. `oka_harness` 12. `oka` ## Docs - Anton one-time checklist: `skills/oka-maintenance/references/publishing.md` - Release sequence updated: `docs/contributing/contribution_guide.mdx` ## Gates (this branch) | Gate | Result | |------|--------| | `actionlint` on `.github/workflows/*.yml` | pass (actionlint v1.7.12) | | `bash -n tool/release/publish_packages.sh` | pass | | `bash tool/release/publish_packages.sh --dry-run` | pass (changelog warning on `resource_composition` pre-existing) | | `dart analyze --fatal-infos` | pass | PR CI `validate` job (per-package dry-run on pull requests) unchanged. ## Type of change - [x] Chore / refactor / tests ## Checklist - [x] Conventional commit title - [x] Docs link to implementation (`publishing.md`, contribution guide) - [x] `dart analyze --fatal-infos` run locally

author: guillaumelauzier
body:
## Objective

PD17's Google Slides option now works. The export writes the chosen version as an editable PowerPoint and creates it as a new presentation in the founder's own Google Drive, then records it. This is #2434 question 2, answer **A**, which the owner confirmed on 2026-10-27 in the session that built this.

Part of #2434
Closes #2683

## Implementation

**The editable PowerPoint** (`services/decks/pptxEditable.ts`) places every D898 block where the print card draws it. D1112 fixes that card at 1920 × 1080, with 3% padding, a 24 px gap and a 12 × 6 grid.
- Text and metric blocks are text boxes. A metric with no figure reads "Not recorded", never 0.
- PNG, JPEG and GIF images are pictures. A WebP image, or one that could not be fetched, is replaced by a sentence saying so.
- A chart is a Browser Rendering screenshot of its own block, taken from a signed print link and clipped to the block's rectangle. At most 30 per file. Otherwise the chart is its type and series in words, as the HTML file writes it.
- Fielded cards and the Sources appendix are the text writer's stacked frames.
- Speaker notes are included only when asked for.
- The PowerPoint *download* is unchanged: still one picture per card. I extracted `notesPackageParts` so both writers share one package. The download is byte-identical before and after the refactor, checked by hashing it.

**The one write** (`services/google/driveCreate.ts`):
- `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_WRITES` is frozen with a single entry: one POST to `https://www.googleapis.com/upload/drive/v3/files?uploadType=multipart`.
- The path has no file id, so the call can only create a file.
- There are no `parents`, no sharing and no permission calls.
- The metadata asks Drive to convert the upload to `application/vnd.google-apps.presentation`.
- The call refuses redirects, has a ten-second limit and caps the answer at 64 KB. A file over 5 MB is refused before any call.
- D1091's `workspace.ts` stays GET-only. A new test scans the whole Worker and finds no other Drive upload.

**The route:** `POST /api/decks/:id/export/google-slides`.
- **Who may call it:** D1091's `member` (support sessions are refused), D895's deck check, and D1091's Workspace scope (the connection is active and the company is enabled). Every refusal is a code returned before any Google call.
- **Order:** create the file, then write one batch: a `deck_exports` row (`google_slides`, the uploaded file's SHA-256, the Drive id in `external_ref`) and one `raise.pitch-deck` audit row.
- **If that batch fails** after the file exists, the route answers `export_not_recorded_created` with the link.
- **No provider body** reaches an answer or a log.

**PD17's Google states** (`ExportDialog.jsx` and `presentExportModel.js`):
- **Not connected:** "Connect Google to create this presentation in your Drive. Axal VC creates only the file you export.", with "Connect Google ›" linking to D1091's connector page, and no Export button.
- **Connected:** the dialog says what the export will do, and afterwards shows "Created in Google Slides · Open ›".
- **Google kept the file as PowerPoint:** the dialog says so and never calls it Slides.
- **Open** links only to `docs.google.com` or `drive.google.com`.
- **Charts written as text:** the dialog says how many.

**Check this:**
- The copy says "Axal VC", as D1091's Google screens do; #2683's draft said "StudioOS".
- The route requires D1091's company enablement for the deck's venture, the same scope as every other Workspace route.

**Main's red D1306 tests:** this PR first carried a port of #3476 for them. Main has since taken #3471's version of the fix, so the merge of main (6e3cca6f) takes main's copy of `account_drawer_d1306.test.mjs`, and this PR no longer changes that file.

## Files changed

- `cloudflare-worker/src/services/decks/pptxEditable.ts` (new): the editable writer.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/services/google/driveCreate.ts` (new): the one Drive create call.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/deck_exports.ts`: the Google Slides route; `fetchImages` split out of `inlineImages`.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/routes/decks.ts`: `exportDeckOf`, the export's deck construction, now shared.
- `cloudflare-worker/src/services/decks/pptx.ts`: shared helpers exported and `notesPackageParts` extracted.
- `frontend/src/pages/raise/pitch/ExportDialog.jsx`, `presentExportModel.js` and `frontend/src/lib/api.js` (`deckExportGoogleSlides`).
- Tests:
  - `cloudflare-worker/test/deck_google_slides_d904.test.ts` (new, 12 tests);
  - `frontend/test/pitch_google_slides_d904.test.mjs` (new, 5 tests);
  - `frontend/test/pitch_present_export_d901.test.mjs` (Google Slides is now offered).
- Docs: `documentation/architecture/decisions/D904.md`, ROUTE_MAP's Pitch Deck Studio row, and the READMEs for `services/decks`, `services/google` and `pages/raise/pitch`.

## Testing

- `rm -rf docs && npm run build && npm run test:drift` → **EXIT=0** on the branch before main's latest merge. CI's full suite runs on the merged head.
- After the merge, the D904, D901 and D1306 suites, the Worker typecheck, `check-decision-ids`, `check-folder-docs`, `build-profile-routing --check` and `check-api-drift` all pass.
- D1091's suites pass, including its GET-only guard.
- Mutation checks: 23 mutations, all caught once I added a check pinning the chart cap at 30. They covered:
  - grid geometry;
  - WebP placement;
  - the empty metric;
  - the chart shot, its clip and the PNG check;
  - the shot cap;
  - notes;
  - conversion metadata;
  - the size check order;
  - `converted`;
  - id validation;
  - the 403 code;
  - `external_ref`;
  - the audit row;
  - the support session and company checks;
  - the created-but-unrecorded answer;
  - the Open href check;
  - the PowerPoint wording;
  - Export while not connected;
  - the options body;
  - the reconnect link.

## Risks

- **Ships:** the Worker (a new route and the first Workspace write) and the frontend build. No migration and no `wrangler.toml` change.
- **Rollback:** revert the PR. Files already created stay in founders' Drives, as files the founders own.
- **Security:**
  - one frozen create call under `drive.file`, which reaches only files the app created or the member chose;
  - no token reaches the browser;
  - codes only in answers;
  - support sessions refused;
  - no secret in the diff.
- **UNVERIFIED:**
  - whether Drive converts the upload to Slides under `drive.file` (the dialog reports what Drive did);
  - whether the `BROWSER` binding honours `screenshotOptions.clip`;
  - whether the editable file renders as expected in PowerPoint and Slides. The tests read its XML; nobody has opened it in PowerPoint or Slides yet.

  #2683's first box, one live export into the owner's Drive confirmed by the owner, is the owner's step.

## Dependencies

- Uses D1091's connection (#2956) and part 7's ledger (#2713).

## Agent

S14 · Claude Code

## Review requested

Owner.

author: arturzrk
body:
## Summary
- Answers "do we have a change-risk anti-pattern metric?" -- no, nothing computed this before. Adds one, as a report only (explicit decision: no CI gate).
- Ranks every backend Domain+Application method by CRAP score: `complexity^2 * (1-coverage)^3 + complexity` (Savoia/Evans). High score = complex AND undertested; that combination is the actual risk, distinct from complexity alone.
- Uses [ReportGenerator](https://github.com/danielpalme/ReportGenerator) (MIT) as a local dotnet tool purely for its accurate per-method cyclomatic complexity (parsed from the C# source) rather than writing a custom analyzer. ReportGenerator's free tier already shows complexity + coverage side by side per method; it just doesn't rank them together across the codebase (that's a paid feature). `backend/tools/CrapReport` (kept out of `HomeMaintenance.sln`, so it never touches the normal build/test/CI path) parses that same free HTML output and does the ranking itself.
- `scripts/crap-report.sh` orchestrates the pipeline and is hermetically tested the same way as the existing `dev.sh`/`dev-stop.sh` scripts (stub `dotnet`, verify pipeline ordering, no real build in tests). Wired into the same CI `validators` job.

## Verification against this codebase
The three handlers already identified as most complex in manual refactoring work this session (`UpdateJobHandler`, `UpdateAssetHandler`, `UpdateJobDefinitionHandler`) are exactly the top of the ranking -- all at 100% coverage, confirming the metric correctly degrades to "just complexity" when coverage is already high. The one exception, `Domain.ScheduleDefinition.OccurrencesInRange()` at 86% coverage, is the single top-15 case where undercoverage (not just complexity) is genuinely driving the risk -- exactly the signal this metric exists to surface.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash scripts/crap-report.test.sh` -- all 4 hermetic tests pass
- [x] `bash scripts/crap-report.sh` run for real end-to-end -- produces `logs/crap/crap-report.md` (190 methods ranked) and prints the top 15
- [x] `dotnet restore` / `dotnet build` from `backend/` confirmed to still only target `HomeMaintenance.sln` -- the new tool project doesn't affect the normal build
- [x] `bash scripts/dev.test.sh` and `bash scripts/dev-stop.test.sh` still pass (no regression to the existing dev-script suites)

author: slyvchenko
body:
## Product defect
Origin allowlisting alone could surface arbitrary Kibana `/api/*`, management or session URLs from untrusted Jira text as supposedly read-only browser actions. Separately, legacy `cconFlowId` extraction could accept credential-bearing URLs whose hostname and port matched the internal Kibana endpoint.

## Fix
- Require exact approved Kibana origin AND a known Discover UI entry point (`/app/kibana` legacy or `/app/discover`); reject API, management, login and lookalike paths, even under a trusted domain.
- Restrict internal flow filter references to HTTP(S), expected `/app/kibana` path/port, no embedded username/password and bounded length.
- Add synthetic tests for unsafe route rejection, known UI URLs, credentials, alternate schemes, and safe legacy extraction.
- Document this boundary for local analysts.

## Release boundary
No live Kibana access or credentials; synthetic only. No real Jira/CCON/Kibana payloads, automation of browser navigation, or user data committed. EVD-06 stays PARTIAL until authorized human testing; Issue #50 stays BLOCKED_INDEPENDENT_UAT.

author: therebelrobot
body:
## Summary

Validated against the October 2026 Node.js security wave.

**Not pre-auth reachable by Node2Shell here** — the app never decompresses
attacker-controlled Brotli (no Express / body-parser anywhere; the runtime is
Hono, a raw `node:http` server, or an nginx-served static bundle). But the Node
version was left floating, so the image is only patched if it happens to be
rebuilt after the fix shipped.

## Changes

- Pin the Dockerfile base image to the exact patched patch on the line already in use.
- Pin the CI `node-version` to the same patched patch.
- Set `engines.node` to `>=22.23.4`.

## Why

CVE-2026-111497 (**Node2Shell**): out-of-bounds write in Node's bundled Brotli
decoder, leading to RCE / memory disclosure. Fixed in **Node 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 /
26.12.1** (released 2026-10-21). A floating major tag (`node:24-alpine`) or a
floating `node-version: 24` only carries the fix if rebuilt after that date;
pinning the exact patch makes the fix explicit and stops it drifting.

No application code changes.

author: sanne-ai-bot
body:
Part of #1703 (step 4.3, a further `cli/command` slice: the instance commands).

> **Stacked on #1731**, which is based on `main`. Until #1731 merges, this PR's diff includes its commit.
> This step's own commits are the last four, `d45dd74a..HEAD`: `9201f016`, `3368f1b1`, `d0ee03dc`, `4c12f1bb` (restacked unchanged from `669c78bc`, `cc390cf4`, `e9d8314b`, `078494b4`, which the text below names; `669c78bc` was originally `fad7f6fb`).
> The branch is rebased onto `main` with `git rebase --onto origin/main <old base>` as soon as #1731 merges.

## What

`BranchCommand`, `ShellCommand`, `RunCommand`, `DestroyCommand` and `ProjectCommand` leave the raw-output baseline (47 raw uses, 5 of them hand-indented).
- Why a command failed is an `error`, with its advice or usage as details. That covers argument conflicts, a missing source, instance or project file, an unknown action, and a task that cannot be joined.
  - `isx run` with an unknown action lists the available ones as details.
  - `isx shell --task` with several tasks lists each with the command that joins it. A busy task's refusal carries what it did lately; a failed guest read of that never hides the refusal.
  - Messages from exceptions go through `BaseCommand.failure`, so a null message never prints nothing.
- What a command does on the way is a step at the step indent: the auto-detected source, `Connecting to ...`, the action it runs and what that action did.
- `isx destroy --all-*` shows what it will destroy as a group. A lock that cannot be taken is an error for one target and a warning in bulk, where the run goes on.
- An action that runs directly (opening a URL, copying to the clipboard) and fails is an error, and `isx run` exits 1 with it (`RunCommand.report`); it printed the failure as a plain line and exited 0. `docs/CLI.md` says so.
- Review's optional items, one commit each:
  - `cc390cf4`: `isx run`'s broken default action warns with the reason, its fallback ("Opening a shell instead.") as a detail. No default at all stays a step.
  - `e9d8314b`: `isx destroy --all-*` that left anything behind, locked or failed, ends on an error instead of a green success line, as its exit 1 already said.
  - `078494b4`: `isx project update`'s wrong-project error has "Use --config ..." as a detail.
- `isx branch --format` and `isx project`'s help print to `BuildOutput.results()`.
- `isx project create`'s advice says `isx build`, no longer `incus-spawn build`.

## Design

- **Chosen:** the mapping of the earlier slices: errors with details, steps, groups, `results()`, questions through `Prompts`.
- **Alternatives:** structured, nested details on `Output.error`, so a detail list could carry sub-items. Detail lines are flat here instead, with no hand indentation.
- **Why:** each message has one kind, which the TUI's log and a recorder keep; nested details are a change to the seam that `CleanCommand`'s slice may want too.

## Regression test

`RunCommandReportTest.aFailedActionIsAnError`: a failed `ActionResult` is one `ERROR` event and `report` returns false, so `isx run` exits 1. Before, `doExecute` printed every result as a step and returned success; `report` does not exist on `c16ff75c`, so the test does not compile there. `DestroyCommandOutputTest.aBulkDestroyThatLeftSomethingBehindEndsOnAnError` pins `e9d8314b`.

`DestroyCommandOutputTest.conflictingArgumentsAreAnError`: each argument refusal is one `ERROR` event. On `295f7a01` (this PR's base) it fails with `expected: <[specify --all-templates or --all-instances, not both.]> but was: <[]>`, since the refusal was a raw stderr line no recorder sees.
`ShellCommandTaskTest.aBusyTaskIsAnErrorWithWhatItDidLately` and `severalTasksAreAnErrorEachWithTheCommandThatJoinsIt` pin `explain`'s errors; on the base `explain` took a `PrintStream`, so they do not compile there.

## CHARACTER

Touches the shell and branch path's narration only: lines move to the step indent, and `Connecting to ...` loses its trailing blank line. No extra Incus request; the one guest read on a busy task is unchanged.

## Docs

none needed: `.claude/rules/terminal-output.md` already describes this mapping, and no architecture changed.

## Verified on

- This box (Fedora 44 x86_64, JVM): `mvn test` green at `078494b4` (first at `fad7f6fb`).
- Native: `./install.sh --native` at `fad7f6fb`; `isx destroy --all-templates --all-instances` and `isx shell box t1` print their errors (with the usage as a detail) at the step indent and exit 1.
- Native at `078494b4`: `mvn package -Dnative -Dquarkus.native.container-build=false` with this box's Oracle GraalVM 25.4.4 (the line the builder image carries), since `./install.sh --native` stalled pulling `container-registry.oracle.com/graalvm/native-image:25i4-ol10` here. `isx destroy` and `isx shell box t1` print their errors at the step indent and exit 1. A failing direct action was not exercised natively (no Incus here); `RunCommandReportTest` covers it.
- Not run: branching, shells and actions against a real Incus. This box has no Incus, and the changes are output only.

## Handoff

none

## Follow-ups

- Noted: `tui/ShellLaunch` still prints `Connecting to ...` raw with a trailing blank line, now unlike the commands. A shared shell-opening helper for both belongs with the TUI's slice.
- Noted: `ProjectCommand.loadProjectConfig` still ends the process with `System.exit(1)` after its error; returning a failure would let it be tested.
- Noted: `withStdoutOnStderr` (`BaseCommand`) still swaps `System.out`; it goes once `DoctorCommand` is migrated.

## Review findings not applied

- `ShellCommand.explain` keeps a `recent` parameter only a busy task uses: it lets the busy refusal be tested as one event.
- A task line joins its description and command with `: `; a summary containing `: ` reads less cleanly. Flat details have no better separator without nesting, noted under Design.
- `BranchCommand`, `RunCommand` and `ProjectCommand`'s conversions have no output test of their own, apart from `RunCommand.report`; they are mechanical, and the gate keeps them off the raw streams.
- The several-tasks list of `isx shell --task` stays the error's details rather than a group of steps: a group goes to stdout and the error to stderr, so they would part when either is redirected.
- An action's failure message is shown as the action words it (often capitalised), not rewritten to the lowercase reason style.
- `isx run` still waits for Enter after an `auto_return: false` action that failed, as it does after one that succeeded.

## Risk

Low to moderate for how these commands look: errors and steps move to the step indent, and a script matching `^Error:` on their stderr stops matching (as for every migrated command). Behaviour and exit codes are unchanged; `isx destroy <name>` reports a lock it cannot take as an error, where it was a warning before its exit 1.

## Timing

- Unit: `mvn test` about 8 min.
- Native: `./install.sh --native` 91 s at `fad7f6fb`; the local CLI build at `078494b4` 33 s.
- Full (ITs): not run.

P1-82 group (3), item 5. 🟢. Closes #1646's nits. Its "accepted limits" list stays as it is.

## What changed in `scripts/mutate.mjs`

- **A tab in a path.** `ls-files -s -z` gives `<mode> <sha> <stage>\t<path>`. It is now split on the first tab only, so a tracked path holding a tab is edited instead of refused as untracked (was `:507-511`).
- **A submodule.** An edit naming a submodule (mode `160000`) is refused by name. Before, it failed with EISDIR at exit 3.
- **A `..x.json` sidecar.** A sidecar inside the repo named like `..x.json` is printed by its relative path. Only `..`, `../…` or an absolute relative path is outside the repo.
- **Linked caches.** In a repo without pnpm, the worktree used to link the checkout's `node_modules` folder, so vitest's `node_modules/.vite` cache landed in the checkout. It now gets a real `node_modules` holding one link per entry (cache folders skipped), so the run's caches stay in the worktree and leave with it. `dirtyLines` ignores everything under `node_modules/`.
- **`--json` on an early stop.** `--json` now prints JSON on an error with no results yet, and on a signal before the first result.

## Verify first

## Why

Renovate opened a pull request per crate (#41 to #47), because only Serde and Tokio were grouped. Its commit types also cut releases:

- `fix(deps)` for every minor update;
- `feat(deps)` for every major, even the Ubuntu runner bump in #48.

## What changes

- **Two Rust PRs instead of one per crate:**
  - **"Rust dependencies":** minor and patch updates, which should merge easily.
  - **"Rust dependencies (major)":** majors, plus a minor bump of a 0.x crate. In Cargo's rules a 0.x minor bump breaks (0.10 to 0.11), so `sha2` 0.11, `rusqlite` 0.41, `reqwest` 0.13 and the like land here. One breaking update never holds back the safe ones.
  - The Serde and Tokio groups fold into these. To split a crate out later, give it its own rule.
- **`build(deps)` for every update**, which is how the project rules type dependencies. It makes no release on its own.
- **Security updates are `fix(deps)`** (`vulnerabilityAlerts`), so they do make a release.
- **Removed:** the dev-dependency automerge rule. It matched `devDependencies`, npm's name, so it never applied to a crate.
- **Unchanged:** the 1st/15th schedule, the limit of 3 PRs, the GitHub Actions group, lock file maintenance, and the Rust toolchain as its own PR.

## After merging

Renovate rebuilds its PRs on its next run: #41 to #47 should close in favour of the two Rust PRs, and the remaining titles move to `build(deps)`.

## Checks

`renovate-config-validator` passes.

author: arch-fan
body:
## Summary

- `nix develop` now installs [git-hooks.nix](https://github.com/cachix/git-hooks.nix) pre-commit hooks:
  - **README package table**: reruns `scripts/generate-package-docs.py` when a commit touches `packages/`, `nix/`, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock`, the generator, or `README.md`. If the table changes, the commit stops so the regenerated README can be reviewed and staged.
  - **treefmt**: the same nixfmt configuration as `nix fmt`.
- CI's Evaluate job runs the same hooks (`nix develop --command pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure`) in place of the standalone README check, so local hooks and CI enforce one definition.
- `pre-commit.check.enable = false`: the table hook evaluates the flake, which the build sandbox cannot do, so the hooks run from the development shell rather than as a flake check.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (a symlink into the store created by the shell hook) is ignored.
- AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the README Development section describe the hooks. The documented commands still work without hooks.

No package derivations change, so no package rebuilds are needed.

## Verification

```console
nix develop --command pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure   # both hooks pass
nix fmt                                                                   # 0 files changed
./scripts/generate-package-docs.py --check                                # up to date
nix run --inputs-from . nixpkgs#nix-eval-jobs -- --flake .#checks.x86_64-linux --check-cache-status --workers 2 | ./scripts/ci-build-plan.py
nix flake check --no-build                                                # all checks passed (after the plan realises IFD sources, as in CI)
```

Hook behaviour, tested by hand and reverted:

- Editing a version in the README table: the hook fails with "files were modified by this hook" and restores the generated value.
- Staging a changed `meta.description` in `packages/dnsx/package.nix`: the hook fails and rewrites the dnsx row.

body:
## Summary
Implements backlog task **H03**: *Design: deleting a client's data on request* (Size S, Depends on E05, E08, FR-44).

### Key Architectural Decisions (ADR-M97):
1. **Taxonomy of Purged vs Retained Data (AC1)**:
   - **Hard Purged**: Evidence files in SeaweedFS (`diffs/`, `proposals/`, `packs/`, `snapshots/`), Langfuse traces and OTLP batches in ClickHouse, and knowledge vector schemas in `knowledge-db`.
   - **In-Place PII Pseudonymization**: Personal data in `users` (`email`, `display_name`) and `user_identities` (`external_login`) is scrubbed in-place (`deleted-<id>@redacted.invalid`) and accounts are disabled, strictly preserving foreign key referential integrity with `ON DELETE RESTRICT`.
   - **Retained Intact**: Append-only tables (`audit_log`, `gate_decisions`, `run_events`, `cost_records`) and cryptographic SHA-256 hash chains are kept untouched for a minimum of 2 years to satisfy enterprise compliance (SOC 2, ISO 27001, handbook Ch.3).
2. **Append-Only Compliance & Invariant (AC2)**:
   - Enforces Client Data Deletion Invariant: zero rows deleted or updated in any append-only table. Trigger `SDA01` remains in effect.
3. **Audit Trail of Deletion (AC1)**:
   - The deletion advances the tenant's hash chain with lifecycle audit events: `client_data.deletion_requested`, `client_data.deletion_approved`, `client_data.deletion_started`, and terminal event `client_data.deleted`.
4. **Safety & Governance**:
   - Dual-authorization (Two-Person rule: Tenant Admin initiator + Platform Operator approver).
   - Mandatory 14-day grace period.
   - Active legal holds (`evidence_holds`) block physical deletion of held intent files until formally released by counsel.
5. **Backlog Decomposition (AC3)**:
   - No runtime code in H03 (pure design); follow-up implementation split into H03a (Database Schema & Anonymizer), H03b (Worker Purge Pass), and H03c (CLI Ops Tooling).

### Deliverables:
- `design/ADR-M97-client-data-deletion.md`
- `design/QUESTIONS.md` (#611–#615)
- `design/README.md` (ADR-M97 registered; next free block: QUESTIONS #616–#620; ADR-M98)
- `CLAUDE.md` (updated next free block)
- `design/D-05-data-model.md` (§10.1 & history v1.65)
- `scripts/generate-backlog.py` (v1.61) & regenerated `D-08`, `CSV`, `ROADMAP.md`
- `CHANGELOG.md` under `[Unreleased]`

author: jamesluoyh
body:
The speed-up commit landed on `plot-layer-curves` after #24 was merged, so it's carried here along with a cleanup of legacy code.

## Extraction speed-ups
- Hooks gather the last real token on the GPU, and `lm_head` runs only at that token, so full-sequence vocabulary logits are never built or copied to the host.
- Extraction stores logit A, logit B, the vocabulary log-normalizer, and the greedy token id: 16 bytes per row instead of ~600KB. This is now the only format; the full-vocabulary scope is removed.
  - Canonical probabilities and greedy choices matched the full-vocabulary scorer exactly before it was removed, and raw probabilities agreed to float32 precision.
- Rows are batched shortest-first at 32.
- A CUDA out-of-memory error now raises `BatchExceededMemory`, so the halving retry actually runs. Before, it never fired.
- Attention uses SDPA instead of eager.

Measured on 256 real MMLU prompts with Qwen2.5-7B on one RTX PRO 6000: the forward pass goes from 3.5 to 51 rows/s (14.5×), before counting the smaller disk writes.

Against an fp32 reference on 24 prompts:
- bf16 eager: residuals ~11% off, and P(A) off by up to 0.88.
- bf16 SDPA: residuals within ~1.4%, and P(A) within 0.03.

So SDPA is also the more accurate choice.

## Removed backward compatibility
- Every shard must store the final norm. `read_final_norm_row` no longer returns `None`.
- `build_row_key` now requires the attention backend, logits scope, and runtime signature. The `eager` and "unspecified" defaults are gone.
- Removed:
  - the `require_all_variants` rename guard
  - the runner's unused `execution_backend`/`batch_size` parameters
  - the runner's precision check, which nothing ever triggered
  - `QwenAdapter.forward`, which is unused now that capture calls `forward_selected`

## Forward-compatible cache keys
- The row key keeps only `backend`, `device_type`, `attention_backend` and `execution_precision` from the runtime signature. Torch, transformers and numpy versions, the GPU name and its compute capability stay on the collection manifest. A library upgrade or a different GPU reuses existing rows.
- Filter report paths are written next to the hashed record, not inside it. Moving `storage_root` keeps the filter digest, view ids and run ids.
- `Record.payload()` leaves out fields equal to their declared default, replacing `omit_if_none`. A field added later with a default no longer changes existing digests. A released default must never change; bump the schema instead.
- `non_default_fields()` replaces `vars()` in the extraction request signature. Optional `InterventionDefinition` fields now have defaults, and `distractor_seed` / `distractor_selection` are omitted when unset.
- `REPORTING_SETTINGS` is now `EXTRACTION_EXCLUDED_KEYS`: one list to update when an analysis setting is renamed.

## Removed legacy code
- The `logits_scope` config key and the full-vocabulary scorer. Both configs now use the summary format.
- Leftovers of the replaced probability-basis decision: `DecisionRecord`, `PROBABILITY_BASES`, the `probability_basis` / `stops_for_probability_basis` placeholders in `behavior.json` and `subset.json`, and tests that only checked the removed concept stayed absent.
- Unused `load_qwen`, `INDEX_KIND` and `layer_choices`.
- Record types never used outside their tests: `ExtractionRecord`, `ProbeSpec`, `RunManifest`, `EvaluationManifest`, `ExecutionProvenance`.
- `pr_plan.md` (a stale PR checklist) and `example.py` (a scratch script).

## Reviewer notes
- Row keys, request signatures, and filter/view/run digests change (adapter v2, SDPA, the narrower runtime key, path-free filter reports), so existing extraction caches and collections can't be reused. Both old caches are being deleted.

## Testing
- `pytest`: 232 passed. Scoring tests now run through the summary path and are checked against a float64 softmax over the vocabulary.
- Old vs new extraction checked on real MMLU prompts with Qwen2.5-7B (numbers above).

## What/Why/How?

The first time a user runs Redocly CLI, it advertizes the agent skills and the `redocly skills` command (or anything else in the future), so users learn new features directly from Redocly CLI.

- The announcement waits until the CLI is up to date, so a run shows either the update notice or the announcement, never both.
- Both now show only when stderr is a terminal, so scripts, pipes, and AI agents neither see the update notice nor use up the announcement.
- The Docker image sets `REDOCLY_SUPPRESS_UPDATE_NOTICE=true`, which turns off both there, because each run starts with an empty home folder.

## Testing

Locally, E2E tests.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> User-facing stderr banners and a small home-directory file; no API or auth changes. Docker explicitly suppresses notices.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **one-time terminal banner** that promotes Redocly CLI agent skills and `redocly skills`, shown on the first interactive run when the CLI is already on the latest cached version.
> 
> Startup messaging is consolidated in `notifier.ts`: the yargs middleware now calls `notify` instead of the old update-only helper. **Update notices take priority** over the announcement; neither appears when stderr is not a TTY (pipes, CI, tests). `REDOCLY_SUPPRESS_UPDATE_NOTICE=true` disables **both** banners—the Docker image sets this so ephemeral containers do not spam or burn the one-shot announcement.
