author: ngl-damien
body:
## Source-backed defect

The bounded readers for `service.json` and the institutional `ledger.json` used replacement-decoding UTF-8 before checking canonical JSON. Invalid bytes can decode to U+FFFD; canonical string comparison alone does not prove the persisted bytes were valid UTF-8.

## Changes

- Reject malformed UTF-8 in service-store envelopes with `SERVICE_STORE_INVALID_UTF8` before JSON parsing.
- Reject malformed UTF-8 in ledger history with `LEDGER_TAMPERED` before replay.
- Add adversarial malformed-byte regressions for the service store, ledger, and decision store; verify fail-closed rejection and writer-lock cleanup.
- Preserve a durable engineering checkpoint at `docs/meteor/STRICT-UTF8-PERSISTED-ENVELOPES-CHECKPOINT-2026-10-27.md`.

## Exact-head verification

Base `main`: `f75a5112d34d0ec189c1ad73f6ba14493ca92f06`.
Head verified: `afcbf8a87cdf2979cb13e51e70985cbaecb42cd2`.

All three exact-head GitHub Actions workflows completed successfully:
- [Full verification — 40525080032](https://github.com/ngl-damien/No-Gas-Labs-Alpha-1/actions/runs/40525080032)
- [Genesis Evidence Invariant — 40525080006](https://github.com/ngl-damien/No-Gas-Labs-Alpha-1/actions/runs/40525080006)
- [Browser acceptance — 40525080452](https://github.com/ngl-damien/No-Gas-Labs-Alpha-1/actions/runs/40525080452)

No local test run is claimed; a local clone attempt could not resolve `github.com`.

## Limits

These checks establish persisted-byte integrity, not writer authentication, Founder identity, or a production trust root. They do not resolve Issue #17's independent Founder-key custody and crash/stale-lock recovery work. Production observation trust remains blocked until trust roots and the live server mutation path are independently verified. No deployment or production key operation is included.

author: jejezz
body:
## 요약
`re_editor` 포크([daylight-editor-flutter](https://github.com/jejezz/daylight-editor-flutter) v0.10.0+1)로 만든 내장 텍스트 에디터를 추가한다. F3 보기와 짝이 되는 F4 편집이다. 설계와 조사 결과는 PLAN.md의 "내장 텍스트 에디터 (F4)" 절에 있다.

## 변경
- **열기**: F4, 우클릭 "편집", F-바 "F4 편집". 5MB 이하는 무엇이든 열고, 바이너리·UTF-8 아님은 Latin-1(바이트 그대로)로 보여 주는 **읽기 전용**으로 연다. 원격 파일과 5MB 초과는 이유를 알리고 열지 않는다
- **편집**: 구문 강조, 줄 번호, 코드 접기, 찾기/바꾸기(정규식·대소문자), 줄 이동, 주석 토글(언어별 규칙 연결 — 포크는 규칙 없이는 ⌘/가 동작하지 않는다), BOM·LF/CRLF 보존
- **저장**: Ctrl/Cmd+S, **다른 이름으로 저장**(Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S, 덮어쓰기 확인), 저장 전 외부 변경 확인, 닫을 때 저장 여부 확인
- **화면**: 툴바(실행 취소·다시 실행·찾기·바꾸기·줄 이동·줄 바꿈·저장·?)와 편집 영역·상태 바를 색과 구분선으로 분리. **(?)** 로 단축키 안내를 툴바 아래에 고정하고 X로 닫는다(열림 여부 기억)
- **마크다운**: `.md`는 오른쪽에 분할 미리보기(`flutter_markdown_plus`), Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V 또는 툴바 버튼으로 끈다
- 새 의존성: `re_editor`(git, 포크), `re_highlight`, `flutter_markdown_plus`. 사용자 대상 문자열은 모두 ARB(ko/en)에 넣었다

## 알아둘 점
- 입력 대화상자를 닫을 때 컨트롤러를 먼저 dispose해 앱이 깨지던 문제를 고쳤다(대화상자가 컨트롤러를 소유)
- re_editor는 포커스를 가진 채 사라지면 커서 깜박임 타이머를 끄지 못하는 것으로 보인다. 닫히는 순간 포커스를 풀어 피했지만 **포크 쪽 근본 수정은 별도**로 필요하다
- 편집은 로컬 파일만이다. 원격(SFTP→FTP→WebDAV) 업로드백, CP949/UTF-16 인코딩 선택은 PLAN.md의 다음 단계

## 확인
- `flutter analyze` 문제 없음
- 새 테스트 23개 통과(`editor_text_file_test`, `editor_screen_test`, `editor_save_as_test`, `editor_toolbar_test`)
- 전체 테스트에서 `settings_menus_test.dart` 2건이 실패하나 **이 변경과 무관**하다(변경을 치우고 돌려도 동일하게 실패)
- macOS 디버그 빌드에서 F4 열기, 한글 타이핑, 저장·다른 이름으로 저장, 찾기, 줄 이동, 주석 토글, 닫기 확인 대화상자, 바이너리 읽기 전용, 마크다운 미리보기, 단축키 패널 열고 닫기를 직접 확인했다
- **확인하지 못한 것**: Windows/Linux, 큰 파일(5MB 근처) 성능, 포크의 타이머 누수가 실제 앱에서 막히는지

author: aasimsayani
body:
Before: Plaid balances and QuickBooks or Xero invoices were stored as events no department read, so nothing knew how much cash the store had or what customers owed, and the console had no way to read it.

After: Finance keeps each bank account's latest balance (`bank.balance`) and each sales invoice with what is still owed (`receivable.invoice`, or `receivable.removed` once deleted from the books) as signals. When $500 or more in US dollar invoices is more than 30 days past due, it recommends following up with those customers, oldest first. A new read-only route, `GET /v1/signals?kind=bank.balance,receivable.invoice`, returns the latest signals of up to 10 kinds (200 by default, up to 1,000), for this instance's organization only.

Signals, unlike event payloads, are kept after raw data retention clears payloads (#335), so the console's money view keeps working once the 30-day window passes.

How: Finance now owns `bank.account_updated`, `accounting.invoice_updated` and `accounting.record_deleted`, with schemas loose enough for what Plaid, QuickBooks and Xero send today. Their existing "produces payloads the retail departments accept" tests now also check the new signals. `recentSignals` takes an optional list of kinds, in memory and in Postgres, where a new index (`20261027000001_signals_by_kind.sql`) serves it. The console's money tiles build on this in a separate private PR.

Checks: secrets scan, typecheck, registry check, build and coverage (805 tests) pass, and the new index is checked against PGlite. A break-it run of 22 mutants ends with every mutant caught or the code simplified. The mutants included reading another organization's signals through a query parameter, dropping the kind check, lifting the 1,000 cap and taking amounts that aren't whole cents.

author: jalehman
body:
Related: #178177
Related: #178346

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw doctor --fix` copies every agent database twice during a schema upgrade, even when the upgrade only bumps version metadata.

## User Impact

User impact: schema upgrades in Doctor finish minutes sooner on hosts with large agent databases and write gigabytes fewer backup bytes. Stores the upgrade did not migrate keep the full rollback backup as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor decided whether to take the full heartbeat rollback backup from the schema check made *before* the declared version phase ran. After that phase had already migrated every pending store and kept its own scoped backups, Doctor still treated them as outdated and made a second full, integrity-checked copy of every agent database plus the shared state database.

The decision now counts only stores the version phase did not commit. Refused or unreadable stores, unmigrated stores, and runs where the version phase returned nothing (for example full-image backups) still take the full backup. Heartbeat-specific pending work still forces it as before.

## Evidence

Isolated reproduction (no network, isolated HOME, never live state): a copy of a real install with 15 agent databases (6.8 GB, largest 6.2 GB) rolled back from schema 32 to 31, timed with `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_STARTUP_TRACE`.

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| `doctor.heartbeat-migration-backups` | 119.3 s | 0.3 s |
| Backup files written | 32 (7.38 GB) | 16 (141 MB) |
| Total wall time | 736.6 s | 555.5 s |

Both runs exited 0 with all 15 databases at schema 32. The same second backup group took about 69 s on the reporting host's real upgrade.

- New `src/commands/doctor-heartbeat-migration-backup.test.ts` (5 tests); 2 fail against the previous logic.
- `pnpm vitest run` on that file, `src/commands/doctor-migration-backup.test.ts` and `src/flows/doctor-health.update-schema.test.ts`: 44 passed, after rebasing on current main.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxfmt and oxlint clean.
- Autoreview (Claude engine; Codex auth was unavailable on this host): scoped-clean at P2.

### Upgrade compatibility proof: published 2026.10.8 → candidate (Crabbox, Mac Studio)

Crabbox `provider=ssh` on the Mac Studio (`100.97.87.71`, macOS 26.5.1 arm64), isolated HOME/state, private Gateway ports. The real published `openclaw@2026.10.8` wrote the state using the `legacy-operator-state` survivor seeding: a real baseline Gateway run with a mock model, agents `main` + `ops`, retired `agents.defaults.heartbeat`, and a Discord plugin. That state is state schema **20** / agent schema **25**. The candidate is at **35 / 37**. The candidate tarball was packed from `4d6f976`, with source hashes checked on the host. `7ad2266` changes only the test file.

A/B: the same seeding, then `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` from each candidate, then `openclaw gateway`:

| | PR head `4d6f976` | PR parent `43dc38e` |
|---|---|---|
| Doctor exit / wall time | 0 / 89 s | 0 / 80 s |
| Live DBs after | state 20→35, agent 25→37, `quick_check ok`, no table lost rows | same |
| Config after | heartbeat migrated to Automations; `config validate` valid | same |
| Full rollback group (heartbeat work pending) | kept: 2 full `pre-startup-migration` backups saved, then reused by `heartbeat-migration-backups` | same |
| Recovery images | agent backup schema 25 / 58 rows, state backup schema 20 / 46 rows, original-state capture with the same DBs + config, all `quick_check ok` | same |
| Gateway on migrated state | `/healthz` live, `/readyz` ready (no failing checks) in 21 s | ready in 19 s |

So on a real multi-version upgrade where heartbeat migration work is still pending, the PR keeps exactly the same backups and recovery images as main. The skip only applies once the version phase has committed every pending store and nothing else needs the full group. That was the case in the metadata-only reproduction above.

**Not covered by this lane:** `openclaw update` from 2026.10.8 to the candidate is refused before Doctor runs (`agents.defaults: unrecognized key` for the retired `heartbeat` block). The PR parent `43dc38e` fails the same way, so this is current main behavior and not caused by this change. The proof above therefore follows the refusal's own instruction: install the candidate, then run `doctor --fix`.

This does not make Doctor fast enough for a short systemd pre-start window on its own. The full original-state copy (about 150–180 s here), archive preparation (about 40 s), and whole-database contribution scans (about 80 s) remain; those are tracked separately.

body:
The first release run on the Contabo runner failed two gates. Both are real bugs that the slower machine exposed.

- **\`bn on tick\` killed by SIGPIPE.** bn restores SIGPIPE's default so it exits quietly in a closed pipe. When a rule's command exited before bn wrote the event to its stdin, the write killed bn (\`bn exited None\` in the reactor e2e tests). SIGPIPE is now ignored for that one write.
- **Blank runs popup.** fzf 0.73 draws its UI on stderr when stderr is not a terminal, and \`runs.py\` captured stderr, so the popup stayed empty. Only stdout (the selection) is captured now.

Verified: \`scripts/test-command-runs.py\` passes on Contabo with the fix and failed without it; reactor e2e and clippy pass locally.

body:
## Intent

Priority (2026-10-27): the ClickUp autopilot must drive the captain's open tickets down overnight with no firstmate turn needed.
Today: (1) fm-spawn exit 75 (capacity) leaves the item queued, and nothing admits it automatically when a slot frees.
Queued authorized work sits idle until firstmate re-dispatches by hand, and the captain woke to idle slots.
(2) work-intake imports tickets but leaves them in scope_review_required with no automatic path forward.
Design and ship the smallest change so that whenever a worker slot frees (teardown, park, or exit), the next authorized queued backlog item (dependencies and date gates clear, project/fleet capacity respected) is spawned automatically using its existing brief and recorded mode/ticket.
Keep the existing safety gates: no merges, no captain-held items, no Andrew-owned tickets.
Evidence: data/dispatch-order.txt (in the main home, ~/firstmate/data/dispatch-order.txt) is the hand-kept order this replaces; its rows are "<task-id> <project> <mode> <ticket> <commit-type>".

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-worker-admit.py`. When `fm-spawn.sh` defers a fresh ship for capacity (exit 75) and the ship has a filled brief, the helper writes `state/<id>.deferred-spawn.json`. That record captures every resolved launch setting (project, mode, yolo, ticket/commit type or branch prefix, harness, model, backend, and so on) and ties them to the brief's SHA256.
- `fm-worker-park.sh tick` now calls the helper's `tick` after it resumes parked workers. The tick takes a home-local lock and replays records in `tasks-axi ready` order. A record is replayed only while its backlog item is still a queued, unheld, unblocked ship with no task metadata; priority and queue age set the order. Each replay goes through `fm-spawn.sh`, which checks the record digest again and runs a new `fm-work-intake.sh admission-check <ENG-n>`. That check refuses tickets the source adapter excludes, such as ones with the wrong owner. Spawn's existing capacity, lock, and backlog gates still apply.
- Replay outcomes:
  - A successful launch consumes the record.
  - A record is discarded if its brief changed, the record is incomplete, or the backlog item is gone or no longer queued.
  - Other refusals retry with backoff. After 3 refusals the record is quarantined and a `blocked` line is added to the task status; an explicit dispatch clears it.
  - Project and harness deferrals skip only that project's or harness's remaining records, and fleet-wide deferrals end the tick. Under replay, the away spend cap and seat-quota gates in `fm-spawn.sh` exit 75 instead of 1.
  - Each first deferral, admission, refusal, quarantine, and discarded record is written to `state/worker-admission.jsonl`.

  Docs and the `deferred:` messages now describe this, and tests are added in `tests/fm-worker-admit.test.sh` and the project/fleet capacity suites.

⚠️ Medium: The only change since the last review is a docstring fix (R5-1), and it is accurate: refusals carry forward only through replay re-records, and an explicit dispatch resets them. The rest of the branch adds unattended worker launches, and the earlier rounds' fixes for that are still intact. The risk is real but bounded: the spawn path re-runs every safety gate under its own locks, the quarantine/backoff bound limits repeated refusals, and the remaining F4 scope gaps were accepted by the user.

I then ran the 10-case tests/fm-worker-admit.test.sh suite (all pass), plus a filtered run of the five new tests in tests/fm-project-capacity.test.sh (all pass). Those five drive the real fm-spawn.sh, the real fm-worker-park.sh tick and a real tasks-axi backlog in throwaway homes, with only tmux and treehouse faked. The worker-admit suite uses a stubbed spawn, so its scenarios are not counted as live results. The logs are in the evidence directory. I did not run a live lab where a primary starts a real Claude worker. The machine was heavily loaded: the five tests took about 17 minutes. Fleet-capacity, work-intake and worker-park stay with CI. No UI surface changed, so there are no screenshots.

author: yoshiofthewire
body:
## What changed

KyDrive now refuses undersized keys at every boundary where its own code accepts one, and ships a supported strong-key profile. This lets the OpenSSF `crypto_keylength` criterion be answered for KyDrive's own code.

- **Session and webhook HMAC secrets:** startup refuses `KY_SESSION_SECRET` and a nonempty `KY_KYSIGNON_HMAC_SECRET` shorter than 16 bytes (`crypto.MinHMACKeyBytes`). The error names the variable. The check runs before any key file is read or created. The webhook also refuses to verify with a short secret before it changes any account.
- **OIDC JWKS:** if any RSA key in the provider's JWKS is under 2048 bits, the whole set is refused (`internal/sso/jwks_strength.go`). The fetch is also capped at 1 MiB and redirects are refused. A mutation check showed this guard is needed: without it, go-oidc/go-jose accept RS256 ID tokens signed with RSA-1024 and RSA-2047 keys, even with `GODEBUG=fips140=on`. JWK members are parsed the way the verifier parses them, so key-casing tricks can't get past the check.
- **Profile (`GODEBUG=fips140=on`):** `docker-compose.strong-crypto.yml` sets only `GODEBUG=fips140=on` on `app`. With it, Go's TLS clients (OIDC, Euro-Office API, KyRecovery) reject any chain containing a weak certificate, including an explicitly trusted root. OIDC issuer, authorization, token and JWKS URLs must also be HTTPS, and discovery and token redirects are refused.
- **Docs:** new `docs/STRONG-CRYPTO.md` with the key table, how to enable the profile, guidance for the HTTPS edge and the out-of-scope list. It is linked from README, SECURITY and ASSURANCE-CASE. AGENTS.md files updated (root, docs, config, crypto, sso).
- **CI:** the `test` job repeats `go test -race ./...` under `GODEBUG=fips140=on`, then runs `python3 docs/check-strong-crypto-compose.py`. That script renders 6 Compose chains (base, each overlay alone, all overlays) and fails if the overlay changes anything besides `GODEBUG`.

No stored key, secret, data or capsule format changes, and nothing is rotated. **Behavior change:** a deployment whose session or webhook secret is shorter than 16 bytes will no longer start. Replace only that value. Changing the session secret invalidates outstanding CSRF tokens and PoW challenges; sessions survive.

## Key inventory

| Boundary | Default | Smaller refused? | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deployment key | 32 random bytes | Yes, exactly 32 (existing) | `internal/config/config.go` (`keyfile`) |
| Session secret (CSRF/PoW HMAC) | 32 random bytes; explicit in production | Yes, under 16 (new) | `internal/config/config.go` |
| Directory webhook HMAC | unset | Yes, under 16, at startup and in the webhook (new) | `internal/config/config.go`, `internal/sso/kysignon.go` |
| Euro-Office JWT HS256 | operator | Yes, under 32 (existing) | `internal/editor/client.go` |
| OIDC ID-token RSA keys | provider JWKS | Yes, under 2048 bits (new) | `internal/sso/jwks_strength.go` |
| Outbound TLS (OIDC, editor, KyRecovery) | Go defaults | With the profile: chains limited to RSA-2048+/P-256+/Ed25519 | `GODEBUG=fips140=on` |
| TOTP | 20 bytes | Yes, under 16 (existing, ky-primitives) | `internal/auth` |
| Recovery capsules | fixed suite | Not selectable | `ky-primitives/recoveryclient` |

## Tested (locally, on 22 GB host)

All heavy runs used `flock /tmp/ky-heavy-test.lock systemd-run --user --scope -q -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -- …`, with restic 0.19.1 on PATH.

- `go test -race -p 2 -count=1 ./...`: pass, 16 packages.
- `GODEBUG=fips140=on go test -race -p 2 -count=1 ./...`: pass, 16 packages.
- `GODEBUG=fips140=on go test -count=1 -v ./internal/backup/`: pass, no skips, so real Restic runs under the profile.
- `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l`, `go mod verify`, `go mod tidy` with no diff: clean.
- `python3 docs/check-strong-crypto-compose.py`: pass. A mutation (adding `read_only: false` to the overlay) makes it fail.
- `python -m unittest discover -s deploy -p '*_test.py'`: 3 tests OK.
- `scripts/smoke-test.sh` against a freshly built binary: all checks passed.
- Mutation: disabling the JWKS bit check makes `TestOIDCRSAKeyFloorMatchesVerifier` fail for RSA-1024/2047 in both modes.

Not run locally: web `npm test`, Playwright browser tests, `docker build` and the repeatable-binary step. There are no web or Dockerfile changes; CI runs them.

A test fixture changed: `internal/api/hardening_test.go` used an 11-byte webhook secret, which the new floor refuses. It now uses a 20-byte one.

## Out of scope

These are stock upstream components with their own key and TLS policy. The guide names them and makes no claim about them: Euro-Office Document Server, Restic (it inherits `GODEBUG`, but its behavior is Restic's), reverse proxies, browsers, WebDAV and desktop clients, PostgreSQL (unsupported), and other suite services. `KY_SCIM_TOKEN` and `KY_KYSIGNON_SECRET` are bearer credentials, not keys, and are documented as such without a floor.

author: callmegautam
body:
HTTP transport: run one long-lived server behind a bearer token instead of a process per MCP client.

## Changes

- **Config** (`src/config.ts`): `TRANSPORT` (`stdio` by default, or `http`), `HTTP_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`), `HTTP_PORT` (default `3000`) and `HTTP_TOKEN`. Startup fails in HTTP mode without a token or with one shorter than 32 characters, like every other bad safety setting.
- **HTTP server** (`src/http.ts`): `Bun.serve` with the SDK's web standard Streamable HTTP transport, so there is no extra dependency.
  - Every `/mcp` request needs `Authorization: Bearer <HTTP_TOKEN>`. The token is compared in constant time, and a wrong or missing token gets 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header.
  - Each session gets its own MCP server built by `createMcpServer`, all sharing the one Discord client. Sessions end on DELETE, unknown session IDs get 404, requests that don't start a session get 400 without leaving a server behind, and sessions idle for an hour are closed.
  - `/health` answers without a token for container health checks.
  - Bun's connection idle timeout is raised so SSE streams survive between keep-alive frames.
- **Entry point** (`src/index.ts`): the tool policy is applied once at startup in both modes, so bad settings still fail before anything listens. Per-session servers skip the policy logging. HTTP mode doesn't exit when stdin closes, which happens right away in a detached container, and SIGTERM closes every session, the HTTP server and the Discord client.
- **Docker**: the image sets `HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0` (only read in HTTP mode, since `127.0.0.1` inside a container can't be reached from the host) and exposes port 3000. The README publishes it on `127.0.0.1` only.
- README section on running as an HTTP server with the `docker run` and `claude mcp add --transport http` commands, `.env.example` entries, version 1.3.0.

author: omegasoftdll
body:
#201 (merged) shipped docs claiming `lume evolve` enforces a "cryptographic maintainer signature" / "nothing merges without a cryptographic signature". That is **false** and now on `main`:

- `ev_maint_key(who) = "lume-maint-key-v1:" + who` — the "key" is the **public maintainer name**; every input to the SHA-256 digest is public, so **anyone can compute a valid `--sig`** (forgeable).
- `ev_verify_approval` also accepts `approved:<name>` with **no digest at all**.

So the digest authenticates nothing. This PR corrects the wording in `docs/04-roadmap.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/PROJECT_STATE.md`, `README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` to state the truth: `lume evolve` records an authorized-maintainer approval and runs real gates (`proofs_ok`, `benchmark_ok`, and the genuine `stage2 == stage3` fixpoint — those from #201 are kept), but its maintainer digest is **not yet a real signature**, and **GitHub branch protection is the enforced merge gate**. Real asymmetric (Ed25519) maintainer signing is tracked in the reopened **#194**.

Docs only — no code. The gate fixes from #201 stand.

author: dgegen
body:
## Problem
`AstraFocuser.move_focuser_to_position` sends `Move` and then waits while `IsMoving` is true. Some focuser drivers still report `IsMoving = False` for a moment after `Move`, before the motor has started. The loop then ends at once, and after the 3 s settle time the next exposure is taken at the old position.

This happened on SPECULOOS Callisto on 2026-10-23, in the three autofocus runs of that night:
- After the reference frame, the focuser had to move 1000 steps to the start of the sweep. The gap between the reference frame and the first sweep frame was the same as between all later frames, which only move about 105 steps (5.1 s in runs 2 and 3, 6.2 s in run 1). So nothing waited for the long move.
- In run 2, a star near focus is small in the first sweep frame, which was meant to be about 850 steps from focus.

astrafocus 0.2.0 now drops such an isolated point, but the frame is still wasted, and an autofocuser can't tell a frame at the wrong position from a real measurement.

## Fix
- The move counts as started once the focuser reports `IsMoving` or has left its old position. A warning is logged if it hasn't started within `start_timeout` (default 5 s), and the method then goes on as before.
- Then it waits while `IsMoving` is true, as before.
- A warning is logged if the focuser doesn't end at the requested position. It doesn't wait for an exact match, so drivers that stop a few steps off can't hang it.

A move to the current position doesn't wait for a start.

## astrafocus 0.2.1
This PR also raises the requirement to `astrafocus>=0.2.1` (`pyproject.toml`, and only the astrafocus entry in `uv.lock`). Astra saves frames as uint16 and passes them to astrafocus as they are. In 0.2.0 and before, the `absolute_gradient`, `auto_correlation`, `brenner` and `squared_gradient` focus measures gave wrong values on uint16 images, because differences of unsigned integers wrap around; `laplacian` and `variance_laplacian` crashed on float32 and int32 images. 0.2.1 converts images to float64 before measuring focus ([release notes](https://github.com/dgegen/astrafocus/releases/tag/v0.2.1)). `hfr`, `gauss`, `fft`, `tenengrad` and `normalized_variance` were already right on uint16.

## Tests
`tests/test_focuser_move.py`, with a fake focuser that reports `IsMoving` only after a few polls: the move is waited for (on `main` the method returns with the focuser still at its old position), a focuser that never moves gives both warnings, and a move to the current position doesn't wait.

`pytest -m "not slow"`: 658 passed. With astrafocus 0.2.1 (`uv sync --locked --dev`): 658 passed, and the two autofocus schedule tests (`test_autofocus_action`, `test_autofocus_action_with_weather_alert`) passed. `pytest -m slow`: 21 passed, 1 failed. The failure, `test_nonsidereal_object_action_with_weather_alert` ("Images were not taken during object action"), happens on `main` too (2 of 2 runs this afternoon). It passed earlier today, so it looks time-dependent; the test doesn't move the focuser.

## Related: `FOCUSPOS` in the headers
The `FOCUSPOS` values of these frames differ from the commanded positions by 25–80 steps, and some aren't whole numbers (`7284.00004821872`). That isn't the focuser: `FOCUSPOS` is `fixed = false`, so it's interpolated linearly in time between focuser positions polled every 5 s. See #159.

author: arch-fan
body:
## Summary

Cachix [garbage-collects](https://docs.cachix.org/garbage-collection) the least recently downloaded paths once a cache reaches its storage limit, so a current but rarely downloaded output (openvas, for example) can be evicted before stale intermediates.

A new daily workflow (`.github/workflows/pin-cache.yml`, also runnable by hand) evaluates `main` and [pins](https://docs.cachix.org/pins) every package output stored in the cache with `--keep-revisions 1`. When a package updates, its previous output loses the pin, so older versions and build intermediates are collected first.

- Outputs identical to Nixpkgs are served by cache.nixos.org, are never pushed to this cache, and are skipped (9 packages today, including dnsx, netexec, smbmap and ssh-audit).
- Pinning runs on a schedule because merges made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger workflows on `main`. A delay of up to a day is harmless: freshly pushed paths are the last in line for collection.

## Verification

```console
nix run --inputs-from . nixpkgs#actionlint -- .github/workflows/pin-cache.yml   # ok
```

Dry run of the pin loop against `arsenal.cachix.org`, with `cachix pin` replaced by `echo`: it would pin 20 outputs and skip 9 served by cache.nixos.org. Nothing was pinned.

## After merging

- Run `gh workflow run pin-cache.yml` once. This confirms that `CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN` is allowed to create pins; if `cachix pin` fails, the token needs write access to the cache.
- The Cachix docs do not say whether a pin also protects the paths it depends on. It is very likely, since pins exist to keep releases downloadable, but it is unconfirmed. The dashboard's Garbage Collection preview shows whether a pinned package's dependencies (metasploit's gem environment, for example) are in line for deletion.

| GHSA-89j4-256r-3pcq, snapshot import symlink traversal | High | `0.5.7`–`0.5.9` | fixed from `0.5.10` |
| GHSA-xgg5-hjwq-2gw8, domain deny bypass via direct-IP TLS | Medium | none | note under the table |

Rows keep the table's order (newest affected range first). `docs/filesystem.md` and the README `0.17.1` row now name GHSA-rh2c. The 0.17.1 CHANGELOG entry described the change only as "path validation" while the upstream advisory was private; released CHANGELOG sections are left as they are.

## Why

Upstream advisories do not list `microsandbox-rb`, so Dependabot and `bundler-audit` do not flag the gem. `SECURITY.md` is the mapping. GHSA-rh2c matters most: upstream lists `rust:microsandbox <= 0.6.16` with no patched version, so a reader on gem `0.17.0` (runtime `v0.6.18`) would conclude they are unaffected. They are affected.

## How each range was derived

Gem → runtime from the README Versioning table, cross-checked against the `tag` pinned in `ext/microsandbox/Cargo.toml` at each gem tag (`v0.5.7`/`v0.5.9` → `v0.5.7`, `v0.5.10`/`v0.7.0` → `v0.5.8`, `v0.9.1` → `v0.6.2`, `v0.9.2` → `v0.6.3`, `v0.17.0`/`v0.17.1` → `v0.6.18`).

- **GHSA-rh2c:** `resolve_relative` in `sdk/rust/lib/volume/fs.rs` hashes the same (`580eff1d…`) at every tag from `v0.5.8` to `v0.7.5`, and is gone at `v0.7.6` (fix `b3843eb1` is an ancestor of `v0.7.6`, not of `v0.7.5`). `VolumeFs` is absent from the gem at `v0.6.0` and present at `v0.7.0`. The `0.17.1` guard (commit `1d955bf`) calls `contained()` for all 11 `VolumeFs` methods, both paths of `copy`/`rename`, in `ext/microsandbox/src/volume.rs` and `lib/microsandbox/volume.rb`. No volume `write_stream` is bound.
- **GHSA-v693:** fix `b15c8fd6` (#1083) is in upstream `v0.6.3`, not `v0.6.2`. Gem `0.9.1` pins `v0.6.2`, `0.9.2` pins `v0.6.3`.
- **GHSA-89j4:** fix `69803ab3` (#998) is in `v0.5.8`, not `v0.5.7`. Gem `0.5.7`–`0.5.9` pin `v0.5.7` and bind `Snapshot.import`. `0.5.10` pins `v0.5.8`.
- **GHSA-xgg5:** fix `8bed4552` (#782) is already in `v0.5.0`. The first gem release embeds `v0.5.7`.

Sources: `gh api repos/superradcompany/microsandbox/security-advisories/<id>` for each advisory (severity, ranges, fix references).

author: therebelrobot
body:
## Summary

Validated against the October 2026 Node.js security wave.

**Not pre-auth reachable by Node2Shell here** — the app never decompresses
attacker-controlled Brotli (no Express / body-parser anywhere; the runtime is
Hono, a raw `node:http` server, or an nginx-served static bundle). But the Node
version was left floating, so the image is only patched if it happens to be
rebuilt after the fix shipped.

## Changes

- Pin the Dockerfile base image to the exact patched patch on the line already in use.
- Pin the CI `node-version` to the same patched patch.
- Set `engines.node` to `>=22.23.4`.

## Why

CVE-2026-111497 (**Node2Shell**): out-of-bounds write in Node's bundled Brotli
decoder, leading to RCE / memory disclosure. Fixed in **Node 22.23.4 / 24.22.1 /
26.12.1** (released 2026-10-21). A floating major tag (`node:24-alpine`) or a
floating `node-version: 24` only carries the fix if rebuilt after that date;
pinning the exact patch makes the fix explicit and stops it drifting.

No application code changes.

author: allenheltondev
body:
Groundwork for recorded, multi-voice narration (ElevenLabs or Gemini TTS). Nothing here touches chapter content or the engine; the game still reads aloud through `speak()` with the device voice.

## What's in it

**The plan** (`docs/voice-narration-plan.md`)
- Every spoken line gets an address and a kind: recorded, templated (`{party}`/`{facets}`), live (player names, which stay on the device voice) or silent.
- A provider-neutral voice bank with **one narrator** for the whole game.
- Per-chapter script sidecars that split narration into voices and carry delivery and beats. They must join back to the screen text, so Gemfall's pinned hashes don't move.
- Content-addressed clips: a text edit regenerates exactly that line.
- Clips live in the **existing site bucket** under `voice/` (outside `assets/`, which deploy syncs with `--delete`).
- A **$75 cap** on the first full render, and phased rollout.

**`npm run voice:cost`** (`tools/voice/`)
- Counts every voiceable line in `content/` (1.05M characters, about 21 hours) and prices it per model from `tools/voice/pricing.json`.
- Handles dated price changes, batch rates and retake padding, and checks against the budget. It calls no API.
- Whole game: about $108 on ElevenLabs v4, $54 on v4 Turbo, $23 on Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS.

**`npm run voice:bakeoff`** (`tools/voice/bakeoff/`, `docs/voice-bakeoff.md`)
- **Samples:** 16 real lines in five tiers, from one narrator to a five-voice flock. They're resolved from `content/` addresses at run time, and a test checks each script still matches the authored words.
- **`--serve`:** a local page where you paste keys (each is checked by listing the provider's models) and pick a model, mode and delivery. You can render a cell or a whole column, recast speakers (including from the ElevenLabs account's voices) and rate blind side by side. Playback highlights the line being spoken.
- **Expression, written per model family as the provider docs describe:**
  - *Delivery* is how a whole line sounds (whisper, shout, grave, chorus…).
  - *Beats* are point-in-time events in the script: `<sigh>`, `<laugh>`, `<chuckle>`, `<gasp>`, `<breath>`, `<pause>`, `<long pause>`.
  - ElevenLabs v3/v4 get free-form `[bracket]` tags, and v2/Flash get SSML breaks for pauses.
  - **Gemini 3.8 speaks everything in its text except `<angle>` vocal tags**, so its delivery and character go in `speechMetadata.style`, one part per turn.
  - Gemini 3.1 uses bracket tags under the documented audio profile / director's notes / transcript prompt.
- **Caching:** clips are cached by a hash of the request, so re-runs are free.
- **Safety:** there's a spending cap, and an unpriced paid model is never treated as free (it needs an approved rate on the page, and the command line refuses it). The server binds to 127.0.0.1, needs a per-session token on every API call, and never writes keys to disk.

**Read-aloud on by default on the TV** (`packages/client/src/speech/read-aloud.ts`, `App.tsx`)
- The shared screen reads aloud unless it was switched off on that device. The choice is remembered in `kad.readaloud` and beats the default.
- Phones stay off by default.
- E2E specs that clicked the TV's switch on now expect it on, and `docs/read-aloud.md` is updated.

## Not verified
This environment couldn't reach either provider, and its network policy blocks their docs sites, so the research came through search summaries. The bake-off has only run against mocked APIs and the fake tone engine. The model IDs, request shapes, premade ElevenLabs voice IDs, a few beat spellings (listed in the doc) and every rate in `pricing.json` (marked `confirmed: false`) will be confirmed by the first real run with keys. A wrong ID or field fails only its own cells, with the provider's error.

## Testing
- `npm run typecheck`: clean
- `npx vitest run tools/voice packages/client/src/speech`: 63 passed
- E2E for the read-aloud change (run locally against the installed Chromium): `read-aloud`, `goal`, `preface`, `layout-fit` and `tv-read-only`, 22 tests, all passed
- Full `npm test`: 8 content-tool tests timed out while e2e was running at the same time; all 3 files pass when re-run on their own
- Live bake-off page driven in Playwright against mocked providers: key check, model picker, Render all, a single cell, two-voice refusal, an unpriced model's approved rate, playback highlighting, recasting, reload, phone width

author: squeebmike
body:
## Why
Store, 2026-10-27: Sonic the Hedgehog #92 Variant RI (15) (Fourdraine) listed 1 as a presale and sold 1. It then stayed Active on eBay at "0 available, 1 sold": eBay's out-of-stock option keeps a sold-out Good 'Til Cancelled listing up. "I want them ended if they cant buy it ... if I do in the future I can list it again."

## What
- **Hourly end:** every hour, right after the eBay order sync brings in sales, every presale listing with nothing left to sell is ended. This is the new internal route `/foc/admin/end-sold-out-ebay-presales` (owner/admin, or the scheduled run).
- **Multi-cover listings** wait until every cover on them is sold out. The other covers are still for sale.
- **One end call per listing:**
  - standalone offer: withdraw the offer;
  - multi-cover REST listing: withdraw the group;
  - Trading listing: `EndFixedPriceItem`.
  
  Any volume-discount promotion attached to the listing is ended too.
- **What happens to the rows:** they get `ebayWithdrawnAt` and `ebayWithdrawnReason: 'sold_out'` and keep `focPresaleOriginalQty`. The sold copies still count as presold, so receiving still holds them for the buyers.
- **Failed end calls:**
  - If the listing is already off eBay (ended by hand, or by eBay), it is recorded as ended rather than retried every hour.
  - A real eBay error is logged and retried on the next run.
- **Left alone:** presale bundles and listings already withdrawn.
- **First run:** checked against production, it would end only one listing, the Sonic #92 one.

## Tests
- New `tests/foc-end-sold-out-presales.test.mjs`:
  - which listings are picked: standalone, a group with everything sold, a group with one cover still selling, Trading, already ended, and bundles;
  - one end call per listing;
  - sold counts are kept;
  - a listing already off eBay is recorded as ended;
  - a real failure leaves the row to retry;
  - the run happens after the order sync.
- Full `npm test` passes.

# PIDASHCONV-1521 Part A: `Issue.save()` hooks + `domain::issues` + app handler migration

Part 1 of 5 for PIDASHCONV-1521 (ORM-03; stacked plan in the issue thread).
Parts B–E (v1 handlers, remaining writers, `move_to_project`, comments/relations) stack on this PR.

## What

- `pidash-db`: `Issue.save()` (`db/models/issue.py:267-351`) as `ActiveModelBehavior` hooks (`entity/issue_hooks.rs`): advisory lock, `sequence_id` max+1, `sort_order` max+10000, pod/state defaults, `completed_at`, `description_stripped`, plus the `issue_sequences` row in `after_save(insert)` (FK order; same transaction).
- `pidash-services`: new `domain::issues` — `create`, `update`, `partial_update`, `soft_delete`, `archive`, `unarchive`, `bulk_archive_*`, `bulk_soft_delete_issues` — with the post-commit effects as one ordered chain step (`ChainOutcome` recorder preserves the handlers' `?` short-circuit, including the transition-driver 500 arm). New `TaskEnqueueHook` transport (services cannot depend on jobs); single-copy kwarg builders, spaced-JSON formatter, task names.
- `pidash-api`: migrated app `create/partial/put/destroy/bulk-delete/archive/unarchive/bulk-archive` onto the service; deleted ~1400 lines of private insert/update SQL and per-file helper twins. `AppTaskEnqueueHook` binding in `domain_hooks.rs`.
- Write guard allowlist: -7 entries (the migrated sites), +0 new (the hook sequence insert goes through the entity).

## Behavior notes

- Translate, don't redesign: same URL paths/JSON/schema/SQL semantics. Consolidations of identical copies only (two `NOT triage` spellings agree on every input incl. NULL; two spaced formatters byte-identical; clear-statement consts match the `format!` text).
- No "Rust bug:" filings: no app-vs-v1 divergence was reachable in this part (v1 migrates in Part B, where D6 comparisons happen).
- Ported bugs: none new; the `touch_save_project`-less archive paths and bulk autocommit shapes are preserved exactly as the port had them.

## Validation (red base — differential)

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p pidash-db -p pidash-services -p pidash-api --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Unit: `pidash-db entity::issue_hooks` 11/11 live; `pidash-services domain::issues` 13/13 (incl. a live create→partial-update roundtrip pinning hooks+m2m+fire+completion+trio through `domain::run`); `pidash-api app_issues::` 207/207.
- Contract `app_issues` on fresh DBs, my server vs HEAD-baseline server: **identical** — 115 pass, 33 fail + 1 error on both, zero new failures. Passing paths exercise the new code (create, delete, archive/unarchive roundtrips).
- The 33 failures are pre-existing at the base commit (CI rust-matrix is red there too): root-caused the PATCH/retrieve 500s to `render_detail_body`, which fails on raw seed data through untouched code (diagnosed with temporary logging, fully reverted). No open fix issue covers the contract-rust matrix redness; flagging for the coordinator.
- `orchestration` on fresh DBs, my server vs HEAD-baseline server: **identical** — 32 pass, 22 fail + 5 errors on both, zero new failures (same red base; suite needs the Django upstream for its probe, as in CI).
- Quarantine: `git diff --name-only origin/rust-dev...HEAD` lists only `rust-api/` files.
- Write guard: `--check` shows only the 11 pre-existing NEW sites (oauth/turn) that are also new at the base commit; zero stale.

## Tier 3 differences

None.

author: diegorv
body:
## Summary

Moves the app to SvelteKit 3. Two advisories, GHSA-pfhg-q3qv-9q6r and GHSA-27mw-82g8-phjj, are fixed only in kit 3. Risk to us is low: neither is exploitable in the static Tauri SPA. The upgrade clears them anyway.

```diff
 svelte.config.js                  -> folded into sveltekit() in vite.config.js
 @sveltejs/kit         2.x         -> 3.1.0
 @sveltejs/adapter-static          -> 4.0.0
 CI Node                           -> 22.17
 import x from '$lib/foo'          -> import x from '#lib/foo.js'   (package.json "imports")
 tsconfig paths                    +  "#lib/*" mapping (keeps .svelte components typed)
 $lib alias                        -  removed
```

Commit groups:
- `build:` move config into `vite.config.js`; kit 3.1.0 + adapter-static 4.0.0 + Node 22.17 in CI
- `chore(build):` add the `#lib` subpath import next to `$lib`
- `refactor(ui|core|features|plugins|...)`, `refactor(tests)`: `$lib` -> `#lib` across `src/` and `src/tests/`
- `fix(types)`: found mid-migration. Components imported through `#lib` lost their typing. The fix maps `#lib/*` in tsconfig `paths` and adds guard tests.
- `refactor!`: drop the `$lib` alias
- `docs`: amend the docs and ADRs; add and close the `.scratch` plan

**Breaking:** Node >= 22.17 is required. `$lib` is gone, so use `#lib/...` with `.js` endings.

## Evidence

Gate on the branch after rebasing onto `origin/main`:

- `pnpm check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `pnpm vitest run`: 298 files, 6628 passed, 1 todo
- `pnpm build`: success (adapter-static wrote `build/`)

Test plan:
- [x] `pnpm check`
- [x] `pnpm vitest run`
- [x] `pnpm build`
- [ ] Manual `pnpm tauri dev` smoke test of the main and composer windows (owner)

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting is mechanical. The import rewrite touches a lot of files, though, so any branch still open on `$lib` will conflict.

**Blast Radius:** app-wide

Every module's imports changed. Runtime regressions would show up at app boot or window load. That is why the manual Tauri smoke test still matters.

Known follow-ups / not done:
- runed 0.35.1 peer warning stays. Ticket 02 was deferred because no bits-ui release accepts runed >= 0.36.
- graphify-out snapshots still show `$lib`.
- `components.json` `$schema` and ADR 0002 still reference `shadcn-svelte@next`.

author: randomparity
body:
Closes #3348

## What this changes

A remote module PREPARE that failed after the System was stopped left its authority journal operation at `mutation-started`. The next PREPARE was then refused with `provider-conflict` and the System teardown with `journal-conflict`, so the System could neither retry nor tear down.

- **Host** (`DurableRemoteModuleVolumePreparationHost`): any failure after admission now goes through an abandon step. The host starts a System that was running before PREPARE stopped it, but only once the attachment inspection shows the appliance absent and the System shut off and exclusive. A restored System leaves no completion behind, so the failure does not latch. The error keeps its `completion` (`refused-before-mutation` is preserved) and gains an `abandoned` detail. A failure with no recorded power is reported `refused-before-mutation`. If the restore fails, the failure stays latched as before.
- **Authority service**: on an `abandoned` failure it closes the PREPARE operation through the existing `provider-returned`, `observed` and `terminal` anchors with a `source` outcome. A replay of the same operation reports `failed-after-mutation` without running the host. A settle that fails is logged and does not replace the provider's failure.
- ADR-0585 and ADR-0714 get dated amendments. No migration, journal phase or wire change.

## Verification

- Tests: new cases in `tests/providers/external_boot_authority/test_service.py`, `tests/providers/remote_libvirt/test_external_boot_authority.py` and `tests/providers/remote_libvirt/test_remote_module_authority_host.py`. One test pins the wedge: an unsettled failure makes the next `begin` raise `provider_conflict`.
- Controlled faults, each reverted afterwards: removing the settle, removing the restore, and removing the latch on a failed restore each turned tests red.
- `just ci` ran as the pre-push gate on `0ee28046e` and passed.
- Not run: a live proof on the remote lab (needs a grant). That the retry resumes the same module attempt relies on the attempt nonce being stable across generations, which was traced in source only.

## Known limits

- A cancellation while the stop itself is in flight behaves as before (recorded in the ADR-0585 amendment).
- If clearing the prior-power record fails after a successful restore, a stale record remains until the next attempt.

author: csarigumba
body:
Closes #37.

## Summary

Adds `19-access-log-stats-cli/`, a zero-dependency Node 24+ CLI `log-stats` that summarizes a Common Log Format access log: total requests, counts per status class (2xx–5xx), the top N paths, and how many lines were skipped. `--top N` and `--since <ISO date>` are strictly validated (bad values exit 1). The file is streamed line by line, so a log larger than the heap works. Also adds the `verify-access-log-stats-cli` skill with a fixture and expected outputs.

## What changed

```text
19-access-log-stats-cli/
├── bin/log-stats.js        # parseArgs, validate --top/--since, open file, print
├── src/stats.js            # toTime (strict ISO), parseLine (CLF/Combined), summarize
├── test/log-stats.test.js  # unit + spawn-the-bin tests, incl. >heap streaming
├── README.md
└── package.json            # bin log-stats, engines node >=24, test: node --test
.claude/skills/verify-access-log-stats-cli/
├── SKILL.md
├── fixtures/access.log     # 13 lines: 11 valid, 2 unparseable
└── features/               # summary, top-flag, since-flag, errors, streaming

log-stats <file> [--top N] [--since <date>]
  validate args             # error -> stderr, exit 1, empty stdout
  open(file)                # ENOENT -> "cannot read <file>: ENOENT", exit 1
  summarize(readline(fh.createReadStream()))
    parseLine               # no match or bad date -> skipped++
    time < since            # -> ignored
    total++, class++, path (query stripped)++
  print total, 2xx..5xx, top paths, skipped
```

## Done when

| # | check | result | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `log-stats access.log` prints total, 2xx–5xx, top 5 paths | pass | `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/1-summary.txt` |
| 2 | `--top N` changes path count; non-positive-integer N exits 1 | pass | `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/2-top.txt` |
| 3 | `--since` counts at-or-after (offsets honored); invalid or zone-less date exits 1 | pass | `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/3-since.txt` |
| 4 | Unparseable lines skipped, counted, printed last; missing file exits 1 | pass | `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/4-skipped-and-errors.txt` |
| 5 | 156 MB log under a 32 MB heap gives correct totals; readFileSync control OOMs | pass | `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/5-streaming.txt` |
| 6 | `npm test` (node --test, no network) passes; README; engines | pass | `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/6-tests-readme.txt`, `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/evidence/00-tests.txt` |

## How to test

```bash
cd 19-access-log-stats-cli
npm test
node bin/log-stats.js ../.claude/skills/verify-access-log-stats-cli/fixtures/access.log
node bin/log-stats.js ../.claude/skills/verify-access-log-stats-cli/fixtures/access.log --top 2 --since 2026-10-11T09:00:05Z
node bin/log-stats.js nope.log; echo "exit=$?"     # cannot read nope.log: ENOENT, exit=1
node bin/log-stats.js ../.claude/skills/verify-access-log-stats-cli/fixtures/access.log --top 0; echo "exit=$?"   # exit=1
```

## Review

Verdict: `ship` (round 2). Round 1 (`fix`): `--since` accepted a time without a zone, which JS reads as local time, so totals depended on the machine's time zone. Resolved in the shared ISO check (`src/stats.js:1`): a zone is now required whenever a time is given; unit and CLI tests added; README and verify map updated.

## Assumptions

- Combined Log Format lines also parse; trailing referer/user-agent fields are ignored, since many servers log that format.
- Query strings are stripped from paths (`/about?ref=home` counts as `/about`), so "paths" means paths.
- Ties in the top list keep first-appearance order, for deterministic output.
- A status outside 2xx–5xx counts in `total` only; the issue names only those four classes.
- Lines before `--since` count nowhere (not in total, not in skipped).
- `--since` takes `YYYY-MM-DD` (midnight UTC) or a date-time with `Z`/`±HH:MM`; a zone-less time is rejected so results do not depend on the machine's time zone. Non-existent dates (`2026-02-30`) are rejected.
- All errors, including usage errors, exit 1, matching the issue text.
- Blank lines and lines with a CLF shape but an invalid timestamp count as skipped.

## Not verified

- Long-term stability of the streaming test's readFileSync OOM control on future V8 versions (passes on Node 26.12.1).
- No-network for `npm test` was observed with network blocked in verify round 1; round 2 inferred it from builtin-only imports.

## Dev dependencies added

None.

## Run

Branch `ship/issue-37` on `main`. Run dir `.sidstack/runs/20261027-222602-issue-37/`. claude-opus-5-5, 2 review rounds (1 fix round). Verify scratch dirs `/tmp/logstats-verify*` not cleaned up (rm denied in this environment).

author: 0xkurt
body:
## Was und warum

Closes #1022 (nachträgliches Review von #1018, MAJOR). Closes #1028 (Zug nach Rollenspiel scheitert an plan_exam mit Sprachcode). Bezug: #946, #950, docs/architecture.md §Material („A model-named subject never blocks learning“).

Konnte der Code ein vom Modell genanntes Fach nicht eindeutig zuordnen, warf `findOrCreateSubject` einen `AppError`. Beim Lesen eines Blatts (`readyTx`) wiederholte der Job deshalb das ganze Lesen samt Modellaufrufen bis zum Parken, Themenübungen endeten mit 422, `plan_exam`/`plan_talk` brachen die Entscheidung ab, statt dem Modell eine Korrektur zu erlauben. In Produktion haben 3 aktive `other_language`-Fächer keinen Sprachcode (Prüfabfrage vom 27.10.), genau der häufigste Auslöser.

- Ein Fehlertyp `SubjectUnresolved` für alle Fälle (unbekannter Code, veralteter oder widersprechender Alias, gleichnamiger Kurs anderer Art, mehrere Fächer gleicher Art ohne exakten Namen, neue Fremdsprache ohne Code).
- Modellwege werfen nie: `subjectIdOf` speichert Blatt und Übung ohne Fach und protokolliert nur den Grund; `toolSubject` (über `planSubject` für beide Pläne) gibt eine `ToolRejection` mit Korrekturhinweis und bei Mehrdeutigkeit den Kandidaten-Refs zurück.
- Unbekannt ist nicht anders: Alias oder exakter Name trifft ein altes Fach ohne Code. Der Code wird nur nachgetragen, wenn `Intl.DisplayNames` den gespeicherten Namen als Namen dieser Sprache belegt und kein anderes aktives Fach den Code trägt (Unique-Index aus 0121).
- Die Modellgrenze aus #946 (`fromModel` in `findOrCreateSubject`) bleibt die eine Stelle für den Sprachcode und wendet jetzt `modelLanguage` an: Ein Nicht-Sprachfach ignoriert den Code (#946), ein festes Sprachfach ignoriert einen Code, den keine Sprache hat. `subjectIdOf` und `toolSubject` setzen `fromModel`; direkte Aufrufe bleiben strikt.

**Dient USP-Punkt:** 2 Ihr Material ist die Quelle – ein Blatt in einem alten Fremdsprachenfach wird wieder gelesen und geübt, statt im Lesejob hängen zu bleiben.

**Wiederverwendet / entfernt:** Wiederverwendet werden die Provider-Grenze `subjects.findOrCreate` (jetzt auch für plan_talk), `ToolRejection`, `subjectLabel`/Intl und der Unique-Index aus 0121; entfernt sind der Direktaufruf von `findOrCreateSubject` in `talkTools.ts` und die doppelte Provider-Aufrufstelle in beiden Plänen (`planSubject`).

## Nachweis

- [x] Hooks grün (typecheck, lint, guards inkl. jscpd/knip, Tests); Pre-Push-Suite beim Push.
- [x] Rot vor grün: neue Datei `subject-unresolved.int.test.ts` war mit 19/19 Fällen rot (Lesejob `failed`, 422, abgebrochene Entscheidung), danach grün. author: elecnix
body:
Closes #203

GitHub creates one check suite per installed App on every push. An App that never posts a check run leaves its suite queued forever with no runs. Readiness counted that suite as pending, so the pull request never became ready.

`pendingChecks` now skips a pending suite that has no check runs, whichever app owns it. A suite with one or more runs keeps today's behaviour, so a real pending run still blocks readiness.

Tests:

- New `TestClassifyPRsFull_RunlessQueuedSuiteDoesNotBlock`, written first and red: one passing suite plus one queued suite with 0 runs is ready; adding a queued suite with 1 pending run makes it not ready.
- Four existing tests modelled a pending suite without runs, a state the fix treats as no verdict. Their fixtures now carry a pending run.
- `TestFetchPRViaREST_RunlessSuitesKeepCIFromReadingGreen` asserted the old rule; it is now `TestFetchPRViaREST_RunlessQueuedSuitesAreNotPending`.

`cmd` and `backend/remote` have failing tests that also fail on `main` without this change.

M7-28 showcase: whoever opens the project for the first time understands in one minute what it does, from real behaviour of a demo instance with made-up data.

Apple platforms build on a Mac with Xcode through an SSH reverse tunnel to the demo. Captured: Android (with video), iPhone, macOS, console, Grafana; Windows is left out (D-W-128).
- `tools/showcase/showcase_cli.py check` (in `make docs`) fails on unlisted or missing files, other formats and any metadata (PNG text, EXIF, time and ICC chunks; MP4 metadata boxes, ISO and QuickTime `meta`, creation times).

Rulings D-M7-28-1 to 6 in `docs/decisions.d/M7-28.md`.

Collection = store type snake_cased. Record id = base64url(SHA-256("type\0entityId")), 43 chars, unique across collections; the entity id travels inside the ciphertext. Prepare each architecture once, scan and smoke its exact digest, then assemble and sign the candidate index. Keep the digest-pinned operator bundle, IMAGE_DIGEST and SHA256SUMS. Bundled Compose uses the qualified multiarch index; public release notes come from the GitHub body. Stable publication requires the same source, signature, native manifests and both stopped lab receipts. Copy the exact qualified index; read back version and latest digests. No RC channel is required.

Sources: IBKR `97161032d5239fd9e2bed72d1bac9d358c722c58`, following separate review of changes after the approved v3.0.0 core. [v3.3.0 stable promotion](https://github.com/flowcool/ghostfolio-ibkr-sync/actions/runs/40505817589) proves the no-rebuild path. Its later metadata/identity update has CI evidence, not a release receipt. The source table and BD adaptation are recorded in the active design.

Operational change. Candidate preparation is manual on main and writes candidate digests only. Stable publication is a separate approved GitHub release action. The release must carry `lab-qualification.json` for the exact signed candidate. Existing AMD64 lab proof cannot qualify changed bytes. No registry or financial action ran for this PR. Revert this commit before dispatch to restore the previous tooling; retain any later uploaded candidate/proof. Never overwrite an existing version after a partial publication.

## Problem
The public effect-utils repository lacks a root license and consistent first-party license metadata. Johannes selected Apache-2.0 in Axe Q3 (decision fdimp6).

## Goal
Make Apache-2.0 explicit at the repository root and throughout first-party npm and Rust package metadata while preserving vendored licensing.

## Decisions
- Add the verbatim text fetched from https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt as root `LICENSE`, leaving its appendix boilerplate untouched.
- Add root `NOTICE`; its copyright-holder string is recorded only there and has been confirmed by Johannes.
- Set `license: 'Apache-2.0'` in `firstPartyPackageDefaults` in `genie/internal.ts`; internal private-package defaults include it, and other first-party manifest generators reuse it. Regenerate 60 manifests (59 package manifests plus the root workspace manifest), including generator-managed examples and fixtures.
- Set the shared `[workspace.package]` license in `rust/Cargo.toml` to Apache-2.0. All 22 workspace crates inherit it, including otel-scrape, otelite, pingping and buck2-tools. An inventory of Cargo manifests found no other standalone license values and no `Cargo.toml.genie.ts` sources; the existing generated contract manifest already inherits the workspace license and is unchanged.
- Preserve both vendored exceptions: `@overeng/react-inspector` keeps its MIT license field and LICENSE; `@overeng/effect-distributed-lock` keeps its existing absent license field and MIT LICENSE.
- Leave the README unchanged: it has no license section. Existing raw dependency-test snapshots and third-party provider-CLI wrapper manifests are not first-party effect-utils packages and are unchanged.

author: vvaz
body:
## Summary

Closes #131. A Site's production Frontend can be served on a hostname in the client's own DNS (a **Custom hostname**). The first case is nomia-bnq → `bioeconomia.apambiente.pt`.

```json
"domains": {
  "admin": "nomia-cms.bnq.pt",
  "frontend": "bioeconomia.apambiente.pt",
  "frontendTarget": "nomia.bnq.pt"
}
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  V[visitor] -->|bioeconomia.apambiente.pt| APA[APA DNS: CNAME to nomia.bnq.pt]
  APA --> Z[bnq.pt zone: custom hostname + TLS]
  Z -->|Worker route bioeconomia.apambiente.pt/*| W[nomia-bnq-fe]
  N[nomia.bnq.pt: Custom Domain] --> W
  Z -.->|hostname without a route| F[fallback origin: start.bnq.pt, set once per zone]
```

```diff
 infra/frontend.run.ts (Astro + TanStack)
-  domain: domains.frontend
+  domain: domains.frontendTarget ?? domains.frontend
+  routes: [{ pattern: "<domains.frontend>/*", zoneId }]   # only with frontendTarget
 src/cloudflare/
+  custom-hostname.mjs   # gq cloudflare custom-hostname [--dry-run] | status [--json]
 src/offboard/
   steps.mjs             # cut removes the route (offboarded.cut.workerRoutes), --restore re-adds it
   archive.mjs           # DNS records at frontendTarget; custom hostname listed as `!`
   guard.mjs             # provisioning refused while offboarded; status allowed
```

- `domains.frontend` stays the public, canonical hostname everywhere it is read: Astro `site`, the CMS `.env` template, `frontend refresh` and `site check`. The schema checks that `frontendTarget` is in `cloudflare.zoneName` and that `frontend` isn't.
- `gq cloudflare custom-hostname` never sets the zone's fallback origin. That origin is shared by every custom hostname and serves any without a route, so it is set once per zone, by hand, to a host that serves no Site (on `bnq.pt`, `start.bnq.pt`). Both commands report it missing or pointing at this Site's own Frontend, and `status` fails on either. The command creates the custom hostname (`ssl.method: txt`, DV, TLS 1.2+) and prints the client's records: the ownership TXT, `_acme-challenge` as a delegated-DCV CNAME, and the traffic CNAME. Its `status` also reads the client's CNAME and CAA over DoH. It uses a 1-hour zone-scoped token (SSL and Certificates Write, or Read for `status`).
- The deploy token needs nothing new: it already has Workers Routes Write on the zone.
- Not automatable, once per zone: enabling Cloudflare for SaaS in the dashboard (no API; needs a payment method) and setting the fallback origin. The command's error says so. Documented in `docs/guides/provisioning.md#a-frontend-on-the-clients-own-domain`, with the CAA prerequisite and the move order for a live Site.

## Evidence

- **Before:** with `domains.frontend: bioeconomia.apambiente.pt`, the deploy tries a Workers Custom Domain outside `bnq.pt` and fails.
  **After:** `pnpm exec vp run check`: 812/812 tests, format and lint clean. New tests:
  - `test/cloudflare/custom-hostname.test.mjs`: creates the hostname and prints the 3 records; never sets the fallback origin, and warns when it is missing or is this Site's Frontend; dry run; SaaS-not-enabled hint; `status` ready vs. pending (route missing, CNAME missing, CAA `harica.gr` only, which names `letsencrypt.org`, `pki.goog`, `ssl.com`); schema rules.
  - offboard: cut deletes the route and records it, restore adds it back, and `gq.ops.json` round-trips; guard covers `custom-hostname` but not `status`.
- The rendered Astro template typechecks with `tsc` against Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.79, as installed in nomia-bnq.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Additive optional key; no migration. Sites without `frontendTarget` keep the same `frontend.run.ts` behaviour (`routes` isn't passed).

**Blast Radius:** small

`infra/frontend.run.ts` is managed, so every Site's copy changes on its next `gq sync`, but the behaviour only changes when `frontendTarget` is set. Not live-tested against a real custom hostname yet; that happens on nomia-bnq after a release.

author: opsydyn
body:
## Why

On a phone, "hovering" a blip meant holding a finger on it. The finger hid the blip and label being read, and the reading vanished when the finger lifted.

## What

The radar learns from `(hover: hover)` whether the reader can hover. On touch:

- A finger's press is not a hover. It reads nothing and its lifting clears nothing, so a tap pins the blip. The readout, label, edges and details card stay until a tap on empty space.
- A tap on an Easter egg (the saucer, probe or CAP moons) reads it as a hover would. It keeps speaking until a tap elsewhere, and the press plus the tap count as one saucer visit.
- The hint reads "Tap a blip to read it · double-tap to fly there · drag to look round".
- The stage readout is larger on narrow screens.

With a mouse nothing changes, except that a click on an egg now reads it too.

## Known limit

A tap on empty space only counts if it moves 2px or less, because that tolerance is set in effect-three's pointer kernel (`missTolerance`). Fingers often move more, so on a real phone unpinning by tapping empty space may need a steady tap. Taps on blips are unaffected. Fixing it is an effect-three change of its own.

## Checks

- `bun run check`, `bun typecheck`, effect-three-samples tests (255, including the new `radar-touch.test.ts`) and apps/web Vitest (408) pass.
- In Chromium's phone emulation, a tap pinned SQLite and kept it readable. On desktop the hover hint and hover behaviour are unchanged.
- Not tried on a real device.

author: dotcoocoo
body:
## Summary

Node.js 24.22.1, 26.12.1 and 22.23.4 fix CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder Node bundles. A crafted Brotli stream can crash the process, disclose memory, or run code. `engines.node` is now `>=24.22.1`. On Node 26, use 26.12.1 or later.

The framework reaches that decoder through TLS certificate compression. On every TLS 1.3 connection it opens, and on listeners that request client certificates, it offers the certificate-compression algorithms Node reports, which include Brotli, so a peer can send a Brotli-compressed certificate that Node decodes during the handshake, before the certificate is verified. `b.safeDecompress` with `algorithm: "brotli"` also passes its input to the decoder. On Node 24.22.1 or 26.12.1 neither path reaches the flaw. `engines` is not enforced at runtime, so upgrade Node itself; installing this release does not patch an older runtime.

## Test plan

- [x] `node test/smoke.js` — passes
- [x] `node test/layer-0-primitives/codebase-patterns.test.js` — clean
- [x] `gitleaks` — no leaks

author: willsawyerrrr
body:
Connects to a ThermoCare thermometer over Bluetooth and lists each reading with the profile that took it, so readings from several household members are not mixed up.

- Polls the thermometer's queue-head record continuously from before subscribing, and pairs each temperature indication with its record by timestamp.
- Holds each indication until its record arrives or polling finishes; a lone live reading reads the current profile, anything else unmatched is marked ambiguous.
- Read-only: nothing is ever written to the thermometer, so queued readings are never deleted. Thermometer timestamps are corrected to host time, non-body readings (outside 32-43 °C) are dropped, and repeats are removed.

Tested with 29 unit tests built on real captured readings (including a full 11-reading queued batch, a missed record and a lone live reading), plus a run on a physical iPhone.

body:
## Problem

The `slop-identity` Worker's hourly `:17` cron throws on production and staging every hour. Intake renewal is healthy (verified 17:17Z today). The exception comes from the Slopbot reporting-readiness refresh it calls: `refreshRegisteredReporting` counts every non-`verified` observation as a failure, and `scheduled` throws when `failed !== 0`.

Production D1 (`repository_reporting_status`, current revisions, read 27 Oct 17:17Z) has five paused listings with `failure = app-not-installed`: canonry, darling-arm64, feed, nurosos and payzcode-ai. Only their owners can change that, so the cron would fail forever, and it feeds the "Slop Worker errors" Cloudflare alert (threshold 1 or more), which has fired and resolved about 60 times since 11:27Z today.

## Change

`workers/slopbot/reporting-readiness.ts`: `app-not-installed` on a **paused** project is no longer counted as a failure. The observation is still refreshed and written with `app-not-installed`, so nothing downstream changes. These still count as failures: an **active** project without the App (activation requires Slopbot), `unavailable` reads and identity mismatches.

New `workers/slopbot/reporting-readiness.test.ts` covers both sides. The first test fails on current `development` (`failed: 1`) and passes with the change.

## PRD

Section 8 (private security reporting: automatic private reporting for registered projects) and section 9 (background jobs refresh cached state). This does not change reporting availability, program terms, or any public state.

body:
Demande : pouvoir cliquer sur les pièces jointes depuis la page « E-mail envoyé ».

- **PDF du document** : rien à changer ici, le site l'ouvre via le proxy `/api/document-preview/<type>/<id>` existant (PDF archivé actuel du document ; identique à l'envoi pour une facture finalisée).
- **Fichiers ajoutés à la main** : jusqu'ici jamais stockés (lus en base64 par le navigateur, transmis à Resend, oubliés). Désormais conservés à l'envoi, en arrière-plan, dans un bucket privé : `EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS_BUCKET`, sinon celui des annexes (`DOCUMENT_ANNEXES_BUCKET`, sinon `QUOTES_BUCKET`), clés `email-attachments/{workspaceId}/{logId}/{index}-{nom}`. Un échec d'enregistrement n'affecte pas l'envoi (nom seulement).
- **Route** `GET /documents/email-logs/:logId/attachment?index=<n>` : session + « Voir » du document dans l'espace de l'envoi. PDF et images (png, jpg, gif, webp) affichés ; tout autre format servi en `application/octet-stream` + `attachment` + `nosniff` (un HTML/SVG choisi par l'utilisateur ne doit jamais s'exécuter sur l'origine du site, servi par son proxy).
- **GraphQL** : `DocumentEmailAttachment.available` (PDF du document ou fichier conservé) ; la clé de stockage n'est pas exposée.

## Agregar acción Eliminar en Gestión de usuarios

Incluye un botón **Eliminar** al lado de **Guardar** en Gestión de usuarios (y en el directorio administrativo alternativo). El botón solo aparece cuando el servidor ya guardó la cuenta como **Desactivado**. Antes de proceder, se solicita una confirmación que indica las consecuencias.

### Seguridad en el backend
- `DELETE /api/admin/users/{id}` exige un administrador autenticado.
- Se rechazan la propia cuenta (409) y cualquier cuenta que aún esté activa (409), independientemente de la interfaz.
- Se bloquea el cambio concurrente de estado mediante el mismo advisory lock utilizado en PATCH.
- Se marca `usuarios.deleted_at` en una transacción, sin DELETE físico ni cascadas de cotizaciones, clientes o auditoría.
- Se revocan sesiones activas, se invalidan códigos OTP pendientes y se registra la operación en `auth_admin_user_audit`.
- No se puede acceder con una cuenta retirada; se oculta del listado.
- El correo queda reservado por la restricción única existente y el historial empresarial se mantiene.

### Verificación
Nueva verificación CI compila .NET/Vue y ejecuta el smoke con PostgreSQL temporal. Incluye rechazo de borrado activo/propio y cliente no autorizado, borrado confirmado de cuenta **creada expresamente en el test**, desaparición de listado y bloqueo de nuevo OTP.

**Solo integrar a main-2 si aprueban las pruebas. NO fusionar directamente a main:** incorporar después a la PR de auditoría #96 y repetir todos sus checks, con el respaldo de producción aún pendiente de restauración aislada.

author: sshivensolanki
body:
Fixes #30557

### Problem

`getDotProdFunc()` (`modules/core/src/matmul.dispatch.cpp`) only has entries for `CV_8U` to `CV_64F`, so `Mat::dot` fails with `func != 0` for every depth added in 5.x.

### Fix

- New kernels in `matmul.simd.hpp` for `CV_16F`, `CV_16BF`, `CV_32U`, `CV_64U`, `CV_64S`, `CV_8F_E4M3FN` and `CV_8F_E4M3FNUZ`, as thin wrappers around `dotProd_` (each element converted to `double`, accumulated in `double`), called through `CV_CPU_DISPATCH` like `dotProd_64f`.
- `CV_Bool` gets its own kernel: any non-zero byte is true, so it counts the positions where both bytes are non-zero.

These depths had no kernel at all, so the kernels are plain loops; SIMD versions can be added separately if needed.

### Tests

- New `Core_DotProduct_NewTypes.accuracy` computes `dot` on random 2-channel integers in [-8, 8] converted to each depth (exact in every depth, including fp8) and compares it with the `CV_64F` dot of the same values, for a continuous Mat and a non-continuous ROI. The 8 cases fail on current 5.x and pass with this patch.
- New `Core_DotProduct.bool_nonzero_bytes` uses bytes like 2 and 255 (via `reinterpret(CV_Bool)`) and checks the exact result; it fails if `CV_Bool` uses `dotProd_8u`.
- New perf test `MatType_Length_dot_new_types.dot_new_types` in `perf_dot.cpp` for the new depths.

All dot product tests in `opencv_test_core` pass locally on Apple M1 Pro, with OpenCL enabled and with `OPENCV_OPENCL_DEVICE=disabled`, and all dot perf tests run. The full `opencv_test_core` passes, except 7 tests that need `opencv_extra` test data, which I didn't have locally (FileStorage base64 and globbing).

### Pull Request Readiness Checklist

See details at https://github.com/opencv/opencv/wiki/How_to_contribute#making-a-good-pull-request

- [x] I agree to contribute to the project under Apache 2 License.
- [x] To the best of my knowledge, the proposed patch is not based on a code under GPL or another license that is incompatible with OpenCV
- [x] The PR is proposed to the proper branch
- [x] There is a reference to the original bug report and related work
- [x] There is accuracy test, performance test and test data in opencv_extra repository, if applicable
      Patch to opencv_extra has the same branch name.
- [ ] The feature is well documented and sample code can be built with the project CMake

The filled button now uses the pill pair (text colour, canvas ink), which the theme test already holds in every bundled palette. `--threads-on-accent` is gone.
- **Keys first (ADR-0153, Drake's pick 9b from the tag `prototype/prompt-send-stop`).** Each button says what it does and its key: **Send ↵** / **Queue ↵**, **Steer ⌘↵**, **Stop ⇧⌘S** (Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Shift+S on Windows and Linux). - **Cmd+Enter (Ctrl+Enter) steers** the typed prompt into the running turn where the provider can take a steer; anywhere else it does what Enter does, as before. Enter still sends, or queues while a turn runs. It is a fixed chord, listed under Settings › Keyboard, and stands down when one of dictation's shortcuts holds those keys.

The queue rows' own **Steer now** stays in words, since a row has no key of its own. The paired phone's composer is unchanged.

author: maheidem
body:
## Bug
Owner, installed 2.24.0, real 1h06 meeting, AI model gemma4-e4b on an own llama.cpp server: "Enhance finished with errors. 1 of 30 steps failed. Speakers: The model reached its output limit." Call records: `identifySpeakers` 5 calls all `length` (764, then 1,528 tokens, 0 reasoning chars); the output was valid JSON that repeated entries (unique-word ratio 0.365, one 8-gram 13 times). `actionTiming:0` spent 4,096 tokens on a hidden thought block before its retry answered.

## Root cause
The schema size limits (`maxItems`, `maxLength`) went only to the built-in MLX model (`appliesSizeLimits`, `apps/server/src/lib/meetings/workflow/unit.ts:42`, since #243). Own OpenAI-compatible servers got unbounded lists, so a small model could repeat entries until the output limit.

## Fix
1. Own servers get the same size limits as MLX (owner decision: all own servers; a server that rejects them with a 400 naming the schema falls back to `prompt_only`, the existing path). Cloud providers still get none. The speakers list is capped at the number of open labels.
2. `identifySpeakers` does not split a unit after a cut answer when limits apply (each half has the same labels and limit). A split for a too-long input stays.
3. `actionTiming` output limit: 16 + 12 tokens per task (was 4,096). `overview`: 1,564 tokens when limits apply (overview is at most 1,500 chars); 4,096 for cloud.
4. Duplicate speakers: `verifyEvidence` already keeps one per label.

## Proof (real llama.cpp server 192.168.31.222, fictional 61-103 min meetings, 5 labels)
| | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| identifySpeakers, gemma4-e2b | 8 calls, 7 `length`, step partial | 1 call, `stop`, 399 tokens |
| actionTiming:1, gemma4-e2b | `length` at 4,096 then 8,192 (28 s) | `stop`, 94 tokens |
| actionTiming:1, gemma4-e4b | `length` at 4,096 then 8,192 (30 s), partial | `stop`, 93 tokens |
| overview, gemma4-e2b | leak 4,096 tokens, 9.1 s | cut at 1,564, 3.7 s, retry `stop` |

- With gemma4-e4b the speaker loop did not reproduce on fictional text on main either; the fix covers it by the same bound.
- Real isolated app (gemma4-e4b on 192.168.31.222, fictional 100-min meeting): Enhance + Summarize `succeeded`, 0 of 39 steps failed, 0 privacy prompts.
- `meeting:eval` E2B (built-in MLX) on both gold meetings: identical scorecards main vs branch, 0 hard fails.
- Server 3,360 tests (after rebase on adc98078), tsc, biome, knip, `meeting:eval:test` 76/76.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): thought-block leaks on stages that keep 4,096 (use the llama.cpp completion route from the first call); `correctChunk` corrections list unbounded (maxItems = segment ids).

## 2. Bayerisches Familiengeld (#54) – Verhaltensänderung
**Der Widerspruch ist aufgelöst:**
- **Beschlossen:** Art. 9a BayFamGG (GVBl. 2025 S. 570). Für ab dem 1.1.2025 geborene Kinder sind Anträge „unbeachtlich“, für früher geborene gilt das alte Recht weiter.
- **Nicht beschlossen:** Der Stichtag 1.9.2026 mit Grenze 100.000 € stammte aus Drs. 19/8839, einem Änderungsantrag der Grünen. Er wurde mit 26 zu 130 Stimmen abgelehnt.

| Geburt | vorher | jetzt |
|---|---|---|
| bis 31.12.2024 | Ja | Ja |

body:
**BORRADOR. No fusionar ni desplegar sin OK de César.** Fase 1, solo el motor: sin formulario, sin pantallas públicas y sin datos de empresas reales.

Según el «Informe - Filtro de licitaciones por empresa.txt» y las decisiones de César del 27-10.

## 1. Lector de PLACSP (`licitaciones_place.py`)
Además de lo que ya guardaba, ahora lee:
- todos los CPV (antes solo el primero);
- cada lote, con su importe sin IVA, sus CPV, su provincia y sus requisitos propios;
- la duración inicial en meses (`DurationMeasure` o fechas) y si hay prórrogas;
- la clasificación exigida (`C2-4`: grupo, subgrupo y categoría);
- los tipos de solvencia económica y técnica, el importe mínimo de solvencia económica cuando viene (`ThresholdQuantity`) y los certificados.

`requisitos_json()` lo guarda en JSON compacto.

## 2. Tabla (`app.py`)
- Columna nueva `requisitos` en `licitaciones` (`ALTER` para la tabla que ya existe). Probado con el esquema actual.
- `LIC_VERSION_LECTOR`: al arrancar, los ZIP de los **últimos 4 meses** se releen **una vez** para rellenar la columna. Los más antiguos ya no tienen licitaciones abiertas y no se tocan.
- La web no cambia nada visible.

## 3. Motor (`filtro_licitaciones.py`, nuevo)
`evaluar(licitacion, perfil)` y `filtrar(licitaciones, perfil)` clasifican cada licitación abierta, **y cada lote por separado**, en:
- **PUEDE OPTAR**: cumple lo que se puede comprobar con el feed.
- **REVISA EL PLIEGO**: hay algo que depende del pliego (solvencia dentro de su tramo, clasificación sin código, experiencia, certificados, contrato grande para su plantilla).
- **SOLO EN UTE O EN UN LOTE**: sola no llega y el perfil acepta UTE (hasta 5 veces su facturación).
- **DESCARTADA**: solo se cuenta, no se enseña.

Cada resultado lleva sus motivos en una línea. El **procedimiento sumario** (código 9, con valor estimado de menos de 80.000 € en obras o de 60.000 € en el resto) se marca y se ordena primero. Las reglas y los umbrales están explicados al principio del módulo.

## 4. Prueba (`filtro_licitaciones_prueba.py`, nuevo)
Tres perfiles inventados (pyme de limpieza de 5 personas en Murcia, constructora de 40 personas clasificada y consultora informática de 2 personas), probados con los ZIP de PLACSP. Los resultados irán en un comentario.

## Riesgo al desplegar
La primera vez, el hilo de licitaciones relee 4 ZIP (unos 100-160 MB cada uno). Lo hace .atom a .atom, como ahora, pero conviene desplegar fuera del refresco nocturno y vigilar la memoria.
