author: dbarger-meng
body:
## Problem
On the rhythm dictation page, players heard only one click before the rhythm. Measured in Chromium:
- **Play** did schedule a full bar of clicks, but the unaccented clicks played at about half the accent's level through a click channel at 40%. That's easy to lose on a phone speaker, leaving just the accented first click.
- **▶ Bar** gave only one beat of lead-in, which is literally one click in 4/4.
- The first click was scheduled only 0.1 s ahead, which is tight for a phone that's just starting its audio.

## Changes
- **A full bar every time:** every play, including a single bar, counts in at least a full bar, which is 4 clicks in 4/4 and 6 in 6/8.
- **No more "off":** the count-in on/off box, which allowed no count-in at all, becomes a **one bar / two bars** choice. Old saved settings get one bar.
- **Louder, even clicks:** the click channel is at full volume on this page, and unaccented clicks are raised to near the accent's level. Rendered peaks are 0.70 for the accent and 0.59 for the rest, up from roughly 0.2 and 0.12 before.
- **Safe start:** playback waits for the audio context to be running and starts 0.25 s ahead, so no count-in click is lost.
- **On-screen count:** the count shows in time, as "Count-in: 1 → ● 2 → ● ● 3 → ● ● ● 4". It clears when playback ends or is stopped.
- The asset version is bumped to 21.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 61 of 61 pass.
- Chromium, counting the click oscillators actually scheduled:
  - 4/4: Play and ▶ Bar both give 4 evenly spaced clicks, even with the old "count-in off" setting saved.
  - 6/8: 6 clicks.
  - Two bars: 8 clicks.
  - Every first click is 0.25 s ahead.
- The dictation flow still scores 4 of 4 for a correct answer in both meters, with no page errors.

author: m4p4
body:
Closes #36

`router.resolve(conn, url)` walks the registry's rungs of the §4 ladder and nothing else:
stage 0 reads `url_cache`, stage 1 falls through (reserved — no pattern store exists at
schema version 1), stage 2 gates the matched pair on `archive`. A stage-0 hit is re-read
through `handlers.load()`, so FR-023's sha256 check demotes an edited script to
`probation` and the URL comes back `Unresolved` rather than routing to a handler that no
longer extracts what it was built to extract.

Results are three frozen dataclasses — `Resolved(handler_key, item_id, stage)`,
`AlreadyHave(handler_key, item_id)`, `Unresolved(site_key, fingerprint)` — unioned as
`Resolution`, so a caller that forgets a case fails to type-check instead of falling
through. `docs/requirements.md` §4 now enumerates stages 0–7 above its FR bullets.

## Verify

```sh
$ uv run pytest tests/registry/test_router.py && uv run ruff check . && uv run mypy src
........                                                                 [100%]
8 passed in 0.07s
All checks passed!
Success: no issues found in 16 source files
```

Full suite for good measure: `360 passed` (352 on `main` plus the 8 here).

## Deviation

The §4 table's ownership column names requirements, registry tables and tools
(`url_cache`, FR-011, `archive` FR-020/FR-021, FR-010, `gallery-dl`, FR-060, FR-011,
FR-012) rather than the phase numbers the issue's draft used. `requirements.md` states
it carries contracts only and has no planning references anywhere else, and phase
numbers go stale there; the Done-when asks for "the requirement that owns each", which
is what the column now gives. Stage 4 has no requirement of its own, so it names the
tool, and stage 5's "is it a plain file to fetch?" is decided by FR-060's single ranged
GET.

author: b-mendoza
body:
Replace husky and lint-staged with lefthook.

The backend Go module owns lefthook as a tool dependency. Run lefthook with `go tool lefthook` from `backend/`, or `go -C backend tool lefthook` from the repository root. Nothing installs lefthook globally.

lefthook.yml at the repository root runs the same staged-file checks as the old husky and lint-staged configs. Git hooks call lefthook with `go -C backend tool lefthook`.

Install hooks once after you clone. From `backend/`, run `go tool lefthook install` or `task hooks:install`. `pnpm install` does not install hooks, and the frontend has no `prepare` script.

Frontend jobs format staged frontend files with oxfmt. They lint staged JavaScript and TypeScript with Oxlint and ESLint. They type-check the frontend when a TypeScript file is staged.

Backend jobs format staged Go files with `golangci-lint fmt`. They then run `golangci-lint` and the custom analyzers when any backend file is staged.

This pull request does not change CI workflows.

## Note

lefthook is no longer a frontend npm package. The backend `go.mod` `tool` list pins lefthook v2.2.2. Anyone with Go can install hooks and run lefthook without a global lefthook binary.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Developer tooling and Git hook wiring only; application runtime and CI are unchanged, with a one-time migration step for existing Husky `core.hooksPath` settings.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replaces **Husky** and **lint-staged** with **lefthook** for local Git hooks. lefthook is pinned in the backend `go.mod` `tool` block (v2.2.2); hooks invoke it via `go -C backend tool lefthook`, and developers install them with **`task hooks:install`** (which also clears the legacy `core.hooksPath` of `frontend/.husky/_` when present). **`pnpm install` no longer installs hooks**—the frontend `prepare` script, Husky pre-commit, and both `lint-staged` configs are removed, along with `husky` and `lint-staged` from `package.json`.
> 
> Root **`lefthook.yml`** defines sequential **pre-commit** jobs that mirror the old behavior: frontend oxfmt → oxlint → ESLint → typecheck; backend `golangci-lint fmt` on staged Go files, then full `golangci-lint` and custom analyzers when backend files are staged. A **`commit-msg`** hook strips the Cursor `Co-authored-by` trailer. **`lefthook-local.yml`** is gitignored for local overrides.

author: littlesurvival
body:
## Problem and behavior
The release workflow previously published only the Android APK. It now builds and signs the APK on Linux while an Apple Silicon macOS runner builds one unsigned iPhone device IPA using Xcode Release. A shared `check` job first checks the changelog, manifest/app version consistency and source manifest rules, existing tag target, and required credential presence. Then `build_android` and `build_ios` run concurrently; `release` depends on all three jobs. Previously manifest validation ran only inside Android while iOS started immediately, and a tag conflict was only detected after both builds. Once both succeed, the release job downloads both artifacts, checks the APK SHA-256 and uploads the same files to GitHub, Gitee and Gitea; mirrors do not build them. The iOS version and build number come from the release manifest, and Android update feeds retain their APK format.

The existing mirror scripts recreate a release on rerun, so they upload both assets in the same operation. Failed checks prevent both builds, and failed/cancelled builds prevent publication. The source tag is checked before builds and rechecked/created only after successful builds. The release job also regenerates stable.json in its own checkout before preparing mirror tags, because the check job workspace is not shared. Later publication failures can leave a partial release; later upload failures require checking all three releases and rerunning. No Apple signing credentials are used. Users must sign and install the IPA themselves. The existing `release.yml` remains the sole release workflow, with a fixed `Release` display name and no hash in production script names.

```text
check --+-- build_android --+-- release
        +-- build_ios -----+
```

## Verification
- Production commit `f0ec052bff7e581457efe1bdc34ec6564633d247`, based on main `9816a0e` after PR #69.
- [Apple validation run 40558556865](https://github.com/LittleSurvival/yamibo-app/actions/runs/40558556865) passed on production commit `eda56a73e89900013af33a679ef394b31173d090`, prior to the workflow-only parallelization. Its validation commit `3c0a2a44654d79e7651911983db63e2ca1150eff` contains the production commit plus one branch-only entry script. The current PR does not change app sources or the IPA build script. Standard Apple Silicon macOS runner, Xcode 26.6, JDK 17, 6 GB Gradle heap, 2 workers; Release, generic iOS device destination, arm64, `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`. Kotlin Release framework succeeded in 28m 55s, then Xcode linking and IPA packaging succeeded.
- Downloaded test IPA: 26,159,328 bytes, SHA-256 `cd1d09203383d43bce97da09a7fdc260cb784a85b1890de924f2eea965d43cee`; ZIP integrity valid; iPhoneOS arm64, bundle `com.yamibo.bbs`, 0.0.10 (11), minimum iOS 18.2; no `LC_CODE_SIGNATURE`, `_CodeSignature`, or embedded provisioning profile.
- Default 4 GB heap failed twice with Java heap exhaustion during Kotlin/Native Release linking; [6 GB ARM test](https://github.com/LittleSurvival/yamibo-app/actions/runs/40552016327) passed on an earlier source. [Intel test](https://github.com/LittleSurvival/yamibo-app/actions/runs/40552091863) hit the 50-minute step timeout.
- `actionlint` v1.7.12, Bash syntax, test-isolation and OpenSpec isolation checks passed. On [workflow run 40564892352](https://github.com/LittleSurvival/yamibo-app/actions/runs/40564892352), Android and iOS jobs started within two seconds of each other, confirming parallel scheduling. Both were cancelled at the user request before builds completed; local Android release build was also interrupted. That run predates the shared check job. The final dependency graph and artifact/output wiring were checked with actionlint but not exercised end-to-end.

- Final review: all named steps from the main release workflow remain present; cross-job metadata references, signed APK checksum/size, IPA artifact names, all three asset publications, mirror tags, published manifest generation/validation, and feed pushes were inspected. `actionlint` v1.7.12, Bash syntax, production test isolation, OpenSpec isolation, and whitespace checks passed on the final change. The actual read-only preflight tag-check shell was run locally: it rejected the current branch because manifest tag 11 already targets the released commit, as expected. No build, workflow dispatch, tag creation, or release publication was run for this revision.

## Limits and rollback
User signing and installation on physical iOS hardware remain unverified. The complete workflow and uploads have not been run against a new release; existing releases are protected during validation. The test IPA is an Action artifact, not a release asset. Revert this commit to restore the Android-only release workflow.

author: cenzihan
body:
Native evidence processing can fail when a fresh HTTP/1.1 connection disconnects before response headers or ends mid-body. This change uses a single pooled HTTP/2 connection for GPT requests on the same official endpoint. Required models, native Mem0 prompts and retrieval behavior remain fixed; embedding traffic keeps its existing transport.

Each request requires a clean HTTP/2 stream end and a complete validated SSE response. Total deadlines, certificate validation, response limits, no redirects and no POST retries are enforced. A trace guard blocks a second send even if the connection pool reassigns the request. Only whitelisted failure scalars are recorded, without source content, response chunks or exception messages.

Validation: 736 offline checks passed, including 12 new tests using real HTTP/2 frames for connection reuse, GOAWAY, disconnects, limits and cancellation. Docker CI40557289720 passed on cde57b84d185c318b1fdbe441d8c47eb2e79cae4, and 73 runtime files matched the built image. An independent public Mem-Gallery pilot passed one Add and two Searches, preserving the original image; all 3 GPT and 4 embedding calls succeeded, with all 3 GPT responses using one HTTP/2 connection and the required returned model. This bounded pilot establishes tested connectivity and protocol behavior, not general network reliability or an official quality improvement.

author: ninguemdev
body:
Fecha #72.

## Resumo

- **Campo “Sentidos”** no painel de experimento: *Legados (círculo + radar)* ou *Olhos (requer NEAT)*, para evoluções novas. Escolher olhos seleciona NEAT; voltar o algoritmo para a MLP de controle volta os sentidos para os legados (sem combinação inválida). Também `-eden-senses legacy|eyes` no player; carregar um checkpoint mostra os sentidos dele.
- **Arena**: a criatura selecionada com olhos mostra o **cone de cada olho** (malha leve, cor fixa por slot, desenhada a partir da pose interpolada) e um **ponto na comida que cada olho vê agora**; o disco circular do sensor deixa de aparecer para ela. A camada só existe para a seleção.
- **Inspetor**: cada slot (direção, abertura, alcance em unidades, gasto/s, ou *ausente*); gasto em repouso com os olhos e o giro máximo; e **o que os olhos entregaram ao cérebro na última decisão** — o `BrainController` passa a guardar uma **cópia** das entradas de olho da decisão observada (o buffer do tick muda depois). Antes da primeira decisão aparece, separada, a “leitura atual dos olhos (ainda não é uma entrada do cérebro)”.
- A captura da rede NEAT antes da primeira decisão também usa as entradas de olho (o runner monta a leitura com o próprio buffer).

author: pastapastapasta
body:
## Summary

After Dash Core V24 activated on testnet (block 1,578,000), `SimplifiedMNList` rejects every testnet masternode list diff. That breaks `@dashevo/dapi-client`'s default node discovery. #318 fixed the first failure (CbTx v4), but two more sit behind it:

1. **ExtAddr (ProTx v3) entries hash differently.** V24 activates ProTx version 3. Core's `CSimplifiedMNListEntry` (`src/evo/simplifiedmns.h`) serializes a v3 entry's addresses as `ExtNetInfo` (`src/evo/netinfo.h`) instead of a single `CService`, and v3 evonodes no longer serialize `platformHTTPPort`. dashcore-lib still hashed v3 entries in the legacy layout, so as soon as the first v3 entry appeared the merkle root stopped matching the coinbase:
   ```
   Error: Merkle root from the diff doesn't match calculated merkle root after diff is applied
       at SimplifiedMNList.applyDiff (lib/deterministicmnlist/SimplifiedMNList.js:96:11)
   ```
2. **The LLMQ_60_75 limit regressed in 0.25.0.** The params table added in #310 set `maximumActiveQuorumsCount` for LLMQ_60_75 to 24. Core keeps 32 active (`signingActiveQuorumCount`, unchanged in v24), and 0.22 had 32. Every current mainnet and testnet diff carries 32, so 0.25.0 also rejects mainnet:
   ```
   Error: Trying to add more quorums to quorum type 5 than its maximumActiveQuorumsCount of 24 permits
   ```

## Changes

- `lib/util/netinfo.js` (new): serializes `ExtNetInfo` from the `addresses` map Core reports for it. For ExtAddr entries that map is exactly `ExtNetInfo::ToJson()`, with no legacy fields added (`GetNetInfoWithLegacyFields`, `src/evo/core_write.cpp`). It handles IPv4, IPv6, CJDNS, Tor v3 and I2P services (BIP155 ids), domains (`DomainPort`), and purposes in ascending code order.
- `SimplifiedMNListEntry`: stores `addresses` and hashes v3 entries with `ExtNetInfo`, without `platformHTTPPort`. It validates v3 addresses instead of requiring an IPv4 `service`. For v3 entries, `service` and `platformHTTPPort` are always taken from the hashed `addresses`. For v1/v2 entries, which hash those fields, Core's reported values are kept. When Core omits them (they only appear with `-deprecatedrpc=service`), they're filled in from `addresses`. A revoked legacy evonode reports no addresses but still hashes its port, so it is still rejected without the deprecated field. Hashing of v1 and v2 entries is unchanged.
- `constants`: LLMQ_60_75 `maximumActiveQuorumsCount` goes back to 32.

Not covered:
- The binary `SimplifiedMNListEntry.fromBuffer` / `SimplifiedMNListDiff.fromBuffer` path. It doesn't read Core's per-entry version, so it can't recognise v3 entries; its `toBuffer` → `fromBuffer` round trip already failed on master. DAPI streams the JSON form, which is what consumers use.
- `getIp()` still reads `service`, which is Core's deprecated primary `core_p2p` field. For a v3 entry with an IPv6/Tor `core_p2p`, or with Platform hosted on a different host or domain, it is not the Platform endpoint. Every testnet v3 evonode today has IPv4 and one shared host. An accessor for `platform_https` belongs in a follow-up.
- `LLMQ_25_67` and `LLMQ_TYPE_TEST_DIP0024` have `threshold` values that differ from Core. Nothing in `lib/` reads `threshold`, so I left them alone.

## Evidence

- Recorded a live testnet full diff at height 1,580,498, which has 12 v3 entries and 32 LLMQ_60_75 quorums, plus the following diff (which happens to carry no changes). They are in `test/fixtures/core24-testnet-mnlistdiffs.json`. With this branch both reproduce Core's `merkleRootMNList` and `merkleRootQuorums`. Without it they fail as shown above.
- A live mainnet full diff (height 2,562,385, pre-V24) also reproduces both roots with this branch.
- Live check: `@dashevo/dapi-client` 5.0.1 using this branch connects to testnet through default discovery once the platform whitelist is refreshed (dashpay/platform PR to follow).
- The `ExtNetInfo` byte vectors for each address kind are written from Core's serialization code. The IPv4-entry and empty-map vectors match rust-dashcore's `net_info.rs`. The Tor v3 and I2P addresses were generated independently, with Python's base32 and SHA3 checksum. Only IPv4 entries occur on testnet so far, so the live roots exercise IPv4 alone.

## Validation

- `npm run lint`: clean.
- `npm run test:types`: passes.
- `npm run test:node`: 3535 passing, 17 pending.
- Karma, ChromeHeadless only: 3529 passing (Firefox isn't installed locally).

Refs #317 (V24 wire formats). That issue doesn't cover the SML entry hash or the quorum limit.

Downstream, `@dashevo/dapi-client` needs a release with this change before it can discover testnet nodes again, and before mainnet's V24 fork.

body:
## Security test gap and cache finding
The cross-account regression added to draft #128 uses `/api/storage/upload`, which generates a `users/<owner>/...` key. That path was already guarded by a prefix check and **does not exercise the original hybrid authorization vulnerability for non-prefixed keys**. The actual `/api/storage/hybrid/upload` creates keys like `<owner>/<folder>/<hash>-<name>` outside `users/`. This difference was verified from the authenticated source at #142's head.

The alternate authenticated `GET /api/storage/hybrid/file/*key` route also did not explicitly set `Cache-Control: private, no-store` on successful byte responses. The primary route had already been hardened in #142.

## Change
- Add a real two-account HTTP integration regression that uploads a private hybrid object, asserts its key is outside `users/`, confirms exact bytes for the owner from **both** download routes, denies another logged-in account, denies anonymous access, and checks no-store response headers. A missing upload/PDIM backend **fails**, never skips as a privacy pass.
- Add `Cache-Control: private, no-store` to the secondary hybrid byte route.
- Use a disposable integration fixture and attempt cleanup without concealing the original assertion failure.

## Provenance and status (2026-10-27)
- `main`: `f227ce74c31848b34183e2256fca3cef304be148`.
- Parent draft #142: `7d2f0183777195da436514a1c033d01704f52b23`.
- Candidate: `47bea3c39eb0634362d85e1aef154264c75d474d`.
- Authenticated changed blobs: `server/routes/storage.ts` `c72de6c9f7dafa9019290256140154e248f71299`; `tests/file-management.test.ts` `46e19a4614dbb86866935c0b979a3d18a23013eb`.
- **PASS**: authenticated two-file scope compare and source-level route/header/test wiring inspection.
- **UNVERIFIED**: this newly committed integration test has **not executed** against a real HTTP server, two accounts, SQL and PDIM. Full repository Vitest/typecheck, CI, production build/start/readiness remain UNVERIFIED/BLOCKED. Do not claim an authorization test pass from the new assertions.

## Release decision
**NO-GO.** Draft, stacked on #142 (and therefore #128); do not merge independently. Requires an isolated disposable environment with actual PDIM and two authenticated sessions, plus working hosted CI. No merges, force pushes, deployments, migrations, production-data writes or Replit changes.

<!-- RECURSEML_SUMMARY:START -->
## High-level PR Summary
Adds a critical security regression test that exercises the **actual hybrid authorization vulnerability** for non-prefixed object keys (e.g., `owner/folder/hash-name`) outside the `users/` path. The existing test in draft #128 only covered prefixed keys under `users/owner/...` which were already protected. The new integration test uploads a private hybrid object, verifies cross-account denial on both download routes (`/api/storage/file/*` and `/api/storage/hybrid/file/*`), checks anonymous access denial, and validates `Cache-Control: no-store` headers. Also hardens the secondary hybrid download route by adding the missing `private, no-store` cache control header.

author: crrelabs
body: ## Why Google has crawled the directory and left almost everything as "Crawled - currently not indexed." Sitemaps, robots, canonicals, and 200s are already fine. The pages themselves were near-duplicates: a city page was a card list plus the same paragraph with the city and category swapped, and "nearby cities" was the same statewide top 12 on every page in a category. Listing pages with a one-sentence imported description had nothing else to read. This PR keeps every URL the same, except city pages with fewer than 3 listings are now `noindex, follow` and are dropped from the cities sitemap. All new sentences are computed from listings already in the database. Nothing invents reviews, ratings, prices, or services. ## City pages (`/services/[category]/[city]`) - Intro, stats block, and FAQ are built from that city + category + state: pro count, how many have a public rating, review-weighted average, share with a phone or website on file, how many publish weekly hours (after `normalizeHours`), ZIP codes in the 32xxx–34xxx range, and the highest-rated pros with at least 5 reviews. - FAQ text on the page and the FAQPage JSON-LD are the same strings. - Internal links are specific to the page: other categories in the same city (with counts), the same category in other cities in the same county (with counts), the category hub, and the county page. Georgia and Alabama cities, which have no county, link to other cities in that state instead. - A city is treated as a neighbor only when this county is its primary county (the `county` column on most of its listings). That stops one mistagged row from offering all of Sarasota as a DeSoto neighbor. - Queries filter by `state`. Stats paginate with `.range()` when a city has more than 500 listings. County logic stays Florida-only. **Noindex threshold: fewer than 3 listings.** Counted live on 27 Oct 2026, grouped the same way the sitemap groups cities (slug + state suffix + category): | | Pages | | --- | ---: | | City × category URLs | 5,299 | | 1 listing | 1,866 | | 2 listings | 880 | | **Noindex and removed from `cities.xml`** | **2,746 (51.8%)** | | Left in the sitemap | 2,553 | The ~5,366 figure is this set plus the 67 Florida county hubs (5,299 + 67 = 5,366). After the change, a rendered `cities.xml` has 2,620 URLs: 2,553 city pages and 67 county pages. Checked: `/services/roofing/midway` and `/services/fencing/slocomb-al` are `noindex, follow` and absent from the sitemap; Windermere landscaping, Arcadia appliance repair, and Miami plumbing stay indexable. ## Category hubs (`/category/[slug]`) - Summary and FAQ use the full category, not the 120 cards on the page: total, cities, review-weighted rating, phone and website coverage. - Florida counties are listed from each listing's `county` column (state `FL` only), with the top cities in that county linked to the city page and the county name linked to `/region/[county]`. - Georgia and Alabama cities are linked in their own section. - The card grid is Florida listings (`state = FL`), under the 1,000-row cap. ## Thin listing pages (`/listing/[slug]`) - Listings have no services column. When the description is empty or the usual one-sentence import ("provides professional … services in …" / "is a professional … serving the … area") and there are no HireAnyPro reviews, the page adds a local block: category, city, valid Florida ZIP, county, normalized hours, how many pros in that city and category, the review-weighted average when at least two are rated, and links to a few other pros plus the city page, category hub, and county page. - BreadcrumbList JSON-LD now includes the city crumb (Home → category → city → business), matching the visible breadcrumbs. - Claim banner, one-click `ct` token, quote form, `ListingViewBeacon`, and layout `FunnelTracker` are unchanged. `listing-redirects.json`, Stripe, auth, and email sending were not touched. `revalidate` and `generateStaticParams` (returning `[]`) stay on all three dynamic routes. Rendered pages send `Cache-Control: s-maxage=3600` (city and listing) or `s-maxage=300` (category), and a repeat request is `x-nextjs-cache: HIT`. ## Checks - `npm run build` passes. City, category, and listing routes stay ISR. - `npx tsx scripts/test-directory-content.ts` covers ZIP filtering, hours normalization, the noindex threshold, weighted ratings, neighbor selection, boilerplate detection, and FAQ JSON-LD matching the visible answers. - Rendered Windermere, Arcadia, Miami, Midway, Slocomb, `/category/plumbing`, and a thin Tampa listing. FAQ answers are visible and match the JSON-LD. County neighbors on Windermere are other Orange County cities, not the statewide top list. ## Unsure / worth a look - Phone and website figures are "on file." Free listings still hide those details until the business is on a paid tier, so the copy does not say the numbers are shown on the cards. - A listing with a real description longer than 180 characters, or any on-site review, does not get the extra market block. Almost every current description is the short template, so most listing pages get it. - Georgia and Alabama ZIP codes are outside 32xxx–34xxx, so those pages do not print a ZIP. That matches the existing junk-ZIP rule. - Category rating and phone percentages are omitted if the city-group total and the per-state rollup ever disagree. They matched for plumbing (1,604). - I did not noindex thin listing pages beyond the rule that was already there (no description and no contact info at all).

author: denisekiremire-a11y
body:
## Summary

The founder asked for Wano's design to feel more hand-built and artistic, and wanted to see options before committing to anything. Three directions were explored as a [design canvas](https://claude.ai/artifact/Bw75MsUFJe7v4boqTj32T3), each rooted in the real homepage's existing editorial system (Fraunces serif, Anton display, JetBrains Mono eyebrow labels, flat ink/paper/vermilion palette, no shadows):

- **A — Field Notes**: a pinned stack of overlapping "instant photos," hand-drawn underline accent, washi tape — scrapbook/personal.
- **B — Press Plate**: poster-scale Anton type, a faint coordinate watermark, a bleed photo — letterpress/print-craft.
- **C — Field Sketch**: a hand-drawn ink-line skyline illustration instead of a photo — the most literally illustrated option.

The founder picked **A**. This PR builds it into the real homepage hero.

## What changed

`src/app/page.tsx` — the hero's right-hand photo side only:

- Replaces the single framed photo + corner marks with `HeroPhotoStack`: three overlapping, slightly rotated photos using existing real assets (`lake-victoria-reeds.jpg`, `kampala-golden-hour.jpg`, `sunset-dinner.jpg`), each with an italic serif caption, plus a small rotated "washi tape" accent pinning the front photo down.
- Adds a loose hand-drawn SVG underline beneath "Uganda?" in the headline.
- Positioning is percentage-based (not px), so the stack rescales with its container at every breakpoint instead of needing separate responsive overrides.
- `priority` loading moved to the largest/most prominent photo (previously the sole hero image) to keep LCP behavior equivalent.

Headline copy, eyebrow/coordinates, subcopy, arrow links, and the category marquee below are all unchanged — this is a visual treatment change only, nothing in content or layout structure otherwise.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint src --max-warnings=0`, `npm run build` — all clean.

author: jlongster
body:
## Summary
- Part 3 of the stack for #25, stacked on #29. Please merge #28 and #29 first.
- Behaviour-preserving refactor: the 10 ms accept loop is unchanged. This PR prepares the loop to become readiness-driven in the next PR.
- New `daemon::Control` holds a private stop flag and the ownership mutex, and is now the only way to stop the daemon or mutate ownership.
    - `request_stop` takes the ownership lock, so the next PR can wake the accept loop under that same lock.
- `run` is split into bind → `Control` → `serve`. Ownership is still created after bind, as before.
- Handler completion is tracked with a `done` flag set by a drop guard in the handler thread (the reap check still also accepts `is_finished()`). The next PR adds a wake there.
- `Ownership::with_timeouts` lets tests use short starting/handoff deadlines.
- New in-process unix tests in `src/daemon/server.rs`, using a `TestDaemon` fixture that runs `serve` on a temp socket:
    - `shutdown_request_stops_immediately`
    - `owner_shutdown_stops_immediately`
    - `owner_disconnect_without_handoff_stops_immediately`
    - `starting_deadline_fires_on_time`
    - `waiting_deadline_fires_on_time`
    - `handoff_claim_transfers_without_spurious_stop`

author: nqxaver
body: ## What this does The Desk tab's headlines now refresh on GitHub's servers, with no PC and no chat. They are grouped into scannable sections instead of one dense table. Claude's desk note, the Grok / X pulse, the economic calendar, earnings, and the live NQ/ES quote are unchanged. The workflow only commits `data/desk/feed.json`. It does not edit `today.json`, `grok.json`, desk days, or any other tab. ## What runs automatically `.github/workflows/desk-news.yml` (`workflow_dispatch`, plus the schedule below) checks out `main`, runs `python3 scripts/refresh_desk_news.py`, and pushes `data/desk/feed.json` only when the headline list actually changed. A second run with the same headlines leaves the file alone, so it does not commit on a timer for its own sake. The script uses the Python standard library only. No API keys and no secrets. It reads free public RSS/Atom feeds: - CNBC (world, economy, earnings, finance, technology, energy, top) - MarketWatch (top stories and real-time headlines) - Federal Reserve press releases (all, and monetary policy) - Bureau of Labor Statistics latest releases - BBC world and business - Al Jazeera - NPR world and business - New York Times world, business, and economy - The Guardian world, business, and economics - OilPrice and EIA Today in Energy - UN peace and security - Wall Street Journal markets and US business Reuters and AP do not offer a working free feed to this job (Reuters returns 401, AP's old host does not resolve). World and business coverage comes from the publishers above. BLS publishes a feed, but some networks get HTTP 403; that failure is logged and the rest of the file is still written. Each run de-duplicates by normalized headline (and a token overlap check), drops items that match no section keyword unless the feed is a narrow one such as Fed press or the earnings wire, and keeps roughly the last 48 hours (72 for war, Fed, and data; 96 for High impact), capped at 10 per section. The Desk page loads `data/desk/feed.json` and merges it with the `news` array Claude still writes in `data/desk/today.json`. Claude's wording wins when the two describe the same story, and Claude's impact is kept. A headline only in the feed is marked Auto. A headline Claude wrote is marked Desk note and still shows his `why` line. Scheduled runs start after this workflow is on `main`. Until then it can be run by hand with **workflow_dispatch** once the file is on the default branch. Locally it was dry-run: `python3 scripts/refresh_desk_news.py --self-test` (18 keyword cases) and a live fetch. A second fetch printed `feed unchanged`. `actionlint` reported the workflow file as valid. ## How often Times are UTC, which is what GitHub Actions cron uses. - **Weekdays, every 30 minutes from 09:00–23:59 UTC.** That is about 5:00 AM–7:59 PM ET during daylight time and 4:00 AM–6:59 PM ET during standard time, so it covers premarket, the cash session, and the early evening. - **Weekday overnights, every 2 hours** at :20 past 00:00, 02:00, 04:00, 06:00, and 08:00 UTC. Globex is quieter then. - **Weekends, every 3 hours.** - **Sunday 22:20 and 23:20 UTC**, around the 6:00 PM ET equity-futures reopen (one of those hours is 6:20 PM ET depending on daylight time). GitHub may start a scheduled job a few minutes late. The Desk page still shows a Headlines stamp and a Desk note stamp in ET, and a "N new headlines since you last opened the desk" line after the first visit (stored on this device only). ## How impact tags are decided The lists are in `data/desk/news-rules.json`. The same rules run in the Python script and in the page, so a desk note Claude did not tag still lands in a section. This is an automatic keyword guess, not trading advice. The page says that in the Market news intro, and each risk pill has the same tooltip. **Section.** Each keyword has a weight. The section with the highest score wins. A tie breaks in this order: Geopolitics / War, Economic Data, Fed and Rates, Energy and Oil, Mega-cap Tech and Earnings, Other Markets. On screen the order is War, Fed, Data, Tech, Oil, Other Markets. The chip row filters to one section. Highest impact, then newest, come first inside a section. **Impact.** - **High** if the headline hits a tier-1 word (FOMC, a rate cut or hike, CPI, PCE, payrolls, the jobs report, GDP, missile, airstrike, ceasefire, Hormuz, escalation, and the other words in `highAny`), or an oil-shock pair (oil, Brent, WTI, crude, Aramco, or Ras Tanura, plus jump, plunge, attack, or fire), or a mega-cap name (Nvidia, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Tesla, Broadcom, Anthropic, and their tickers) plus earnings, guidance, revenue, results, or IPO. War plus the word "nuclear" is also High. - **Medium** if it is not High and the section is war, Fed, economic data, or energy, or it hits a second-tier word (earnings, yields, sanctions, OPEC, Nasdaq, tariffs, and the rest of `mediumAny`). - **Low** for other headlines that were still worth keeping, such as a generic futures or gold line. **Risk lean.** `riskOff` and `riskOn` phrases are counted separately. One side produces that lean. Both produce Mixed (a ceasefire headline that also says "attacks" is Mixed). Neither produces no lean. Claude's written impact is not replaced. The lean on a desk note is still the keyword guess. ## What stays the same Accountability, Journal, Calendar, and Spending are not part of this change, and neither is the GitHub key or the save logic. The Grok block still reads `data/desk/grok.json` when it is newer than the copy inside `today.json`. [Desktop Desk news, grouped into sections with impact and risk tags](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5e8a35b5-665e-5abd-958c-a36b0f5bfd18/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fdesk_news_desktop.png) [Phone Desk news filtered to Geopolitics / War](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5e8a35b5-665e-5abd-958c-a36b0f5bfd18/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fdesk_news_phone.png) [desk_news_filters.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-5e8a35b5-665e-5abd-958c-a36b0f5bfd18/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fdesk_news_filters.mp4) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: xuelink
body:
Since #2038, an emoji reaction on the other person's newest message counts as an answer. The catch is that `reactToMessage` sets `lastMessage.reacted` only at the moment someone reacts. A reaction left before that API was running never set the flag, so those threads still show "Your turn" to someone who already answered. They stay that way until somebody writes again.

The gap is longer than the merge time suggests. #2038 merged at 15:36 UTC on 25 October, but its own `Deploy API` run failed: deploys were broken that afternoon. The first successful deploy that includes it is #2055, at about 18:15 UTC.

## What it does

`apps/api/scripts/backfill-reacted-last-message.ts` follows the same pattern as the other `backfill-*` scripts. It runs dry by default; `--apply` writes.

- **Scans reacted messages, not threads.** It finds messages whose `reactions` are non-empty and keeps those reacted to by someone other than the writer. Reacted messages are a small part of the collection, so this is one server-side scan. Going thread by thread would mean one round trip per conversation from wherever the script runs.
- **Checks those threads in one query.** It loads them with a single `$in`. It marks a thread only when that message is still the thread's `lastMessage` (same `createdAt`/`senderId` pair) and the thread isn't already marked.
- **Guards each write.** The filter carries the same pair, so a message that arrives mid-run makes the write match nothing. Re-running finds nothing to do.

The dry run prints up to 10 of the conversation ids it would mark.

## Testing

- `pnpm --filter @langx/api typecheck` (covers `scripts/`), eslint and prettier on the file: clean.
- **Not run against a MongoDB.** The session that wrote this couldn't download a `mongod` binary. Run the dry run first and check that a thread you know about appears in its sample before passing `--apply`.

author: bouloschaaya
body:
## Finding (trace map: cron trace, question "together")
A blocked FORBID_OVERLAP occurrence was delayed until the holder's execution lease **expired**. The holder renews that lease to `now + 300 s` every 10 s, and nothing wakes a delayed job when the lease is released. So the next occurrence started **up to 5 minutes after the previous one finished**, contradicting ARCHITECTURE.md ("re-activates after the lease holder finishes"). If runs take longer than the interval, throughput fell to ~1 run per 5 minutes.

**Reproduced before the fix:** new test 4b, with the lease held and its expiry 300 s ahead → wake-up scheduled **302 s** later.

## Fix
`deferUntil = min(lease expiry + margin, now + SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_RECHECK_MS)`, default **5 s**.
- The next occurrence runs within one recheck of the holder finishing.
- A crashed holder is still covered: its lease expires, and the next recheck wins.
- Cost: each blocked occurrence makes one short PostgreSQL transaction per 5 s.
- A recheck doesn't use a BullMQ attempt (same as before).

**Not changed, on purpose:** FORBID_OVERLAP still runs every occurrence serially and drops none (the documented design). The backlog now drains at the speed of the runs.

## Evidence
| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 4b: 5-minute lease held | wake at +302 s | wake within 10 s |
| 4: lease ends in 1 s | — | wake at expiry + margin |
| worker suite | — | 55/55 |

ARCHITECTURE.md and the README env table updated. Part of v1.0.1.

author: tmm
body:
`Zero.init` opens and loads the store on the main thread. When another program held the file locked (a SQLite browser, say), SQLite's 5 s busy timeout froze the app for 5 s before the client fell back to memory.

**Change:** opening and loading wait at most 250 ms for the lock, then the client runs on memory and calls `onStorageFailure`, as before. The 5 s timeout is restored once the store is loaded, so writes still wait it out (the existing busy-write tests cover that).

**Test:** `openingALockedDatabaseFallsBackWithoutWaitingOutTheBusyTimeout` holds an exclusive lock from a second connection. Before the fix, `Zero.init` took 5.01 s; after, the test passes in 0.28 s. The full suite (269 tests, excluding E2E) passes.

**Not done: opening the store off the main actor.** It would make `clientGroupID`/`profileID` async and give `materialize` an empty first frame at launch, both breaking. Measured cold-launch `Zero.init` with a stored replica (release build, orb x64): 10k rows ≈ 50 ms, 50k ≈ 0.3–0.4 s, 100k ≈ 0.7–0.8 s. Not worth it at typical sizes; revisit if an app keeps 50k+ rows locally.

author: satvik-somashekar
body:
Before: Only spending questions could get a suggestion, and the Knowledge Base sections only filtered which accounts were searched. A normal user could not ask "is my insurance enough?" or "am I too concentrated in one fund?".

After: Each section answers plain-language planning questions about its own records only.
- Insurance: cover, premiums per year, term and health cover, and (only when income is visible, i.e. in All accounts) term cover as a multiple of yearly salary against the common 10 to 15 times starting point.
- Mutual Fund Holdings: value, gain over cost, largest scheme's share against a 40% concentration flag, split by scheme type, recent monthly investing.
- Stocks & Demat: value, largest and top-three share against a 25% flag.
- EPF & Retirement: balance, monthly and yearly contributions, balance in a year before interest, employer's share.
- All accounts: net worth mix and months of spending the savings accounts would cover against a 6 month cushion.
A question that names no area ("how can I improve?") is read as being about the selected section. A question about another area is declined without reading any data. A question a section cannot answer gets that section's own help text. Product picks, predictions, tax and loan questions are still declined.

How: `AdviceEngine` computes each review in Java with record citations; the rules of thumb come back as figures so they show as assumptions and are never typed into a sentence. Wording comes from a template, or from Gemini/Claude through placeholders only. The parser flags generic questions and `QueryService` resolves them from the section. Ten new tests in `SectionAdviceTest`; all backend tests pass and the evaluation set is unchanged at 100% with no misses. Checked in the browser for every section with the Meera Rao demo customer.

author: btcforplebs
body:
User report (Logen, 17:24Z): blocking someone in Nostr Vault on the web wiped the blocks they had added in Amethyst.

## Cause
A kind 10000 replaces the whole list. `setBlock` looked for the newest list only on `account.relays`. Until the account's kind 10002 loads, or when it has none, those are just the defaults (damus, primal). When most of those relays answered with nothing, the guard took that as "no list yet" and published a fresh one-entry list. A list that Amethyst kept on the user's own relays was never seen.

## Fix (`web-vault/src/net/blocks.js` only)
- `findLatestBlockList` also asks the relays named in the user's newest kind 10002, which it finds on the account, default and index relays. It also asks the broadcast relays the new list goes to.
- `blockGuard`: when no relay of the user's had a list, a fresh list is started only if **every** one of them answered, not most. Otherwise nothing is signed and the dialog shows the reason.
- The edit itself is unchanged. It builds on the newest list and keeps every untouched entry: people, `word`, `t`, `e` and the private NIP-44/NIP-04 content. Unblock removes that one `p` from the public and private parts and nothing else.

## Testing
- `node --test 'test/*.test.mjs'` in web-vault: 1150/1150 pass. `scripts/check-file-sizes.sh`: OK.
- New tests: an Amethyst-style list (p, word, t, e, plus a private part) reachable only through the user's 10002, block then unblock. Also a relay that times out means nothing is signed. All 3 new or changed tests fail on master.
- Live run with a throwaway key: a 10002 on primal naming relay.nostr.net, and an "Amethyst" 10000 on relay.nostr.net only, with account relays = [primal].
  - master: the new list was `[["p",B]]` with the private part gone, which reproduces the wipe.
  - this branch: the new list kept p/word/t/e plus the new `p`, and the private content was byte-identical.

Web only. Tim is fixing the native apps in nv-fips.

author: radomird
body:
Stage 6's TV side of a build (boards 10, 17 and 20), on top of radomird/agentv-os#114's daemon routes.

## What's here

- **Asking.** Apps' "+ add your own" (it said coming soon) opens a page that asks what to make. You type it on the TV or the phone. What setup's "+ add your own" kept for later is one press away, and it's dropped from setup's list once asked.
- **Confirming.** The agent's reading comes back to confirm: the name, the recipe (or "no recipe fits: a plan first"), what it'll be, the cost and the time. On a key the cost reads "about $0.50 to $3.00 on your claude key, and never more than $5.00", from the recipe or the plan. On a plan it reads "within its own limits". "Not this" puts the build away.
- **Following it.** A build shows its steps (`[x]`, `[~]`, `[ ]`, `[!]`) and a bar on its page. It also shows on its tile in Apps under "# your agent's builds", in home's first free cell (not saved in the layout), and in home's bar. The TV toasts when a build needs confirming, has a plan to approve on the phone, is ready to approve on the phone, is on home, or failed.
- **Failing.** A failed build says why, with the step it stopped on. It can be tried again, or put away with Delete, as its tile says.
- **A child's profile** gets no "+ add your own" and no builds. The daemon already refuses them.

The daemon gets:

- **Starting.** A build reads "starting" until root takes its request and the builder writes. Before, a confirmed build kept saying "confirm" until the builder's first status.
- **Install refusals.** Root's reason shows when it couldn't install an approved app.
- **Putting a build away.** `POST /api/builds/:build/forget` drops a build that never reached home, and its folder once no other version is left. A starting build is stopped first. A running one is refused, and an installed one points to remove.
- **More on each build:** its provider, path (plan or key), cost range and minutes.
- **Wishes.** `GET /api/builds` lists setup's wishes.
- **The phone's state** now carries an adult's builds (name, state, steps done) for its notices. The phone's screens are in radomird/agentv-os#118.

The runner now marks a build it was stopping as failed, "you stopped it", instead of leaving it "running".

## Checks

- Layer 4: a new `builds.test.mts` (5 tests) plays root's part through each build's `status.json` and drives the TV through asking, confirming, following, failing, retrying, putting away, setup's wishes and a child's profile. The full layer 4 passes, 159 tests, after S2.7 caught a "your agent" label on the tile (now "make one").
- Layer 2: four new unit tests in `builds.test.mts` cover starting, putting away, a refused install and a stopped build. The daemon test now covers the wishes and the phone's state. All 59 unit files pass.
- Types check. Layer 1 passes except shellcheck's SC2015 info in `bin/agentv-screen`, which my local shellcheck flags and CI's doesn't.

Nothing here marks an acceptance check passed.

author: sakuga-agent[bot]
body:
## Summary « Lecture des traductions… » took 13 s on eskaipu. Measured in production (read-only script in the app container, cold read of `en`): | Step | eskaipu (43 files) | detectivebox-front (5 files) | |---|---|---| | head commit | 0.5 s | 0.8 s | | two directory listings | 0.4 s | 0.2 s | | source history since the connection | 0.3 s | 0.3 s | | **file contents, one file after the other (2 calls each)** | **12.3 s** | 1.2 s | | total | 13.5 s | 2.5 s | The same 43 files fetched in parallel take 0.64 s. So the time was the `for … await` loop over the files. - **In parallel**: the files of a catalogue are read 8 at a time (`READS_AT_ONCE`), so a large repository stays under GitHub's secondary rate limit. - **By blob SHA**: each file is fetched with `GET /git/blobs/{sha}`, with the SHA its directory listing at the head commit gives, and its parsed content is kept by that SHA (`blobs`, up to 2,000 files, least recently read out first). A SHA names one content forever, so the entry is never stale. After a push — which empties the catalogue cache through the webhook of DB-651 — a read asks again only for the files whose SHA changed. A language read after another shares the files of the source. - The listing still comes from the head commit, so a catalogue is still read at one revision, and `shas` still names what a publication writes against (DB-212). The write path is unchanged. After, measured the same way on eskaipu (3 runs): **cold read 2.8–2.9 s** (was 13.5 s), **read after a push of one file 1.1–1.5 s** (head + listings + history + 1 blob; was a full cold read). The streaming progress of the second half of DB-654 comes in a PR stacked on this one. ## Test plan - [x] `catalogue-blobs.spec.ts` on the fake GitHub: after a push that changes one file, a new read fetches exactly 1 blob (cold read: 24); 12 files are read several at once and never more than 8 files (16 blobs) at a time. Reversals: with the blob cache switched off the first test fails (24 fetches), with `READS_AT_ONCE = 1` the second fails. - [x] typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, tests (api 389, web 147, mcp 26). - No visual change. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---

Sakuga Review · Score de confiance : 4/5

Fusion mergeable en l'état : aucun défaut bloquant trouvé. Le seul point est une incohérence mineure entre la limite de 8 fichiers annoncée et la concurrence réelle de 16 requêtes.

Constats

1.  **Concurrence réelle double de la limite annoncée** `packages/api/src/services/i18n-catalogue.service.ts:417` READS_AT_ONCE vaut 8 et la doc annonce 8 requêtes à la fois, mais chaque tâche lance deux blobs (source et cible) en parallèle. Un dépôt de 43 fichiers peut donc ouvrir 16 requêtes simultanées, soit le risque de limite secondaire que la constante veut éviter. Le test accepte d'ailleurs jusqu'à 16. **Correction :** Soit réduire la limite à 4 pour garder 8 requêtes simultanées, soit corriger la doc et le nom de la constante pour dire 8 blobs au total.
Résumé La PR lit les fichiers de locale en parallèle, par groupes de 8, et garde les fichiers parsés par SHA de blob dans un cache borné à 2000 entrées. Les SHA de blob étant des empreintes de contenu, le cache ne peut pas renvoyer un contenu périmé. J'ai vérifié la gestion des erreurs de blobOf, l'ordre des résultats de inParallel, le cas d'un fichier absent côté cible et la réutilisation du contenu source quand la langue est la source. Je n'ai pas pu vérifier les appelants de getCatalogue ni le comportement réel de l'API GitHub sur les blobs volumineux.
Diagramme ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR A["read"] --> B["inParallel"] B --> C["blobOf source"] B --> D["blobOf cible"] C --> E["blobs cache"] D --> E ```
Non relu - packages/db/src/types.ts: définition de I18nRepository lue en contexte seulement - packages/api/src/services/github-app.service.ts: ask et insideRepository lus en contexte seulement, pas de vérification des codes d'erreur de ask pour les blobs

author: rastislavpapp
body:
Closes #122

## Summary

**Go to Time (Ctrl+G, Edit › Go To…; in the plugin on the IDE's Go to Line keys)**: a modal dialog, as Go to Line asks for a line, the same in the app and the plugin.

```text
GoToDialog OK
  GoToTime.parse(text, reference, zone)   # 2026-10-09 08:30, 08:30 (selected row's day), 1h30m, -10s
  ShownLog.landingAt(time)                # first shown row at or after; miss = HIDDEN | PAST_LAST
  select row, follow off, close           # bad text: the reason under the field, dialog stays open
                                          # miss: once closed, a hint over the rows says why
```

**Timestamp shift** per file of a merge, set in the Open Files dialog's Shift column (shown for a merge choice) or the Source cell's menu; kept in recent sessions and `--shifts`.

```diff
 MergedLog.build(parts, names, shifts)
   timestampNanos(record)      = time + shifts[part]     # one long add per record
   heads[part]                 = time + shifts[part]     # merge order
 MergedFilter: TimeCondition bounds unshifted per part
 TimeCount / VariableSeries: + shift of the part
 LogSession.shiftTimestamps(shifts) → reload, keeping the selected and top record
 Time cell: original text + dim "+2h" mark and tooltip; Source cell: "app-2.log (+2h)"
```

**Date/time picker** (plain Swing in `ui`, colors through `Look`), opened by a click in the Go to Time field or in a filter's time value (no calendar button):

```text
TimePicker (non-focusable popup; the field keeps the focus and stays typable)
├── calendar: 6 whole weeks, today ringed, a dot on every day with records (ShownLog.anyRecordIn, shown or not)
├── TimeOfDayField: HH:mm:ss edited a part at a time, Up/Down carry over midnight into the calendar
└── shortcuts: Now, 15 minutes ago, 1 hour ago, 24 hours ago, Today, Yesterday, This week, 7 days ago
writes TimeLiteral.format text only; follows what is typed in the field
```

Also:
- A Timestamp rule starts at "at or after", a Level rule at "at least".
- GLOSSARY: **Timestamp shift**, and Recent session keeps it.
- Plugin changelog: Go to Time and the picker under Unreleased (the shift is merge-only, so not in the plugin).

## Evidence

- **Before:** no way to jump to a time; a merge of files logged in different time zones interleaves wrongly; time values typed by hand only.
  **After:**
  - `./gradlew build` (tests + detekt) passes on the branch rebased onto `main`. New tests: `GoToTimeTest`, `TimestampShiftTest`, `ShownLogTest` (landing, hidden-at-same-time, `anyRecordIn`), `MergedLogTest` / `LogSessionTest` shifts, `SessionArgsTest` / `RecentSessionsTest` / `TabPlanTest` shifts, `EditorRuleTest` default operators, `TimeOfDayFieldTest`, `TimeShortcutTest`.
  - GUI sandbox, on a 10 GB log and a 2-file merge: Go to with absolute, relative and past-the-end times and a bad one; Shift column and Source menu re-merge keeping the position; picker typing both ways, keyboard, shortcuts, day dots matching the file (1, 2 and 9 October), Esc closing only the picker.
  - `./gradlew -q :tools:benchmark`: merge rows pass; "follow: filter appended records" was noisy once (+223%) and passed with `-PbenchmarkForks=8` (that path is untouched).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

New settings keys (`shift.N` in recent sessions) and the `--shifts` argument are only added; older builds ignore them.

**Blast Radius:** merging, Go to Line keys in the plugin

A shift is a per-record add in `MergedLog` and per-part bounds in `MergedFilter`; with no shift both are + 0. Changing a shift reloads the session, so it re-reads the files: slow for very large merges. In the plugin, Go to Line in a logxy view now opens Go to Time.

author: antoni-czaplicki
body:
## Summary

Replaces the boolean `multiple` with a question `type` — `single_choice`, `multiple_choice`, `true_false`, `open` — adds per-question `open_matching`, and adds a flashcard study page. Clean break: `multiple` is gone from the API, so this deploys together with the backend PR (linked below).

### Model (`@testownik/core`)
- `Question.type` and `open_matching`, with `QUESTION_TYPES`, Polish labels and `TRUE_FALSE_LABELS`. Choice questions always shuffle their answers; true/false and open never do, so there is no per-question shuffle flag.
- True/false is exactly two answers: order 1 is the "true" label, order 2 the "false" one, labels editable, never shuffled. Open questions hold accepted answers (all marked correct, no images).
- `quiz/grading.ts`: one grader for every type. Open answers match exactly or, with `open_matching: "similar"`, with typo tolerance: NFC + whitespace + case normalisation, then diacritics stripped, an edit-distance allowance by length (4–7 chars: 1, 8–15: 2, 16+: 3), OSA distance, equality only above 512 code points. `grading.vectors.json` is byte-identical to the backend's copy and both suites run it.
- Session: `shufflesAnswers`, `createSelfAssessmentRecord`, answer records accept a caller-supplied ID (Expo UUID), `.sort` on copies instead of `toSorted` for Hermes.
- Zod schema with per-type errors (true/false count and correct flag, open accepted answers and images).

### Editor
- "Typ pytania" dropdown per question and "Sprawdzanie odpowiedzi" for open questions. True/false has fixed two labels with no add/remove; open questions add accepted answers. A one-line hint under the answers explains the type.
- `withQuestionType` converts between types: leaving true/false drops its default labels, open marks everything correct and strips images, choice ↔ choice keeps the answers. Undo of a deleted answer refits it to the current type.
- Bulk "set type for all questions" with toast and undo; quick edit, version history, question summaries and rows show the type.

### Player
- `ChoiceAnswers` and `OpenAnswer` (typed answer, Enter checks, "Zaliczono z tolerancją literówek" when matched with tolerance).
- Flashcards: their own page at `/quiz/<id>/flashcards`, reached from the quiz info menu, with a progress line and a finished state. Tap or Space flips, swipe right / `2` / "Umiem" records a known card, swipe left / `1` / "Nie umiem" an unknown one. Self-grades go through the regular session and the new `self_assessment` API field, so reoccurrences, stats and history work unchanged.
- History dialog, dashboard question card and stats are type-aware.

### Continuity
- `answer_checked` now carries the record, so a peer shows the same selection and grade; every message carries the sender's instance ID; duplicate records are ignored.
- A tab never connects to or listens to itself. A re-initialisation (StrictMode, HMR) could leave an unopened host alive, and the tab then connected to its own ghost host which echoed its messages back, re-recording answers in a loop. Pre-existing; found during QA.

### Periphery
- Import/export, legacy validation and guest-quiz migration, AI chat tools and prompts (open questions in the practice card, edit tool keeps the type when omitted), `quiz.service.recordAnswer(..., selfAssessment)`, mocks and specs.

## Review

Implementation with GPT-6.1 Sol and two review rounds with GPT-6 Astra via T3; every must-fix finding is applied (grading parity, flashcard lifecycle, record transport over continuity, undo correctness, AI tool handling).

## Verification

- Driven in headless Chromium against the local stack with a quiz holding all four types: editor type switching and undo, import; answering each type; flashcard swipe, buttons and keys; two tabs over continuity.
- `vitest` 370 passing (core + web), uncached `eslint` and `tsc` clean.

## Not in this PR

Mobile lives on `feat/mobile-question-types` on top of `feat/mobile`.

Backend counterpart: Solvro/backend-testownik#300.

RECORDED_RUN_ID and RECORDED_EXECUTIONS are derived from it (evidence/run-0e16414b71d7.executions.json). DRILL_RUN_ID is 40533087300, and that drill's evidence names commit 42bd5bc.   - One fails if the recorded run in evidence.ts is not the first run in web/runs/index.json. It also checks the run file's bundle, approval and label date, and that the executions file names this run and the drill run id. The worker must have ended at the pause before a new fleet process started: two fleet executions, one intake, one publisher.
  - One fails if the agents, interpret step, gate verdicts or card flags that the status lines name differ from the run's sealed manifest and card. The card's hash is held to the manifest.

## Why

Judges flagged it as a consistency defect: How it works described a different run from every other screen.

## How it was checked

- Every file and line cited in evidence.ts was read at 19248db with git show, and each still holds its snippet. That includes lines 15, 23, 31 and 39 of the new executions file, and line 1 of the sealed card.

- No readiness marker pinned How it works or the old run, so ci/readiness.json and ci/readiness.py are unchanged. The readiness gate's forbidden-string rules (the pinned defaults plus the extra terms in readiness.json) were run over both changed source files and found nothing.
- python ci/check_dashes.py reports problems: 0.

With this change, How it works, Approve and Newsroom all describe run-0e16414b71d7, so they must agree on who flagged s7. How it works says what the sealed card records: the s7 flag is the Fact Gate's (card.json: "by":"factgate", code factgate_template_line), and the Desk Editor added no flag of its own. On main, the Approve screen lists that flag under "Desk Editor flags" (approve.tsx:204), and the Newsroom desk trace says the Desk Editor "Flagged 1 sentence for a person".

This PR therefore takes no heading change of its own, because one on approve.tsx would conflict with #69 on the same lines. author: g-r-ay
body: A Vertex express (API-key) key cannot be list-checked: Bifrost reports `list_models_failed` for every one of them, good or bad. The previous note ("Nothing to fix. Calls still route") said a key was fine without checking it. This replaces that note with a real probe of that key. ## Route Bifrost v2.2.1, the image this repo runs, pins one request to one stored key with `x-bf-api-key-id`. The probe is `POST /v1/responses/input_tokens` with model `vertex/gemini-2.5-flash`. That is `count_tokens` (free; not a generate), it only reaches Gemini models, and the response names the key that answered, so another key cannot stand in. The provider secret stays in Bifrost. This path does not read or log it. Confirmed on the running gateway: a fake express key, pinned by id, came back HTTP 401 from Vertex with `routing_info.provider=vertex` and `routing_info.key` equal to that key's name. ## Verdict Shown in the same Health chip as every other key: - the call succeeds → Healthy (Good), and the key is routable - 401/403, or a body that says the key is invalid → Rejected (Poor), with Google's reason shortened to 140 characters, and the key is not routable - the probe could not run (network, Bifrost down, timeout, or the pin did not land on this key) → chip **Not checked**, title "Couldn't reach Vertex to check this key." Not checked stays routable. That is what main already does for an unverifiable key whose credential is set (`key_is_routable` returns true unless the credential is an unresolved env reference). A missing network must not take that key out of rotation. Rejected does. A service-account Vertex key is not probed. Listing still cannot verify it, so it stays Unverifiable. The result is cached per key for 10 minutes. `GET /api/bifrost/routability` reads the cache and does not call the model again. A key write drops that key's entry. **Test again** (`POST /api/bifrost/routability/recheck/{key_id}`) drops it and probes immediately; the following routability read reuses the fresh entry. Closes #3251 ## Live bad key Fake express key `vertex-express` (`d6d900b0-7e7e-48f6-9c4c-8bd8bbf6719f`) through the real gateway on port 8080: ``` POST /v1/responses/input_tokens model: vertex/gemini-2.5-flash x-bf-api-key-id: d6d900b0-7e7e-48f6-9c4c-8bd8bbf6719f status 401 verdict health=rejected routable=false description=API key not valid. Please pass a valid API key. ``` ## Verification **Ran** - `python -m pytest tests/unit/llm/test_bifrost_mirror.py` — 26 passed. A 200 from the probe is healthy and routable. A 401 is rejected, not routable, with Google's reason, and a long reason is cut at 140 characters. A timeout is Not checked and routable. A second routability read inside the TTL makes no probe call; invalidating the cache (what a key edit does) probes again. An OpenAI key that failed listing stays rejected and is not probed. A Vertex service account stays unverifiable and is not probed. - `npx vitest run src/screens/settings/AiProvidersPanel.test.tsx` — 26 passed. Healthy is Good, rejected is Poor with the reason as the title, Not checked is that chip with "Couldn't reach Vertex to check this key." Test again calls recheck. No "Nothing to fix" or "Calls still route". - Live probe above, against Vertex via Bifrost, with a fake express key. Rejected, with Google's reason. **Did not run** - Full backend and frontend CI suites. CI runs them on the PR. - The Settings screen in a browser. The console listens on 6988, and this rework was not allowed to use ports 6987–6990. **Blocked by the machine** - none for this rework. The earlier empty `BIFROST_ADMIN_PASSWORD` (management API 500) and `VIGIL_COOKIE_SECURE=true` on plain HTTP are unchanged and were not needed: the probe is inference, which does not use the admin password, and it was called on port 8080.

author: aksharp5
body:
## What changed

A CLI available on SkillSync's inherited PATH could still be reported as missing. Command checks loaded a login shell profile that changed PATH, while actual execution kept the original environment. This could block setup or report Codex plugin inspection as unavailable.

Availability checks now use a non-login shell, matching the environment used to execute commands.

## Why

The check used `sh -lc`; execution used `spawn` with the inherited environment. A temporary login profile reproduces both mismatches: hiding an inherited executable and advertising a profile-only executable that the process cannot run.

The integration comparison uses the production command runner and plugin inspector with a harmless Codex fixture returning one enabled `demo@test` plugin. Baseline: `5f54eaf`.

| Same temporary environment | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct Codex fixture execution | Returns one plugin | Same |
| Check an inherited executable | Missing | Available |
| Check a login-profile-only executable | Available despite direct ENOENT | Missing |
| Plugin inspection | `Codex CLI is not installed` | Available; reports `demo@test` |

Closes #176.

## Safety and compatibility

- Existing vault migration: none; config, assignment, registry, and report formats are unchanged.
- Local-file behavior: no target or instruction-path change. Tool detection follows the running process's PATH.
- Destructive behavior: no new installation, removal, or replacement behavior.
- Cross-device behavior: each device checks its own execution environment. Plugin installation and provider policies remain unchanged.

## Validation

- [x] Both new regressions fail on baseline and pass after the correction.
- [x] All 35 focused command, Git, and plugin tests pass, including missing tools and successful direct execution.
- [x] Matched standalone plugin-inspection runs reproduce the failure and correction.
- [x] `npm test -- --test-concurrency=4`: 408 passed, zero skips on `aa54297`, after integrating latest main from #175.
- [x] `npm pack --dry-run`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] All six Node 20/22/24 Linux/macOS checks passed on `aa54297`, using locked dependencies. [CI run](https://github.com/AksharP5/skillsync/actions/runs/40551906238)

Local checks use Linux, Node 24.22.1, disposable homes, login profiles, and command fixtures. No real shell configuration, service, vault, or plugin is changed. Full-suite tests temporarily reuse prompts 7.10.1 rather than declared `^8.5.2` and locked 8.7.0; no packages were installed. CI uses locked dependencies. The standalone comparison invokes the production core functions without replacing their command boundaries.

## Resumo
- `scripts/interacoes-fonte.py` → `data/interacoes.json`: base passa de 101 para 123 fármacos e de 114 para 204 regras.
  - **19 antirretrovirais**: dolutegravir, raltegravir, bictegravir, tenofovir (TDF), tenofovir alafenamida (TAF), lamivudina, entricitabina, zidovudina, abacavir, efavirenz, nevirapina, etravirina, rilpivirina, doravirina, atazanavir, darunavir, lopinavir, ritonavir e cobicistate.
  - Também entram budesonida e fluticasona inalatórias e metadona, que interagem com antirretrovirais.
  - **90 regras novas** com fármacos da APS: estatinas, anticoagulantes, anticonvulsivantes indutores, rifampicina, IBP, antiácidos, cálcio e ferro, contraceptivos, corticoides inalatórios, quetiapina, sildenafila, colchicina, benzodiazepínicos, metformina, AINEs com TDF, entre outros.
- Classes novas: inibidor de integrase (quelação por cátions) e inibidor de protease potencializado (atazanavir, darunavir e lopinavir considerados com ritonavir ou cobicistate). Efavirenz, lopinavir e metadona entram na classe "prolonga QT".
- `interacoes-medicamentosas.html`:
  - Link para o **HIV Drug Interactions (Universidade de Liverpool)** no aviso inicial e na legenda.
  - Quando a lista tem um antirretroviral, aparece um aviso para conferir lá também.
  - Subtítulo e cartão da página inicial passam a citar os antirretrovirais; o SEO e o sitemap foram regenerados (a página de ferro ganhou o bloco de SEO que faltava).

## REMUME Blumenau (2º commit)
- Conferidos os 194 itens da REMUME de Blumenau (atualizada em 30/07/2026): a base passa a **185 fármacos e 276 regras**.
- **62 fármacos novos**, entre eles: aminofilina, salbutamol, adrenalina, dipirona, paracetamol, nifedipino, metildopa, doxazosina, timolol colírio, levodopa (com benserazida ou carbidopa), clorpromazina, levomepromazina, flufenazina, clomipramina, imipramina, biperideno, bromazepam, metilfenidato, dexametasona, hidrocortisona, prednisolona, anti-histamínicos, antibióticos (amoxicilina, penicilinas, cefalexina, ceftriaxona, doxiciclina, gentamicina, nitrofurantoína, norfloxacino, sulfadiazina, espiramicina), pirimetamina, ácido fólico e folínico, alendronato, albendazol, oseltamivir, hormônios (pílula de emergência, minipílula, injetáveis mensal e trimestral, estrogênios conjugados), propiltiouracila, miconazol tópico e guaco.
- **74 regras novas** (ex.: aminofilina + ciprofloxacino, salbutamol + betabloqueador não seletivo, miconazol creme + varfarina, levonorgestrel de emergência + indutores, antipsicóticos + levodopa, gentamicina + furosemida, nifedipino + rifampicina, dipirona + AAS, paracetamol + varfarina, anticolinérgicos somados).
- Novas classes: antipsicótico, anticolinérgico, anti-histamínico sedativo, betabloqueador não seletivo, penicilina. As regras específicas de haloperidol e risperidona com metoclopramida viraram uma regra de classe.
- **Busca por sinônimos** (ex.: "ácido valproico", "carbonato de lítio", "bactrim", "benzetacil", "levonorgestrel + etinilestradiol").
- Itens da REMUME sem entrada (sem interação sistêmica relevante): água destilada, glicose 50%, sais de reidratação oral, solução fisiológica nasal, vaselina e permanganato de potássio. Lidocaína, nistatina, óleo mineral, permetrina, tobramicina colírio e polimixina otológica entraram na busca, sem regras.

## Pontos para revisão
- Conferi nas bulas da FDA (DailyMed) as regras do Tivicay (dolutegravir), do Norvir (ritonavir) e do Prezista (darunavir). As demais (Reyataz, Sustiva, Viramune, Intelence, Edurant, Pifeltro, Isentress, Biktarvy, Viread, Descovy) vêm do conhecimento das bulas, sem conferência linha a linha nesta sessão. **Recomendo revisão por infectologista ou farmacêutico.**
- As interações entre os antirretrovirais do mesmo esquema não estão completas (só dolutegravir + efavirenz).
- Efavirenz + rifampicina: a bula americana sugere 800 mg se peso ≥ 50 kg; a conduta remete ao serviço especializado.

author: qarlus
body:
### What Changed

Foundation stage of the approved UI redesign ([BUILD-PLAN.md](../blob/docs/ui-redesign/docs/design/ui-redesign/BUILD-PLAN.md), stage 1). Token layer and every `@obiter/ui` primitive now match `docs/design/ui-redesign/final/obiter.css`. The shell, the screens, auth and the Redact/Verify views are untouched; they will look partly old until their stages land.

- **Tokens** (`packages/ui/src/tokens.css`): light is `:root`, dark is `[data-theme="dark"]`; warm light surfaces, restrained steel-blue brand, near-white paper, charcoal inset (`#20242a`) around paper in dark. Six text levels (28/600 · 18/600 · 14/500 · 14/400 · 13/400 · 12/400) with line-height and tracking, the 0/4/8/12/16/24/32/40/48/56 spacing scale, row (52px) and control (28/32/40px) heights, serif for paper and the auth panel only, status tints and hover washes. Exposed through `tailwind.css` `@theme inline` as `text-page` … `text-caption`, `h-control`, `h-row`, `bg-fill`, `bg-hover`, `bg-paper`, `font-serif`, etc.
- **Primitives restyled** (Base UI behaviour unchanged): `Button` 28/32/40px with a Phosphor spinner and `aria-busy`; `Input`/`Select` 32px at 13px with hairline borders; `Dialog` 24px padding, 18/600 title, `DialogFooter` button row; 52px `Table`/`ListRow` rows at 16px vertical padding; `Tabs` as the 28px segmented control; `Badge` as quiet tints at 12px; `Tooltip`, `Toast` (tone dot instead of the old colour bar), `ProgressBar` (4px track, a narrow pulsing indicator when indeterminate), static `Skeleton` (no animation that survives a failed load), `EmptyState` (36px icon tile, prose measure) and `Popover`.
- **New primitives**, only where two or more final screens need them: `ListRow`, `StatusDot` (status word plus decorative dot, never colour alone), `KeyboardHint` (hidden inside a disabled control) and `SidePanel`, built on Base UI Dialog so focus trap, Escape and focus return are Base UI's.
- **Brand mark** is now the approved "ob" monogram from `final/icons.svg#i-obiter`, replacing the old comma mark in `packages/ui/src/brand/obiter-mark.svg`. App-shell's `Wordmark` is untouched (stage 2 replaces it).
- **Deleted**: `Card` (exported, unused in every package), the old gradient-shimmer `Skeleton`, the hand-rolled button spinner, the `--obiter-active` token I added then found unused, and the "night IDE" comments and values. `cn()` now registers the semantic type scale with tailwind-merge.

### Why

The mock-ups are the reference and the primitives are the only place a design change is paid for once. Until the token and primitive layer matches `final/obiter.css`, every later stage would restyle by exception. Doing it first also means stages 2–9 branch from a stable base and the contract never describes something the code does not do.

### Implementation Notes

- **Theme default.** Flipping the product to light is *not* a one-line change: it needs both document roots (`apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx`, `apps/desktop/src/renderer/index.html`), `readInitialTheme`, `readThemeAttribute` and the auth `useForceNightTheme`. Per the stage brief, that stays in stage 2; the contract records it. With dark still seeded, this PR is visually a retune, not a theme flip.
- **Token names are frozen.** Values were retuned in place; new names were added only where the design needs them (`--obiter-inset`, `--obiter-fill`, `--obiter-fill-hover`, `--obiter-paper*`, `--obiter-hover`, `--obiter-brand-{hover,soft}`, `--obiter-status-*-soft`, `--obiter-text-*`, `--obiter-space-*`, `--obiter-row-height`, `--obiter-control-*`, `--obiter-panel-width`, `--obiter-font-serif`). Radius keeps the frozen names: `sm` 4px, `md` 6px (controls), `lg` 10px (panels), `xl` 14px, so `rounded-md` still means a control and `rounded-lg` a panel.
- **`cn()` bug.** tailwind-merge classified `text-item`/`text-body`/… as text *colours*, so `cn('bg-brand text-brand-fg', 'text-item')` dropped `text-brand-fg` — a primary button would have rendered ink-on-brand. `packages/ui/src/lib/cn.ts` now registers the six levels as font sizes; `src/__tests__/cn.test.ts` guards it.
- **Skeleton is static.** The old shimmer ran forever, so a failed query looked like a slow one. Screens that fail must render an error, not a skeleton; the primitive no longer animates at all.
- **Desktop budget.** The first push broke `perf:desktop-budget` (JS +3,759 B, CSS +1,481 B over; the base had ~4.7 kB / ~1.7 kB of headroom). The budget was not raised: the toast uses a tone dot rather than four Phosphor icons (about 6 kB of renderer JS), floating surfaces keep `border-line` instead of `inset-ring-*`, `shadow-lg` aliases `shadow-md` because the design has one floating level, the danger button hovers with opacity rather than a `brightness` filter, and `--obiter-space-0` and two redundant type sub-properties are gone. Final: renderer initial JS 3,397,732 / 3,400,000 B, CSS 92,963 / 93,000 B — 37 bytes of CSS margin, so stage 2 should expect to trim before it adds.
- **Underline tabs** from `final/obiter.css` (`.ob-tabs`) are not built: the product's `Tabs` is the segmented control (`.ob-seg`), and the only in-product consumer, the editor ribbon, overrides the list entirely. Underline tabs arrive with the shell/editor stages if they are needed.
- **Raw theme switching quirk (pre-existing):** the theme attribute is written by `ThemeToggle`'s mount effect, so setting `data-theme` from outside without also updating `localStorage` is reverted on a shell remount. Not introduced here; stage 2 owns the hook.

### Testing

Commands, from the repo root unless stated:

```
~/.bun/bin/bun install --frozen-lockfile
bun run typecheck                       # all workspaces + script tsconfigs, 0 errors
bun run lint                            # oxlint + eslint, clean
bun run format:check                    # prettier, clean
cd packages/ui && bun run test          # 23 pass, 0 fail (7 files)
cd packages/app-shell && bun run test   # 1742 pass, 0 fail (174 files)
cd packages/redact-ui && bun run test   # 36 pass, 0 fail (6 files)
bun run build                           # all workspaces, 0 errors (run twice)
bun run perf:bundle-budget              # ok — 187.3/212, 407.4/410, 155.8/200, 286.6/320 kB gzip
bun --bun run perf:desktop-budget       # fails on the first commit, passes on HEAD
bun x knip --workspace packages/ui      # 1 finding, fixed: unused @tailwindcss/vite devDependency
```

Tests rewritten rather than deleted where they asserted old markup: `__tests__/tokens.test.ts` (light is the default block now), `__tests__/button.test.tsx` (secondary is `bg-fill`, plus `aria-busy`). New tests only where a primitive gained behaviour: `cn.test.ts` (size/colour merge), `select.test.tsx` (label + `aria-invalid` wiring), `side-panel.test.tsx` (named dialog, Escape dismisses).

Manual, in a browser against this checkout at 1440×900 and 1024×768, both themes: home, a matter, a document, search, settings, sign-in, and the Verify and Redact lists. Screens still show their old layout (uppercase eyebrows, raw `ver_…` ids, night top bar over warm paper) — that is the expected mid-stage state; every screen reads legibly in both themes. A throwaway route rendered every primitive in both themes (deleted, not committed) to check buttons, fields, tables, rows, tabs, badges, dialog, side panel, toast, tooltip, progress and skeleton. Keyboard pass: tabbing to the password field shows the 2px ring, Escape closes the dialog and the side panel and returns focus, and `KeyboardHint` compiles to `:where(:disabled) .in-disabled\:hidden`.

Not tested: the desktop renderer was built but not launched; the Redact review/finalise and editor dialogs were not opened individually (they use the same primitives); no automated visual regression suite exists.

```
