author: grgmiller
body:
### Purpose
When comparing OGE data to eGRID, we noticed that the University of Washington Power Plant (54809), which is a CHP plant in SCL, reported a lot more emissions in OGE than eGRID. This was a result of a bug in the the reported data, which influenced the Electric Allocation Factor (EAF) calculation: This unit reported zero generation for several months where it reported non-zero fuel consumption for electricity, which triggered a backstop that assigned a 100% EAF to the unit. This PR corrects this backstop behavior to handle these edge cases more consistently.

Closes DAT-1025
Part of DAT-922

### What the code is doing
**Zero or negative generation at CHP subplants**: when a subplant that reports heat in at least one month reports zero or negative generation, none of its emissions now go to electricity.
- Result: the rule only applies to CHP subplants. Applying it everywhere would have dropped about 1.21 Mt at 203 non-CHP plants, where fuel burned with no generation is usually startup or standby fuel. We define CHP per subplant rather than per plant, so a power-only unit at a cogen site isn't treated as making heat. The two definitions give the same results in 2023 and 2024.

**Missing generation**: generation was summed to subplants in a way that turned missing values into zeros.
- Fix: keep missing generation missing, so those months use the fuel split reported in EIA-923.
- Result: this causes the few increases below, e.g. Warrick (6705).

**Not fixed here**: about 21 kt of UW's remaining CO2 comes from fuel that EIA-923 allocation puts on generators outside their operating window: TG3 before it came online in November 2023, and TG2 after its 2022 retirement. That's being fixed upstream in PUDL (DAT-1045). We tried assigning 0% to missing generation at CHP subplants instead, but UW was the only place it mattered, and missing generation doesn't generally mean a unit wasn't operating. We also rejected capping fuel for electricity at a plausible heat rate, since that overrides reported data. So UW's September subplant (2 MWh of generation on 30,768 MMBtu of fuel for electricity) still gets 100%.

**Impact** (allocation factors on PUDL's allocated EIA-923 data, compared with main):

| Year | Plants changed | Electricity CO2 | Largest changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 6 | −0.035 Mt | UW (54809): 59.6 → 23.1 kt |
| 2024 | 11 | −0.051 Mt | 54041: −43.9 kt; 992: −21.9 kt; Warrick (6705): +15.4 kt |

Every changed plant is a CHP plant.

### Testing
- Added unit tests for zero, negative, positive and missing generation at CHP subplants, at a non-CHP subplant of a CHP plant, and at a non-CHP plant.
- Compared allocation factors with main on PUDL's 2023 and 2024 allocated EIA-923 data.
- Haven't rerun the full pipeline, so the CEMS path (same function, with the fuel split taken from EIA-923) hasn't been checked end to end.

### Where to look
* `emissions.calculate_electric_allocation_factor`: the order of the fill rules, the subplant-level CHP definition, and `.sum(min_count=1)`.
* The CHP methodology page: the new section on undefined cases and the two new known issues.

### LLM use description
Claude Code helped trace the allocation factor, write the change, tests and docs, run the comparisons, and draft this description.

### Usage Example/Visuals
N/A

### Review estimate
10 minutes.

### Future work
- DAT-1045: stop PUDL from allocating fuel to generators outside their operating window.
- Months with near-zero generation but all fuel reported as fuel for electricity still get 100%.
- The CHP methodology page says the CEMS allocation factor is calculated for each hour, but it's calculated for each subplant-month.

### Checklist
- [x] Update the documentation (in `docs/docs/`) to reflect changes made in this PR
- [x] Format all updated python files using `ruff`
- [x] Clear outputs from all notebooks modified
- [x] Add docstrings and type hints to any new functions created

author: quidong
body:
The REST API has no authentication, but every configuration endpoint returned the configuration including credentials, e.g. GET /v1/config or GET /v1/config/elecprice/tibber/access_token returned the token in clear text to anyone who can reach the port.

All configuration responses (GET/PUT /v1/config, GET/PUT /v1/config/{path}, reset, revert, file) now mask secret values (token, access_token, api_key, password, secret, ... and the password part of a DSN) as "***". The response schema is unchanged.

A masked value written back (EOSdash export/import, a client that writes what it read) leaves the stored secret unchanged, so round trips keep working. Real values can still be set by PUT, environment variables or the config file.

## Summary

Fixes the critical and high Dependabot alerts in the root `uv.lock`. Both packages are transitive dependencies of `meltano==4.2.0`, so the fix raises the `[tool.uv] constraint-dependencies` floors, the same pattern as #190.

- `uv>=0.13.4` (was `>=0.11.15`): lock moves 0.11.32 → 0.13.6
- `virtualenv>=21.14.9` (was `>=21.7.12`): lock moves 21.14.5 → 21.15.0
- `distlib` 0.4.0 → 0.4.4 and `packaging` 26.2 → 26.3 came along as patch bumps

| Alert | Severity | Package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#22](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-v1-sync-helper/security/dependabot/22) | Critical | `uv` (compromised emSign root in bundled CA store) |
| [#24](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-v1-sync-helper/security/dependabot/24) | High | `virtualenv` |
| [#26](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-v1-sync-helper/security/dependabot/26) | High | `virtualenv` |
| [#25](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-v1-sync-helper/security/dependabot/25), [#27](https://github.com/linuxfoundation/lfx-v1-sync-helper/security/dependabot/27) | Medium | `virtualenv` (closed by the same bump) |

The medium `Mako` alert (#21) is not part of this change.

Tracking issue: linuxfoundation/lfx-self-serve-ops#1143

## Compatibility

- `meltano` 4.2.0 requires `uv>=0.8.14` and `virtualenv>=20.26.6,<22`, so it is unchanged.
- `uv` 0.12.0 and 0.13.0 are breaking releases. None of their listed breaking changes touch how this repo uses uv: `UV_OVERRIDE` points at one file, plugins install into real venvs, and Python is pinned to 3.12.
- The `uv` binary in the Dockerfile builder image (0.9.18) is unchanged. This PR only changes the `uv` package Meltano uses to install plugins.

## Testing

Built `docker/Dockerfile.meltano` locally:

- `uv sync --locked` installs 52 packages
- `meltano install` succeeds for `tap-postgres`, `target-nats-kv`, and `tap-dynamodb` (with `UV_OVERRIDE`)
- The image reports `uv` 0.13.6, `virtualenv` 21.15.0, `meltano` 4.2.0
- `meltano invoke tap-dynamodb --about` runs

Not run: a live sync against Postgres, DynamoDB, or NATS.

author: karibhou
body:
Closes #14705

## Problem
When the relay recorded a dispatched review verdict, the reviewer head that wrote it was free and the PR could be ready for its next head or its decision kick — but nothing woke the governor loop, so the next dispatch waited for an unrelated webhook delivery or `governor.eval_interval_webhook_s`.

## Change
- `pkg/github`: `writeOneVerdict` reports whether the verdict was bound to a review dispatch (`auth.Dispatched`); only then does the relay fire a new review-verdict hook (`review_verdict_hook.go`, `atomic.Pointer` like `agentStartHook`). Advisory and refused verdicts wake nothing; a multi-perspective review fires once.
- `cmd/hive`: a dedicated `webhookWaker` (`verdictWaker`) is installed at boot and wired to the hook; the governor loop runs `tick(evalSourceCached)` on it — verdict/dispatch state is local, so the cached snapshot is the right source. Debounce is 0 (the first verdict wakes at once) and bursts coalesce to at most one wake per `governor.webhook_wake_min_gap_s`.
- Docs: `operator-reference.md` and `webhooks.md`; changelog fragment.

## Tests
`review_verdict_hook_test.go` (dispatched vs advisory/refused, single call per combined review) and `review_event_dispatch_test.go` (coalescing inside the gap, nil-waker no-op, loop wake).

Proved with `bun run ci` (34 tests), `bun run build`, generated CSS inspection, and Safari on the shared iOS 27 simulator: open the participant Drawer, enter a participant, add them, and dismiss with Cancel. Physical touch feel remains unverified.

author: fabiosm46
body:
## Sintesi

Closes #212

Una cartella leggibile senza fingerprint (per esempio `EllesmereUIForeverEssentials`, che ha solo un `.toc` `_Camelot`, suffisso che il calcolo di CurseForge non conta) non è più segnalata come "Unreadable folder".

### Modifiche
- `updates.rs`: la ricerca del progetto di una cartella è ora `MatchIndex::locate`, che restituisce `Located::{Found, NotMatched, Unreadable}`. Con un fingerprint decide solo quello, come prima. Senza fingerprint, una cartella leggibile appartiene al file abbinato (esatto o parziale, l'esatto vince) che la elenca tra i suoi `modules`, confrontando i nomi senza distinguere maiuscole e minuscole; se nessun file la elenca è `notMatched`. Solo una cartella che la scansione non ha potuto elencare resta un errore. È il punto dove #216 aggiungerà il ripiego sui record dell'app.
- `addons/scan.rs`: `InstalledAddon::is_unreadable` riconosce l'errore `Unreadable folder (<kind>).` della scansione, prodotto ora da una sola funzione (`unreadable_folder`), così il testo e il controllo non possono divergere.
- `TOC_SUFFIXES` e `addons/fingerprint.rs` non sono toccati: il fingerprint resta quello di CurseForge.

### Test
- `a_folder_without_fingerprint_joins_the_project_of_the_file_that_lists_it`: con match esatto e parziale, la cartella senza fingerprint ha lo stesso stato, progetto, file installato, cartelle del progetto e file di reinstallazione delle altre cartelle del progetto (il nome nel file differisce solo per le maiuscole).
- `a_folder_without_fingerprint_that_no_file_lists_is_not_matched`: `notMatched` senza fonte; una cartella davvero illeggibile resta `Error` anche se un file la elenca.
- `a_readable_folder_with_only_a_toc_of_its_flavor_is_never_an_error` (guardia): per ogni flavor con un tipo di versione (e controllando che ogni tipo di `VERSION_TYPES` ne abbia uno) e per ogni suffisso di `toc::toc_suffixes(flavor)`, una cartella vera sotto una cartella temporanea con solo `<Cartella>_<suffisso>.toc` non produce mai `Error`, né sconosciuta né elencata da un file abbinato; quando il fingerprint manca si attribuisce al progetto. Il test controlla anche che il caso senza fingerprint capiti davvero. Prova tutti i suffissi, non solo quelli fuori da `TOC_SUFFIXES`, perché la costante è privata di `fingerprint.rs` (fuori scope): l'insieme provato contiene quello richiesto. Nessun nome differisce solo per le maiuscole sul disco.
- I test esistenti con una cartella "illeggibile" usano ora l'errore vero della scansione.

### Dimensione per la review
- Stima prima dell'implementazione: una PR, un'area (backend), un solo meccanismo (abbinamento in `evaluate_with`) più i test; circa 15.000 caratteri.
- Diff misurato: 15476 caratteri.

### Gate eseguiti
- [x] cargo fmt --check / clippy -D warnings
- [x] cargo build --locked (frontend non toccato: niente `pnpm build`)
- [x] cargo test --locked — 477 passati
- [x] suite di automazione (`scripts/test/*.test.sh` e `test_deepseek_review.py`)
- [x] controlli di privacy su contenuto e commit

### Verifica dei criteri di accettazione
- [x] Cartella leggibile senza fingerprint elencata nei `modules` di un file abbinato (esatto o parziale): stesso progetto e stato delle altre cartelle, niente errore.
- [x] Cartella leggibile senza fingerprint che nessun file elenca: `notMatched`, niente errore.
- [x] Solo `Unreadable folder (<kind>).` della scansione resta un errore.
- [x] Il giro automatico non la segnala più: `auto_update.rs::plan` raccoglie solo gli `Error`, che per questa cartella non nascono più (file non toccato).
- [x] Test di guardia su tutti i suffissi di `toc::toc_suffixes(flavor)` per ogni flavor noto.
- Il riconoscimento dai record dell'app resta a #216.

### Fuori scope (verificato)
Non toccati: `addons/fingerprint.rs` e `TOC_SUFFIXES`, `auto_update.rs`, `tray.rs`, `src/`, le fonti in `src-tauri/src/sources/`.

## Summary
Fixes #379. Stacked on #431 (`fix/390-dark-accent-contrast`).

High-frequency `aria-live="polite"` updates were spamming screen readers:

author: cmyfqwq
body:
## Issue 批次 2（安全项）：#675 / #679 / #682 / #686（对应 open issue，各一条独立小修）

> **交接说明（2026-10-28 晚更新 base）**：本分支原由 ZCode 侧基于 `fix/issue-batch1-20261028` 拉出，当时是**堆叠 PR**（等 692 合并后由 GitHub 自动把 base 重定向到 main）。本轮对 main 做了一次合并后，两者的 merge-base 已经变成 main 本身（`git merge-base fix/issue-batch1 fix/issue-batch2` = 当前 main），堆叠关系自然解除，故 base 直接改为 `main`，本 PR 现在**独立可合并、不再依赖 #692**。

### #675 更新链补上真实性防线：安装前发布者连续性校验 + CI 密钥接缝

- `UpdateChecker.signerContinuityHolds()`：待装 APK 的签名证书必须与**当前安装**的本应用一致（fail-closed：读不出/不一致一律拒装）。`invokeInstaller()` 内强制前置（任何调用方绕不过）；`ApkUpdateAction.install()` 再先行校验并给出诚实文案（`KIND_ARTIFACT_REJECTED`），被拒产物即刻删除。
- 锚点选「已安装证书」而非硬编码指纹：repoDebug 私钥随公开仓分发，硬编码它的指纹等于没有校验（任何人可签出同证书的包）；已安装应用的证书是发行链可信的最小事实。
- `app/build.gradle.kts`：新增 CI secret 接缝（`DSH_RELEASE_KEYSTORE` / `DSH_RELEASE_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` / `DSH_RELEASE_KEY_ALIAS` / `DSH_RELEASE_KEY_PASSWORD`），真发布密钥经 CI 注入不再随仓分发；无该环境变量时**显式回落 repoDebug**（本地/PR 构建不受影响；repoDebug 签的包装上官方签名设备会被连续性校验拒装，本地构建只用于本地覆盖安装）。
- 纠正两处注释里的假承诺（「签名不匹配由系统安装器天然拒绝」在私钥公开的前提下不成立，摘要又由投递方自带）。
- 测试：`UpdateSignerContinuityTest` +7（纯判据 4：同证书通过 / 异证书拒 / 双侧读不出拒 / 多签名者集合无序比较；静态 3：invokeInstaller 先校验后拉起、状态机用 ARTIFACT_REJECTED 语义、gradle 接缝存在）。

### #679 AdbKeyboard 撤销 uid 2000 隐式信任

- `AdbKeyboardService.isTrustedUid()` 收紧为仅 root(0)：Shizuku 的核心能力就是让任意第三方应用持 uid 2000，uid 层面无法区分「真 adb 会话」与「持 shell 身份的应用」。root 保留隐式信任（能以 root 执行的调用方本已拥有设备全部权限）。
- 非 root 一律要求 nonce：引擎路径不变（本就带 `--es auth`）；经典 adb 直发改走 nonce（`adb shell` 读不到应用私有 nonce 文件，需经引擎/应用侧取得——`ime-broadcast.ts` 注释同步改口径，如实登记桌面宿主经 adb 直发的旧行为在新壳上会被拒 result=3）。
- 判据抽成纯函数 `isTrustedSenderFor(uid, givenNonce, fileSecret)` 供 JVM 单测；nonce 文件缺失/不可读对非 root 一律 fail-closed（`isTrustedSender` 负责收敛 context 读取）。
- 测试：`AdbKeyboardContractTest` 白名单断言改判（uid 2000 不再隐式可信）+ 新增 nonce 判据面（7 断言：无 nonce 拒 / secret 缺失拒 / 不匹配拒 / 匹配放行 / 引擎路径放行 / root 放行）。

### #682 MainActivity 特权 action 收口

- `ACTION_RETRY_ENGINE` 改进程内一次性标志 `pendingSelfRetry`（`@Volatile`，RepairActivity 置位、onCreate/onNewIntent 消费一次，读后即清）——exported launcher 上外部应用无法再冒充重试 intent 清掉持久修复闸门与快照刷新账本（`RepairState`「explicit user retry is the only way past the persistent gate」契约恢复完整）。进程死亡时标志随之消失，该次重试退化为普通启动（无副作用）。
- `ACTION_UPDATE` 的 adb 触发入口移除（`runUpdate` 定义保留、当前无调用点）；known-gaps 该行理由①更新为如实口径（旧「adb-only、普通用户不可达」的理由不成立：manifest 未声明并不挡显式组件 intent）。
- 文档同步：`docs/design.md`（启动树两处）、`docs/AGENTS/known-gaps.md`、`docs/AGENTS/EXECUTION-MAP.md`（K01 入口列、§6.6、runUpdate 例外说明）。
- 测试：`MainActivityPrivilegeEntryTest` +3（无特权 action 残留 / RepairActivity 是唯一置位方 / 一次性标志 @Volatile + 读后即清）；`RepairGateTest` 的一次性动作断言迁移到新机制。

### #686 androidBridge 顶层帧来源门禁

- 77 个 `@JavascriptInterface` 入口统一过 `checkTrustedFrame()` / `trusted{}`：**顶层帧必须始终是引擎 origin**（与导航闸门 `shouldOverrideUrlLoading` 同一判据 `isEngineSource`，MainActivity 接线），fail-closed（未接线 / WebView 未初始化 / 首帧前一律拒）。
- 结构性关死「顶层被劫持出引擎 origin」形态（子帧 top-navigation、外部跳转落回本 WebView）。**如实登记残余缺口**：引擎 origin 顶层之下的跨源子帧本门禁无法按帧区分（Android 桥机制在 Java 侧取不到调用方 frame），彻底关法是 token 握手（JS 契约变更、跨仓协调），登记为后续项，不在本批范围。
- `docs/design.md` 桥注解计数漂移一并修正（71/70 → 77/76，实测）。
- 测试：`AndroidBridgeFrameGuardTest` +4（核心是反射 sweep：默认构造（门禁恒拒）下逐个调用全部 @JavascriptInterface 入口，任何漏网入口判红；另有动态判据翻转、放行路径、未接线全拒）。4 个钉旧签名形状的契约测试（DevActionsBatch9 / W3ShellContract / BrowserHostCommandWiring / RepairGate）迁移到新形状——委托链断言语义不变，只多了门禁包裹。

### 验证

- 全量单测：**1913 例全绿**（基线 1898 → 1913，`scripts/kotlin-test-baseline.json` 已升档，只升未降，SKIP=0）。
- 门禁链：`./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest -x lint` → `check-kotlin-comments` PASS（无嵌套块注释）/ `check-code-map` PASS（锚点有效、编号一致）/ `check-kotlin-test-count` PASS（逐类不低于基线 + 无缺席 + 结果新鲜 + 无失败用例）。
- **未做设备验证**（NAS 侧无模拟器/真机）：本批全部为 L2 安全敏感面（签名 / 授权面 / 导出组件 / 桥协议），按 AGENTS.md 铁律 2，发版候选前必须补三层验收；本 PR 证据止于代码层 + 静态门禁，不冒充设备结论。
- CI 期望：pr-gate 三项（Kotlin 编译门禁 / 冲突标记与敏感信息扫描 / 维护文档一致性）应全绿。

### 剩余台账（批次 3 起，按 PR 692 优先级）

- 功能坏死：#668 / #674 / #683 / #684
- 资源/UX：#687 / #690 / #688 / #670 / #689
- 门禁：#677 / #678 / #662
- 低：#676（更新包落公共可写目录——本批只保证被拒产物即刻删除，目录迁移仍待 #676 自己收口）/ #658
- 另：#672 由 PC 侧 I-9A 分支（BrowserHost 截图有界保留）覆盖，本批未重复修；PR #691 未触碰。


## base 变更说明（2026-10-28 晚）

- **变更**：`base` 从 `fix/issue-batch1-20261028` 改为 **`main`**；`changed_files` 由 74 → **30**，`commits` 由 15 → 4。
- **为什么现在可以独立**：本轮把 main 合并进来后，`git merge-base(batch1, batch2)` 已等于当前 main ⇒ 堆叠关系消失，再挂 base 到批次 1 只会让 diff 变"反向改动"。改 base 后本 PR 不依赖任何其它未合并 PR。
- **与 #692 有 8 个文件重叠**（`EngineManager.kt` / `GlobalActionCatalog.kt` / `LogCollector.kt` / `SnapshotExtractor.kt` / `VdisplayController.kt` / `BootFailLogTest.kt` / `GlobalActionCatalogTest.kt` / `kotlin-test-baseline.json`）：这是本分支从批次 1 分叉的历史原因，**两边内容一致、合并不会冲突**。若 #692 先合，这 8 个在本 PR 里会自动变成无差异，只剩 22 个自有文件。
- **基线**：合并 main 后实测 180 个测试类 / **1926 例**，`--update-baseline` 升档（逐类合计也是 1926）。

> **注意（合并顺序）**：#692 与 #696 都改 `scripts/kotlin-test-baseline.json`。两个都合之后若基线数字落后于实际，属正常——门禁只判"不低于基线"，下一次改动会再升档。

## O que muda

No iPad deitado (1024 e 1080px de largura), o destaque da capa mostrava o texto à esquerda e o lado direito vazio. As telas do sistema caíam para baixo do texto, porque as duas colunas só começavam em 1101px.

Entre 1000 e 1100px, o texto e as telas agora dividem a largura, como no notebook. As medidas foram ajustadas para caber na metade da tela:
- título em 38px;
- os seis módulos em uma coluna;
- os dois botões lado a lado;
- celular de 128px no vão entre as colunas.

O atributo `sizes` das imagens também acompanha, para o tablet não baixar a imagem na largura da tela inteira.

## Como foi conferido

- Capturas em 768, 820, 999, 1000, 1024 (deitado e em pé), 1080, 1112, 1180, 1366 e 1440px.
- Abaixo de 1000px e a partir de 1101px nada mudou.
- Nenhuma largura com rolagem lateral.
- 1641 testes passando, `tsc` e `next build` sem erro.

author: suiso11
body:
## 背景

記憶抽出の `user_fact` は #142 で evidence クォートの grounding を導入済みですが、クォートが本物でも BODY がユーザーの発話に無い内容（モデル側の補足・推測）で構成され得ます。本 PR は #166 (`fix/learning-speaker-grounding`) の上に積む **stacked PR** です（base: `fix/learning-speaker-grounding`）。

初版の body coverage 判定は「ユーザー発話との表層一致 0.6 以上」を要求していたため、口語から丁寧語への言い換えのような忠実な paraphrase まで downgrade していました。本更新では判定対象を **assistant だけが導入した内容語** に切り替えます。

## 変更

- `apps/server/src/extraction_grounding.ts`
  - NFKC/小文字化/空白・句読点除去に加え、katakana→hiragana の安価な folding を行う。
  - framing（`ユーザーは`, `と考えている`, `している`, `における`, `として` 等）と generic な動詞・機能語を除去してから比較する。
  - body に「ユーザー発話に無く、assistant 発話にはある」内容語（日本語 4 文字以上 / ASCII 5 文字以上）があれば downgrade。ただし候補語の bigram の半分以上がユーザー発話に既出なら paraphrase とみなして許容する。
  - coverage floor は **0.12** まで緩和し、ほぼ重なりゼロ（挨拶ターンが無関係な事実 body を生成する等）だけを拾う。
  - **downgrade のみ**（memory: `model_inference`、learning: `observation`）。項目は削除しない。
- memory / learning の双方で同じ body チェックを使用。
- 固定 diagnostic counts `downgraded_by_coverage` / `downgraded_by_assistant_terms` は変更なし。内容はログしません。
- `docs/operations.md` の body grounding 記述を新方式に更新。

## 本番監査データでの判定精度（集計のみ）

対象: `/tmp/opencode/memory-audit.md` に列挙された 87 行（LIKELY 67 + UNCLEAR 20。OK 33 行はファイルに列挙なし）。positive = `/tmp/opencode/memory-fix-result.md` の 27 ID、それ以外の列挙行を negative としました。

| setting | TP | FN | FP | TN | recall | FP rate (of 93) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 初版: coverage<0.6 + AT(3/4) | 27 | 0 | 54 | 5 | 100.0% | 58.1% |
| coverage-only <0.12 | 22 | 5 | 6 | 54 | 81.5% | 6.5% |
| assistant-only terms のみ | 12 | 15 | 4 | 56 | 44.4% | 4.3% |
| **採用: terms + floor 0.12** | **25** | **2** | **10** | **50** | **92.6%** | **10.8%** |

- 採用設定の FP は列挙された 60 negative に対して 16.7%（10/60）で、93 分母でも 10.8%。93 分母は列挙されていない OK 33 行を TN と仮定した値です。
- coverage-only は paraphrase を保てますが assistant-only の補足を取り逃します。terms-only は precision が高い一方、ほぼ重なりゼロの body や候補語が assistant excerpt に現れないケースを取り逃します。併用が recall 目標を満たしつつ false-downgrade を低く抑えます。
- paraphrase（口語→丁寧語）は `user_fact` のまま、assistant だけが導入した技術名は downgrade、挨拶ターン＋無関係な事実 body は coverage floor で downgrade、という合成テストを追加/更新。

## 検証

- `pnpm typecheck`: 0 errors（svelte-check の既存 warning のみ）
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0（既存 warning/info のみ）
- `pnpm vitest run apps/server/test/memory_service.test.ts apps/server/test/learning_service.test.ts packages/kernel/test/conversation_learning.test.ts`: 81 passed
- 追加テストは合成テキストのみ（本番監査の文面は不使用）

author: eyalamirmusic
body:
## Problem

An iOS app built by `makeasound_add_plugin` always rotated with the device and always installed on both iPhone and iPad. `_makeasound_ios_bundle` hard-coded `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY "1,2"` (Xcode) or `UIDeviceFamily [1,2]` (Ninja), the AUv3's plist did the same, and nothing wrote `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations`. So an app that is meant to be, say, iPad-only and landscape-only could not say so.

## Change

Two new arguments. Both are ignored when not building for iOS:

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `ORIENTATION portrait\|landscape` | Locks the app to one orientation by writing `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations`. `landscape` allows both landscape directions. The values and their meaning match `eacp_add_app`'s. If unset, nothing is written and the app rotates with the device, as before. |
| `DEVICE_FAMILY iphone\|ipad...` | Names the devices the app and its AUv3 install on, under both generators: Xcode's `TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY`, and the Ninja `UIDeviceFamily` in the app's and the extension's plists. The default is both, as before. |

`_makeasound_ios_shape` resolves and validates both on every platform, so a typo also fails a macOS configure. It needs no target. Without either argument, the plists and the Xcode attributes are byte-identical to before.

The header comment in `CMake/MakeASoundPlugin.cmake` documents both arguments. It also notes that iPad multitasking needs every orientation, so an iPad app that sets `ORIENTATION` must also add `UIRequiresFullScreen` itself (through `eacp_add_plist_entries`).

## Testing

- New script-mode tests, so they run on every platform:

author: runekingtony
body:
## Summary

- A wallet spend now locks its children's `student` rows after the wallet row and before it reads what each child owes. A payment, adjustment or void posting for the same child at that moment finishes first, so the spend is checked against the true balance instead of over-paying the child. One change covers the manual spend and auto-pay (D-422).
- A staff payment (`writePayment`, also used by store sales) locks the children it allocates to, in id order, before it posts. Without it a multi-child payment takes the rows in allocation order while a spend takes them in id order, and Postgres can deadlock (40P01).
- Staff wallet reads no longer run the oldest-unpaid query. Only the guardian's own wallet (`GET /portal/wallet`) orders children by it; staff reads answer `oldestUnpaidOn: null`, which the contract already allows (D-420).

Two review findings left from EDU-306 (#325); the other findings have merged since.

## Changes

- api: `wallet-spend.ts` calls `lockStudents` after `lockWallet`; `write-payment.ts` calls it before it posts. `kysely-wallet-read.repository.ts` takes `{ scope, withOldestUnpaid }` in `viewOf`; `findWallet` passes `false`, `findOwnWallet` passes `true`, and the fake repository follows.
- api tests: a held lock on the child plus a committed posting that clears the debt makes the spend answer 422, and it answers 201 (over-pay) without the lock. A payment allocating `[higher, lower]` must not hold the higher child while it waits (probed with `FOR UPDATE NOWAIT`), and fails without its lock. Two concurrent store sales to one student still both record. Staff answer `null` and the portal answers a date. The lock-wait polls share `test/support/lock-wait.ts`.
- docs: D-420 and D-422 in `docs/technical-reference.md`; PRD 59 API note and rule 8.

Lock order is wallet, then children by id, the same as the credit migration (D-416). No path locks a student and then the wallet, and concurrent store sales are already serialised by the sale-number counter. No schema change, so no drift.

## Verification

- [x] `pnpm validate:quick`
- [x] `nx run api:test-integration` on the wallet, payment, void, store-sale, gateway and adjustment specs touched by this change (11 files). The full five-shard run was done on the first commit only, not repeated after the second.
- [ ] `pnpm drift` (not needed: no schema or Better Auth change)

## Not verified

- The Monnify sandbox top-up, the account number with its copy button, Trace, and auto-pay on a Monnify credit in a browser. The local stack has no sandbox credentials, and EDU-306 left this unexercised.
- The browser e2e (`eduvault-e2e`): staff wallet view in web-admin and the guardian's pay table order in web-portal were not driven in a browser. The API tests cover the data they read.
- A real wallet spend racing a real multi-child payment. That interleaving can't be made deterministic; the probe test covers the mechanism.

Refs #327

author: alexberardi
body:
A collaborator's Go Pi showed a Voice card that never loaded, so he couldn't raise wake sensitivity on a node that kept waking falsely. We couldn't tell why from his report: the card shows the same endless spinner for every state except loaded.

**Card states** (Voice and Maintenance, through a shared `SnapshotStatus`):
- **Timed out / error:** the hook's reason (e.g. "Node did not respond in time. Is it online?", "Failed to decrypt settings: …"), plus **Try again**.
- **No key on either side:** **Set up encryption key** (the hook's existing `provisionKey`).
- **Loaded but no settings:** "This node doesn't report voice settings."
- **Loading:** the spinner, as before.

**Automatic wake sensitivity.** With `wake_word_threshold_auto` on, the node calibrates the threshold from recent wakes, **capped at 0.50**, and ignores the slider. Raising the slider did nothing, which looked like a broken slider while the false wakes went on.
- The card shows the switch for a node that reports the key (the Go node). While it's on, the slider is disabled and reads "Automatic".
- A node that doesn't report the key (the Python node) gets no switch, and the key is never sent, so a save can't turn off an automatic mode someone set by hand.

**Verification:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. `npm test -- --ci`: 166 suites, 1,848 passed. New `__tests__/components/NodeVoiceSettings.test.tsx` covers each state's message and action, the switch overriding the slider and saving `false`, and a node without the key.

Touches no files on the hold list. It ships to TestFlight/Play on merge.

body:
Implements #727 (epic #723, Auto-moderation v1). The evidence bundle the harness reads — **pure gathering, no sanctions** (contract).

## Always included
- **Rules text** (specific error if cleared since intake), **referral block** from the `automod_cases` row (referrer, note, message link, named user), and full **warnings + staff notes for the explicitly referred user only** — named target, else the anchor message's author.
- **Message referral:** anchor + bounded surround using Gork's `read_discord` caps imported by value (**40 before / 10 after**), re-enforced collector-side so an over-delivering producer can't bloat the prompt; anchor channel must be referrer-viewable (re-checked).
- **User-only referral:** that user's recent messages in **referrer-viewable channels only** (decision-46 asker parity), bounded by explicit caps (≤15 channels fetched × ≤25/fetch, ≤100 collected, newest-first) with honest `channels_skipped_not_visible` / `truncated` counts. Open-ticket blackout carried over. Never a whole-server scan.

## Participants vs subjects (contract)
Window authors are **context, not subjects** — `participant_user_ids` ∥ `subject_user_ids`; the card (#730) renders 'seen and not considered'. The collector **never** calls `createStaffNote`/`createWarning` (pinned by row-count tests + no mutators imported).

## Lookup tools (decision 5)
`read_warnings(user)` / `read_staff_notes(user)` — read-only, **no mode flag**, guild-isolated (no member row → specific refusal). #728 wires them as model tools.

## Privacy
Notes + warning history stay in harness/staff-channel scope; module docblock + docs state #735 must scrub ticket text.

## Evidence
- Full `npm test`: **6254** / 0 fail · `docs:build` zero dead links
- 46 new tests (window caps exact, invisible-channel arms, user-scan caps, subject-only preload, bystander zero-preload, deleted-anchor / rules-cleared specific errors, lookup guild-isolation + no-gate, zero-write fuzz on throwing deps)
- Internal service — no commands/settings/env/migration; Fluxer no-parity restated in docs (decision 8)

Closes #727

author: dodulana-tech
body:
## Summary

Production admins could sign in and see nothing, and the only admin couldn't add the team. This fixes every cause found, plus a build failure that has likely kept prod on a pre-June deploy.

### Build fix (deploy blocker)
- `/partner/wallet/history` used `useSearchParams` without a Suspense boundary, so `next build` failed during prerender. This came in with #1, so `main` has not built since. Render keeps the last good deploy live when a build fails.

### Admin access
- **Live permissions.** Admin role and permissions are re-read from the DB on each request (30s in-memory cache) instead of being frozen in the 30-day JWT. Role changes apply without re-login; removal still revokes immediately.
- **Allow-list bootstrap.** `ADMIN_PHONES` / `ADMIN_EMAILS` users were created with no role (no permissions), and pre-existing accounts were never upgraded. They now get `ADMIN` + `ADMIN_DEFAULT_ROLE` (default `super-admin`) on login and on every deploy via `sync:roles`. An already-assigned role is never overwritten. Logic lives in `src/lib/admin-bootstrap.ts` (no Next imports, so the script can use it).
- **`/admin/login` reachable.** It wasn't public and was nested under the admin layout, so it always redirected to the customer `/auth`. Moved to `(admin-auth)`, made public, and middleware, the layout, the wallet pages and the invite email all point there, with `?redirect=` honoured (limited to `/admin`).
- **No-role screen.** A role-less admin sees "No role assigned yet" instead of an empty dashboard.
- **Apprenticeship permissions.** `apprenticeships.view` / `.manage` were missing from the permission catalogue (only `seed.ts` had them), so no prod role could grant them. Added to the catalogue, the Team UI groups, and Ops Manager and Pro Manager.
- **Email OTP failures surface.** A failed SMTP send now returns 502 with a hint to use phone, instead of reporting success.
- **WhatsApp invites.** Team invites now notify the invitee on WhatsApp; email was optional.
- **DEV BYPASS removed.** Local permission checks now match production.

## Deploy notes
- Optional env: `ADMIN_DEFAULT_ROLE` (role slug, default `super-admin`).
- `sync:roles` will log any allow-listed admins it fixes, and warn about any remaining role-less admins.
- Expect a small `src/middleware.ts` conflict with the uncommitted public-path work on `main`.

## Test plan
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run build` passes (it fails on `main`)
- [x] `npm run smoke:admin`: all admin pages and GET APIs return 2xx
- [x] 21-step scenario run against a local server, all passing:
  - signed-out redirects to `/admin/login`, including deep links
  - a customer session is sent to `/admin/login`
  - a role-less admin sees the notice and gets 403 from the API
  - Ops Manager sidebar and API scoping
  - a live role change applies on the existing cookie
  - an allow-listed pre-existing customer is upgraded to Super Admin on OTP login
  - a non-admin email is refused
  - a removed admin's cookie is refused
- [ ] After deploy: existing admin signs in and sees Team; invite one team member end to end

author: mrlogic85
body:
## What & why

Build kept a selection as 13 per-kind sets, which `PartSet` took as 13 positional arguments and `BuildViewModel.Selection` repeated for count, singleton, clear, prune, replace, notifications and box selection. A selection is now one set of `CreatureElementSelection` values, so a new part kind needs no new selection field.

Closes #1324

## Scope

- `PartSet`: one set of parts, built from any sequence. `Count`, `Parts` (kind by kind, then id), `Contains`, `IdsOf(kind)` and `SetEquals`.
- `BuildViewModel.Selection`: one `_selected` set. Toggle, joint-stack stepping, clear, replace, prune and undo reselection each have one path. The undo swap of a joint for its parts takes the top of `JointPartsAt`, which is the same order as before.
- Public API, App-internal: the 13 `Selected<Kind>Count` and 13 `SingleSelected<Kind>Id` properties are replaced by `SingleSelected`, `SingleSelectedId(kind)` and `IsSelected(kind, id)`. Selection changes now notify `SelectedNodeCount`, `SelectedPartCount` and `SingleSelected`. `BuildPresentationViewModel.SelectedBeamCount` had no caller and is removed.
- Box selection collects parts through `LinkRef.All` and `JointParts` instead of one line per kind.
- Copy, Delete, Placement and Restore read the one set. Their per-kind logic is left for #1325.
- Godot: `CreatureParts`, `BuildCanvas` and `BuildServoDrawing` swap each typed lookup one for one, and the selected hinge part is found through `HingeParts`.
- Tests: `PartSetTests` and `BuildSelectionTests`, over `EveryPartPinTests.Creature()`, which is now public. The existing tests move onto the new API.

## How to verify

- Automated: `dotnet test NodeRunner.slnx` passes, 1,936 tests. `dotnet build NodeRunner.slnx -warnaserror` and `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` are clean. Save pins, the share code and the network layout are unchanged.
- Manual testing: not yet done. The issue planned none, but the diff also touches three Godot drawing files. `design-lead` built and opened Build on the desktop (1600x720, clean log). Its Screenshot tool cannot select anything, so these are left to a person with `godot --path project`, on a creation with stacked joints, a hinge part, a Piston and a Spring:
  - the halo on a selected part;
  - tapping a stacked joint (Servo over Touch sensor, Brake over Wheel);
  - the Select box preview;
  - the preview while a sensor moves;
  - the Fixed and Target bands;
  - the Piston and Spring travel marks.

## Notes for the reviewer

Auto-merge is **off**. `design-lead` reported insufficient evidence, which blocks this UI-touching PR until the check above is done or a human waiver is recorded here (`docs/REVIEW.md` → "Definition of Done").

- **concurrency-reviewer:** No findings.
- **errors-reviewer:** No findings.
- **docs-reviewer:** Minor, the `SelectedPartIds` comment restated the code: fixed, it now says why the ids are mixed across kinds. Simple.
- **performance-reviewer:** Minor, `Selection` copies, `IdsOf` and `Parts` allocate on redraws, and `LinkDrawnFrom` copied the selection per joint. Partly dismissed: the old `Selection` copied all 13 sets on every read too. Fixed the new copies: `LinkDrawnFrom` and `DrawSelectedTravels` call a public `IsSelected(kind, id)` instead. Simple (same behaviour).
- **structure-reviewer:** Minor, `PartSet.Single` was used only by tests and repeated `SingleSelected`'s rule: fixed, removed. Simple.
- **tests-reviewer:** First run: No findings, but it finished in seconds, so it ran again with the new test files and acceptance criteria named. Second run:
  - Minor, notifications checked only after the first toggle and the clear: fixed, every step asserts the three names, and clearing nothing raises none. Simple.
  - Minor, `ToggleSelected` on a missing part was untested: fixed with a `Should.Throw` row. Simple.
  - Minor, `IdsOf` asserted again in the Build test and two overlapping `Contains` checks: fixed, removed and merged. Simple.
- **design-lead:** No findings, but insufficient evidence. On desktop (1600x720, phone not used) Build opens and the log is clean, but the Screenshot tool cannot select, so halos, stacked-joint taps, the Select box and sensor-move previews, Fixed/Target bands and travel marks are left to the human. The Godot edits swap each typed lookup one for one.

author: danieljhkim
body: ## Task ORB-19183 — App: a "Set up your Library" card on Today when the workspace has no Library yet ### Description ## Why When the app runs against a workspace whose Library is not scaffolded, every screen fails or shows nothing. That happens after a partial install, or when someone points the app at a new folder. For office workers, setting up should be one click, not a terminal command. SWEs keep `office init` (ORB-19181). ## What - **Server:** a setup feature in the app server. - `GET /api/setup` reports whether the Library is scaffolded, from `office.status`, which already reports Library health. - `POST /api/setup` runs `office.init` with `--full` semantics through the Orbit client, acting as the user. It returns `created` and `already_initialized`, and maps office error codes to plain words. - A plugin that is not enabled in the workspace, or a workspace that is not registered, is reported as such, with the `office init` command as the fix. The app cannot enable plugins or register workspaces itself. - **Today:** when the Library is missing, a top "Set up your Library" card replaces Needs you. - It explains in one sentence what will be created, with a primary "Set up" button and progress. - On success, Today loads normally and the rail counts refresh. - On failure, it shows the plain-words reason and the fix. It never retries `office.init` on its own. - **Other screens:** they show a short "Your Library isn't set up yet" state that links to Today, instead of a generic failure. - The card follows the app's dark theme and patterns: a card with a kicker, and the primary action. ## Docs first Update `docs/design/office/specs/web-app.md` (Today and the screen list), `specs/plugin-surface.md` and `specs/library.md`, where they say `office.init` is called only by the install script. The app, acting as the user, becomes a second caller. Then build to it. ### Acceptance Criteria - `web-app.md`, `plugin-surface.md` and `library.md` name the app as a caller of `office.init` and describe the setup card, its states and `/api/setup`. - Against a workspace whose Library is missing, Today shows the "Set up your Library" card; pressing Set up calls `office.init` once, and on success Today renders its normal sections without a reload. - A second press, or a Library that already exists, is handled as already initialized and never as an error. - An `office.init` failure shows the plain-words reason and fix; no automatic retry happens; a plugin-not-enabled or unregistered-workspace state shows the `office init` command instead of a Set up button. - Other screens show the not-set-up state linking to Today instead of a generic failure when the Library is missing. - A browser suite (fixture Orbit client, like the existing `*.browser.mjs`) covers missing → set up → normal Today, already initialized, and failure, at 1440px and 375px, with no horizontal overflow. ## Screenshots | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | setup, error, 1440 | — | | | setup, library, 1440 | — | | | setup, error, 375 | — | | | setup, library, 375 | — | | ## Validation - Not reported ## Branch Freshness - Base ref: `origin/main` - Head ref: `orbit/ORB-19183-a299bb5d` - Behind base: 0 - Ahead of base: 1

author: danieldarrenjones
body:
Step 5 of the suspicious activity and blocking spec, core part. **Stacked on [Porrodev/php-core#6](https://github.com/Porrodev/php-core/pull/6)**: merge that first, and this retargets to `main`.

**`Porro\Core\Activity\Cloudflare`** uses one account IP List, `porro_blocklist`, plus one custom rule on the site's zone: `ip.src in $porro_blocklist`, action `block`.

- **`connect($host)`**
  - Finds the zone serving the host, walking up from `www.shop.example.co.uk` to `example.co.uk`.
  - Finds or creates the list.
  - Adds the rule **next to the zone's existing custom rules** with `POST …/rulesets/{id}/rules`. It never sends `PUT` to the phase entrypoint, which would delete the client's own rules.
  - When the zone has no custom rules yet, it creates the phase ruleset with just ours.
  - Idempotent: running it again changes nothing.
- **`sync($connection, $siteId, $entries)`**
  - Adds and removes only items whose comment starts `porro:{site}:`, because the list is shared by every site on the account.
  - Never uses the replace-all `PUT items`.
  - Reads every page of items and polls bulk operations until they complete or fail.
  - Handles open question 2 from the spec: Cloudflare keeps one item per IP, and adding it again replaces the comment. So an IP another site already added is left alone and counted as `shared`, because it's blocked either way. If that site removes it, the next sync here adds it back.
- **`disconnect()`** removes this site's items and rule, and the list once nothing else is in it.
- **Errors** become messages that say what to check: token permissions, a missing zone, or the Free plan's one-list limit.

**Checked against Cloudflare's docs:** list items accept IPv4 /8–/32 and IPv6 single addresses or /12–/128, so our /16 and /48 limits fit. Adding the same IP again replaces its comment. Item adds and deletes return an `operation_id` to poll.

**Not checked against a real Cloudflare account**, because I don't have a token. Tests run against an in-memory fake of the API: zones, paged list items, rulesets, bulk operations. The fake refuses `PUT` on list items and records every call, so the tests prove we never send one. Worth one real run on a test zone before release.

**Tests:** 12 new in `tests/CloudflareTest.php`; 220 pass, Pint clean.

body:
Adds a `.coderabbit.yaml` so CodeRabbit reviews to this project's standards instead of its defaults.

On pull requests, CodeRabbit approves or requests changes, but its approval stays advisory. It never approves changes to workflows, the Action, the manifest and lockfile, build config or scripts. A blocking check fails any PR that adds a runtime dependency. On new issues, it adds context and a label from a fixed set, and it never applies the maintainer-only labels.

CodeRabbit reads its configuration from the PR branch, so its review here is the first run under these settings.

Closes #1432

author: aaymeloglu
body:
`/transactions/get` is Plaid's legacy endpoint; `/transactions/sync` is the supported replacement. This moves `listTransactions` over to sync.

**How it works**
- **Per-connection copy in memory:** each connection keeps its own in-memory copy of its transactions and a cursor, for as long as the server runs. The first call fetches the full history with no cursor. Later calls send the cursor and apply only what was added, modified or removed. Removals now take effect: a pending charge that posts under a new ID no longer lingers.
- **Filtering:** account and date filtering now happen locally. The tool layer above is unchanged.
- **Mid-sync changes:** all pages are collected before any are applied. If Plaid returns `TRANSACTIONS_SYNC_MUTATION_DURING_PAGINATION`, paging restarts from the starting cursor, up to 3 retries.
- **One request per connection:** concurrent calls share one in-flight sync, and a sync from the last 60 seconds is reused. `list_transactions` asks once per account, so this keeps it to one Plaid request per connection.
- **Raw bank description:** `include_original_description` is now requested, so `reference` holds the raw bank description instead of repeating the cleaned name.

**Scope:** nothing is written to disk. State lives in memory, so a server restart triggers one full sync per connection. That's about 0.4-0.7s each on the live connections.

**Live check:** for 7/29-10/27 the transaction IDs from sync match `/transactions/get` exactly on all five connections (33 / 197 / 21 / 0 / 109). Repeat calls take under 1ms.

`npm test`: 133 pass. The tests were rewritten as sync responses and add coverage for cursor paging, incremental modified/removed, the mutation restart, and reuse of a recent sync.

author: adudley78
body:
## What this does

The documented agent exfiltrations of 2025–2026 did not leave through a generic web request. They left through the platform the agent was already working in: a private repository's contents in a public pull request (Invariant Labs, official GitHub MCP server), internal data in an outsider's Jira ticket (Cato CTRL, Atlassian's MCP), data in a link Slack fetched for a preview (CVE-2025-34072, reference Slack server, CVSS 9.3 from VulnCheck), and, from a CI harness rather than MCP, credentials in a PR comment, a public issue comment and a `git push` (Comment and Control, ACM CCS 2026). An egress allowlist does not stop these, because the platform's own host is the destination: Copilot's firewall allowed `github.com`, and the secrets left as a push. mcp-audit ranked all of them like any fetch (`network_out`).

This PR adds a capability, **`comms_out`**: a server that posts to a shared service (issue, PR or review comments, pushed commits or files, chat messages, Jira/Confluence, social posts, webhooks). It is wired as a sink, not tag-only, and joins the default `scan` / `check` / `scan --project` / GitHub Action path with no new flag and no network call.

| ID | Severity | Pair | Network twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| **TOXIC-008** | HIGH | file read + `comms_out` | TOXIC-001 (HIGH) |
| **TOXIC-009** | CRITICAL | secrets + `comms_out` | TOXIC-003 (CRITICAL) |
| **TOXIC-010** | HIGH | database + `comms_out` | TOXIC-005 (HIGH) |
| **TOXIC-011** | CRITICAL | shell execution + `comms_out` | TOXIC-006 (CRITICAL) |

**Why these severities:** the evidence confirms the sink class, mostly in single-server form (Invariant, Cato, CVE-2025-34072, GitLost each ran inside one server that could read and post). Comment and Control was a CI harness (GitHub Actions), not MCP, so it supports the sink class and the shell-plus-post shape of TOXIC-011 only. Nothing shows two separate MCP servers combined, so TOXIC-008 and TOXIC-010 are HIGH like their network twins; a laptop also has no egress allowlist for this sink to get around. TOXIC-009 and TOXIC-011 are CRITICAL like TOXIC-003 and TOXIC-006. Reasoning: `docs/severity-framework.md` ("comms_out sinks").

**Where it comes from:**
- **Registry** (from each package's own tool list): `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github` (+`comms_out`: `add_issue_comment`, `create_pull_request`, `push_files`), `server-slack` (+`comms_out`: `slack_post_message`), `mcp-atlassian` (+`comms_out`: `jira_create_issue`, `confluence_add_comment`), `@autoposting.ai/cli` (+`comms_out`: `publish-post`), `server-gitlab` (null → `["git", "comms_out"]`). Entries keep `network_out` where they had it, so **no existing TOXIC-* finding stops firing**.
- **Keywords** (servers outside the registry): code hosts only as a whole token or package fragment (`" github "`, `server-github`, `github-mcp`, `mcp-gitlab`, …), never the bare substring, so a local server under `~/github/…` or `…/github.com/org/repo` is **not** tagged; Atlassian, Azure DevOps, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Mattermost, Teams, webhook, Twitter/Mastodon/Bluesky, each anchored as a whole token or package fragment (`slack-mcp`, `mcp-slack`, `server-slack`) and **never matched inside a local path or `scheme://` argument** (so `server-filesystem /Users/dev/code/discord-bot` and `postgres://localhost/webhooks` stay silent); and, with `--connect`, verified write-tool names (`add_issue_comment`, `create_pull_request`, `push_files`, `slack_post_message`, `confluence_add_comment`, `git_push`, …). Read verbs are not keywords.
- **Email stays `email`.** It already has its own wired sink (TOXIC-002, `CAPABILITY_FLOWS`), and its destination is a recipient the attacker names, not a shared space. The submission template tells email senders to use the email box.

**Attack graph:** the four edges are in `CAPABILITY_FLOWS` (only those, so every comms edge is backed by a pair), `COMMS_OUT` is in `_SINK_CAPS`, and `_candidates_from_toxic_findings` now keeps the **most severe** pair when several findings name the same servers. It kept the first one listed, which also hid `server-everything`'s CRITICAL TOXIC-006 path behind a HIGH TOXIC-001 one.

**Registry submission form:** one new checkbox ("Post to a shared service: issue or PR comments, git push, chat messages, social posts, webhooks"), pinned 1:1 to the enum by `tests/test_registry_submission_template.py`. Adam released this story from the hold list on 2026-10-25 ("Include it"), which covers the new `Capability` member and the `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` edit.

## Measured first (as R37 did)

One server per registry entry (`npx -y <name>`), all 55 together; the same with heuristics only; the published top-100 npm corpus (`docs/research/2026-10-top100-npm/scan-config-100-servers.mcp.json`, pinned, so the registry lookup misses and only keywords tag); `demo/configs/`.

| Corpus | Posting servers tagged | 008 | 009 | 010 | 011 | Pair already had its network twin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Registry (55) | 5 | 30 (29 cross, 1 self: `mcp-atlassian`) | 0 | 30 | 20 | 63 of 80 same-direction; the other 17 are 16 `server-gitlab` pairs and `mcptoon` → `mcp-atlassian` (twin only the other way round) |
| Registry names, heuristics only | 4 | 12 | 0 | 16 | 4 | 16 of 32 |
| Top-100 npm | 4 (`@azure-devops/mcp`, `slack-mcp-server`, `@zencoderai/slack-mcp-server`, `@zereight/mcp-gitlab`) | 8 | 0 | 4 | 4 | 0 of 16 |
| `demo/configs/` | 1 (`github`) | 2 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 4 of 4 |

- Registry hits are spread evenly over the five posting servers (6 per source each), not concentrated on one generic server (the reason R37 declined `FILE_WRITE + NETWORK_OUT`). A posting server alone fires nothing new.

author: rsasaki0109
body:
## Summary

Root-causes why `param/istanbul_gtsam_smoother.yaml` drifted 6-24 m on the Istanbul localization bag (#245). Three causes were stacked, and each one hid the next. Full record: `experiments/istanbul_ndt_tracking/README.md`.

1. **The full-map NDT target was empty.** The map's bounding box (15.2 x 12.7 km, 284 m of height) needs 5.5e10 NDT cells at 1 m, which overflows pclomp's int32 index. pclomp leaves the target empty, so NDT returns its initial guess on every scan and the pose is pure twist dead reckoning.
   - **Fix:** the localizer now logs an ERROR at map load with the map extent and points to `enable_local_map_crop`. This covers the full-map target and the GICP backends' NDT initializer.
   - **Preset:** the Istanbul preset now crops (150 m radius, 10 m update distance).
2. **The smoother put each NDT pose at the processing time.** `TwistGtsamSmoother::update()` ignored its scan stamp, so every update dropped the motion made while the scan waited and was aligned. With registration actually working (crop on), the replay diverged once the car reached about 3 m/s.
   - **Fix:** the smoother now splits the twist at the scan stamp, carries the later twist over to the new node, and seeds NDT with the pose predicted at the scan stamp. New `test/test_twist_gtsam_smoother.cpp` covers this.
3. **Twist was dropped while a scan held the state lock.** A crop rebuild holds the lock for 1.7 s here, and the twist subscription only kept the default depth of 5 messages.
   - **Fix:** the subscription now queues 1000 messages.

Also:
- The GNSS orientation in this bag is about 2° off the direction of travel. That explains the old preset's cross-track drift, and it means yaw RMSE scored against GNSS carries about a 2° reference bias.
- The old window C (3160 s) started inside a GNSS outage (sigma up to 92 m). `compare.py` now uses 2300-2420 s instead (4-5 % climb at up to 21 m/s, sigma ≤ 0.52 m). The twist_smoother_slope README now notes this and the empty-target issue.
- `replay.py` / `compare.py` take `--set` / `--cand-set` preset overrides.
- New troubleshooting section: *NDT Does Not Correct the Pose on a Large Map*.

## Result

Horizontal RMSE, median of three runs (range). Baseline is `971e29a`.

| Window | preset (no crop) | baseline + crop | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A 0-60 s | 5.90 m | 53.0 m | **0.26 m** (0.22-0.27) |
| B 2820-2970 s, 6-10 % grades | 20.1 m | 249 m | **1.11 m** (0.91-9.07) |
| C 2300-2420 s, 21 m/s climb | 51.1 m | 252 m | **0.51 m** (0.47-0.59) |

- One run per window with the committed build gave 0.22 / 0.92 / 0.50 m.
- The candidate runs used a 200-message twist queue; the committed build uses 1000.

## Known limits (recorded, not fixed here)

- **z on grades.** The smoother is planar and keeps the last NDT z. In one of the three window B runs, z fell behind on the 6 % descent while NDT was rejected, and NDT did not recover (9.1 m). The slope-aware z seed rejected in #245 was measured while NDT was not registering, so it should be measured again on top of this fix.
- **Throughput.** Rebuilding the 150 m crop takes about 1.7 s on 4 cores, so the pose rate drops to 0.9-3 Hz while driving.
- **Twist EKF.** `TwistEkf::update()` also takes no stamp, so it has the same timing bug (cause 2). No preset enables it; it is left for a separate change.

## Validation

- `colcon build --symlink-install --packages-select lidar_localization_ros2` (Jazzy): OK
- `ctest`: 78/78 passed, including the new `twist_gtsam_smoother` test and the extended `map_initialization_policy` test
- `python3 -m pytest test/`: 379 passed
- `clang-tidy` (repo config, warnings as errors) on `component_alignment.cpp`, `component_lifecycle.cpp`, `component_subscribers.cpp`: clean
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on `experiments/twist_smoother_slope/`: clean
- A replay without the crop logs the new ERROR (map extent, 5.5e+10 cells) right before PCL's overflow warning; the cropped replays log no error.
- **Not run:** the `check_*_bringup.py --help` acceptance scripts (no bringup or launch files changed) and the Humble build. Local development here is on Jazzy; CI builds both.

This is a public-dataset replay, not a physical-robot test.

author: ashesfall
body:
A performance round added Semaphore.isOrderedOnDevice() and Submittable.chainOnDevice() so that calling code could keep waiting on every step for the backends that could not keep up with a long chain, instead of fixing those backends. The review that saw it recorded the abstraction break as a design question and approved the change. This adds a mechanical guard for that shape and changes the two prompts that steered toward it.

Guard (.claude/hooks/block-async-bypass.sh, lib/async_bypass_check.py): a PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit/MultiEdit for production Java sources (tests are exempt). It blocks:
- a new method on Semaphore or Submittable that asks about the backend behind it (is/has/supports...Device/Native/Ordered/Queue/...) or a second submit variant (chain/submit/enqueue/dispatch...Device/Ordered/Native/...), and any call to isOrderedOnDevice or chainOnDevice;
- in calling code outside base/, a new instanceof check against a Semaphore type, or a new in-flight cap in a file that waits;
- a new waitFor() followed by submit(null). It warns on a new waitFor() in calling code that also submits, since the wait belongs at the host boundary. Only lines the edit adds are judged, so existing code is not reported again. Run against the files of the original change it blocks all three; run over the current tree it blocks nothing. test_async_bypass_check.py covers the contract, caller, replay and scope cases.

Registration: settings.json registers the hook beside block-interface-bypass.py, and source_write_check.py adds it to REPLAYED_GUARDS so source files modified by a Bash command are checked against HEAD as well.

Prompts:
- general-review.txt: an abstraction break - an interface method that asks about its implementation, a backend-dependent variant of an interface method, or a caller that waits, caps work in flight or branches on the type of a completion - is a defect to fix in the broken implementation, not a design question to approve and record.
- performance.txt: a change that exposes a backend unable to keep up with an interface used as intended makes fixing that backend part of the change; preserving the old behaviour for one backend through a semaphore query, a second submit method, a backend-dependent wait or a caller-side cap is not allowed.

The guard's messages and both prompts point to
docs/internals/asynchronous-submission.md, which arrives with the branch that removed chainOnDevice and fixed the native and Metal receivers.

author: calinwolf08
body:
## Problem

In Demo C, Dr. Mia Chen (Psychiatry) never showed as an option in `/plan`. She only works half days: Tue/Thu mornings and Fri afternoons. The planner's Session field defaulted to **Full day**, and a full day never fits her availability. So she had no open days: she was hidden, listed as "No open days left" under Show all, and the date picker showed nothing. The capacity card counts any session, which is why it still showed her days.

## Changes

- **Session defaults to "All sessions"** (`session: 'any'`). Each day is checked in whichever session fits, full day first, then AM, then PM, and is added as that session. Half days get half credit. If none fits, the reported reason comes from a session the preceptor is at least available for. "Full day only", "Mornings only" and "Afternoons only" still narrow the choice.
- **Date picker:** each open day is labelled `Full`, `AM` or `PM` (`DayState.planSession`, `data-session`). The tooltip says what it adds, e.g. "adds a morning (½ day credit)", and a hint explains the labels. The assignment dialog doesn't set `planSession`, so it is unchanged.
- **Form:**
  - The picked days show their session mix ("1 AM · 1 PM").
  - Each day is staged with its own session and credit, so one add can mix sessions.
  - "Pick the next N open days" counts half days as half.
- **Options API:** accepts `session: 'any'`. Date checks report the session each day resolves to, and `openSessions` gives the session for each open day.

## Tests
- **Integration:** with "All sessions", a half-day preceptor has more open days than with "Full day only". Each day resolves to the right session, and a student already booked in the morning is offered the afternoon of a full day.
- **E2E MP-10** (`mp-sessions.spec.ts`), driven through the page with a half-day preceptor:
  - the default is "All sessions" and the preceptor is offered with her open days;
  - "Full day only" hides her;
  - picker days are labelled AM/PM;
  - a morning and an afternoon add 1 credit in total;
  - the list rows show (AM)/(PM);
  - "Pick the next 2 open days" meets the requirement.
- `npm run check`, lint, vitest (2027 passed), `coverage:check` and `test:e2e:full` (125 passed) are green locally.

author: geovannimp
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
Move sample rate from an app-wide engine setting to a per-bus route, and have each bus follow its device's mix rate unless an explicit rate is set.

The global `sample_rate` and `low_latency` fields are removed from `EngineConfig`/`AppSettings`; both now live on `BusConfig`/`BusRouteSettings` (`BusConfig::with_sample_rate` / `with_low_latency`). A bus rate of `None` means "follow the device mix rate," and zero/negative rates fall back to `None` in normalization.

Device introspection gains `mix_sample_rate` (the system mix rate, e.g. WASAPI shared-mode format) and `sample_rate_ranges` (inclusive spans the device can open, so a rate inside a span is still valid even if not listed as an endpoint). The CPAL backend advertises only openable `f32` ranges, resolves an explicitly selected device as terminal, refuses an unavailable rate instead of silently substituting, requests the device minimum callback period when any shared bus asks for low latency (floored at 16 frames), and reports which device it actually opened.

Engine stream planning resolves each device's rate (`resolve_plan_rate`) from an explicit bus rate or the device mix rate, rejects conflicting explicit rates on a shared device ("one stream runs at one rate"), and the producer now resamples per-device when a stream runs off the DSP clock — using a new fixed-input `DeviceRateConverter` so 48 kHz→44.1 kHz stays time-accurate instead of drifting. The DSP still renders whole chunks at its own rate (the master bus rate).

The Flutter UI moves sample-rate selection onto each bus route, labels the default as "Device default" (with the mix rate when known), validates a remembered rate against the selected device's spans, and migrates legacy global `sample_rate`/`low_latency` from existing settings files. Documentation and the FFI layer are updated to match.

Reviewers noted a medium-gap on legacy global settings migration (handled as described) and one high item in `settings_bus_route_fields.dart` to watch: the "Device default" label can still show the mix rate even while a sibling bus on the same device pins another rate.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

author: some-du6e
body:
## Problem

A thread can't move to another project once it exists. A chat started under **No project** stays there after the work turns out to belong to a real repo, and so does one started in the wrong project. Right now the only way to move one is to quit T3 Code and edit `statev2.sqlite` by hand (#6857).

## Change

`thread.metadata.update` takes an optional `projectId`. A move is allowed only when the thread is **settled**, is not a subagent, has no child threads, and the target project exists.

Requiring a settled thread keeps the change small. Settling already:
- refuses while a run is active or queued, or an approval or question is pending
- ends PR watches, and a settled thread can't start a new one
- disconnects provider sessions and stops idle background work

So the move doesn't repeat any of that. Child threads are refused because they inherit the parent's project and workspace, and moving only the parent would leave them behind.

A move clears `branch` and `worktreePath`, because both belong to the old repo. The other pieces were already in place: the projection writes `project_id` from the event payload, and each turn works out its folder as `worktreePath ?? project.workspaceRoot`. Old checkpoints keep their recorded `cwd`, so diffs of past turns still work.

This PR only covers the server and contract. There's no "Move to project…" menu or MCP tool yet. Either can come in a follow-up once the direction is settled.

## Scope and approval

Feature request: #6857. **No maintainer has approved this direction yet.** I'm opening this so there's a small concrete version to look at. Close it if you'd rather design this another way.

## Verification

New test in `apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.test.ts`, `moves a settled thread to another project`:
- a settled thread moves, and `projectId` updates in the thread projection and the shell snapshot, with `branch` and `worktreePath` cleared
- after a new message unsettles the thread, a move is rejected

```
vp test run src/orchestration-v2/runtimeLayer.test.ts -t "moves a settled thread"
Tests  1 passed | 89 skipped (90)
```

`vp fmt --check` and `vp lint` pass on the changed files, and `tsc --noEmit` passes for `apps/server`.

Not checked:
- **Child-thread refusal:** no test of its own, because creating a child needs a fake provider run that this test file doesn't set up.
- **Failed worktree setup:** if a settled thread's last run failed worktree setup, a later `queue_after_active` message is held after a move, just as it is without one.
- **Real session resume:** a real Claude or Codex session resuming after a move. If the transcript isn't in the new folder's `~/.claude/projects/<slug>`, Claude falls back to its existing fresh-session-plus-handoff path.

> [!NOTE]
> Filed by Claude Opus 5.5 using Claude Code (in T3 Code).

author: atikulmunna
body:
A pass on how CVSight looks and how fast review goes. It gives CVSight its own look and adds review tools built for shelves.

## Stockroom theme
- **Palette:** graphite ink (#1e2b2a) on a sage-grey board (#e8ebe4), from the shelving, pencil and price tags of a shelf audit. Price-tag yellow (#ffd23f) is the one accent and only ever a fill: primary actions, the active tab, the selection. Text, lines and the focus ring stay graphite.
- **Active tabs:** a yellow fill with a graphite underline, because a yellow line alone is too faint on a light band.
- **Gradients and dark leftovers:** every gradient is removed, the project band and sign-in screen are light, and dark-era translucent colours map onto tokens. Buttons no longer glow or lift on hover.
- **Overlays:** they keep their own set, picked to stand out against packaging.
  - Gaps are lime hatching instead of magenta, which vanished against pink packs.
  - Flagged boxes are orange.
  - Marks drawn on the photo use overlay colours with a dark edge.
- **Type:** Archivo with its width axis replaces Bricolage Grotesque and IBM Plex Sans: expanded for titles, condensed with tabular figures for dense data. IBM Plex Mono stays for codes only.
- **Logo:** the price tag turns yellow.

## Faster review on the canvas
- **Shelf row strip:** under the canvas, the selected box's row shows as crops with names and state. Clicking a crop selects that box.
- **Least confident first:** waiting proposals come first, lowest score first, and J and K follow the order. "Accept N at 90% or more" accepts the confident ones as one undo step.
- **SAM status:** `GET /api/segmenter/status` returns ready, unreachable, rejected or off, using a 5 second health check through the tunnel. The header shows it and checks again every minute.
- **Performance panel:** the canvas check appears only with `?fixture=local`.

## Projects list
The page is now a table with these columns: preview, name and description, type, images, a reviewed bar ("N of M reviewed"), working version (Editable or None), created date, and Open. Progress loads per project after the list renders. The narrow layout stacks rows.

## SKU lineup in Review QA
- **Crop route:** `GET /api/annotations/{id}/crop?revision=N` returns a JPEG crop with 8% context, at most 256 px. When the revision is pinned it may be cached privately.
- **Lineup route:** `GET /api/dataset-versions/{id}/sku-lineup?sku_id=...` returns the SKU's reference images and every accepted box with that SKU in the version, up to 200.
- **Panel:** Review QA shows the lineup beside the selected item, with the item first, so a wrong SKU stands out.
- **Media helpers:** they move into `media.py`, shared by export and crops.
- **Cache header:** the API middleware now keeps a `Cache-Control` a route sets; every other route still sends `private, no-store`.

## Checks
- `scripts/check.ps1` passes: 455 Python tests, Ruff and mypy clean, 329 frontend tests, build.
- **Browser check:** the branch's build was checked in a local preview against the live data, covering the projects list, project overview, images, canvas with boxes, Review QA and Analytics.
- **Not yet checked live:** the crop, lineup and status routes need the deployment rebuilt.

author: byrcolin
body:
Replaces #18. It's the same change, redone on top of #19.

## Summary
The repository mixed CRLF (most files) and LF (`.github/*` and newer files). Every editor or script was a chance to flip a whole file and bury a one-line change in a full-file diff, and that happened several times during this cleanup.

- **`.gitattributes`:** `* text=auto eol=lf`. LF is stored and checked out everywhere, whatever the platform or local `core.autocrlf`.
  - Exceptions: Windows scripts (`*.bat`, `*.cmd`, `*.ps1`) keep CRLF, and the bundled canonical schemas are `-text`, so they stay byte-for-byte copies of canonical.o3de.org.
- **`.editorconfig`:** tells editors the same thing (LF, UTF-8, final newline, 4-space Python, 100 columns).
- **`scripts/sync_schemas.py`:** writes `SOURCE` as bytes. In text mode it wrote CRLF on Windows.

**This is a line-endings-only change** apart from the two new files and the one-line script fix. `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` shows nothing else. A follow-up adds this commit to `.git-blame-ignore-revs` once it has its final hash.

**After this merges**, existing checkouts may show files as modified until you run `git add --renormalize .` or re-check them out. A fresh clone is clean.

## Test plan
- [x] Checked out fresh as LF: 1492 tests pass; mypy 0 errors; ruff clean
- [x] `scripts/sync_schemas.py` re-run: no diff

author: palango
body:
celo-org/op-succinct is merging upstream op-succinct v4.9.3, which needs SP1 6.10.0 and hokulea v1.4.2, but it gets hokulea through celo-kona, and celo-kona's hokulea-client/v1.4.1 pins its SP1 crates to `=6.8.1`. This moves the three hokulea pins (`hokulea-eigenda`, `hokulea-proof`, `hokulea-host-bin`) to the Layr-Labs tag `hokulea-client/v1.4.2`, the same way we already pin upstream hokulea tags rather than a fork. op-succinct will pin the main commit this produces.

## What changes

hokulea v1.4.1..v1.4.2 is a single commit, Layr-Labs/hokulea@e7ff01d ("chore(deps): bump SP1 to v6.10.0 (#339)"). Its manifest changes are the SP1 and sp1-contract-call pins and the sp1-patches tags. No celo-kona code changes.

The `Cargo.lock` diff covers:

- the hokulea and canoe packages, which move from `ab007dd` to `e7ff01d` at the same version;
- `substrate-bn` (sp1-patches), from tag `patch-0.6.0-sp1-6.0.0-substrate-bn` (`13747d2`) to `patch-0.6.0-sp1-6.10.0-substrate-bn` (`ab4d008`), which `hokulea-sp1-bn-verifier` now requires;
- `sp1-lib`, `sp1-primitives` and seven `slop-*` crates, 6.4.0 to 6.10.0, pulled in by the new `substrate-bn`.

`cargo update -p` also moved dependency edges in 11 unrelated packages (for example `tempfile`'s `getrandom` and `data-encoding-macro-internal`'s `syn`) to other versions already in the lock. I restored those entries from main, so the lockfile only carries the bump; `cargo metadata --locked` accepts it. `cargo tree -d` shows no second version of any hokulea, canoe, sp1, slop or kona crate. The crates.io + sp1-patches `substrate-bn` pair was already there on main.

## Effect on the guest program

celo-kona commits no ELF or vkey, but the celo-client guest does change when built for SP1. `hokulea-proof`'s `sp1-bn` feature compiles `substrate-bn` and `sp1-lib` into celo-client under `target_os = "zkvm"`. The new `substrate-bn` patch hardens hint handling in its field arithmetic (invalid hints halt instead of panicking, stricter canonicality checks), so op-succinct's range program and vkey will change with this bump. None of those changes touch the calls hokulea makes. The FPVM build does not include these crates.

Taking this commit also forces op-succinct onto SP1 >= 6.10, since the new `substrate-bn` requires `sp1-lib ^6.10.0`. op-succinct is moving to 6.10.0 anyway.

## cargo deny

`cargo deny check` was already red on main for six advisories, and the second commit fixes that. tokio (1.53.1 to 1.53.3, the smallest patched release, RUSTSEC-2026-0386) and zstd-sys (2.0.16 to 2.1.2, RUSTSEC-2026-0410) only need a lockfile bump. zstd-sys 2.1.2 changes its license from MIT/Apache-2.0 to BSD-3-Clause, which `deny.toml` already allows.

The other four go into the `deny.toml` ignore list, each with a comment naming what blocks the fix. RUSTSEC-2026-0387 (crypto-bigint) is only fixed in 0.7.6, which needs elliptic-curve 0.14, while alloy, revm-precompile and sp1-lib are on elliptic-curve 0.13. RUSTSEC-2026-0391, -0398 and -0403 need zstd 0.14 / zstd-safe 8.2, but our workspace, the celo-org/reth and celo-org/optimism forks and reth-zstd-compressors all require zstd ^0.13.

## Verification

I ran what CI runs locally on the final tree (`bd2a7ab`), and everything passed: `just build-native`, `just lint-native`, `just test` (764 passed, 2 skipped), `just test-trybuild`, `just hack`, `.github/scripts/check_no_std.sh`, `cargo deny check`, `just check-udeps` (with the pinned nightly-2026-05-17), the offline host + client run from `proof.yaml` (Celo Sepolia block 34620000, output root matches) and `e2e_test/run_all_tests.sh` (22/22). The same suite also passed on the first commit alone, except for deny.

body:
## Summary

The dashboard's status footer shows the open run's tokens in, out and cached, abbreviated. Until now, once a run had journaled its first call, the footer read the Summary's totals, which are written only at call boundaries, so a running call's live Usage was missing. While the run is live the footer now sums the stage cards' tokens, which hold ended and live sessions; once the run has ended it keeps the Summary's final totals.

## Changes

- `feat(dashboard): the footer's tokens count a running call's live usage`: `tokensOf` in `src/dashboard/page/run-view.ts` reads the summary's totals only when the run has ended (or the model holds no cards), and otherwise sums the cards' tokens. Adds footer tests in `test/dashboard/page/run-view.test.ts` and the 10m boundary to the `tokens` test in `test/dashboard/page/format.test.ts`.

## Testing

- `the footer shows the golden run's tokens from its summary once it has ended`: the ended golden run's footer reads `28.4k in · 9.0k out · 189k cached`.
- `while a call runs, the footer's tokens count its live usage over a summary written before it`: the golden run cut mid-session, with a Summary from before that call, shows the cards' tokens (live usage included) and not the stale Summary's.
- The `tokens` boundary test now covers `9_949_999` → `9.9m` and `9_950_000` → `10m`.
- The existing footer assertions for the golden cut and FAKE-2 pass unchanged.
- `bun run gate` passes. CI runs the full `bun run verify`.

## Demonstration

Surface: `dashboard`.

- Ended golden-like run: in a demo repository holding `test/fixtures/repo/.sail/` (the `ticket-to-pr` workflow on fake ports, `FAKE-1` seeded), run `sail FAKE-1` and expect exit code 0. Then run `sail dashboard` and open that run's view in headless Chrome. The footer element `footer#status` contains a span whose text is `tokens 28.4k in · 9.0k out · 189k cached`, beside `calls`, `tools`, `denied` and `cost`.
- The live-usage criterion gets no bullet: showing it needs the dashboard open while a run is mid-call, which takes two commands running at once. The run-view test `while a call runs, the footer's tokens count its live usage over a summary written before it` observes it.
- The format boundaries are observed only by `test/dashboard/page/format.test.ts`, so they get no bullet.

Closes ADW-309

author: talentumtuum
body:
Add NestJS integration and a node-ts publisher adapter so applications can wire storage and event delivery through DI and run outbox workers using native Nest scheduling.

`@taleland/outbox-nestjs` provides `OutboxModule.register` / `registerAsync`, an injectable `OutboxService`, and individual operation tokens. `registerJobs` / `registerJobsAsync` additionally enable `@Cron` providers for processing every second and cleanup at midnight UTC. Nest manages scheduling, overlap prevention, and error logging; a drain hook waits for active scheduled operations during shutdown.

`@taleland/outbox-nodets-bus` provides `createNodeTsPublish(getBus)`. It validates persisted `busToken`, `eventName`, and `eventVersion` metadata, publishes through the selected bus, and forwards the stable `outboxId` attribute. Resolution and publication errors propagate to the core retry mechanism. The adapter accepts the named resolver from `@taleland/nodets-bus-core` without depending on NestJS or MikroORM. The core remains transport-independent.

English READMEs cover storage/publisher composition, sync and async Nest DI, individual provider tokens, built-in and custom Cron jobs, routing metadata, per-module queues, and shutdown. Packaging, release scripts, and the fixed Changesets version group cover all four packages. Versions remain `0.0.0` and publishing remains disabled.

Validation: frozen pnpm install, lint, build, all 34 tests (10 core, 9 Nest container/scheduler, 6 publisher/retry tests, 9 PostgreSQL integration), and all four package-content checks pass locally. README publisher examples type-check against the packed adapter and the published `GetBus` type from `@taleland/nodets-bus-core`; Nest/MikroORM and custom Cron examples were also checked in an isolated npm consumer.

body:
A worker service now listens on TCP 7461 for builds (every coordinator's
sessions and route measurements) and TCP 7462 for fleet joins, instead of
ports macOS picks at each start. Coordinators still find workers with
Bonjour (mDNS, UDP 5353), so nothing changes on their side.

- `worker serve --port <n> --join-port <n>` changes them per Mac (0: any
  free port); the two must differ. Updates keep the plist, so the ports stay.
- A port another program holds stops the service with "port 7461: ... Address
  already in use" in agent.log; launchd starts it again.
- RemoteListener::stop() now waits until the port is released, so the join
  listener restarted after a fleet join can take its fixed port at once.
- When a key change cannot rebind the session port, the listener still falls
  back to any free port; the agent now logs that, since a firewall opened by
  port number blocks the new one.
- Worker Fleet Setup gains "Network and firewalls"; the README points to it.

author: chriskolenko
body:
This is Q4 of the one job queue (runsheet ADR 075). Claims now come from Mesh's priority queue, which ranks validations first, so the node no longer keeps slots away from builds. These were the per-kind lanes of runsheet ADR 069 decision 2b: one validation slot and one evaluation slot by default at capacity 4 or more. Since v0.2.612 a node on the queue already kept no lanes; this PR removes them everywhere.

**Old config**
- node.yaml's `capacity.reserve` is still read without error, whatever values it holds (negative or too big included).
- The node ignores it and logs once: `node.yaml: capacity.reserve is retired and ignored — claims come from Mesh's queue, which ranks validations first; remove it`.
- It isn't written back when the node saves node.yaml.

**Without the one claim** (an older platform), the node's own pass still asks for batch, main and pull request validations first every tick, in free slots. When none is free, it logs `main validation: a merge batch candidate waits for a free slot` once per set.

**Removed:** `Reserve`, `ReserveOf`, `ReserveFloor`, `Capacity.Lanes`, `Loop.Lanes`, `laneSummary`, `ValidatingInLane`, `laneTakes` and `laneHeld`. The holding summary no longer ends with `; lanes kept: …`. AGENTS.md is updated.

**Tests** (`lane_test.go`, rewritten)
- The retired reserve parses with any values, is noted, and isn't marshalled back.
- `LoadConfig` reads a node.yaml that still names it.
- No slot is kept from builds: at capacity 4 with three builds running, the ready item is claimed.
- The retired line is logged once across ticks.

author: rauhul
body:
Expat can deliver the text of one element in many chunks. It splits
the text at newlines, entity and character references, comments, and
CDATA sections. The builder kept only the last chunk, so
`<name>F & G</name>` decoded as " G" and multi-line descriptions
kept only their last line. This affected 1611 of 1880 SVD files.

Join all chunks of an element in order. Keep white space as raw bytes
until text follows it or the element ends, so that an element with
only white space, such as indentation around child elements, keeps a
nil value as before.
