## Change Description
Adds a "Ready" section to `Drv/ByteStreamDriverModel/docs/sdd.md`. It describes what `Svc::ComStub` does after a send answered with `OTHER_ERROR`, or after `SEND_RETRY` past its retry limit: it reports `FAILURE`, `Svc::ComQueue` pauses, and traffic resumes when the driver invokes `ready` again. It also notes that ComStub retries `SEND_RETRY` immediately and a bounded number of times and does not retry a send answered with `OTHER_ERROR`, so a driver facing a longer-lasting condition can return `OTHER_ERROR` and signal `ready` later. The `OTHER_ERROR` row of the send status table links to the new section, and the `ready` port annotations in `Drv/Interfaces/ByteStreamDriver.fpp` and `AsyncByteStreamDriver.fpp` mention the behaviour.

## Rationale
A driver author implementing the ByteStreamDriver interface could only learn this by reading ComStub (`m_reinitialize`, `drvConnected_handler`), which is what #3601 ran into. The text is scoped to ComStub because other clients, such as `Drv::ByteStreamBufferAdapter`, do not stop sending on `OTHER_ERROR`.

Step 6, stacked on #36. The crate asks for clippy's pedantic and nursery lints; this clears almost all of them without changing any arithmetic.

## What changed
- **Allowed with a written reason** (instead of silently ignored or "fixed" in a way that changes behavior): `cast_precision_loss` crate-wide (image sizes and counts are far below 2^23, so the float conversions are exact); `float_cmp` where equal floats are the point (the exact cycle detection of the lockstep loops and of the probes in `auto_iterations`, the exact default scale 1.0 for saving); `inline_always` on the two lockstep loops (a measured requirement, see their documentation); `struct_excessive_bools` for the independent switches of the window.
- **Idiomatic replacements**: `Option::is_none_or` instead of `map_or(true, ..)`; `slice::as_chunks::<LANES>()` instead of `chunks_exact(LANES)` with `remainder()`; `clone_from` instead of `x = y.clone()` (2 places); `write!` instead of `+= &format!(..)`; `#[derive(Eq)]` for `AdaptiveSampling` and `Appearance`; the loop variable of the scalar smooth iteration is the iteration count (no separate counter); `Copy` arguments by value (`to_32_bit_resolved`, `colors_to_rgb_bytes`).
- Doc backticks.

- **Output: identical**: 115/115 checksums.

This PR touches a few hot-path lines (`as_chunks`, `is_none_or`, the scalar loop), so I looked at these numbers specifically: no trend.
- 97 lib tests + 4 regression tests pass.

`render_*` functions in `rendering/progressive.rs` take 9 to 12 arguments, `controls_ui` is 172 lines, and the old whole-buffer renderer in `rendering/buffer.rs` has two stylistic lints (`%` instead of `is_multiple_of`, a loop counter). author: mbriones98
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** In a dashboard session, an agent runs a git command other than a known read only after the person confirms it, even when the session would otherwise approve the command on its own.

An agent ran `git commit` without being asked (#21267). Under session trust, YOLO, a native crew, a trusted pattern or a hook auto-approve, the dashboard approval ladder approved shell commands without a card, so a history-writing git command ran with no confirm step.

## Why it matters

A commit, reset, push or branch change the person did not ask for changes their repository's history, and it can be hard to notice and undo. The modes that skip approval are the ones people use for long unattended work, which is exactly where nobody sees the command go by.

## Not a goal

- The Slack, messaging, `spawn_run` and task-runner approval ladders. They have their own trust handling and unattended callers; tracked in #24596.
- Seeing what a repository's own configuration makes a listed read do (see Known limits).
- Changing what a hook deny or the existing deny floors refuse.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Symptom: a git write ran under trust with no card. Root cause: every auto-approve branch in the dashboard ladder (`tool_approval.py`) approved any shell command, and nothing on that path looked at whether it was a git write.

Approach: a confirm step that sits above the auto-approve branches, driven by a classifier that is fail-closed by construction. Earlier review rounds showed a list of write verbs keeps missing forms, so the classifier is a positive list instead:

- `security/git_write.py`: a command that names git is a read only when the WHOLE command is one plain git call (printable ASCII; no pipe, chain, redirection, group, substitution, expansion, glob, brace, comment, escape, runner or environment prefix), its global options are only `--no-pager`/`-P`/`--no-optional-locks` (or the command is exactly `git --version`), its subcommand is one of `status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `rev-parse`, `config --get <key>` / `config --list`, and every option is on that subcommand's own allow-list. Everything else that names git asks, including unknown subcommands, unlisted options and anything it cannot read.
- `dashboard/chat_turn/tool_approval.py`: when the classifier does not return a read, the call goes to the approval card even under session trust, YOLO, native crew, trusted patterns, trust-reads or a hook auto-approve. A hook deny still wins. Switching to Trust or YOLO leaves a pending git card open.
- New setting `hooks.confirm_git_writes`, on by default; `false` restores the previous ladder. Documented in `src/kiro_crew/docs/configuration.md`.
- Per-session allow (`dashboard/git_write_grant.py`): the person picks "Allow git writes in this session" from Trust on a git card, or a session is opened with `session_create(allow_git_writes=true)`. It is SEL-audited, shown on the slot, not inherited, ends when the approval mode is set to Normal, and does not survive a restart. A `session_create` that asks for the allow is confirmed the same way, and a session that received the allow from `session_create` cannot pass it on.
- Critical rules: a steering line telling agents to run a history-writing git command only when the user's own message asks for it.
- Specs: `security.md`, `session-control.md`, `memory-skills-hooks.md`.

Product-shape note: this adds an on-by-default confirm step. There is no RFC under `docs/request-for-change/` for it; the decision was made by the issue owner on #21267, so the First Principles lane needs a maintainer override.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: with `hooks.confirm_git_writes` unset the new confirm applies, but every command still runs once the person approves it, and `hooks.confirm_git_writes: false` restores the previous behaviour exactly. Existing config files load unchanged.

Removes nothing: the change adds a confirm step and a setting; no key, record, path or public function is removed or renamed.

## Known limits

The check reads the command line only. It does not see the repository's configuration or how the repository was cloned, so a listed read keeps whatever that configuration makes git do:

- `core.fsmonitor`: the configured hook runs during `git status` and `git diff`.
- `diff.external` and textconv drivers: the configured program runs during `git diff`, `git show` and `git log -p`; with `cachetextconv` set, the driver's output is stored under `refs/notes/textconv/<driver>`.
- `log.showSignature`: `git log` checks signatures, which starts the signing program.
- Partial clones: `git show`, `git log` and `git diff` fetch missing objects from the remote.

Also outside what it reads: a script the command starts, inline interpreter code that spells git another way, and a tool pre-approved in an agent's `allowedTools`, which skips this ladder. These are recorded in the `git_write.py` entry of `docs/system-specs/modules/security.md` and tracked in #24596.

## Tests

- `test/test_git_write_confirm.py`: the classifier. Known reads stay reads; every compound form, unknown future subcommand, unlisted option, abbreviation and input from the review rounds asks; `git --version --help`, `git --version x` and `git branch -- name --list` ask; plain `git --version` is a read.
- `test/test_git_write_ladder.py`: the dashboard ladder asks for a git command under trust, YOLO, native crew, trusted patterns, trust-reads and hook auto-approve; a hook deny still wins; the setting turns it off.
- `test/test_git_write_allow.py`: the per-session allow (set from the card and from `session_create`, SEL audit, not inherited, cleared by Normal, request card offers approve-once only, Trust/YOLO switch leaves the card open).
- `website/src/test/TrustDropdown.test.tsx`: the new Trust menu item.
- Pinned contracts updated on purpose: critical-rules hash/size, security package line budget, slot field order, config baseline.

Proof: not provable -- other: the new test files import the new modules, so with the fix reverted they fail at collection and no test runs. Run by hand against a clean origin/main worktree instead, 23 of the 28 tests in `test_git_write_ladder.py` fail and the 5 controls pass; on this branch all 28 pass.

## Manual verification

- A stub `git` that only records its arguments, run through real bash, confirmed the classifier flags every command that would run a non-read git call; the only mismatches are commands that ask without needing to.
- Ordinary commands (`curl https://github.com/...`, `gh pr view`, `ls`, `make`) still run under trust without a card.

## Screenshots / video

Still owed: the Trust menu on a git approval card gains an "Allow git writes in this session" item. A screenshot of that menu will be added to this description before merge.

## Related Issues

Fixes #21267
Refs #24596

## Sibling sweep

Swept: git grep -nE "auto_approve|trusted_patterns|yolo" -- src/kiro_crew/
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/dashboard/chat_turn/tool_approval.py -- changed here
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/handler_runtime/permission_ladder.py -- tracked in #24596
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/task_executor.py -- tracked in #24596

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: a security classifier built as a list of things to refuse keeps missing forms; build it as a short positive list of known-safe shapes and treat everything else as unsafe.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality

```diff
 scan_previously_declined / scan_standalone_smells / scan_closer_filing
```

- given a missing `docker/compose.yaml`, when `scan_build_args` runs, then its whole output is `docker/compose.yaml: missing`. Red: got `''`.
- given a `.gitignore` Secrets block with unanchored, trailing-slash, negated, slash-bearing and leading-`/` patterns, when `.dockerignore` misses each mapped form in turn, then only that form is flagged; a pattern after the block is never required; a `.gitignore` with no Secrets block is flagged.

None.

author: mykkezin
body:
## Objetivo
Acrescentar coordenação por papéis especializados para tarefas complexas sem montar um segundo runtime, usar provedores remotos ou contornar o catálogo de ferramentas existente.

## Como funciona
- O modo só ativa quando a mensagem pede explicitamente coordenação (por exemplo, “Use modo especialistas para planejar esta mudança” ou “Faça uma revisão multiagente desta arquitetura”).
- Duas passagens curtas usam o mesmo modelo local configurado: **Arquiteto** prepara objetivo, pressupostos, plano e critérios; **Revisor de Segurança e Qualidade** aponta riscos, casos-limite e testes.
- A resposta final continua no fluxo normal do diálogo Qwen e no mesmo ciclo de function calling governado.

## Limites e segurança
- Perguntas comuns não geram chamadas extras.
- A coordenação só executa as passagens extras com provedor local (`ollama`, `local` ou `nyxal`); quando o provedor é remoto, a conversa segue sem essas passagens.
- As passagens não recebem ferramentas. Se o modelo emitir `tool_calls` numa passagem, ela é descartada e a conversa normal prossegue.
- No máximo duas passagens extras, entrada limitada a 8.000 caracteres e saída limitada a 1.500 caracteres por papel.
- Os resumos são explicitamente rotulados como dados não confiáveis, não fatos verificados nem instruções privilegiadas.
- O modo não afirma que são modelos independentes: são dois papéis no mesmo modelo local.
- Falhas nas passagens não bloqueiam a resposta normal e não concedem autorizações nem executam ações.

## Testes
Adiciona testes de ativação explícita, ausência de chamadas extra em perguntas comuns, recusa do modo fora do modelo local, descarte de tentativa de ferramenta nas passagens e limites de tamanho. Atualiza a documentação de ferramentas governadas.

author: chrisgoddard
body:
## Problem

A routed child question expires after the dialog's timeout, or `agents.childQuestionTimeoutMs` (default 10 minutes). That suits an agent asking a quick question while someone watches. It does not suit a workflow that must wait for an operator who may be away for hours: the question is cancelled, the child sees a cancelled dialog, and the run carries on without the answer or fails.

To reproduce on `main`: set `agents.childQuestions: "route"`, spawn a durable or headless run whose extension opens a `select` with no `timeout`, and leave it. After the default deadline the decision expires with `onExpire: "cancel"` and the child gets `cancelled: true`. Raising `childQuestionTimeoutMs` does not help much: it is capped at 24 hours, and it applies to every run, not only the one that should wait.

## Change

A new optional request field, `holdQuestions: true`, on `agents.run` and `agents.spawn`.

- `src/agents/types.ts`, `src/agents/request.ts`, `src/providers/agents-actions.ts`, `src/runtime/guest-types.ts`: the field on `AgentRunRequest` and in the action schema (`const: true`). Only a literal `true` passes through.
- `src/agents/manager.ts`: fails closed before admission when the value is not `true`, or when `agents.childQuestions` is not `"route"` or the runner does not declare `questions`. A held run passes `--child-questions-hold 1` to its worker and sets `hold: true` on each `AgentChildQuestionRequest` that has no timeout of its own.
- `src/worker/options.ts`, `src/worker.ts`, `src/worker/questions.ts`: `ChildQuestionRelay` sets no timer on a held question and marks the lifecycle record `hold: true`. A dialog that sets its own `timeout` keeps it.
- `src/agents/hosted-run.ts`, `src/agents/runner-protocol.ts`: hosted runners follow the same rule, and `HostedRunState` persists `holdQuestions`, so a re-attached run still holds.
- `src/decisions/host.ts`: `routeChildQuestion` raises a held question as a `kind: "question"` decision held by `"root"` with `MAX_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS` (30 days) as its deadline, even when the parent has a UI. The UI only gets a `notify` that the decision is waiting, so no blocking dialog stalls the session. A parent with a UI and no decision store asks through the UI dialog with no timeout.
- `docs/agents.md`, `docs/decisions.md`: a new section, "Holding a question for a person".

## Why this approach

- Per run, not per config. Only the run that must wait for a person holds; every other run keeps the short default.
- A decision, not a dialog. A decision is durable, shows in `/fabric decisions`, and can be answered from `pi-fabric decisions answer` or another root session. A blocking dialog would stall the parent session for hours.
- The longest deadline, not none. If the session that raised the decision dies without a clean shutdown, nothing else cancels it, and answering it would reach no one. With a 30-day deadline it expires and drops out of the open list. The operator still has a month.
- The run's own `timeoutMs` and settlement still end the wait, and a stopped run cancels the decision as before.

## Compatibility and risk

- Additive. Without `holdQuestions`, every path runs as before; the existing child-question tests pass unchanged.
- The new worker flag `--child-questions-hold` is only passed with `holdQuestions: true`, which the manager refuses unless the runner declares `questions`.
- The lifecycle record gains an optional `hold: true`. Readers that ignore unknown fields are unaffected.
- A held decision can sit for up to 30 days. That is the store's existing maximum (`MAX_DECISION_DEADLINE_MS`); no limit is raised.

## Tests

- `tests/decisions-host.test.ts`: a held question becomes a root decision with the 30-day deadline even with a parent UI; it expires at that deadline; with a UI and no store it asks through the UI with no timeout.
- `tests/worker-child-questions.test.ts`: the relay never times out a held question that has no timeout of its own; a worker round trip holds past the worker deadline; the manager refuses `holdQuestions` unless questions are routed, and refuses any value other than `true`.
- `tests/runner-adapters.test.ts`: a hosted question holds past the question deadline and the hold is persisted for recovery.
- `tests/agent-request-alias.test.ts`: only a literal `true` passes through the request normalizer.

8 of 55 tests in these four files fail without the change; all pass with it (rechecked 2026-10-28 on the split base). The base for this count is the branch this PR stacks on (see Notes for review), because the field builds on child-question routing that `main` does not have yet.

## Notes for review

- This PR stacks on the durable-child-questions PR (durable child questions routed to root-held decisions, `blockedOn.decisionId`, and the restart cancel). Please land that one first. This PR adds two commits on top of it.
- It adds one field to the `agents.run` and `agents.spawn` request. If you would rather not grow that surface, an alternative is a per-question opt-in: a dialog with `timeout: 0` or a dedicated option could ask to be held. We chose the run field because the caller, not the extension that opens the dialog, knows whether a person is expected to answer. We will rework it if you prefer the other shape.
- The UI notice text names `/fabric decisions` and the 30-day limit; tell us if you want it worded differently.

author: kthyng
body:
# Summary
With `UPSCALING`, the advective tracer flux across each open-boundary face is now first-order upwind in both flow directions; before, only the inflow side was. On outflow faces the higher-order stencil's curvature term reached into the boundary row, which the OBC overwrites every step, so the flux it borrowed there was never paid back. The `_uscl` export then recorded a spurious inward anomaly flux whenever the tracer sponge was off: 1.2 % of the release in the tiny nesting tutorial, and 0.3-0.6 % on the CCS child's south edge. The investigation is CWorthy-ocean/claude-docs#127.

## Breaking Changes
- `UPSCALING` builds give different answers at their open-boundary faces, for every tracer including temperature and salinity, so results don't match earlier runs bit for bit.
  - No test reference hashes change, because no hashed test compiles `UPSCALING`.

## New Features
- N/A

## Bug Fixes
- The `_uscl` boundary export no longer runs inward on outflow faces, which made the child gain anomaly from nowhere and the upscaled parent lose it.

## Improvements
- N/A

## Miscellaneous
- The `UPSCALING` description in the docs and in `cppdefs.opt` now says that the switch also makes the open-boundary tracer face flux first-order upwind.
- A new test releases ALK one column inside the east boundary and checks that the east-face export never goes inward.

## Notes for Reviewers
- **The new test discriminates.** Face-summed east `ALK_add_east` per 200 s window, in meq/s, over four windows: on `main` -611.9, -2662.0, -5006.5, -7317.2; on this branch +187.9, +933.5, +2108.6, +3760.9. On `main` the new test fails and the other nine pass.
- **The existing upscaling tests barely move.** In `test_upscaling.py`, the perturbation budget still closes to 1e-8 with the tracer sponge on and off. Under the old code, the export is +1.363240e9 meq with the sponge on and -1.118420e9 with it off; this branch gives +1.362876e9 and -1.118266e9. The uniform perturbation has almost no curvature at the faces.
- **Interior schemes.** The boundary face flux is now an assignment, not an increment, so it doesn't depend on the interior advection scheme. Under `UPSTREAM_TS`, inflow answers are unchanged, since the old inflow patch was already pure upwind there. Under the 4th-order and `AKIMA` schemes, inflow changes too, because the old increment left a gradient term in place.
- **Periodic directions.** The blocks are now inside `#ifndef EW_PERIODIC` / `#ifndef NS_PERIODIC`, the same pattern the header uses for its edge extrapolation. Without that, the `inode`/`jnode` guards would make a periodic seam first-order upwind when `npx=1` or `npy=1`.
- **Guards.** Every `UPSCALING` use in `src/` is guarded by `MARBL && MARBL_DIAGS && UPSCALING`, including the call to `init_upscale`. So a build with `UPSCALING` alone silently has no upscaling at all: no patch and no `_uscl` output. No build records an export without this fix, but that silent no-op may deserve its own error.
- **C-Star needs no code change,** because the upscaler passes the export through. Forge's `cppdefs.opt.j2` comment for `UPSCALING` could mention the numerics change as a comment-only follow-up.
- **End to end, C-Star's tiny nesting tutorial** (ucla-roms 0.13.0, currents-only sponge), with the child rerun on this commit and nothing else changed: the east-face ALK export goes from -3.36e8 meq (inward in all 24 hours, -1.17 % of the release) to +3.56e8 meq. Six early hours remain slightly inward, -1.4e7 meq in all (0.05 %).
- **End to end, the CCS example** (the child rerun 2010-01-16 to 02-23 on this commit, currents-only sponge): the south edge's inward ALK export falls from 0.31 % to 0.068 % of the release, and the inward hours from 236 to 168.
  - An upwind rebuild from restarts matches the recorded export to within 2-8 %.
  - What remains inward is mostly outflow of negative anomaly that the interior third-order scheme's undershoots carry to the edge. This change doesn't remove that.
  - Net export rises by 1.35 % of the release, because every open face, and with it the child's state, changes.
- **Local test environment.** The tests ran on macOS in the `cstar-nest` conda env (gfortran 15.3, mpich).

## Code Review Checklist
- [x] Closes CWorthy-ocean/claude-docs#130
- [ ] Any updates to namelist options or cppdefs are being propagated to C-Star/Forge (no new keys; only the Forge template comment, as a follow-up)
- [x] New functionality has documentation and tests
- [x] Tests and `pre-commit run --all-files` are passing (locally `test_upscale.py` + `test_upscaling.py`, 10 passed; pre-commit on the changed files)

author: muj-04
body:
A rejected drawing save could be overwritten by an older cloud bitmap on reopening the document. Drawing writes also swallowed database errors, and clearing drawings bypassed the document queue, allowing an earlier save to recreate cleared strokes.

Persist pending page keys alongside the existing local drawing cache, protect unsaved and current-mount edits during hydration, and acknowledge only the matching save version. Clearing uses the document queue and a document marker to cover pages not yet returned by initial hydration. Supabase errors now reject so failed writes are not acknowledged. Unmounted workspaces cannot acknowledge newer edits.

Validation: three original regressions failed before the fix (stale-cloud overwrite, swallowed database failure, save/clear race); an additional clear-before-initial-fetch regression also failed then passed. Final local suite: 144 passed, no failures/skips; TypeScript passed; ESLint 0 errors / 28 existing warnings; independent review passed. Eight focused regressions cover remount, failed clear, delayed acknowledgment, clean cloud updates and late hydration.

No migration or provider setting change. Integrate together with the annotation hydration PR #27, which adds document-deletion cleanup for these pending drawing markers; both build independently. Existing `studysync_` sign-out cleanup covers the new pending-key entry. Rollback is a code revert; the extra local key is harmless to old code. This preserves unsynced data but does not add automatic replay, cross-tab merge, quota recovery, or a durable sync outbox. Local mock/hook evidence is not authenticated hosted PDF acceptance. Production unchanged.

Combined verification: all six fixes together passed 179 tests, TypeScript, production build, and ESLint (0 errors / 28 existing warnings) on unpublished commit `874b6651a1d1afee2f23ed915cd09b91d7145cbd`. [Audit report and full coverage matrix](https://github.com/Muj-04/studysync/pull/28). All six code PR heads passed GitHub CI and Vercel Preview deployment; no PR was merged.

author: muj-04
body:
Room recordings could insert metadata with no playable URL after upload/signing failure, disappear silently on failed deletion, or reappear when a pending upload completed after deletion.

Require upload, signed URL and metadata success before announcing a shared recording. Surface failures while retaining the local recording, wait for pending saves before deleting, and remove/broadcast deletion only after the helper succeeds. Ignore completion notifications for unmounted or replaced rooms. Native alerts now explain failed save/delete outcomes; there is no new layout.

Validation: upload/sign failure and pending-save/delete race reproduced locally. Original regression failures were observed before the fix. Final suite: 149 passed, no failures/skips; 13 focused regressions; TypeScript passed; scoped ESLint passed. Tests exercise actual service error handling and hook lifecycle with synthetic media/provider boundaries. Independent review completed. No real microphone, two-user room, or provider acceptance is claimed.

No migration/configuration changes or PR dependencies; targets dev. Rollback: revert commit. Storage and DB remain separate resources: signing/metadata failure can leave an orphan, while a later DB-delete failure can leave metadata for removed audio. Blind rollback of an upserted object could delete previously published audio and is deliberately avoided. No durable offline recording queue/retry is added; the retained Blob lasts only for the current tab. Title updates/reconnect reconciliation and zero-row RLS mutation detection remain outside scope. See `docs/room-voice-failures.md`. Production unchanged.

Combined verification: all six fixes together passed 179 tests, TypeScript, production build, and ESLint (0 errors / 28 existing warnings) on unpublished commit `874b6651a1d1afee2f23ed915cd09b91d7145cbd`. [Audit report and full coverage matrix](https://github.com/Muj-04/studysync/pull/28). All six code PR heads passed GitHub CI and Vercel Preview deployment; no PR was merged.

author: scbrown
body:
## What

The first Python library slice from `docs/design/cross-language-bindings.md` (aegis-gqo.1). It adds a new crate at `bindings/python`, built with PyO3 and maturin. The distribution is `quipu-kg` and the import is `quipu`. The crate depends on the core by path, and every call goes through `quipu::bindings::Engine`. That is the same registry the WASM `Database` uses, so the handlers, transactions, vocabulary gate and SHACL write gate are the native ones. The binding has no second validator and writes no SQL.

- **Core:** adds `Engine::open(path)` for file-backed stores. Capabilities now report `storage: "file"` or `"memory"`. Shapes adopted in a file persist and are enforced again after reopen (Rust test included).
- **Python API:** `Store.memory()` and `Store.open(path)`, context-manager close, `load_shapes`/`remove_shapes`/`shapes`, `knot`, `episode`, `set`, `query` (current, `as_of_tx`, `valid_at`) and `history`.
  - SELECT returns a list of dicts, ASK a bool, CONSTRUCT a list of `(s, p, o)` tuples.
  - Tagged and typed literals come back as `quipu.Literal`. Integers stay lossless (9007199254740993 is tested).
  - The low-level `invoke` / `invoke_json` entry points return exact native results; `capabilities()` is exposed too.
- **Errors:** typed classes in `quipu.errors`. Each carries `code`, `operation`, `commit_state`, `retryable=False` and `details`. A knot refused by the write gate raises `ValidationError` with the native SHACL report.
- **Thread affinity:** this is a stated limitation, not a concurrency promise. A handle refuses calls from any thread except the one that opened it, with `ThreadAffinityError` (`not_started`), and the owner keeps working afterwards. Tests cover query, capabilities, shapes, invoke_json and close. The GIL is held for every call, no Python runs under a store borrow, and there is no free-threaded support.
- **Shared conformance corpus:** `tests/fixtures/bindings-conformance/v1.json` (6 cases). Two runners read the same file:
  - natively, `tests/bindings_conformance.rs`;
  - in Python, through both the object path and the JSON-text path.
  - The cases cover: unsupported operation, writes before schema adoption, shapes, knot, set, current and as-of query, history, a SHACL refusal with no leaked fact plus a positive control, large integers and language tags, and an off-vocabulary episode refusal plus a control.
  - A test perturbs one expectation to prove the matcher can fail.
- **CI:** builds manylinux x86_64/aarch64 and macOS arm64 wheels for CPython 3.11–3.14, plus an sdist. Each artifact is installed into a clean venv (`--no-index`) and tested from outside the tree. The sdist is built into a wheel and tested. The binding crate gets fmt and clippy. **There is no publish job.**
- **Test fix:** `share_alignments_tests` now creates its FIFO with `mkfifo(1)`. `rustix::fs::mkfifoat` does not exist on Apple targets, so the lib tests did not compile on macOS.

## Workflow

`.github/workflows/python-bindings.yml` (pushed over SSH; the gh token lacks `workflow` scope). Every job runs `scripts/sync-python-binding.py` before its `--locked` build. Follow-up aegis-sw4: run the same script from release.yml on release PRs.

## Evidence (local, macOS arm64, CPython 3.14)

- `cargo test --lib bindings::`: 11 passed. `cargo test --test bindings_conformance`: 1 passed (all 6 cases).
- `maturin build`, then `pip install` of the wheel into a fresh venv, then `pytest` run from outside the tree: **32 passed**.
- The acceptance script opens a file store, loads a shape and knots data. A bad write is refused with "MinCount(1) not satisfied". The current query returns `Second` and the as-of query returns `First`. History reads `assert First / retract First / assert Second`. Capabilities report `0.16.4`, the revision `4f99659…` and `file` storage.
- `maturin sdist` built (3.7 MB). I did not build a wheel from the sdist locally because the shared host was below its disk floor; that check is in the staged workflow.

## Still open (not in this slice)

- PyPI publication, which needs the one-way release gate and an owner Trusted Publisher; free-threaded CPython; Python hook callbacks.
- Query results return IRIs and plain strings both as `str`, because the native JSON does not tell them apart. Typed IRI results are an open fidelity row.
- An sdist built outside a git checkout reports revision `unknown`. Pinning the revision into the sdist is open.
- `bindings/python/Cargo.lock` pins `quipu-ai 0.16.4`. A release-plz root bump will leave it stale, and the wheel jobs build with `--locked`, so release-plz needs to refresh this lock as well. A test also checks that the binding's Cargo version equals the core version.
- Windows wheels, and macOS x86_64.

Do not merge without an independent, non-author review.

author: nedymax
body:
## Key change

Brings the iOS chat list header to the sidebar.

- **Folder bar:** each folder gets its own glass pill under the header, as in Telegram for iOS. The selected folder is tinted in the accent color. The selected folder is scrolled into view, and the strip fades its ends only where more folders continue. Opened forums keep the chat list header above the pills.
  - With the Liquid Glass setting off or Reduce Transparency on, the pills become plain. It switches live when either setting changes.
  - The folder bar recolors itself when the theme changes.
- **Search:** the search field is hidden until the chat list is pulled down, as on iOS. It reuses the stories reveal model (`StoryRevealModel` now takes its pull distance as a parameter). The first pull reveals search, and only a second pull opens stories. Scrolling down closes stories first, then search.
- **Header edge:** the chat list header gets the system soft scroll edge effect, and the chat list is clipped to the sidebar panel's existing rounded outline. The folder pills are left out of the edge effect so they keep their own glass.

## Reason

The macOS 26 sidebar keeps the older chat list header: a permanent search field and a flat folder strip with an underline. Telegram for iOS already moved to glass folder pills and a pull-down search, so the Mac sidebar looked worse next to it.

This replaces #131, which used a single capsule with a lens bubble. The pills version drops that bubble and the code that drove it.

## Screenshot/video result (before/after)

### Before

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b544a97-d3b0-497b-9e0d-772d92169d22

### After

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8dc4da89-8fb3-4b57-8ad6-e70f6d73d7b1

## Confirmation

- Checked: switching folders by clicking and with keyboard shortcuts, scrolling the folder strip, pulling the chat list down to reveal search and then stories, scrolling back up, and switching between light and dark themes.
- The header edge uses AppKit's scroll pocket through private selectors (`registerPocketContainer:onEdge:`), the same mechanism `ScrollView` already uses to turn pockets off.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body: ## Summary Fixes code-scan finding sfind-ca01b9e4 (CWE-117, access log injection). `fpm_log_write` copied request-derived strings into the access log as-is. A Basic-auth user name that base64-decodes to `bob\n127.0.0.1 - admin ...` (or CR/LF in the URI or query string) therefore started a forged log line, and the default `access.format` (`%R - %u %t "%m %r" %s`) includes `%u`. New static helper `fpm_log_stream_escaped_str()` in `sapi/fpm/fpm/fpm_log.c` writes each byte `< 0x20` and `0x7f` as `\xNN` (lowercase hex). Runs of safe bytes still go to `zlog_stream_str` in chunks, so `log_limit` truncation behaves as before. These tokens now use the helper: | token | source | |---|---| | `%u` | `proc.auth_user` | | `%r` | `proc.request_uri` | | `%q` | `proc.query_string` | | `%m` | `proc.request_method` | | `%f` | `proc.script_filename` | | `%{VAR}e` | FastCGI env | | `%{Header}o` | response header value | Printable ASCII and UTF-8 bytes (≥ 0x80) are unchanged, so existing log lines look the same. `"` and `\` are not escaped, which keeps the change minimal and limited to line splitting. Example: `Authorization: Basic base64("bob\n127.0.0.1 - admin [fake entry]:x")` with `%u` now logs one line, `bob\x0a127.0.0.1 - admin [fake entry]`. Regression test: `sapi/fpm/tests/log-access-escape-control-chars.phpt` covers CR/LF in auth user, URI and query, TAB/DEL in `%e`, and a normal request that is not escaped. NEWS entry added under FPM. **Verification status:** the new `.phpt` has **not been run anywhere**. - **No local build:** php-src isn't built on the session VM, and building it needs `re2c`. Installing that needs apt access, which is blocked by the session network policy (access requested). - **No CI:** the repo's GitHub Actions `Test` workflow did not start for this PR (only Socket Security and Devin Review ran). Actions appear to be disabled on this fork. What was run: I extracted the helper from `fpm_log.c` and compiled it in a standalone gcc `-Wall -Wextra -Werror` harness with a stub `zlog_stream_str`. All 7 cases passed: CR/LF, 0x01/0x1f/0x7f, TAB, UTF-8 passthrough, empty string, and `-`. Before merging, run `TEST_FPM_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 make test TESTS=sapi/fpm/tests/log-access-escape-control-chars.phpt` (or the whole `sapi/fpm/tests`) on a php-fpm build. author: castronova
body:
## Summary

Lake time-series charts now show the Quality Level in their tooltips, draw each observation once, and no longer offer point selection. Jira: [CAM-1483](https://cuahsi.atlassian.net/browse/CAM-1483).

**Quality Level in lake tooltips.** The tooltip footer read only `reach_q`, so lake charts (Quality Flag `quality_f`) never showed a Quality Level. It now uses the same lookup as the point colours:

```diff
 tooltip footer (LineChart.vue)
   if plot has no Quality Flags (Discharge)
     return ''
-  look up reach_q
+  chartStore.getQualityLevelOption(point)
+    determineQualityLabel(point)   # quality_f, reach_q or node_q
```

**Duplicate observations.** HydroCron's `SWOT_L2_HR_LakeSP_D` collection holds two versions of some granules (product counters `_01` and `_02`) and returns both. Lake charts drew two identical points at the same time, and the tooltip listed both values. Chart datasets now keep one measurement per `time_str`:

```diff
 getChartDatasets (charts.js)
-  measurements = removeInvalidMeasurements(measurements)
+  measurements = removeDuplicateMeasurements(removeInvalidMeasurements(measurements))
```

**Point selection on lakes.** Selecting time-series points only filters the Long Profile, which lakes don't have. On a lake, the View Long Profile button stayed in a loading state forever. Lake charts now ignore point clicks and hide the Selected Timestamps card. The "Timstamp deselected" alert, shown when a reach point is deselected, is also removed.

```diff
 handleTimeseriesPointClick
+  if active feature is a PriorLake
+    return
   addSelectedTimeseriesPoint
     if already selected
-      displayAlert('Timstamp deselected')
       removeSelectedTimeseriesPoint
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** lake `6350036102` from HydroCron has 108 time-series points, with 2 at `2023-08-03T19:03:42Z` (one from each granule version). Its tooltips show no Data Quality line.
  **After:** the same data runs through the new rule and gives 106 points, with 1 at `2023-08-03T19:03:42Z`. The tooltip footer reads `quality_f`, so lake points show `Data Quality: <level>`.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run format` and `npm run build` pass in `frontend/`.
- Not yet checked in a browser. To check: open lake `6350036102` with a time range that includes August 2023, hover over points, and click one. Then open a reach and confirm its tooltips, point selection and View Long Profile are unchanged.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

author: erickweyunga
body:
A session check used to make three queries in a row: the schema version, the session, then its record. Against a distant database, a signed-in page waited for all three.

- The schema version, the session and the record are now read in one query, with one branch per auth collection in the cached schema.
- The record comes back as JSON and is decoded with the same parsers a select uses, so it is identical field for field.
- After a schema change, the schema is reloaded and the record is read again. A query naming a renamed table is retried once.
- Renewal is still a separate update, at most once a day. Revocation and password changes still apply on the next request.

Tests cover the query count, schema changes made by another instance, and a record with every field type compared to a plain select.

## Summary by Sourcery

Make session validation read the schema version, session, and authenticated record in a single database round trip.

Bug Fixes:
- Reduce signed-in session checks from three database queries to one while preserving revocation, password-change, renewal, and schema-change behavior.

Enhancements:
- Return authenticated records from the combined session lookup with the same values and field fidelity as normal selects.
- Detect stale cached schemas during session checks, reload them when needed, and retry once after concurrent collection changes.

Tests:
- Add coverage for session query counts, renewal behavior, cross-instance schema changes, revocations, and record equivalence across field types.

body:
Runs bivium on Bun instead of Node, and clones history without old file
contents.

`bunx bivium` runs the bin under its `#!/usr/bin/env node` shebang.
Timed on sveld with the published 0.2.0 bundle, `bivium plan` takes 110
ms on Node and 60 ms on Bun, and `--bun` uses the Bun the job already
installed.

A PR's checkout fetches full history for the merge base, but a plan only
reads the old version of a changed barrel or lockfile. With
`filter: blob:none` git fetches those on demand. On
carbon-components-svelte
(carbon-design-system/carbon-components-svelte#5203) that cut the
checkout step from a 6.3 s median to 3.8 s.

author: ypark
body:
On 27 October one key on a marked map trashed ~1,800 messages (Sent, STAT_LAB, Inbox), and the filter learnt each as thrown away; the auto filter then trashed a colleague's mail on its own. Nothing was lost: the mail was restored with the new `letterbox trash restore`. This release keeps it from happening again.

## Rules, each held by tests
- **The map is looked at.** On its clusters no key moves mail; down at a message, or reading it, it is acted on alone. Fixes `d` while reading on the map trashing the list's hidden message.
- **Selection by mouse only** (drag over rows, Ctrl-click, Shift-click; S-↑↓ too). `v` and space select nothing; nothing is selected on the map.
- **Several are asked about first**: trash, archive, filing (`Y`, `m`, `N`), moving to another account. Inbox and sent mail are left out of a bulk trash unless taken (`i`, `s`).
- **Nothing is removed from Trash for good.** The 7-day expunge, `Ask::Expunge` and `Store::expunge` are removed; the trash record ages out after a month, the mail untouched.
- **`C-x u`** undoes the last bulk trash by where each landed (no Message-ID lookup), taking back what it taught; or a label renamed.
- **Only single decisions teach.** Bulk acts, selections, and the filter's own guess taken teach nothing. `filter learn` skips mail letterbox trashed.
- **The auto filter only asks**: said at the foot; `J` lists each with why; `space` chooses, `d` throws those chosen, `n` says not junk (learnt as kept).

## Commands
- `letterbox trash restore --since … [--until] [--account] [--origin …] [--dry-run] [--yes]`: counted put back only once found back in its folder; refused while letterbox is open; the record written once.
- `letterbox filter forget --since … [--until] [--yes]`: says how many, asks first; a date typed as bare digits (`20261027`) is refused, not read as 1970.

## Also
- Rename from the map (`R`, or right-click a label's anchor): asked first, never onto a label there is, undone by `C-x u`.
- The Trash folder asked for never offers Inbox, Sent or Drafts.
- README: "What letterbox never does".

Reviewed by an audit of every mail-moving path and by `/code-review`; all findings addressed. 314 tests pass; fmt and clippy (all features) clean.

## After merge
On the laptop, with letterbox closed: install 0.4.11, then
`letterbox filter forget --since "2026-10-27 13:50" --until "2026-10-27 14:00"` to drop the 1,794 mistaken lessons.

author: tomas7744
body:
## Co se mění
Fronta čtení z cache a fronta vykreslování offline map už nejsou FIFO. Pořadí se vyhodnocuje až při výběru úlohy podle toho, co uživatel vidí právě teď:

- **Třídy:** hlavní mapa před překryvem (trasy, reliéf) před kachlovníkem v rohu; předvykreslení okolí a ostatní (bez příjemce s naléhavostí) až na konci.
- **Uvnitř třídy:** dlaždice ve viditelné oblasti před ostatními, od středu ven; při shodě dřívější požadavek.
- **Zastaralé:** dlaždice, která už v kachlovníku není (nebo ji nikdo nechce), se při výběru bez chyby zahodí. Rozpracovaná dlaždice se nikdy nepřerušuje. Kontrola je při výběru z fronty, tedy těsně před začátkem čtení/vykreslování.
- **Hladovění:** úloha ve třídách 1–2, která čeká déle než 2 s, předběhne ostatní. Předvykreslení okolí může při nepřetržitém posunu čekat, což je záměr.
- Počet vláken (disk i mapsforge) beze změny. Stahování z webu beze změny.
- Výpočet pořadí nebere žádný zámek dlaždice (kopie příjemců ve `volatile` poli, čtení polohy komponenty), takže nehrozí deadlock s `Kachlice`; `zahod()` se volá mimo zámek fronty.

Nové: `PrioritniFronta`, `ImageReceiver.dulezitost()`, `JKachle.dulezitost()`, `JKachlovnik.trida()`.

## Testy
- `PrioritniFrontaTest` (8): pořadí podle priority, shoda = dřívější, pořadí až při výběru, přeskočení zastaralých, probuzení čekajícího `take`, souběh bez deadlocku, posun mapy (100 úloh, polovina vypadne z výřezu, ostatní od středu).
- Mutace porovnání pořadí rozbije 3 testy.
- `./mvnw -B verify`: BUILD SUCCESS, SpotBugs 0.

## Měření (Linux, Xvfb, 4 jádra, cache 1,6 GB, offline mapa; základ = main + #606, diagnostika dlaždic)
Scénář `scenar-dlazdice.py`, rychlé skoky (pauza 0,25 s), 2 běhy každé varianty střídavě:

| | základ | s prioritami |
|---|---|---|
| posun, do poslední dlaždice p95 | 69 / 13 ms | 38 / 16 ms |
| zoom ±3, do poslední dlaždice p95 | 34 / 27 ms | 30 / 30 ms |
| vykreslení, čekání ve frontě p95 | 169 / 21 ms | 8 / 11 ms |
| disk, čekání ve frontě p95 | 96 / 179 ms | 151 / 265 ms |

Na Linuxu se strojovou cache jsou fronty mělké (čeká typicky 5–40 dlaždic, čekání pod ~20 ms), takže rozdíl je v rozptylu měření; zhoršení neukazuje. Efekt se čeká tam, kde fronta narůstá (pomalejší disk, Windows); to změří RC13.

## Návrh řádku do CHANGELOGu
- Mapa po posunu nejdřív vykreslí dlaždice, které jsou vidět.

author: dghosef
body:
Ready for review.

**Stacked on #858.**

With data parallelism, each replica keeps its own per-request resource state: KV and prefix caches today, and recurrent snapshots or LoRA adapters later. But #858 picks a replica by load only. A request that one replica could serve cheaply, for example because it already holds the request's prefix, can land on another replica and redo that work. This PR makes the replica pick resource-aware:

1. For each declared resource that opts in, the conductor keeps a lightweight per-replica mirror. A mirror copies its resource's own decision rules and is updated at dispatch and release.
2. For a new request, each mirror reports named facts about what that replica would have to do: here `work` (the prompt positions) and `kv_hit` (the tokens it could skip).
3. One function prices those facts plus load, and the cheapest replica wins: `cost = w.load·load − w.prefix·kv_hit/work`. Weights come from `routing_weights: {load, prefix}`, 1 and 8 by default.
4. Node groups that share ranks now pick their replica together.

The KV prefix cache is the first resource with a mirror. Another resource plugs in with one mirror and one term in the cost function, with no router change.

## Results

DP2 on 2×H200 (Eras), this PR against #858. Orpheus, BAGEL and Qwen3.5 0.8B, with 3 server restarts per arm.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A predicted hit goes to the replica holding the prefix | Orpheus 8/8, BAGEL 8/8 |
| Predicted hit tokens = served | Orpheus 12/12, and 28/29 in a pool that evicts. BAGEL is one partial page low per hit, because the image ends inside a page. |
| `prefix: 1` only breaks ties | 0/264 picks went to a busier replica. Hit rates are the same as #858. |
| `prefix: 2` goes past ties | 35–37 picks to a busier replica. c=4 hit rate .74–.76 vs .64–.67 |
| Groups on the same ranks pick together | 0 splits, vs 58/96 (Orpheus) and 82/96 (BAGEL) on #858 at c=16 |
| Qwen3.5 doesn't regress | c=32 14.1k vs 13.8–13.9k tok/s. c=64 13.9–14.2k vs 13.5–13.9k |
| Failures | 0 in 64 jobs |

Orpheus at c=16 goes from 11.6–14.2 to 16.1–16.9 req/s. That gain comes from same-rank groups picking together, not from the KV term: hit rates are equal on both arms.

Router CPU per request (pick + add + remove), mean / p99 µs:

| Model | This PR | #858 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Orpheus | 54 / 97 | 60 / 138 |
| BAGEL | 88 / 235 | 84 / 147 |
| Qwen3.5 | 22 / 62 | 32 / 122 |

## Choosing the prefix weight

A resource's term prices what a replica would save as a share of the request's work, so work held whole is worth up to `prefix` live requests. The default is 8.

**Analytic.** A saved prefill token is worth τ; one more live request costs every request on the replica δ per decode step for L_out steps. So one live request is worth H₀ = δ·L_out/τ saved tokens:

| | τ (µs/token) | δ (ms/request) | H₀ (tokens) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3.5 0.8B | 4.1 | 0.042 | 3,073 |
| Qwen3.5 9B | 24.2 | 0.051 | 626 |
| BAGEL | 24.6 | 0.068 | 464 |

A term priced in tokens would need a per-model constant that varies 6.6×. A share needs none.

**Simulation.** An event simulator runs this PR's router and mirrors against replicas timed by the measurements above. It covers DP 2 and 8, load at 0.3–1.0 of capacity, pools from full to ⅛, ShareGPT multi-turn (with and without a 4k document), the Mooncake conversation and tool-agent traces, and a no-reuse control. TTFT is relative to load-only, as a geomean over the scenarios load-only serves stably (38 on 0.8B, 29 on 9B):

| Prefix term | 0.8B p50 / p99 | 9B p50 / p99 | Worst p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| share, 1 (old default) | 0.98 / 0.99 | 0.89 / 0.98 | 1.05 |
| **share, 8** | **0.90 / 0.98** | **0.77 / 0.89** | 1.04 |
| share, 32 | 0.92 / 0.98 | 0.79 / 0.88 | 1.34 |
| tokens, best H₀ (768 / 626) | 0.92 / 0.98 | 0.78 / 0.92 | 1.05 |

Weights from 4 to 16 come within 1.5% of 8. Above 16 the worst case regresses as replicas fall out of balance: the busiest replica carries up to 1.28× the mean load at 32, against 1.12× at 8. The no-reuse control is 1.00 at every setting.

**Real test.** BAGEL DP2 on 2×H200 with 512 pages per replica: 256 ShareGPT conversations at c=16, then a no-reuse control at c=16. Each arm ran 3 rounds across restarts, in rotated order. Medians, with the simulator's prediction (it has no CPU overhead, so compare deltas):

| Arm | Follow-on TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) | Hit rate | Sim p50 / p99 (ms), hit | Control p50 / p99 (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #858 | 24.6 / 58.7 | .55 | 12.8 / 38.5, .55 | 22.8 / 71.6 |
| share, 8 | 23.6 / 40.7 | .74 | 10.7 / 21.4, .76 | 19.5 / 64.5 |
| tokens, H₀ = 58 | 23.6 / 40.3 | .74 | 10.7 / 20.9, .76 | 21.9 / 63.3 |

The simulator's order held: both forms cut follow-on p99 by about a third, and they tie with each other. Failures: 0 in 36 jobs. In the `MSTAR_PHASE_TIMING` profile no phase moved (iter_total 4.97–5.07 ms, event_sync 54–56% on every arm). The share form is kept because one weight fits every model.

## How it was tested

- The CPU Core suite on the Eras CPU box: 7763 passed. 2 failed (`test_eval_compare_multigpu` sudo retries), the same 2 that fail on this PR's previous head, so none are new.
- The routing tests were run with each mechanism switched off; all 12 fail that way.
- The GPU results above.

author: maxnezdyur
body:
Part of #33821. Depends on #33820, which adds the multipoint constraint layer this PR builds on. Until #33820 merges, this diff also shows its commit; review the last commit only.

The three PRs that replace #33820's single change set are:

1. #33820: the multipoint constraint layer, with RBE2 and RBE3;
2. this PR: `formulation = exact` on the nodal tie constraints;
3. #34250: `InclinedNoDisplacementConstraint`.

## Reason

The nodal tie constraints enforce `u_secondary = sum_j w_j u_primary_j` with a penalty or kinematically. The penalty tie is approximate, grows ill conditioned with the penalty, and is wrong in the mass matrix of an eigen solve. The kinematic tie is a residual transfer that stalls when no kernel couples the tied variables and after refinement.

## Design

- `LinearNodalConstraint`, `EqualValueBoundaryConstraint` and `EqualValueEmbeddedConstraint` gain `formulation = exact`. The constraint assembles nothing and hands one `DofConstraintRow` per secondary node to the `DofMap` through the hub of #33820. The `penalty` parameter becomes optional under `exact`.
- A nodal boundary condition on a secondary node wins over the tie, as it does in the residual formulations.
- `LinearNodalConstraint` keeps the weights it last handed to the `DofMap`, so a Control that changes `weights` rebuilds the exact constraints before the next solve.
- `NodalStickConstraint` and `MassFreeConstraint` reject `formulation = exact`, because neither is a fixed tie.
- `NodalConstraint::ghostPrimaryNodes()` keeps every primary node on every rank. Before, `LinearNodalConstraint` skipped a primary node that was remote on a distributed mesh, so the penalty formulation returned a wrong tie. The nodal constraint tests drop their replicated-mesh and single-rank restrictions (#29005).

## Impact

A new option on three existing constraints. The results of the penalty and kinematic formulations are unchanged. `penalty` is no longer required when `formulation = exact`.

author: nayskutzu
body:
Phase 1 of bring-your-own backup storage (builds on #400).

**What it adds**
- `featherpanel_user_storage_destinations` (encrypted config, status, last_error, soft delete) and `server_backups.destination_id`.
- `/api/user/storage-destinations`: list (with capabilities `byo_enabled`, `byo_s3`), create (tests the bucket automatically), update (a blank secret keeps the current one), `/test`, and delete (soft delete; returns how many backups are now orphaned). Activity log entries for every change.
- Admin settings (Backup storage category): `backup_byo_enabled`, `backup_byo_providers`, `backup_byo_max_per_user`. The existing `backup_s3_use_by_default` stays the global default.
- SSRF guard: https only, no credentials in the URL, and every resolved address must be public. Checked when a destination is saved and again on each use; DNS is pinned with CURLOPT_RESOLVE so it can't be rebound. `FEATHERPANEL_BYO_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=true` exists for local development only.
- `destination_id` on backup create (files and full). Download, restore and delete go to the destination's bucket using presigned URLs. Schedules, lifecycle hooks and cron accept only the server owner's destinations; if a destination is unusable, the backup is skipped and an activity entry is recorded. These backups still count toward the server backup limit.
- UI: an Account → Backup storage tab, a storage picker on Create Backup and in schedule tasks, and a storage badge on backup rows with an orphaned or disconnected state (download and restore are hidden in that state).
- WebSpace and VDS backups are not changed, because they don't use the Wings S3 flow.

**Verified locally (real requests)**
- SeaweedFS S3 with signature checks plus a fake Wings: create → object size and sha256 match → presigned download sha256 matches → restore (a browser-supplied URL is ignored) → delete removes the object, with no multipart uploads left behind.
- A scheduled backup through the cron processor path landed in the user bucket with a matching sha256. An unknown destination was skipped.
- After removing a destination: the backups show as orphaned, download and restore return 409 `DESTINATION_ORPHANED`, and delete removes only the record.
- SSRF rejections are covered by unit tests: http, loopback, 169.254, 10/8, ::1, ::ffff:127.0.0.1, 100.64/10, mixed answers, and unresolvable hosts.

body:
Closes #656

The concept's course look (docs/art/CONCEPT-LOOK.md steps 3 and 4; the owner, 2026-10-27: "this is the look and feel we need to get to"), baked into the ground chunks.

## What changed
- **`src/game/course-finish.ts`** (new, pure): the course finish's knobs, clamped: `on`, `along`, `bandWidth`, `bandStrength`, `greenWidth`, `greenStrength`, `collarWidth`, `collarTone`, `lip`. They ride in `painted-surfaces.json` as an optional `course` block (missing: the tuned look). `on: false` is the course exactly as before T227. Each additive knob at 0 leaves its part as before.
- **Fairway bands** now run **along** the line of play, as the concept's do. Doglegs keep T218's per-leg split, so the bands mitre round each bend (T218's across-the-hole bands showed a hard seam there). They are drawn by `renderer.mowBands`:
  - the dark bands are a multiply;
  - the light bands are a shine textured by the grass, as a lift in proportion to it (`shine(..., squared=false)` times a warm pale tint), so the texture and hue stay.
  - Tuned: 3 tiles (6 m) wide, strength 0.8: light x1.13, dark x0.82.
- **Range outfield** (Grass the outfield): the same bands along its line of play. `rangehost.outfieldStripes` passes the line (`MowStripes.lx/ly`). The desert outfield still has no stripes.
- **Greens**: fine stripes, 0.75 tile at strength 0.3, mown one way along the hole's last leg. `patch.ts stripeAreas` now also walks the green's cells.
- **Collar**:
  - Every first cut and the greens' fringe are toned darker: a multiply of a deep green at 0.45 over the fill and the feathers alike, so the texture stays and the edges match.
  - It is laid wider by default: the fairway's first cut is 4 m, the green's fringe 2 m.
  - The engine's `courseBorders` uses the Border slider's width, else the finish's, else BLOB_STYLE's. The slider starts from the finish's width (`PaintHost.collarDefault`). A surfaces save that changes the width lays the course again.
  - T204's rugged edge and spill sit at the band's new outer edge.
- **Bunker lips** (lip 1):
  - A cool, textured crescent on the sand along the far rim (the one facing the sun at the upper right), starting at the far wall's foot.
  - A textured light near lip, a gap inside the near rim.
  - The lip band is laid in the fairway's first cut, toned as the collar, unless the player picked a Border texture for the bunker (`CourseLooks.lipGrass` -> collar `g`). Its far side is lifted and its near side lightly shaded, so the bunker sits in the collar as in the concept.
  - The rims are sorted by sun facing in `course-finish lipRuns`. The paths are cached per layer (T217's pattern).
- **Studio > Painted > Course finish**: sliders and switches for every knob, Save writes the `course` block. `server.mjs` keeps the block in `writeSurfaces`. A studio from before this PR drops the block on save, which means the tuned look, so nothing breaks before it is restarted.
- **Console**: `window.__game.ground.setCourseFinish({ on: false })`, or any knobs.
- **`shine`** now clips its buffer work to the box it reads back. Before, a `copy` cleared the whole chunk-sized canvas on each call. The light inside the box is the same.

## Cost (same chunks, finish off vs on, alternating runs)
- Pooled worker bake ms per chunk, from `scripts/dev/course-look-shots.mjs --only bake --reps 8`:

  | Zoom | Bakes | Off: median / mean | On: median / mean |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | 30% | 96 | 20.9 / 20.5 | 19.7 / 19.9 |
  | 8% | 72 | 8.0 / 9.13 | 8.5 / 9.91 |

  So 0 to +0.8 ms, within T217's budget. The PC was shared with other agents' node processes, so single runs were noisy.
- `npm run bench -- --course` (dev server, finish off -> on):
  - fps: street 30% 57.0 -> 58.3, 17% 56.2 -> 57.2, district 8% 58.3 -> 58.8, 4.5% 59.9 -> 60, planner 60 -> 60;
  - average bake 15.4 -> 15.4 ms;
  - the course-paint stage's bake 25.4 -> 27.5 ms (it re-bakes course chunks continuously).

## Checks
- `npm run typecheck`: clean after merging origin/main.
- `tests/course-finish.test.ts` (new, 10 tests) covers:
  - the knobs clamp;
  - the file round trip;
  - off and each knob at 0 give the look before T227;
  - the bands follow the line of play (a straight hole, a dogleg's mitre, the range outfield);
  - the collar widths and who wins;
  - the green's line and the bunker lip's grass in the patch;
  - the lip lies on the far side (tile space against SUN_TILE_DIR, and the upper right on screen).
- With the neighbours: 172/172 pass across 20 files: course-stripes, the ext-course-* files, the golf-range ones, the painted ones (#637), swamp, waste-area-brush, rough-yards, ground-layers, living-ground.

- `hole-30pct-{off,on}.jpg`, `hole-15pct-{off,on}.jpg`: a hole with bunkers.
- `green-30pct-{off,on}.jpg`, `green-15pct-{off,on}.jpg`: a green with its collar.

author: jesuuss23
body:
Si el administrador desactivaba una categoría después de añadir un plato al carrito, OrderService todavía podía cotizarlo y registrarlo. El catálogo y ComboService ya filtraban categorías activas, pero faltaba hacerlo para productos y recomendaciones en el servicio de pedidos.

Se agregan filtros whereHas sobre category y product.category, respectivamente, para exigir is_active=true y aplicar el scope de borrado lógico de Category. El cambio cubre previewLine, quote y create, usados por carrito y checkout JSON. Conserva los mensajes de disponibilidad existentes y el recálculo de precios.

Los pedidos ya confirmados conservan sus datos históricos. Un reintento con token válido recupera el pedido existente aunque posteriormente se desactive su categoría; no se vuelve a crear ni notificar.

Alcance:
- Seis líneas de validación en OrderService.
- Un archivo de pruebas con 16 casos.
- Sin migraciones, cambios de interfaz, proveedores ni modificaciones del flujo de combos.
- No se pretende resolver desactivaciones concurrentes dentro de una transacción ya en ejecución; se valida el estado consultado al calcular las líneas.

Pruebas añadidas:
- Categorías inactivas y eliminadas lógicamente para productos y recomendaciones.
- Rechazo en preview, cotización y creación directa sin pedidos parciales ni avisos.
- Confirmación de carrito previamente válido: error de validación y conservación del carrito/token.
- Registro JSON después de cotizar: se vuelve a comprobar la categoría.
- Reactivación: permite comprar con el mismo token después de un intento rechazado.
- Reintento de pedido ya registrado: conserva pedido, total e historial, sin duplicar notificaciones.

Validación realizada: revisión estática de modelos, scopes, rutas, servicio y diff contra main 5abe53d. PHP y Composer no están disponibles en este entorno: no se ejecutaron php -l ni PHPUnit. El PR permanece en borrador hasta validar en la instalación del usuario.

Con SQLite en memoria de phpunit.xml (RefreshDatabase, nunca la base de producción):
```bash
php artisan test --filter=CheckoutCategoryAvailabilityTest
php artisan test --filter=JsonCheckoutTokenTest
php artisan test --filter=CartCheckoutConfirmationTest
php artisan test --filter=AdminOrderPaymentAndDispatchTest
```

Prueba manual: añadir un plato/recomendación y cotizar; desactivar su categoría desde administración; intentar confirmar sin volver a abrir el carrito. Debe rechazarse sin registrar pedido. Reactivar la categoría debe permitir volver a intentar la compra.

author: miikka-niemela
body:
Closes #37

## Spec
`specs/004-periods-and-sessions.md`

## Decision record
`decisions/f004-periods-and-sessions.md`

## Summary
The parent builds a period (*jakso*) on the trainer side. A period is numbered sessions (*treeni*), each with a place, the equipment at hand and a target length, made of blocks (*osio*) of library exercises with their own amounts. A new period starts as a copy of the latest. Deleting a library exercise is refused while a period uses it, naming the periods.

The database holds what the app cannot hold alone:
- An exclusion keeps a parent's periods from overlapping (migration 0004, with `btree_gist`).
- Positions are unique at commit, so a move swaps two in one transaction.
- The block exercise's key to its exercise is deferrable, so deleting a whole account works whichever cascade runs first.

Every write that counts or renumbers locks its parent row, and locks are always taken from the period down.

## How to verify
- [ ] `tests/e2e/periods.spec.ts`, on desktop and phone:
  - the menu's `Jaksot` and the lock page for every new address;
  - a first period, a session with its defaults, two blocks from the picker, an amount refused and then changed, a block and an exercise moved;
  - the second period copied in full;
  - an overlap refused, naming the period;
  - a used library exercise refused deletion, naming both periods;
  - a session deleted, renumbering the next;
  - a period deleted after its confirmation.
- [ ] `tests/integration/periods.test.ts`, against Postgres:
  - the exclusion deciding two saves at once;
  - 21 sessions added at once, giving 20;
  - neighbouring moves and deletes at once without a deadlock (all three fail with `deadlock detected` under the earlier lock order);
  - a library exercise taken by a block while it is being deleted;
  - one parent's rows out of another's reach;
  - one log line per write, ids only.
- [ ] `tests/unit/lib/periods/`:
  - today in Finnish time, at a year's turn and across the start of summer time;
  - each field at its boundaries;
  - a start date with month 13, year 0, or a last day past 9999 refused, not thrown.

## Checklist
- [x] The issue's boxes are ticked where verified, and an unticked one says why: all 15 ticked, each checked by the tests above, and the session page, a refused form and the picker looked at in screenshots on the phone layout
- [x] Self-review and the `code-review` skill were run on this diff before the first push. What they changed:
  - **Deadlocks:** moving or deleting a block, a block exercise or a session locked the row before its parent and then renumbered its siblings, so two neighbouring clicks could deadlock. Locks are now taken from the period down.
  - **A crashed refusal:** `isDay("2026-13-01")` threw instead of refusing.
  - **Lost input:** a refused field lost what was typed.
  - **The copy:** creating a period now copies the latest in one snapshot.
  - **A missing assertion:** most log lines were written but not asserted.
  - **Dead code:** a `clearOnSave` option did nothing.
  - **Duplicates removed:** the form reader, the refusal component, the label ordering and the span helper.
  - **Answered in the decision record instead of changed:** the server does not refuse an exercise that does not fit, and two refusals are told imperfectly in millisecond races.
  - **Mutations:** run on each new unit test and on the deadlock and log tests; all caught.
- [x] Tests pass, with unit coverage at 100%: `npm run verify` green (672 unit, 140 integration, 42 end-to-end), and the log test added after it passes on its own
- [x] User-facing strings are Finnish
- [x] No secrets and no personal data in the diff

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Enable trainers to build, copy, organize, and maintain complete training periods and sessions from the trainer side.

New Features:
- Add trainer-side period management with Finnish pages for creating, copying, editing, listing, and deleting training periods.
- Add ordered training sessions with configurable locations, equipment, target durations, blocks, and library exercises.
- Add exercise picking, per-block amounts, ordering controls, validation, confirmations, and progress against session targets.
- Prevent deletion of library exercises that are used by periods and report the affected periods.

Bug Fixes:
- Ensure concurrent period, session, block, and exercise writes preserve limits, ordering, ownership, and deletion safety.
- Handle calendar-date validation across Finnish time zones, year boundaries, daylight-saving changes, and invalid dates without throwing.
- Preserve refused form input and refresh forms with values saved elsewhere.

Enhancements:
- Add database-backed period overlap protection, deferred position uniqueness, cascading relationships, and concurrency-safe locking.
- Add UUID validation, parent-scoped access checks, snapshot-consistent reads and copies, and ID-only write logging.

Documentation:
- Add the period and session specification and decision record.

Tests:
- Add comprehensive unit, PostgreSQL integration, and end-to-end coverage for periods, sessions, concurrency, validation, ownership, logging, and exercise usage.

Chores:
- Refactor shared form, refusal, label-ordering, and deletion components for reuse across trainer features.

author: the-first-infiltrator
body:
Defragmenter's FAT12 and FAT16 operations now look up the installed Filesystems modules instead of carrying their own FAT engine. The old engine also served FAT32, so its corresponding module keeps FAT32 analysis, defragmentation and recovery working. A small child-process host preserves the existing command protocol and generic safety services; it checks root-owned module paths, ABI and width, and the module validates the opened volume again before writing. The ambiguous 4,085-cluster FAT boundary is rejected before mutation.

This requires the corresponding Filesystems change, https://github.com/Infiltrator-Projects/Filesystems/pull/64, which is stacked on PRs #63 and #60. The matching FAT module must be installed or upgraded before that format can be used. The quality gate checks out the exact Filesystems revision and builds disposable test modules rather than altering /System.

Validation: full warnings-as-errors build; FAT volume/directory/journal/model, relayout, module trust, boundary and wrong-target tests; interrupted recovery at all four durable journal stages and after each of twelve target writes for FAT12, FAT16 and FAT32, with mirrored FAT copies checked; ASan/UBSan on the host and modules; and Test Media full-payload packed and Growth Defrag checks for all three formats. The broader local suite passed after rerunning the clean-tree packaging test; the device-topology case was skipped in this environment. The FAT32 test separately checks that an unjournalled pre-transaction write changes only the FSInfo hint.

Draft: the existing exact-source and release-governance audit baselines predate this migration. They have not been advanced or bypassed; review and qualification of the new baseline are required before release. Physical media and actual power-loss behaviour remain unqualified.

body:
## Data-integrity issue
The squad parser checked the URL scheme and league path, but not the host. An external URL using the same path (for example `https://outside.example/premier/club.html`) could pass the filter and be fetched as if it were part of the trusted roster source.

## Fix
- Require squad links to use the same origin as the configured index page.
- Keep both `.htm` and `.html` support and the existing league-directory restriction.
- Extend the deterministic parser fixture with a same-path external-host link and verify it is rejected.

author: eric8810
body:
Refs #682。查 #754 CI 上两项偶发失败时发现，两个文件都不在 #754 里。

## 1. 连进来的运行时连接在行加载时断开，实例要拖 30 秒才结束（真问题）

`rutis-host --test kotlin` 的 `kotlin_runtimes_that_dial_in_are_instances` 偶发 `timed out (20s): the pixel's instance closed`。

- 本地加 CPU 负载复现：修复前 15 次失败 5 次，每次都卡满约 21 秒；修复后 15 次 0 次。
- 卡住时打出状态：被杀掉的那个连接的实例里，`probe` 还是 `starting`。测试数的是行的条目，数到两份就杀 pixel，这时其中一份还在加载。

原因：#682（cb84c553）让运行时进程结束时还在加载的行等它的运行时（`wait_for_the_runtime`，最多 `RUNTIME_GONE` 30 秒），由运行时的结束来取消。可是连进来的连接上的行（`RowRuntime::Connection`）没有谁来取消：
- 连接不会回来；
- 这个连接的实例要等这次加载：`AcceptInstances::accept` 等 `create_instance` 的 `settle`；
- 所以接入点到不了 `session.closed()` 和 release，实例留到 30 秒后才删掉。

修复：只有具名运行时的行才等；连接上的行和插件定义的副本立即失败，实例随连接结束。#682 对具名运行时的行为不变：`fault_containment` 的 Node、Python、Bun 15 项通过。远程运行时的行是 `RowRuntime::Named`，不受影响。

新测试 `crates/rutis-loader/tests/runtime_instances.rs::a_connection_dropping_while_its_rows_load_ends_its_instance_at_once`：运行时在 `rows.load` 时断开，实例立即结束（Connected 之后接着 Disconnected），下一个连接照常拿到实例。修复前 10 秒超时，修复后 0.03 秒。

## 2. `a_manifest_that_leaves_its_output_open_is_killed` 偶发 `no pid was written`（测试的问题）

读清单的期限只有 300 毫秒。负载高时，sh 还没执行到 `echo $! > pid`，读取就到了期限（`did not print`），把整组进程杀掉。代码这样做是对的，但测试接受了这个错误，又要求 pid 一定写过。

- 期限改为 5 秒。正常路径是脚本立即结束，`sleep` 占着输出，1 秒宽限后整组被杀（`output was still open`），正是这个测试要测的。
- 仍到期限且没有 pid 文件时，组已被杀，直接返回。
- 本地加负载跑 6 遍 `runtime::binary::tests`，都通过。

## 测试

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p rutis-loader --all-features --all-targets -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p rutis-loader --all-features`
- `cargo test -p rutis-host --features kotlin --test kotlin`

另有独立复审，无阻塞问题。

author: maxnezdyur
body:
Part of #33821. Depends on #33820, which adds the multipoint constraint layer this PR builds on. Until #33820 merges, this diff also shows its commit; review the last commit only.

The three PRs that replace #33820's single change set are:

1. #33820: the multipoint constraint layer, with RBE2 and RBE3;
2. #34249: `formulation = exact` on the nodal tie constraints;
3. this PR: `InclinedNoDisplacementConstraint`.

## Reason

`PenaltyInclinedNoDisplacementBC` enforces `u . n = 0` on a boundary that is not axis aligned with a penalty. The penalty adds stiffness to the support and must be tuned against the scaling of the displacements.

## Design

`InclinedNoDisplacementConstraint` is a `MultiPointConstraint`. It holds every node of a boundary in the plane of its support with one exact constraint per node, so the node slides freely in the plane and the support adds no stiffness. The normal is a given constant, or the area-weighted average of the normals of the boundary faces at each node, computed once from the undisplaced mesh. Where two supports meet, the constraints are triangularized so that each node has one exact constraint per support plane. The penalty form stays the right choice for large sliding on a curved support.

## Impact

One new solid mechanics object. No existing gold changes.

author: arob5
body:
## Summary

Slides for the 6th AIMES land data assimilation community virtual workshop
(10/28/2026), and the toy experiment and illustrations behind them, in
`experiments/presentation_aimes_talk/`. Everything is self-contained in that
directory; nothing outside it changes.

The deck (Quarto reveal.js on the dissertation brand theme) argues for
spatial parameter calibration over site-by-site or per-PFT calibration, shows
what a spatial prior and its posterior look like over North America, and
tests the idea on a toy problem: a one-pool carbon model at 200 sites with a
Gaussian process prior over two parameters, calibrated site by site (exact,
on a grid), spatially by NUTS (the reference), and by iterated posterior
linearization (the scalable, gradient-free method).

## Layout

The package is organized by role, so each figure can be traced to every
assumption behind it:

- `config.py`: every number (sizes, seeds, model constants, prior, noise,
  algorithm settings)
- `toy/`: the problem (region and drivers, carbon model, spatial prior,
  observations)
- `inference/`: the algorithms (site by site, NUTS, IPL), the common
  `PosteriorMoments` form, evaluation, and 2D posterior densities with KDE
  checks
- `illustrations/`: continental grids, prior draws, uncertainty maps,
  calibration options
- `results.py`: one schema per results file, shared by writer and reader
- `run/`: short workflow scripts; `plots.py` and `style.py` draw from saved
  results only
- `slides.qmd`, `slides.css`, `theme/`: the deck

`README.md` lists every figure, the script that makes it, and the
assumptions.

## Results quoted on the slides

- Held-out sites (no data): turnover RMSE 0.84 site by site (the prior) vs
  0.30 spatially; IPL 0.31.
- Cost: NUTS 1,906,877 model runs per site (with gradients) vs IPL 210 (no
  gradients), and essentially the same posterior mean map.
- The spatial posterior's contours (slide 7) come from a Gaussian KDE of the
  MCMC draws, checked against the exact site-by-site posterior: its 50% and
  90% regions hold within a few percent of their probability, on the wide
  side, which can only understate the narrowing.

## Caveats

One synthetic dataset and seed; the prior's hyperparameters are known; the
toy model is far simpler than SIPNET. The North America maps illustrate the
prior's form, with numbers chosen to look plausible, not fitted. The ProbPipe
diagram is copied from that repository's README (source and commit in the
README).

## Reproducing

```bash
uv run python -m experiments.presentation_aimes_talk.run.toy_experiment
uv run python -m experiments.presentation_aimes_talk.run.site_posteriors
uv run python -m experiments.presentation_aimes_talk.run.illustrations
uv run python -m experiments.presentation_aimes_talk.run.draw_figures
QUARTO_PYTHON=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.venv/bin/python quarto render experiments/presentation_aimes_talk/slides.qmd
```

No tests were added; the experiment is a talk artifact. `ruff check` passes
on the directory.

body:
Follow-up to the Clawd's Studio home screen (merged in #2/#3) after a day on the desk.

## What changes
- **Helpers**: one Clawd for the first active session, a mini helper for every other busy/waiting session and every active subagent (idle sessions don't count), capped at 20. 11 extra floor spots so a crowd still fits; helpers walk in and out through the door.
- **HUD**: the working / need you / idle / helpers counters are gone (the room shows that). Clock and date on the left, the 5-hour and weekly plan limits as two small colour-coded bars (5H, 7D) bottom right, tap opens Usage.
- **Flicker fix**: the room is now upscaled straight into LVGL's draw buffer from the draw callback (no intermediate 480x424 PSRAM image, 400 KB PSRAM freed), the index canvases are in internal RAM, and the speech bubble invalidates only its tail. LCD scan-out stalls (`lcd_n100`) per 30 s: 11-16 before, 1 after (same as the other screens).
- Clawd's feet redrawn as two chunky pairs; the speech bubble fades again (an unsigned `dt` was negated in the fade formula).
- Removes the `iso-clawd/` browser prototypes and `tools/mock_gen.py`, leftovers of the isometric home.

## Verified
- Flashed on the ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-4B; screenshots of code / wait / idle / crowded states; `dev.py perf` under the demo stream: 21 fps, cpu 38 %, `lcd_n100` 1 / 30 s.
- `tools/room_sim.py` renders 20 helpers and the scripted session with no stuck walks.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

https://claude.ai/code/session_01VkqiL74p392t39VrTb4BpQ

## Scan-out stalls (second commit)
The flicker reported after the first commit was the panel missing frames (`lcd_underruns`), 10-40 per minute with the room visible, 2-4 per minute on other screens. Device bisect against the pre-room firmware (0 in the same windows) with synthetic per-tick bursts: register-only compute harmless, one hammered `.bss` word up to 30 per 2 min, layout dependent. The engine's `Director` state sat in `.bss`; allocated in PSRAM it reads **0 in every 120 s window** (code, wait, idle, hidden). IRAM placement, a 4x vertical front porch and PSRAM canvases were tried and are unnecessary. Details in `docs/STATUS.md` ("Scan-out stalls") and `docs/PERF.md`.
