author: reztib
body:
# Pull Request: Initialisierung und erfolgreicher Übergang in den laxOS-Kernel

## Beschreibung
Dieser Pull Request implementiert das Fundament für das Laden und Ausführen des eigentlichen Betriebssystem-Kernels (`kernel.asm`) aus dem Bootloader heraus. Es markiert den erfolgreichen Übergang vom Master Boot Record (MBR) zur eigenständigen Kernel-Infrastruktur im 16-Bit Real Mode.

Zuvor scheiterte der Bootloader beim Sektoren-Lesen (`int 0x13`), da Geometrie-Konflikte in der Emulation vorlagen und der Kernel-Binärdatei die Mindestgröße fehlte. Diese strukturellen Hürden wurden vollständig behoben.

## Technische Änderungen

### 1. Bootloader-Optimierung (`boot/boot.asm`)
* **Laufwerks-Erzwingung:** Das Register `DL` wird vor dem BIOS-Aufruf explizit auf `0x00` gesetzt, um das korrekte erste Diskettenlaufwerk für den Ladevorgang zu garantieren.
* **Sicherheit:** Ein expliziter `cld`-Befehl (Clear Direction Flag) stellt sicher, dass das BIOS die Sektorendaten in der korrekten Speicherreihenfolge ablegt.
* **Fehlerbehandlung:** Das `disk_error`-Szenario wurde robust ausgebaut. Schlägt das Laden fehl, greift ein blockierender 5-Sekunden-Timer (`int 0x15, AH=0x86`), bevor das System via APM kontrolliert heruntergefahren wird.

### 2. Kernel-Infrastruktur (`boot/kernel.asm`)
* **Register- und Stack-Ausrichtung:** Nach dem Far-Jump (`jmp 0x1000:0000`) werden `DS`, `ES` und `SS` synchron an das Code-Segment `0x1000` angepasst. Der Stack-Pointer (`SP`) wird sicher auf `0xFFFF` gesetzt.
* **Bildschirm-Reset:** Implementierung einer sauberen Bildschirm-Bereinigung mittels BIOS-Scroll-Funktion (`int 0x10, AX=0x0600`) inklusive anschließender Cursor-Nullstellung.
* **Kontrollfluss-Korrektur:** Die Funktion `print_messageOnScreen` wurde mit einem lokalen `.done`-Label und einem korrekten `ret` versehen, um Registersalat und unkontrolliertes Hineinlaufen der CPU in andere Speichersegmente zu verhindern.
* **Sektoren-Padding:** Am Ende des Kernels wurde ein `times`-Padding eingefügt, welches die `kernel.bin` auf exakt 5 Sektoren (2560 Bytes) fixiert. Dies verhindert Unterlauf-Fehler beim BIOS-Laufwerks-Interrupt.

### 3. Build-System und Emulation (`Makefile`)
* Das Makefile wurde erweitert, um `boot.bin` und `kernel.bin` über `dd` lückenlos in ein standardisiertes 1,44 MB Disketten-Image (`laxOS.img`) zusammenzuführen (`seek=1`).
* Der QEMU-Aufruf wurde auf den Parameter `-fda` (Floppy Disk A) umgestellt, um die korrekte Sektorengeometrie und Laufwerks-ID im Real Mode bereitzustellen.

## Status & Testung
* **Erfolgreich getestet unter QEMU.**
* Nach der Auswahl von "laxOS starten" im Bootloader-Menü wird der Bildschirm zuverlässig geleert, die Kernel-Meldung ausgegeben, exakt 5 Sekunden gewartet und die CPU anschließend im `kernel_hang` sicher schlafen gelegt (`hlt`).

author: kopipengsiewdai
body:
Item 5 of the food fixes, first half: about half of the residents' thoughts were still in Malay, though they're asked to think in English.

**Cause.** The live save's last game day had 190 of 406 thoughts in Malay or dialect, by the project's own `looksForeign`. Plans were 2 of 13 and reflections 3 of 12. Only the act and business asks end with the language hint, "(If you speak to Fatimah, use Malay.)". That's the last thing read before the thought is written, and the thought took it up.

**Fix.** The ask now ends with "Think to yourself in English.", after the language to speak. The system prompt is unchanged byte for byte, so the cached prefix holds. The user prompt grows by about 7 uncached tokens a call.

`cleanThought` also strips a leading "Think:" or "Thinking:" echo, along with its closing emphasis. "Thinking about it, …" and "Think of the lorry: …" are left alone.

**Living town:** nothing saved changes. It applies from the next thought.

**Tests:** in `test/language-ask.test.ts`. The full suite and typecheck pass. A fresh-context Opus review found nothing blocking, and its cosmetic finding is fixed.

author: loopydev
body:
## What this changes

CodeQL's "clear text storage of sensitive information" (code-scanning alert 11, and the alert this PR first raised) is about what the browser remembers in `localStorage` (`wikid:user`). It turned out to be about the `mustChangePassword` flag (by its name), not the email. Neither is a secret: the session is an HttpOnly cookie, and the server is what enforces a password change. But neither needs storing either:

- The browser now remembers only the signed-in user's id and name.
- The email comes from the server as the app loads (the user's own profile request).
- Whether they must choose a new password also comes from the server: the first request is refused with `PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED`, which the store now recognises directly and shows the choose-a-new-password screen, without recording an error.
- While the server answers, the app shows a plain "Signing in…" screen, so nothing half-loaded flashes.
- Entries saved by earlier versions are rewritten without the email and the flag on the next load.

The browser-test sign-in helper no longer stores the email either.

## How it was tested

- New browser test: signs in through the form and checks no email is saved; then plants an old-style entry with an email, reloads, and checks it's removed.
- The "chooses their own password" browser test now also checks nothing password-related is stored, and that after a reload it goes straight back to the choose-a-new-password screen without the app showing. Passed 15/15.
- Watched a must-change-password user's reload: only "Signing in…" appeared before the password screen.
- Browser tests (51 passed, 2 skipped), API tests (101) and web unit tests (120) pass.

author: louishughes
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"louishughes"} -->
_Requested by **Louis** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01P6VtFc7ypog8VJUsR6DQcc?thread=cmsg_01P6VtFc7ypog8VJUsR6DQccV7qjhRnXypYd8Zq3AedjJ2)_

Closes #34

## What
- `importer/lock.py`: `import_lock(workspace_root, timeout_s=...)`, an OS file lock (`fcntl.flock` / `msvcrt.locking`) on `<workspace>/import.lock`. The OS releases it if the process dies.
- `importer/run.py`: the whole import holds the lock. Without it, two interleaved imports misjudge each other's live batch as crashed and mark each other's chats `not_seen`.
- `Limits.import_lock_timeout_s` (default 600), documented in `ke.example.toml`.
- Checkpoint resume stays deferred per M1_CONSOLIDATION; crash-and-rerun is already covered from slice I2.

## Tests
`tests/integration/test_concurrent_import.py` (3 new): two concurrent subprocess imports leave the same row counts as one serial import (one reports new, the other unchanged); the lock times out while held; it's free again after an error. The concurrency test fails 3/3 with the lock removed and passes 5/5 with it. ruff, mypy clean; 485 passed, 6 skipped. No existing test changed.

## Teach-back (`importer/lock.py`)
Only one import can write to a workspace at a time, because an import assumes it's alone when it decides what crashed and what's missing. It holds an operating-system lock on a file in the workspace, and a second import waits its turn. If the process crashes, the OS releases the lock, so nothing ever stays stuck.

author: therenow9
body: #### What's changed? Wood themes can show a small badge on the top screen with the loader the selected game will run in, and whether it will get widescreen. A theme opts in: ```ini [loader badge] show = 1 x = 137 y = 120 ``` `loader_badges.bmp` (in the theme folder) holds 4 frames of equal height, stacked vertically: 0 Pico Loader, 1 nds-bootstrap, 2 nds-bootstrap in widescreen (16:10), 3 Kernel. Pure black (0,0,0) is transparent. A bottom-up BMP at 1, 8, 16, 24 or 32 bits works; any other format is skipped. The 16:10 indicator is optional and up to the theme: frame 2 is only used when the game will get widescreen, so a theme can mark it (DSpico Dark adds a separate 16:10 tag next to BOOTSTRAP, below) or draw frame 2 the same as frame 1 to leave it out. How the frame is chosen (`loaderBadgeFrame()` in `fileBrowse.cpp`), following the launch code in `main.cpp`: - No badge for homebrew, TWLMenu++ files and invalid files. - `.ndz` files: Pico Loader. - DSiWare (#2697): Pico Loader when that launch applies (flashcard, DSi mode, saves in the games folder, Game Loader set to Pico Loader, save not kept as a `.sav`); otherwise nds-bootstrap when it is the DSiWare booter, and no badge for Unlaunch. - Retail games on the flashcard (`fat:`), by the game's Game Loader (`FC_GAME_LOADER`), else the global one: - Pico Loader, unless a DSi-only game outside DSi mode (then nds-bootstrap, as in `main.cpp`); - Kernel, unless the kernel isn't usable, the game is DSi-only, or it is a DSi-enhanced game in DSi mode on a console with DSi features (then nds-bootstrap). - Games on `sd:` and nds-bootstrap show nds-bootstrap. - nds-bootstrap shows the 16:10 frame when `SetWidescreen()` would run and find a patch: - It runs on `sd:`, or on `fat:` with DSi features (DSi mode for DSiWare). - Its own checks pass: widescreen on (per-game, else global), `Widescreen.cxi` found, 3DS, not macro mode, SCFG unlocked in DSi mode. - It finds a patch in its search order: `extras/widescreen/.bin`, then `-.bin`, then an entry in `widescreen.pck`. The `.pck` index is read once and capped at 8192 entries; the shipped file has 546. The badge sits next to the box art (icon views only, like #2698). It is worked out once per game, and again after the per-game settings menu closes. It keeps a copy of the pixels it covers: the box art panel writes behind it instead of over it, and changing frames goes straight from one to the other, so it never flickers and never cuts a hole in a cover. - Changes are in `graphics.cpp`, `graphics.h` and `fileBrowse.cpp` (+207/−9). Themes without the section are unchanged; skipped in macro mode. - Rebased on #2701 and #2704. It touches the same spots as #2703 (the statics after `loadedBoxArt`, after `drawWeekday()`, the `ImageType` enum tail and the `loadBmp` branches), so whichever merges later needs a small rebase; I'll do it. #### Where have you tested it? New Nintendo 3DS XL with a DSpico, TWiLight on the console SD, Pico Loader as the global Game Loader (v27.25.1 + #2695–#2698 + this change): - games on Pico Loader show its badge, with or without a cover; - games set to nds-bootstrap per game show the 16:10 badge when a widescreen patch is found, and the plain nds-bootstrap badge with widescreen off; - DSiWare on the DSpico shows Pico Loader, and nds-bootstrap after switching its Game Loader in the per-game menu; the badge updates when the menu closes; - scrolling through games with covers keeps the badge steady; - a theme without the section (CD - Indigo) is unchanged. nds-bootstrap with a widescreen patch (16:10), and with widescreen off: Pico Loader on a game without a cover: DSiWare on Pico Loader, and switched to nds-bootstrap in the per-game menu: *** #### Pull Request status - [ ] This PR has been tested using the latest version of devkitARM and libnds. Built in the `devkitpro/devkitarm:20241104` Docker image that the nightly workflow uses (no new warnings). The code was written with help from an AI assistant (Claude Code). I reviewed it and tested it on my console.
